author: jpoley
body:
## Problem

The testcontainers API turned client-supplied volume specs into Docker bind mounts with **no validation of the source path or the image name** (issue #190, HIGH). `plugins/testcontainers/lib/docker-client.ts` built `HostConfig.Binds` directly from `request.volumes[].source`:

```ts
const binds = (request.volumes || []).map((v) => `${v.source}:${v.target}${v.readOnly ? ":ro" : ""}`);
```

Exploit: `POST /api/testcontainers {"image":"alpine","volumes":[{"source":"/","target":"/host"}]}` mounts the whole host FS; `source:"/var/run/docker.sock"` yields full Docker-daemon control (host takeover) from a container the caller controls.

## Approach

New `plugins/testcontainers/lib/volume-validation.ts`:
- **Denylist first** (independent of the allowlist, survives a misconfigured workspace root): rejects `/`, `/var/run/docker.sock` (canonicalized — trailing slash, `//`, `.`/`..` segments, and **symlinks to the socket** all rejected), and daemon/system dirs.
- **Workspace-root allowlist**: `isValidPath(source, resolveWorkspaceRoot())` (the merged #189 realpath-canonicalized confinement) — the source must resolve within the configured workspace root. Named Docker volumes (non-host-path) are allowed; symlinks resolving outside the root are rejected.

Enforced at two layers:
- **Route (`app/api/testcontainers/route.ts`)** — authoritative: validates `image` (via `isValidDockerImageName`, the same helper `docker/pull` uses) and every volume source, returning **400 before any create** (whole-request reject, no partial creation).
- **`docker-client.createContainer` sink** — defense-in-depth throw before pull/create; this is the **sole gate** for non-route paths (`startComposeProject`, template-driven creation), so it is load-bearing.

## Testing (reusable)

- `tests/plugins/testcontainers/volume-validation.test.ts` — real temp dirs + symlink: legit path pass; `/` reject; `/var/run/docker.sock` reject (denylist); out-of-workspace reject; symlink-under-root-resolving-outside reject; named volume pass; denylist-independent-of-allowlist (docker.sock rejected even with root `/`).
- `tests/api/testcontainers-route.test.ts` — invalid image → 400 no create; `/` / docker.sock → 400 no create; valid image → 201; named volume → 201; unauth → 401 no create.
- `tests/plugins/testcontainers/docker-client-volume-confinement.test.ts` — sink throws for docker.sock/`/`; dockerode `createContainer`/`pull` never called.

### Gate (mirrors CI) — re-run against current main (merged in)

- `bun run typecheck` — clean · `bun run lint` — 0 errors · `bun run test` — 1379 passed / 2 skipped · `bun run build` — success · `bun run audit:auth` — 0 offenders / 0 stale

Both modes confirmed: workspace root is `/workspace` (container) or `expandPath(getSettings().basePath)` (host); the bind source is never rewritten (the host daemon resolves it), so confinement holds in both.

## Validation

- Producer: Claude Opus 4.8. Validator: independent Claude Sonnet — **PASS**, high confidence. Enumerated every bind-construction sink (only `docker-client.ts`), traced both route and compose paths (compose covered by the sink throw), and executed the validator against docker.sock variants including a **live symlink to the real host socket** — all rejected; denylist independent of allowlist proven. Full gate re-run green. Cross-provider (Codex) unavailable on this account; separate-model Claude reviewer used per project fallback.

Note (non-blocking, out of scope): `startComposeProject` marks a bad service `status: error` rather than aborting the whole project — but never creates the malicious container. Compose image names skip `isValidDockerImageName` (no marginal security impact — dockerode uses the Docker HTTP API, no shell).

Closes #190.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Update (round 2)

Supersedes closed PR #229. Its 1 Copilot comment is addressed in `cc6e1ba`: `validateVolumes` now **fails closed on non-array/malformed input** rather than throwing. A non-array `volumes` (object/string/number) → validation failure → route returns **400** (not a 500 from an uncaught `for...of` TypeError); `undefined`/`null` → treated as "no volumes" (allowed, unchanged); malformed entries (`[null]`, `{source: 123}`) → rejected without throwing (optional chaining + the existing non-string-source check). Applied at BOTH the route and the compose-path `docker-client` sink (controlled throw). Tests cover each malformed shape asserting 400 / controlled throw and no container created.

## Update (round 3)

Supersedes closed PR #232. Its 2 Copilot comments are addressed in `bc960f3`:
- **Type safety:** `image` and `tag` are now explicitly rejected with 400 if non-string (previously `image: 123` coerced to `"123"` via `RegExp#test`'s `ToString` and could pass the regex); the combined `imageRef` (`image:tag`) is validated.
- **Single validation:** removed the redundant second `validateVolumeSource` call in `createContainer` — `validateVolumes(request.volumes)` runs once and remains the authoritative sink-level gate (still hit by the compose path that bypasses the route, still fails closed on non-array/malformed). Verified: the docker.sock / `/` / out-of-workspace / non-array reject tests all stay green (single validation blocks every exploit path; no double realpath work).

## Update (round 4)

Supersedes closed PR #234. Copilot found a real defense-in-depth gap: `canonicalizeForDenylist` fell back to lexical `resolve()` when `realpathSync` threw, so a non-existent leaf under a symlinked ancestor (`link/newdir` where `link -> /dev`) was not dereferenced — the docker.sock/sensitive-path denylist could miss it when the workspace root is permissive. Fixed in `5d05054` with **walk-up-to-existing-ancestor canonicalization** (lstat no-follow walk → `realpathSync` the existing ancestor → re-append trailing segments), mirroring the merged #189 approach (implemented locally, no edit to worktree-manager). Fails **closed**: `isDeniedSource` treats an uncanonicalizable source (total realpath failure / dangling-symlink ancestor) as denied. A new test proves the symlinked-ancestor + non-existent-leaf case is now denied (and would have passed under the old lexical fallback).

author: akhmialeuski
body:
## Why

Structured PDF annotation import is the flagship feature of Zotero Integration — the most popular Zotero↔Obsidian plugin, which is now unmaintained (last release Aug 2024) and breaking with Zotero 9. Its users are actively looking for a replacement, and our live Zotero source currently only surfaces annotations as flat `{{note}}` text (and only ones converted to child notes). This PR gives Citation Extended first-class annotation import — with zero new prerequisites and **no external binaries** (Zotero Integration's `pdfannots2json` binary is one of its top breakage sources).

## What

### Data path
Native Zotero annotations are fetched via the Better BibTeX **JSON-RPC `item.attachments`** method — the same local endpoint (`127.0.0.1:23119/better-bibtex/json-rpc`) the live connection already uses for "Test connection". Requests are batched (50 citekeys per JSON-RPC batch POST); per-citekey errors are collected without failing the fetch; a transport failure degrades to a load warning so the bibliography always stays usable.

Verified against BBT source: `item.attachments` returns, per attachment, the `zotero://open-pdf` link, the file path, and the raw Zotero annotation JSON (`annotationType/Text/Comment/Color/PageLabel/SortIndex`, parsed position, `annotationImagePath` for image annotations).

### Template surface
- **`{{annotations}}`** — per annotation: `text`, `comment`, `type`, `color` (hex), `colorName` (Zotero's 8-color palette: yellow/red/green/blue/purple/magenta/orange/gray, verified against `Zotero.Annotations.COLORS`), `page` (1-based, from `position.pageIndex` with numeric-pageLabel fallback), `pageLabel`, `tags`, `imagePath`, `sortIndex` (document order), and **`openURI`** — a `zotero://open-pdf/library/items/KEY?page=N&annotation=ANNOT` deep link that opens the PDF in Zotero at the exact annotation (URL format verified against `ZoteroProtocolHandler.mjs`).
- **`{{attachments}}`** — key/path/title/openURI/annotationCount per attachment (also gives CSL-JSON users PDF links they previously lacked).
- **`{{annotationCount}}`** — for conditionals.

### Settings & lifecycle
- New per-database toggle **Import PDF annotations** (default off). The old combined "Import notes & annotations" toggle is renamed to **Import notes** — accurate, since BBT's `exportNotes` only ever exported child notes.
- The flag is folded into the source identity key, so toggling recreates the source.
- Offline cache upgraded to **v2** (raw export + annotation payload) so annotations survive Zotero-closed loads; v1 caches remain readable.

## Tests

- `tests/core/zotero/zotero-annotations.spec.ts` — normalization: color names, page derivation (position object / JSON string / numeric label / roman label), deep-link building, Windows storage paths, image annotations, sort order, malformed input tolerance
- `zotero-client.spec.ts` — batching (3 POSTs for 120 keys), per-key JSON-RPC errors, bare non-array response, unknown ids, HTTP/network errors, abort
- `zotero-source.spec.ts` — enrichment on/off, template-context exposure, graceful degradation, v2 cache write, offline re-attach, v1 compat
- schema/resolver/source-identity/settings-tab tests
- Full suite: **1388 tests, 82 suites pass**; statement coverage 95.75% (gate ≥95%); lint and build clean

## Docs

- `docs/templates/variables.md` — new "Zotero PDF Annotations" section (field tables + recipes incl. color-based grouping)
- `docs/use-cases/zotero-integration.md` — annotation import walkthrough with template examples
- `docs/data-sources.md` — split Notes / PDF annotations, cache note
- README — feature bullet + Network Use entry for the loopback Zotero connection

## Merge-order note

Independent of PR #81 (persist blocks) and the upcoming local-API PR — can merge in any order. Shares no new files with them; the only overlap is adjacent lines in `settings-schema`/`DatabaseConfig`, which git resolves or conflicts trivially.

RootTabs still handled the home canvas close button as direct view logic by calling the screen model from the SwiftUI button. That kept one more root interaction outside the TCA migration path and made the behavior harder to test as reducer-owned logic.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a narrow RootCanvasPresentationFeature with a dependency-backed client for hiding the canvas, then routes the overlay close button through that reducer effect. The migration follows the same slice shape as the adjacent root gateway problem and scene refresh reducers: keep the live NodeAppModel bridge small, keep the reducer action explicit, and keep RootTabs as the handoff point while the larger root model is migrated incrementally.

## User Impact

No intended UI behavior change. Tapping the canvas close button still hides the canvas, but the action now has reducer coverage and a source guard so future RootTabs work keeps this interaction in TCA.

body:
Closes #769.

## Defect
`_build_verdict`'s equity-IRR note gated "negative to sponsors" on `equity_irr <= 0`, so an exactly-0.00% (break-even) return printed the literally-false **"Equity IRR 0.00% — negative to sponsors."** Same falsehood class as the #706 `_build_ic_summary` `<= 0` → `< 0` fix. `finance/irr.py` (and the `analytics/core/metrics` sentinels) can emit an **exact** `0.0`, so the boundary is reachable.

## Fix
Gate the negative wording on strict `< 0`; give exactly-`0.0` its own honest word (`"break-even to sponsors"`). Four exhaustive cases: negative / break-even / positive-below-hurdle / positive-to-sponsors. Regression test at `equity_irr == 0.0` asserts the note shows `0.00%` + `break-even` and is **not** "negative".

## Financial impact
**None.** Pure presentation. Every committed/fixture `equity_irr` is strictly negative (lendercase −0.0486) → all stay in the `< 0` branch → rendered report byte-identical; the KPI oracle is unaffected. The new `== 0` branch is unreachable for any committed run.

body:
## Summary

Kat (social media manager) asked for a text update at the end of the 3rd and end of the 6th inning so she doesn't have to pull up the site mid-inning while she's at away games (e.g. Rougarou games). This wires that up:

- New `INNING_ALERT_TO` env var (comma-separated, same convention as `STATS_TO`) — an email-to-SMS carrier gateway address, e.g. `5551234567@vtext.com` for Verizon, `@txt.att.net` for AT&T, `@tmomail.net` for T-Mobile. No new paid service — reuses the existing Gmail/nodemailer sender.
- Fires once per game per configured inning (`3`, `6`), detected once the live feed shows the game has moved past that inning (or ended during/before it via walk-off/mercy rule).
- Sent-state is persisted to disk (`inning-alert-sent.json` in `CACHE_DIR`, same pattern as the existing `report-dispatched.json`), so a Render restart mid-game never re-sends a text or fires one retroactively for a boundary already passed.
- Feature is off by default — if `INNING_ALERT_TO` is unset, nothing changes.

Example text sent (formatted from the actual line score at that point):
```
End of 3rd: Gators 6-5 Bombers
Gators 0 0 0
Bombers 1 3 1
```

## Test plan

- [x] `node -c server.js` — syntax check passes
- [x] Booted the server locally (after `npm install`) — no startup errors, poll loop runs normally
- [x] Unit-verified the pure formatting/boundary-detection logic against the exact game state from the screenshots (Gators 6, Bombers 5, end of 3rd) — output matches expected text

## ENV KIT PHASE 1 — render-mode ruling + proof piece (Steps 0–3; HARD STOP before the batch)

**Lane:** env-kit-p1 (Blender manifests/scripts, rendered sheets, assets, docs). `src/sim`, `IsoScene.ts`, `realtime.ts`, `commands.ts` untouched. Step-0 territory check: zero open PRs; no live branch touches these files (combat lane branch not yet pushed — expected, different territory anyway).

### Step 2 — RULING (docs/env-kit/DECISION_KIT_RENDER_SCALE.md)

**FIXED tile-calibrated scale for ALL kit pieces; frame-to-fit BANNED for anything that recombines.** The prior is confirmed with one precision upgrade: the canon invariant is the **density** `canvas / ortho_scale = 64·√2 ≈ 90.5097 px per Blender unit` (1 BU = 1 tile edge) — **`2.8284` is that density at the unit pipeline's 256 canvas**. Kit pieces need per-piece canvases, so each job locks `ortho = canvas / 90.5097` (identical world→px scale, different frame). Locking the raw number instead of the density would silently shrink any piece rendered on a larger canvas.

**Root cause filed:** the character path's bbox auto-fit makes px-per-BU a function of the subject's own bounds — two modules meant to butt or stack disagree on the pixel height of the same world edge (1-px+ seams, storey misalignment, the 76px door no longer clearing the 56px thug). Units survive auto-fit because each is standalone and display-scaled at runtime via `figurePxH`; kit sheets have **no runtime rescale**.

**Verified in the shipped pipeline first** (per dispatch): anchor `(0.5, 1.0)` foot-baseline in `frame_camera` + both shipped manifests; uniform-cell 8-dir packer confirmed structurally wrong for static pieces (as #53 ruled); `force_ortho_scale` hook + both unit jobs already lock 2.8284. **Empirical calibration cube** (headless EEVEE in-container): 90.5105 px/BU measured, 128px tile diamond, 78.38px vertical edge — pixel-exact match to the derivation.

### Step 3 — PROOF PIECE (K's pixel eyeball gate)

**Sheet:** `public/assets/sprites/env/kit_storefront_low_2bay.png` (228² canvas, RAW PNG, no pngquant)
**Manifest:** `public/assets/sprites/env/kit_storefront_low_2bay_manifest.json`
**Render log:** `docs/env-kit/proof_kit_storefront_low.render.out`

Low-tier storefront ground floor (kit inventory #4), 2-tile frontage, procedural bpy geometry through `tools/blender/render_iso_kit.py` (new kit entry — single view, fixed density, reuses `render_iso_common`'s 60/45 camera + toon + Freestyle + lights). Corrected canon stack: bulkhead 20 / display glass 56 / transom 20 / fascia sign band 36 = **FLOOR_GROUND 132px**; commercial door **76px** (clears the 56px thug); warm noir neutrals only (no brass/red/green on scenery).

Receipts in the log: `FIXED-SCALE density=90.5097`, `VERIFY-STACK alpha-run=137px expect~132px` (the +5 is the 1.75px Freestyle outline top+bottom plus the pilaster's projected top face), `baseEdgePx` spans exactly **+128 / +64 px** — the 2-tile diamond edge.

**Blender scars honoured:** `BLENDER_EEVEE` (bpy 5.0.1 — this container CAN render headlessly: pip `bpy` + Mesa llvmpipe), `clear_scene()` first, split streams to files, RAW png, renders committed on this branch. Note for K: the same job runs locally via `blender -b -P tools/blender/render_iso_kit.py -- --job tools/blender/render_jobs/kit_storefront_low.json`.

### Green gate

`tsc --noEmit` clean · **1467 tests pass** (133 files; +4 in `tests/renderJobKitStorefront.test.ts` tying the emitted manifest to the `facadeKit.ts` constants and the density invariant) · `vite build` succeeds.

### ⚠️ HARD STOP — K gates before Step 4

Per dispatch: **no batch until K approves the proof pixels.** K's gates: (a) reads as a 1920s storefront band at correct scale next to a 56px thug; (b) iso skew right (2:1 top slope, dead-vertical edges); (c) values read (sign board / glass / door / bulkhead separate); (d) noir palette held.

**One discrepancy for K to rule:** the dispatch says a **28**-piece kit; the research spec (2026-06-30, brain) inventories **24** core pieces (§4, ≤30 band). Step 4 will follow whichever number K confirms — the index doc template is ready either way.

author: miguel-heygen
body:
## What

Two tracks on this branch, cleanly separable by path.

### media-use v2 — the agent Media OS (`skills/media-use/`)

**One verb, `resolve`, for every media need. Free-first, then local-first generation with cloud upsells.** media-use holds no keys; each external tool owns its own auth.

**Resolve + providers**
- `bgm` / `sfx` / `image` / `icon` / `voice`, HeyGen catalog first (free retrieval), deterministic provider cascade, freeze-to-disk + ledger + cross-project cache (`~/.media`).
- Consolidated the `hyperframes-media` skill in (audio engine now under `media-use/audio/`); 20 skills.
- Ingest (`--from` local files + direct URLs, SSRF-guarded), `--adopt`, `--local-only` offline mode.

**Generation is local-first with graceful cloud upsells** (all live-verified on a 24GB Mac):
- **Image**: HeyGen search → **local mflux (FLUX)** → **codex CLI** upsell. Local models are **RAM-graded**: `resolve` probes *available* RAM and auto-picks the best FLUX that fits (schnell int4 medium ~8GB `--low-ram`, FLUX.2 Klein 4B large, Qwen-Image xlarge). The agent can inspect the ladder (`describeModelLadder`) and override.
- **Voice**: **local Kokoro (free)** → **HeyGen TTS paid upsell** (HeyGen TTS now costs credits).
- **Video**: **local LTX 2.3 on MLX** (`videogen` ladder) → **`heygen video create` avatar-video** CLI upsell.
- **`--provider <name>`** forces one generator (e.g. a user says "make this image with codex" → `--provider codex`), bypassing the free-first default.

**Editing capabilities that were impossible before**
- **Transcript-driven cutting** (`transcript-cut.mjs`): word-timestamp edits (filler removal, silence-cut, ranges) compiled into frame-accurate ffmpeg cuts.
- **Declarative auto-duck** (`audio-duck.mjs`): speech spans → ready GSAP volume-tween block the runtime renders identically in preview + export; plus sidechain + two-pass `loudnorm` (-14/-16 LUFS) recipes.
- Media ops as agent guidance (ffmpeg/auto-editor/scenedetect) per OP1.

### Non-destructive Studio crop (`packages/studio/`, decision OP2)

Crop any element visually; persists as `clip-path: inset(...)` (one undo step per drag, media file untouched). Enter via canvas toolbar / Clip panel / double-click; Escape or click-outside exits. Pro-editor presentation (dim, crop frame, edge handles on the crop lines, drag the frame to move the window). **Every overlay surface respects the crop** — selection box, hover ring, rotate/resize handles, snap lines, marquee, off-canvas indicators — via one `toVisibleOverlayRect` primitive. Shortcuts panel documents the crop keys.

## Notable fixes found by real-data / live testing
- **muted preview↔render parity**: muted media was silent in preview but mixed at full volume in renders. Now pruned from the mix (pure `pruneMutedBrowserMedia` + tests).
- transcript-cut: punctuation/case-proof filler matching; codec-by-extension (AAC-in-WAV halved audio duration); `--copy` keyframe-snap warning.
- audio-duck: multi-line meta placement (`--sequential`/`--offsets`) — file-relative word times were merging into one bogus span.
- global manifest path (`~/.media/manifest.jsonl`) — the Studio cross-project asset view was reading the wrong location and always saw zero.
- CodeQL: removed polynomial-backtracking regexes from clip-path parsing.
- `tts --out` alias; `HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON` env override for local-model bootstrapping.

## Testing
All live-verified end-to-end on a 24GB M-series Mac: catalog resolve (bgm/sfx/image/icon/voice), HeyGen TTS + local Kokoro, local mflux/FLUX image gen (~20s photoreal), local LTX video gen (clip + audio), local Whisper + u2net, transcript-cut + audio-duck against real Whisper output, and a full producer render with the duck envelope (ffmpeg-measured). Unit suites: media-use libs (73), studio (1300+), studio-server (223); lint/format/typecheck clean.

## Parked by decision (not in scope)
Side-by-side local-vs-cloud comparison assets (CDN pending); TTS eval re-run; batch audio-engine TTS default stays HeyGen-if-credentialed (video skills lean on it for caption timing).

Fifth senior rotation — one module per track, off a clean main (#60/#61 merged). Sonnet-authored from specs, adversarially reviewed, findings fixed, all gates green.

## New modules (validator green on all four courses; 81 modules total)
- **iOS 17 · Widgets & Live Activities** — WidgetKit timelines + App Groups, ActivityKit (ActivityAttributes / nested ContentState), update/end wired to the live-tracking module

## Real pawwalk-api change (what Ruby 20 teaches, shipped for real)
- **rack-attack** IP throttle (300 req / 5 min), disabled in the test env so the suite isn't throttled
- **Pagination** on the bookings index — a capped `per_page` with limit/offset, response stays backward-compatible (still returns the array, adds `page`/`per_page` keys)

iOS and Python modules **clean**. Fixed the Android **BLOCKER** — the LocationRequest exercise returned a value but its checks weren't anchored to the return (a learner could build the right request into a dead variable and return a wrong one); both checks now anchor to `return LocationRequest.Builder(...)`. I deliberately **kept** the Ruby versioning check's strict anchor (the reviewer flagged it as over-strict, but its suggested loosening would let a route placed *after* the block's end wrongly pass — the anchor is protective, and the reviewer agreed it's non-exploitable).

body:
Closes #83. Addresses #62 (residents lack visible purpose).

## What changed

Charter-defined **festivals & town events**: the charter declares a `calendar` of recurring events; the sim schedules them off the world clock; residents gather via a new behavior-tree node; the HUD announces the event; the chronicle records each occurrence. Events are **DATA, not code** (CLAUDE.md invariant 1) — the engine interprets the calendar, nothing is hardcoded.

**Charter schema → v2** (with `migrateV1toV2`). Pre-calendar charters — including the flagship and every existing world — migrate to an empty calendar untouched, so there are **no `worlds/` edits**.

- **`engine/src/schemas/charter.ts`** — `CalendarEventSchema` + `calendar` section: `cadence.every_days`/`offset_days`, optional `phases` (subset of `day_phases`), all defaulted; versioned, round-trip-tested.
- **`engine/src/charter/migrate.ts`** — `migrateV1toV2` adds an empty calendar to older charters.
- **`engine/src/sim/calendar.ts`** — pure `activeEvent(calendar, clock)`: the event in effect now, derived entirely from the `founded_at`-derived world clock (#57). First-declared wins on overlap. No wall-clock reads.
- **`engine/src/schemas/behavior.ts`** — `on_event` node (`event` / `child` / optional `otherwise`); `"*"` matches any active event. The validation gate resolves `on_event.event` against the charter calendar.
- **`engine/src/sim/npcRuntime.ts` + `worldSim.ts`** — the runtime re-plans on the active event as well as the phase; the sim emits a `SimEvent` of type `event` once per occurrence.
- **`engine/src/api/worldApi.ts`** — `/api/world` returns the current `event`; the chronicle records `the <event> begins`.
- **`client`** — `WorldInfo.event` + HUD **"Today: <event>"**.

## How it was verified

```
$ pnpm typecheck
engine typecheck: Done · client typecheck: Done · studio typecheck: Done

$ pnpm test
engine test:  Test Files 18 passed (18) · Tests 122 passed (122)
client test:  Test Files  3 passed (3) · Tests  26 passed (26)
studio test:  Test Files  1 passed (1) · Tests   6 passed (6)

$ pnpm validate

body:
## Summary
- Refreshes /now-playing when the radio tab returns to the foreground
- Reconnects the metadata SSE stream on resume so mobile background drops do not leave stale track info
- Reuses the same metadata helpers for initial load and SSE updates

## Root cause
Mobile browsers can freeze or silently drop Server-Sent Events while a tab is backgrounded. If a track changes during that window, the existing EventSource may not deliver the update and the UI can keep showing the old title/artist/album/cover. Browsers emit resume signals like visibilitychange, pageshow, and focus; the client should treat those as a chance to reconcile state.

## Test Plan
- corepack pnpm build
- Playwright/Chromium mock: serve old /now-playing + inert /now-playing/events, change mocked track while UI remains stale, dispatch focus, verify title/artist/album update to the new track and EventSource reconnects

Notes: existing Astro/Vite warnings remain pre-existing.

body:
## Summary

Ships the B slice (B1-B6) of the Layer 3 bundle-intelligence design: memory
kind taxonomy, confidence surfaced on retrieval, and structured retrieval
warnings, wired end to end from write path through every read surface.

- **B1** — `MemoryKind` vocabulary (`decision`, `convention`, `gotcha`,
  `architecture`, `incident`, `digest`) written by distillation and
  observation candidate paths; carried through the console approve path and
  the distillation reduce path.
- **B2** — `confidence`/`kind` on context and search item payloads and on the
  rendered context text (`(kind, confidence X)` annotation).
- **B3** — structured retrieval warnings module (`budget_dropped`,
  `semantic_unavailable`, `stale_match`, `refuted_match`,
  `conflicting_memory`), each `{code, message, memory_id}`, persisted in
  bundle metadata and surfaced in the `> Warnings:` rendered block.
- **B4** — `kinds` request filter (up to 6 values) on `/v1/context` and
  `/v1/search`.
- **B5** — `kind`/`confidence` on inspection (memory + context-bundle
  endpoints), search-debug (exact/semantic/lexical/packed candidates,
  including a new `lexical_enabled`/`lexical_candidates` pair), MCP
  (`engram_search` render suffix), and the CLI `search` command.
- **B6** (this commit) — frontend rendering, docs, and e2e coverage:
  - Console: context bundle detail page gets a warnings banner (amber, one
    row per `{code, message}`) above the items list, plus a kind badge and
    confidence readout on each item.
  - Search debugger: kind badge + confidence readout on exact, semantic, and
    packed rows, plus a new "Lexical candidates" section shown when
    `lexical_enabled`.
  - `design.ts`: `incident` (red/danger) and `digest` (slate) kind styles
    added alongside the existing four.
  - Docs: `/v1/context` and `/v1/search` payload docs in
    `docs/api-reference.md` gain the `kinds` request filter, per-item
    `kind`/`confidence` fields, and the warnings array shape; `mcp-tools.md`
    documents the `engram_search` render suffix.
  - `scripts/e2e_golden_path.py`: shape-level assertions that every context
    item has `kind` (str) and `confidence` (str|None), and that the
    top-level `warnings` array entries are exactly `{code, message,
    memory_id}`.

## Migration note

`0027_memorycandidate_kind` (from B1) adds `MemoryCandidate.kind`. No data
backfill required — new candidates get a kind at creation; existing
candidates default to `''` and resolve through the same fallback the
frontend already uses for memories (`resolveKind`).

## Compatibility

All additions are additive: existing `items`/`warnings` consumers are
unaffected, and an empty `warnings` list is preserved for bundles with
nothing to flag.

- `docker exec engram-tester-l3b python -m pytest engram/ -q` — 1393 passed
  (pre-merge), 1404 passed, 1 skipped (post-merge with master), exit 0.
- `docker exec engram-tester-l3b ruff check engram/` — All checks passed,
  exit 0.
- `cd apps/frontend && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build` — clean
  build, all routes compiled (including `/context-bundles/[id]` and
  `/search-debug`), exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint <changed files>` — All checks passed, exit 0.
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('scripts/e2e_golden_path.py').read())"` —

body:
## Summary

A Telegram message whose first token is an http(s) URL is now archived instead of inboxed:

- **`dross-bot/web.go` (new)** — `splitURLMessage` detects leading-URL messages; `fetchPage` snapshots the page with [obelisk](https://github.com/go-shiori/obelisk) (one self-contained HTML file, images/CSS inlined as data URIs, JS stripped; 90s budget, 50 MB cap) and runs go-readability on the archived bytes for title + plain text (2 MB cap); `snapshotName` picks the user-visible attach filename. Non-HTML links (direct PDFs etc.) pass through raw.
- **`dross-bot/main.go`** — new `archiveURL` path calls the existing `archive-document` tool with the snapshot, the URL as `:SOURCE:` (forwards credited "via …"), trailing message text as the note body, extracted text for indexing, and an extra `inbox` tag → a `:literature:inbox:ATTACH:` note that inbox triage still sees. Fetch failure falls back to a plain inbox capture, so the URL is never lost. Reply shows title, URL, similar-notes nudges, and a caveat when a JS-rendered page yields no readable text.
- **Server unchanged** — URL fetching stays the client's job per the existing CONCEPT.md decision; `archive-document` already handles the attach copy, `.extract.txt` sidecar, and indexing.
- **Docs** — new URL-capture decision in CONCEPT.md, updated bot paragraph in CLAUDE.md, inbox/literature workflow notes in docs/notes-CLAUDE.md.

## Testing

- Offline tests: URL detection (10 cases), fetch pipeline against `httptest` (asserts the image is inlined as a data URI and the remote `src` is gone; readability title/text; non-HTML pass-through; timeout), snapshot naming.
- End-to-end smoke through the real `dross-mcp` binary + DB: snapshot → `archive-document` → verified the `:literature:inbox:ATTACH:` note, the attached HTML with its inlined image, and the `.extract.txt` sidecar.
- `go vet`, `go test ./...`, `make bot-build` all clean.

Known limitation (documented): JS-rendered pages (SPAs, paywalls) archive as shells; the reply flags it and `:SOURCE:` keeps the URL.

## What changed?

Several Loupe paths resolve selectors by walking the full
`LoupeSnapshot.nodes` map and recomputing derived state such as display text and
visibility.

That is fine for one-off CLI calls, but it adds avoidable work when an agent or
runtime flow performs multiple queries, inspections, actions, or mutations
against the same captured snapshot.

This PR adds an internal `LoupeSnapshotContext` that keeps reusable per-snapshot
lookup state for refs, app-authored `testID`s, accessibility ID metadata, roles,
exact display text, display text by ref, and visibility sets.

## Compatibility

The public command interface stays unchanged. Full snapshots and
view/accessibility trees remain the source of truth.

This does not make `ref` a durable cross-snapshot selector, and it does not
change the snapshot JSON format or add sidecar indexes.

author: duncaneddy
body:
## Description

Clears the pre-commit debt that accumulated because git hooks were never installed in this clone. Five mechanical, tool-separated commits:

1. `style: apply cargo fmt across crate` — `cargo fmt --all` on the 9 drifted files.
2. `style: fix ruff errors and apply ruff format` — fixes all 35 `ruff check` errors (15 auto-fixed unused imports, 20 manual `E702` semicolon-statement splits in `benchmarks/comparative/implementations/gmat/propagation.py`), then `ruff format .` (73 files, pure reflow).
3. `test: mark live-network tests as integration` — adds `@pytest.mark.integration` to every test that reaches a live network call (CelesTrak, space-weather download) in `tests/cli/test_access.py`, `tests/space_weather/test_sw_caching_provider.py`, `tests/space_weather/test_global_sw.py`, and `tests/earth_models/test_nrlmsise00.py`. `tests/celestrak/`, `tests/cli/test_celestrak.py`, and `tests/propagators/test_gp_record_propagators.py` were audited and were already correctly marked or already network-free — no changes needed there.
4. `fix: add safety docs to brahe-py attitude bindings; lint whole workspace in pre-commit` — the pre-commit config's clippy hook ran without `--workspace`, so `crates/brahe-py` was never linted; adding `--workspace` surfaced 10 pre-existing `brahe-py` errors. Fixed all of them: `# Safety` doc sections for 5 `pub unsafe fn` numpy-conversion methods in `crates/brahe-py/src/attitude.rs` (verified none actually perform an unsafe operation — `into_pyarray`/`reshape` are safe in the `numpy` crate version this repo pins, and the `unsafe` marker predates the file's earliest commit, so it's documented rather than removed to keep this change signature-preserving), plus `Default` impls and `is_empty()` methods for 3 `PyEOPProvider` structs in `crates/brahe-py/src/eop.rs` (clippy's own suggested idiomatic fix for `new_without_default`/`len_without_is_empty`).
5. `test: make access CLI validation tests hermetic against EOP cache age` — a reviewer proved empirically (aging the real EOP cache file to 9+ days and timing a "validation-only" test) that all 26 tests in `tests/cli/test_access.py`, not just the 17 marked in commit 3, reach live network: `compute()` calls `set_cli_eop()` → `brahe.initialize_eop()` **before any argument validation**, and `CachingEOPProvider::new` unconditionally re-downloads the cached EOP file whenever it's stale, independent of which code path runs afterward. Rather than marking all 26 integration (losing fast local coverage of the CLI's validation logic), added an autouse `tmp_path`-backed `BRAHE_CACHE` fixture so every test in the file cold-seeds from the bundled EOP data (always fresh) instead of reading the real on-disk cache. Verified by replicating the reviewer's exact experiment against the real cache file: with it artificially aged to 9+ days, the fixture keeps the 9 unmarked tests fast (0.02s each, same as before) and leaves the real cache file's mtime and content completely untouched.

None of these commits change behavior: `ruff format` and `cargo fmt` are pure formatters, the manual ruff fixes are dead-import removals plus semicolon-to-newline statement splits, the `integration` marker only gates test *selection* (`addopts = "-m 'not integration'"` already existed and already gated 83 tests before this PR), and the safety-doc/lint fixes in commit 4 add no new unsafe behavior (`is_empty()` is a new but trivial Python-facing method delegating to an existing trait default; `Default` is Rust-side only and doesn't change the PyO3 `__new__` constructor).

After merge, hooks should be enabled with `pre-commit install` so this doesn't drift again.

**Rebased** onto the final `de/clenshaw-gravity` tip (`c7fffa75`) once that branch was done. Commit 1 (`cargo fmt`) was regenerated fresh against the new base rather than rebased (formatter commits don't rebase cleanly); commits 2-5 cherry-picked cleanly with no conflicts. All gates below were re-run against the merged state.

## Changelog

### Fixed
- Repo-wide `cargo fmt` and `ruff` lint/format debt that had accumulated since pre-commit hooks were never installed locally.
- Live-network tests (CelesTrak CLI/API calls, space-weather cache downloads) that previously hung or failed in sandboxed/CI environments are now marked `@pytest.mark.integration` and deselected by default.
- `crates/brahe-py` clippy errors (missing `# Safety` docs, missing `Default`/`is_empty`) that were silently exempted from the pre-commit gate because the clippy hook lacked `--workspace`; the hook now covers the whole workspace.
- `tests/cli/test_access.py`'s 9 non-`integration`-marked tests could still silently hit the network (and rewrite the real on-disk EOP cache) via `set_cli_eop()`'s unconditional cache-age check; they now run against an isolated, always-fresh temp cache.

### Added
- `is_empty()` method on `StaticEOPProvider`, `FileEOPProvider`, and `CachingEOPProvider` (Python bindings), matching the existing `Trajectory.is_empty()` convention.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Note to Reviewers

The diff is large but entirely mechanical — each commit is scoped to one tool/fix so they can be reviewed independently. Commit 4 was added after an independent reviewer found that `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (without `--workspace`) never lints `crates/brahe-py`, which let 10 clippy errors accumulate there undetected by this repo's own pre-commit hook. Commit 5 was added after a second reviewer found that commit 3's network-test audit had a gap: it only traced the CelesTrak fetch inside `compute()` and missed that `set_cli_eop()` reaches a network-capable code path (EOP cache refresh) earlier, before any validation runs.

author: jesseedcp
body:
# Devflow v0.7.0

## Summary

v0.7.0 adds a local long-term wiki / knowledge distillation loop: `closeout -> wiki candidate -> review -> promote`. Wiki candidates are distilled deterministically from closeout material, reviewed by a human, and promoted into a project-local searchable wiki store under `.devflow/wiki`. No LLM, embeddings, or external wiki write-back is involved.

## Changes

- Added `closeout-raw-log.md` and `wiki-candidates.md` as standard demand artifacts.
- Added a local wiki store (`.devflow/wiki/`) with safe slug validation and an index (`WIKI.md`).
- Added `devflow wiki distill` to deterministically extract stable business knowledge from memory-candidate bullets, process improvement signals from implementation-review recommendations and MR/return events, and an archive pointer from closeout material.
- Added `devflow wiki list`, `wiki promote`, `wiki reject`, and `wiki search` for human-gated candidate review.
- Recorded `wiki.candidates_distilled`, `wiki.candidate_promoted`, and `wiki.candidate_rejected` events.
- Added `closeout.wiki_candidates` and `closeout.wiki_decisions` closeout evaluation checks (warning-only, non-blocking).
- Surfaced wiki candidate counts (`pending`/`promoted`/`rejected`) in `status`, `console`, and `workbench --snapshot`.
- Closeout next actions now suggest `wiki distill` (candidates missing) or `wiki list`/`wiki promote` (candidates pending), and stay silent once all candidates are decided.
- Added a wiki knowledge distillation smoke to release-readiness.

## How It Works

- Distillation is deterministic text extraction, not semantic truth. It reads `closeout.md`, `memory-candidates.md`, `implementation-review.md`, and `events.jsonl`.
- Stable business candidates come from bullet lines under `## Stable Knowledge Candidates`, `## 稳定知识候选`, and `## Stable Business Knowledge` in `memory-candidates.md`.
- Process improvement candidates come from non-ready implementation-review recommendations and MR/review events containing `action_required`, `returned_to_requirements`, `returned_to_plan`, or `returned_to_implementation`.
- Archive-only material points to `closeout-raw-log.md` when any closeout material exists.
- Promotion writes `.devflow/wiki/<slug>.md` and updates `.devflow/wiki/WIKI.md`. Rejection records a reason without writing a wiki entry. Search is a case-insensitive substring scan over promoted entries (excluding the index).

## Verification

- go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 5m
- go vet ./...
- go build ./cmd/devflow
- git diff --check
- scripts\release-readiness.ps1 -Version 0.7.0

## Known Limits

- Wiki distillation is deterministic text extraction, not semantic truth. Human review remains mandatory.
- Local wiki search is substring-based and intentionally not semantic or a dependency graph.
- `.devflow/wiki` is project-local; cross-project knowledge sharing remains out of scope.
- External wiki providers (Feishu, GitHub Wiki, Notion, Confluence) remain out of scope until a later adapter wave.
- Closeout wiki checks are warning-level in v0.7.0; promoting them to blockers should require dogfood evidence.

author: tamnd
body:
JavaScript && and || return an operand, not a boolean. a || b is a when a is truthy and b otherwise, and a && b is a when a is falsy and b otherwise. Over two booleans that operand is a bool Go own && and || return with the same short-circuit, so that case stays the operator. Over two numbers or two strings the operand is the value itself, so the expression lowers to a value-returning if wrapped in a func, guarding on the left operand truthiness through the test the truthiness slice already spells.

The left operand appears in both the guard and the returned value, so the no-temporary form is taken only when it is repeatable: a pure value, or a getter-free property or element read this typed subset can name twice. That covers x || 0, obj.prop || d, and arr[i] || d. An impure left hands back for the temporary a later slice hoists, and a mixed or non-primitive pair hands back through the operator table.

Stacked on lower-truthiness (base main); its diff cleans up once that merges.

Tests: emit tests for the || and && func shapes over numbers and strings, the property-read repeatable path, a boolean-stays-operator boundary, and an impure-left hand-back; a run test against the Node oracle over both operators, both types, and a property-read left.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Replaces the earlier "one resource per format" stdlib (`write-tar`, `gz-lines`, `base64-encode`, …) with a small set of **generic primitives** whose behaviour is driven by a shared codec + framing system. Fewer resources, strictly more capability.

The centerpiece is a new `stdlib/data` package: a two-interface data model that everything else is built on.

## The data model (`stdlib/data`)

Every message decodes into one of two shapes:

- **Continuous** — array-like, referenced by index or linear pattern (bytes, strings, lists, encoded byte forms).
- **Discrete** — struct-like, referenced by key (JSON objects).

Both satisfy a `Kind`-discriminated `Value`. A `Pattern` codec chain is the machinery behind continuous `.By()`; `Walk`/`ByJQ` back the two selectors; `Transpose`/`TryGet` back the discrete ops. Interfaces are non-generic with a runtime `Kind`, and generics live only at the typed boundaries (`FromBytes[T]`, `As[T]`, the `~[]E` slice helpers, `Transpose`/`TryGet`) — because Go has no method type parameters and no core type across `string | []byte | []rune`.

Selection mirrors the data domain everywhere a resource names a value:
- **`path = ["a","b"]`** walks discrete/object data by key.
- **`by = "<jq>"`** selects continuous/linear data with jq.

Error handling is `on-error = "err" | "drop"` (extensible).

## Resources

**Transports** — `file`, `socket`, `listen`, `request`, `http-listen`. `file`/`socket`/`request` are **dual-role**: `produce "file"` reads, `consume "file"` writes. All share one framing model — `sep` / `sep-byte` / `sep-byte-index` / `group` (mutually exclusive separators + grouping), which also joins on write.

**Codec transformers** — `recode` (universal format converter), `pick`, `pick-map`, `set`, `drop`, `slice`, `chunk`, `every`, `render` (`engine = template | printf | jq`, merging the old sprintf + template).

**jq escape hatches** — `jq`, `filter` (kept).

**Keyed** — `dedupe`, `uniq`, `batch`. **Flow** — `wait`, `throttle`, `head`, `tail`, `sample`. **Text** — `split`, `join`, `replace`, `regex`, `trim`, `upper`, `lower`, `hash`. **Dev** — `constant`, `sequence`, `generate`, `ticker`, `inspect`, `assert`, `count`, `trash`.

## Codecs

`bytes`, `utf-8`/`ascii`/`latin1` (invalid bytes error per `on-error`), `json`/`json-pretty`, `csv`, `base64`/`base64-url`/`hex`/`url`, `gzip` — composable as chains: `decode = "gzip|json"`.

## Key use case: data → local socket → meta-producer

A `render`+`socket` pipeline writes generated `produce {}` HCL into a unix socket; a `listen` producer reads that stream as its `produce-from` description. Many writers fan into one listener. Covered by an integration test.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` green
- [x] `stdlib/data`: codec round-trips; **garbage / partial-rune / high-byte input** per string codec; JSON number/bool/null fidelity; continuous ops; Walk/ByJQ/Transpose/TryGet
- [x] every transformer (unit)
- [x] framer edge cases (empty, no-trailing-sep, fixed-size, group, whole-stream, byte-delimited)
- [x] socket round-trip (`consume.socket` → `produce.listen`)
- [x] two end-to-end pipelines through the real HCL decode + build + run path
- [x] `docs/hcl` examples updated (`increment`→`sequence`, `sprintf`→`render`) and `docs/stdlib/README.md` rewritten

## Notes

- Targets `decouple-hcl-config` (PR #6) for the format-agnostic SDK v0.5.0.
- The external SDK is not modified: extended flow control lands as standalone transformers and `on-error` as a transformer attr, rather than forking `sdk.BlockMeta`. The existing host-owned per-minute / stop-after meta still applies.

body:
**The bug:** account creation *claims* a person's public survey response by copying it into `survey_responses`. Every analytics surface that merged both tables counted that person twice. Verified against prod: 16 unique Security+ applications rendered as **32** (16 public + 16 claimed copies); headline tiles inflated identically.

**The fix:** `dedupeClaimedResponses` — when an authenticated response exists for the same `(email, survey_type)`, its public twin is dropped (the authenticated copy wins: it carries the student link and cohort tag). Applied at every merge point:
- `getDashboardAllSurveyResponses` → fixes the Survey Insights dashboard, its PDF export, the CSV export, and Outcomes analytics in one place
- `getDashboardSurveyResponses` → the single-survey viewer
- `getBCCSurveyResponses` → currently unconsumed, same class

**Audit of everything else** touching both tables: per-track insights shows public XOR auth sources (safe); engagement analytics is activity-based (safe); the raw stats tallies are existence-gating only and now carry an explicit do-not-display warning.

Expected after deploy: CompTIA Security+ Application card reads **16**; will verify against the live page with the known-true numbers.

body:
authRateLimit was written, exported and covered by tests (auth.rate-limit.test.ts) but never wired into any route. Both /api/auth/login and /api/auth/admin/login remained open to unlimited brute-force attempts.

Applies the middleware in front of both login controllers. The shared attemptsByIp map already keys by client IP so vendor and admin attempts share the same 5-per-30-min budget — that is the intent, since the attacker is the same IP either way. Register, change-password and logout are untouched (either not credential guessing or already require an authenticated session).

author: skypace
body:
## Bug

The admin **Freshpet Billing** tab showed no completed stops. Root cause: `loadAll()` selected a `city` column from `completed_pms`, but that table has no `city` (it lives on `assets`). PostgREST returned `42703 column completed_pms.city does not exist`, so the load failed and `completedPMs` stayed empty — while Routes/Payments (which don't touch that query) kept working.

Confirmed live: the exact select 400s on `city`; dropping it returns rows.

## Fix
- `loadAll()` now selects `asset_id` instead of `city`.
- New `cityOf(p)` helper derives the city from the already-loaded `assets` (via `asset_id`); used in the search filter and the City column.

## Note on the design point
Billing reads `completed_pms` (pure completion) and never reads `payouts`, so **completion → bill Freshpet** and **completion → pay tech** are independent — an unpaid tech never hides a completed stop from Freshpet. This bug was the only thing blocking the stops from showing.

## Verification
- Corrected select returns `[]` for anon (RLS) instead of a 400 — column list valid; authenticated returns all 266 completed rows.
- Inline JS passes `node --check`.

author: ataru-kurihara
body:
## 概要

無職（どの職業にも就いていない）プレイヤーが石ピッケルで石炭鉱石などを採掘できてしまう問題を修正します。本番で発生を確認済み。

## 根本原因

`UnifiedEventHandler.onBlockBreak` で、職業採掘制限チェック（`canPlayerBreakBlock`）が `shouldProcessEvent` の**後ろ**に置かれていました。

`shouldProcessEvent`（→ `EventProcessor.shouldProcessEvent`）は報酬/経験値システム用のフィルタで、経済有効ワールドのホワイトリスト・除外ワールド・ゲームモード・イベントシステム有効フラグのいずれかが不成立だと `false` を返します。その場合 `onBlockBreak` が早期returnし、**採掘制限チェックに到達せず、無職でも鉱石が掘れてしまう**状態でした。

同クラスの `onBlockPlace` では、植え付け制限が `shouldProcessEvent` の**前**で実行されており、採掘系だけ順序が逆になっていたのが原因です。

## 修正内容

- `onBlockBreak` の職業採掘制限チェックを `shouldProcessEvent` の**前**（メソッド冒頭）へ移動し、`onBlockPlace` と対称の順序に統一
- 制限判定は `canPlayerBreakBlock` 内で「制限無効なら許可」「管理者権限バイパス」を先頭で自己ガードしているため、前倒ししても制限無効サーバー・管理者には影響なし
- 報酬/経験値/クエスト処理は従来どおり `shouldProcessEvent` ゲートの後ろに維持

## テスト

- `JobBlockPermissionManagerTest` に採掘制限の回帰テスト7件を追加（無職は鉱石不可／深層岩鉱石も正規化して不可／鉱夫は可／基本ブロックは誰でも可／制限無効時は可／管理者バイパス／拒否メッセージ）
- 全387テスト緑・BUILD SUCCESS
- ゲーム内で動作確認済み（無職は鉱石不可＋メッセージ表示、鉱夫は採掘可＋経験値、石・原木は誰でも可）

author: braden-w
body: The hosted `/sign-in` page is the one credential screen every Epicenter surface funnels into: the in-app `SignInPanel`, the billing dashboard, and Whispering settings all just redirect here through `auth.startSignIn()`. It was a plain left-aligned "Sign in" heading with two buttons and no dark mode, visibly out of step with the rest of the product. This restyles it to the app's design language and extends the provider set. The page is now a centered card with the Epicenter mark, an `epicenter` wordmark, and stacked provider buttons laid out as a grid (brand icon in a left column, label centered). The shared auth-page CSS is tokenized to CSS custom properties sourced from `packages/ui/src/app.css`'s oklch values, so a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` palette, `:focus-visible` rings, and a `prefers-reduced-motion` guard all come along without pulling Tailwind or the UI package into the server render. Every auth page (consent, signed-in, CLI callback) inherits the tokens and dark mode. Microsoft joins Google and GitHub as a register-when-present social provider: it is only offered when `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` / `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` are configured, so this lands with no deploy or secret changes and simply lights up once those are provisioned. Like GitHub, Microsoft is deliberately kept out of `trustedProviders` because a personal MSA email is not a guaranteed-verified assertion; only Google bypasses the incoming `emailVerified` link check. Apple and passkey are intentionally left for follow-up PRs rather than folded in here: Apple needs a dynamically generated JWT client secret (Team ID + Key ID + private key) plus `https://appleid.apple.com` in `trustedOrigins`, and passkey needs the WebAuthn ceremony wired into this bundler-free page. No dead flags were added for them. ## Changelog - Redesigned the sign-in page with a cleaner card layout, the Epicenter wordmark, and automatic dark mode. - Added **Sign in with Microsoft** (appears once Microsoft credentials are configured). --- Need help on this PR? author: odelot
body:
This pull request implements "Phase D" support for delta/prior parent edges in the memory reference tracking and snapshot protocol, enabling more advanced verification and synchronization between the emulator and the ESP. The changes introduce a new mechanism for tracking and verifying parent value accesses (current, previous-frame, or last-different) across frames, improving robustness and enabling new features.

Key changes include:

**Protocol and Data Structure Updates:**

* Added new constants and bitfields (`RC_PHASEC_PSZ_DP_SHIFT`, `RC_PHASEC_DP_DELTA`, `RC_PHASEC_DP_PRIOR`, `RC_PHASEC_MAX_DP`, etc.) to encode the "dp-kind" (current, delta, prior) in the high bits of the `psize` field, and updated the snapshot header (`ra_snapshot_header_t`) to include a shipped list of dp-parent verification values. This ensures both the emulator and ESP can verify alignment every frame. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b60daadf47cb7dd2a0b1c582caca4f987b9cfd89c7aa2a31eaf124f9034cfe7cR375-R382) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-408efb3fc9190bad1efb64023c48bfc65e6f3b21b8cb75ff7c849ff85c155040R471-R478) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-849ba1ad4945bceb797c6996d0eab86bd2704319bc995e2789ad4fc89492ae51R329-R340) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-849ba1ad4945bceb797c6996d0eab86bd2704319bc995e2789ad4fc89492ae51R502-R520)

**Delta/Prior Edge Handling:**

* Changed the logic in `rc_phasec_follow` to allow DELTA and PRIOR edges to be walkable, leveraging the new verification mechanism. Previously, these edges were refused for walking.

**Emission and Verification Logic:**

* Updated the emission logic in `rc_phasec_emit_memref` to encode the dp-kind in the `psize` high bits, register distinct (parent,kind) pairs for verification, and refuse chains that exceed the cap (`RC_PHASEC_MAX_DP`). BCD/INVERTED types are still refused. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1b0d3c05ce07d7dd97e06d5173dbc56489b6b0c71a3bad178869f4c638a1c05aR1802) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1b0d3c05ce07d7dd97e06d5173dbc56489b6b0c71a3bad178869f4c638a1c05aL1794-R1827)

* Added a new context structure and helper (`rc_phasec_emit_ctx_t` and `rc_phasec_dp_register`) to track and enforce the cap on distinct dp-parent verification entries during emission.

These changes collectively enable robust, verifiable tracking of DELTA and PRIOR accesses, laying groundwork for future features and improved emulator-ESP synchronization.…that

author: uayten
body:
## Summary

This PR adds full support for the **Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller** over USB, a Blueprint API to **join two Joy-Cons into a single player**, and fixes several **editor freezes and crashes** related to controller connection, disconnection, and rumble.

## Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller (USB)

The Switch 2 Pro Controller uses a new protocol that isn't compatible with Switch 1 controllers. Support was reverse-engineered from a USB capture of Steam talking to the controller, and verified on real hardware:

- **Device detection** (VID 057E / PID 2069).
- **Initialization over WinUSB**: the controller's HID interface is input-only, so init/config/rumble commands are sent over its WinUSB (bulk) interface via SetupAPI/WinUSB, which is what starts input streaming.
- **Full input parsing** of its 0x05 report: all buttons, both sticks, and the three new buttons — **C (GameChat)**, **GL** and **GR** — exposed as dedicated Unreal keys with new public masks (`JSMASK_C`, `JSMASK_GL`, `JSMASK_GR`).
- **Motion/IMU**: gyro and accelerometer are parsed and integrated with the existing motion pipeline (`JslGetIMUState`, `JslGetMotionState`, accumulated gyro, calibration). Axis mapping and signs were verified on hardware against a Switch 1 controller held in identical poses.
- **Factory stick calibration** is read from the controller's flash over SPI (the same reads Steam performs), so sticks use each unit's real center/range instead of fixed values. Body/button/grip **colors** are also read (`JslGetControllerColor`).
- **Rumble**: sustained vibration (matches the behavior of other controllers — vibrates until you call `(0, 0)`) by retriggering the controller's built-in vibration preset. Amplitude control isn't available yet — see "Known limitations" below.
- **Multiple Switch 2 controllers** are supported: each unit's WinUSB command interface is matched to its HID input interface through the USB device tree.
- Bluetooth is out of scope: the Switch 2 uses BLE (GATT), which Windows doesn't expose as a gamepad. Listed as future work.
- **Note:** Steam holds the controller's WinUSB command interface exclusively while running, which blocks this plugin's init and rumble for the Switch 2 Pro Controller specifically. The plugin logs a clear warning when this happens and automatically re-acquires the interface once Steam is closed — no reconnect needed.

## Joy-Con pairing (Blueprint API)

New nodes under **JoyShockLibrary | JoyConPairing**:

- `JSL4U Get Connected Controllers` — lists connected controllers (device id, type, name, player index, join partner).
- `JSL4U Join Joy Cons (A, B)` — joins a left and a right Joy-Con so they feed a single player (left half drives the left stick and its buttons, right half drives the right stick and its buttons; the engine sees one player per pair).
- `JSL4U Unjoin Joy Con` / `JSL4U Unjoin All Joy Cons` / `JSL4U Get Player Index`.

Player slots are dense and compact: 4 solo Joy-Cons = 4 players; two joined pairs = 2 players. When a controller disconnects, remaining player slots shift down (the last controller left is always player 0). Joins dissolve automatically on disconnect.

## Rumble improvements

- **Switch 1 (Joy-Con / Pro Controller)**: implemented full HD-rumble amplitude control (`JslSetRumble`'s `SmallRumble`/`BigRumble` map to the high/low-frequency actuator components), sustained automatically by the polling thread (Switch 1 rumble packets decay on their own after a single write).
- `JslSetRumble` now has a full Blueprint tooltip describing parameters and per-controller behavior.

## Stability fixes

- **Editor freezes fixed**: device enumeration/initialization performed blocking HID I/O (and thread joins) on the game thread via `WM_DEVICECHANGE`; it now runs on a background thread, with connect/disconnect events marshalled to the game thread.
- **Freeze during play fixed**: Switch 1 controllers were re-initialized (blocking Bluetooth I/O while holding a shared lock) on every device change, because `init_usb`/`init_bt` never set `initialised`.
- **Critical freeze fixed in SPI calibration reads** (`get_spi_data`): its retry loop only exited on an exact response match or `res == 0`, but once input streaming starts the device almost always returns *some* data — so a single lost SPI response (flaky Bluetooth) spun forever while the enumeration thread held the exclusive device lock, silently blocking further connect notifications and freezing the game thread on the next call. Now bounded with a clean failure/retry path.
- **Use-after-free fixed** in the polling thread's cleanup path (device flags were read after `delete`).
- **Input-device mapper corruption fixed**: controllers now get globally unique `FInputDeviceId`s (`AllocateNewInputDeviceId`) instead of legacy "best guess" ids that could collide with the keyboard, which could hang Enhanced Input when entering PIE with several controllers.
- **Stable player numbering**: device handles are reused (lowest free) and released on disconnect, so reconnecting controllers keep low indices instead of ever-increasing ones.
- **Deprecation**: migrated from `FInputDeviceScope` (deprecated in 5.8) to `FInputDeviceRegistry`.
- Misc cleanup: per-device cached names (a `static` name previously mislabeled every controller), removed dead includes/variables/debug code.

## Documentation

README updated: Switch 2 Pro Controller section, Joy-Con pairing section, Rumble section, new input events, installation notes (hidapi bundled on Windows; HIDUE only needed on other platforms), tested engine versions, known limitations, future work.

## Known limitations

- Switch 2 Pro Controller rumble is on/off only (no amplitude control) — its dedicated amplitude-accurate vibration channel hasn't been mapped over USB (confirmed via a dedicated capture that Steam itself never rumbles this controller, so there was no traffic available to reverse-engineer it from).
- Switch 2 Pro Controller Bluetooth is not supported (BLE/GATT, out of scope for this PR).
- Steam must be closed to use rumble/init on a Switch 2 Pro Controller (see note above).

## Testing

Verified on Windows 11 / UE 5.8 with: 4 Joy-Cons (solo and as two joined pairs), connect/disconnect/re-pair cycles, Bluetooth off/on, controllers connected before and after editor launch, Switch 1 HD rumble, and a Switch 2 Pro Controller over USB (buttons, calibrated sticks, C/GL/GR keys, gyro/accelerometer/orientation verified against a Switch 1 reference, controller colors, sustained rumble).

The automatic `pages-build-deployment` dynamic workflow lacks `concurrency` controls, causing `actions/deploy-pages` to return `Deployment failed, try again later.` when the GitHub Pages infrastructure still has a prior deployment in transition — observed when runs #8 and #9 triggered only 7 minutes apart.

```

## Brief Information

This pull request is in the type of:

- [x] bug fixing
- [ ] new feature
- [ ] others



### What does this PR do?

Allow radar indicator axis names to respect configured `axisName.width` and `axisName.overflow` instead of always using the internal truncate fallback.



### Fixed issues

- #14449: Radar indicator name `width` and `overflow` settings were not taking effect.


## Details

### Before: What was the problem?

Radar indicator names are rendered through the shared axis-name builder. That builder always passed `overflow: 'truncate'` and `width: maxWidth` as fixed style values for axis names, so user-provided radar `axisName` text style options such as:

```js
radar: {
    axisName: {
        width: 50,
        overflow: 'break'
    }
}
```

were overwritten before reaching the ZRender text element. In an SSR reproduction, long radar indicator labels remained a single SVG `<text>` element even with `width: 50` and `overflow: 'break'`.



### After: How does it behave after the fixing?

Axis-name rendering now uses `nameTextStyle` / radar `axisName` `overflow` and `width` when they are provided, while preserving the existing truncate fallback when they are not. With `width: 50` and `overflow: 'break'`, the SSR output now emits multiple text lines for long radar indicator labels.

A focused visual case was added to `test/radar-axis.html` to cover long radar indicator names wrapping within `50px`.

author: mvanhorn
body:
## Summary

The Trustpilot source returned 0 items on company topics even when active. Reproduced live on a ThriftBooks run: the engine passed the raw topic name to a CLI keyed by review-page domain (`info ThriftBooks` -> HTTP 404, misreported by the CLI as an auth failure), and N parallel subqueries each invoked the CLI, racing N concurrent headless-Chrome WAF-cookie harvests that all failed.

Companion CLI PR (error taxonomy + help-text spelling): mvanhorn/printing-press-library `fix/trustpilot-404-taxonomy-help-text`.

## Changes

- **`--trustpilot-domain` flag** - used verbatim, bypasses the brand-shape gate (an explicit domain is proof of brand intent, and it unlocks multi-word company names), threads into vs-mode via a per-entity `trustpilot_domain` key in `--competitors-plan`. Provenance matters: user-set domains are final; auto-resolved hints retry via search on a miss.
- **Name -> domain resolution** via the CLI's `search`, cached per normalized topic (thread-safe; vs-mode entities resolve independently). Name-match is mandatory; among name-matching hits the winner must dominate 50x on review volume - ambiguous cases fall back to today's behavior and log the candidate, because silently attributing another company's reviews is worse than a visible miss. Transient search errors are never cached.
- **Session warm-up at first fetch** - `ensure_session_ready` runs inside `search_trustpilot` behind a module lock with a 240s monotonic TTL: one serialized `auth status` (+ `auth login` only when stale) per token window, so concurrent vs-mode sub-runs never race Chrome harvests, other sources' streams are never delayed, and generic topics never launch a browser. Logs only structured status strings (the raw CLI payload carries WAF-token prefixes).
- **`MAX_SOURCE_FETCHES["trustpilot"] = 1`** - N subqueries used identical identifiers; also excluded from the thin-source retry (it returns at most one item by design, so "<3 items" re-fetched it after every success, bypassing the cap and dropping the resolved domain).
- **Auto-resolve hint** - headless `--auto-resolve` fills `trustpilot_domain` from official-site URLs whose registrable label matches the topic (hint provenance; the engine verifies and recovers via search).
- **SKILL.md** - Step 0.5d resolution subsection, pre-flight checklist row, engine-command flag bullet, Resolved-block line, vs-mode per-entity lookup type; **CONFIGURATION.md** source-table row updated.

Reviewed by a 10-reviewer pass (correctness, security, adversarial, testing, maintainability, project-standards, reliability, agent-native, learnings, plus a cross-model Codex adversarial pass); all actionable findings applied in the `fix(review)` commit.

## Testing

- [x] `uv run python -m pytest -q --tb=short` (full suite green; coverage 83.8% vs 60% gate)
- Live smoke (the original failure): `INCLUDE_SOURCES=trustpilot` run on `ThriftBooks` -> one `warm-up: harvested`, `resolved 'ThriftBooks' -> 'www.thriftbooks.com' via search`, Trustpilot 1 item (TrustScore 4.7, 2.8M reviews). Before this PR the same run produced 0 items and three concurrent failed harvests.
- New tests: domain-resolution chain (verbatim flag, brand-gate bypass, hint retry, ambiguous fallback, per-topic cache, transient-error no-cache), warm-up (once-lock concurrency, TTL lapse, opt-out, no-Chrome-on-generic-topics, token-byte-free logs), fetch cap, thin-retry exclusion, `main()`-level flag plumbing, vs-mode plan provenance, auto-resolve extraction.

## Known Residuals

- Two same-named Trustpilot pages under a 50x review ratio (regional-domain brands) resolve as ambiguous and fall back to the bare name (today's 0-items behavior for that class); the log line points users at `--trustpilot-domain`.
- `_extract_official_domain` can return a non-`www` subdomain; the hint-retry path absorbs it at the cost of one extra CLI call.
- A failed warm-up login is not retried within the 240s TTL window; per-call CLI auto-harvest remains the fallback.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- Watch stderr logs on brand-topic runs for `[Trustpilot] warm-up:` (expect exactly one per token window) and `resolved '<topic>' -> '<domain>' via search`.
- Failure signal: `ambiguous search hits` or `no name-matching search hit` lines on topics that should resolve - user remediation is `--trustpilot-domain`; recurring cases may warrant tuning `DOMAIN_DOMINANCE_FACTOR`.
- Validation: any company topic with `INCLUDE_SOURCES=trustpilot` should show `Trustpilot: 1 item` in Source Coverage. Owner: @mvanhorn; window: next few brand-topic runs.

## Related Issues

None filed; root-caused live in-session (2026-07-03 ThriftBooks run).

body:
## Summary

- reject unsupported DoltLite remote URLs at `bd dolt remote add` time
- guard existing unsupported DoltLite remotes before push, pull, fetch, and peer sync transfer SQL
- add DoltLite regression coverage for git-protocol rejection, native file/http acceptance, and missing-remote passthrough
- add the missing non-CGO `newDoltliteStore` stub so pure-Go `cmd/bd` builds report the intended CGO/libdoltlite error instead of failing to compile
- refresh generated CLI docs now that the pure-Go docs build can run on this branch
- clear existing CI policy/lint blockers by removing disallowed `testing.Short()` skips, documenting constrained gosec cases, and handling `Rows.Close()` errors
- refresh the Nix `vendorHash` to match the current Go module graph

## Context

DoltLite remote transfer currently fails late inside libdoltlite for `git+ssh://...` remotes with `URL must start with file:// or http://`. The normal Dolt backend has a CLI fallback for git-protocol remotes, but DoltLite's CLI path is a SQLite database file rather than a `.dolt` repository, so that fallback is not available in this backend.

This change keeps DoltLite's backend boundary explicit: new unsupported remotes are rejected before they are persisted, and existing bad remotes fail before transfer with guidance to use the Dolt backend for GitHub/git+ssh sync or replace the remote with a DoltLite-supported `file://` or `http://` URL.

author: devrickyyy
body:
## Problem

Clicking the top-right session-completion notification/toast to focus an already-open conversation window shrinks/recenters that window back to a default size instead of just bringing it to front (Feishu tracker recvojHGdZwd6J, P1).

## Root cause

`openLaunchResult`'s re-focus path in `packages/workbench/surface/src/host/session.ts` applies the `"cascade-same-type-centered"` frame policy to any exactly-matching existing node whenever a launch resolves to it — appropriate for a generic re-open (e.g. a dock icon click, where centering a possibly-off-screen window is desirable), but wrong when the launch specifically targets a window that is already showing that exact conversation (e.g. a completion-notification click), which should only focus it, not touch its frame.

## Fix

- Added `WorkbenchHostLaunchResult.preserveExistingNodeFrame` (`packages/workbench/surface/src/host/types.ts`).
- `session.ts`'s `openLaunchResult` now skips the cascade re-center/resize step when `preserveExistingNodeFrame` is set on an exact-match existing node (`packages/workbench/surface/src/host/session.ts:711-715`).
- The agent-gui workbench contribution sets `preserveExistingNodeFrame: existingInstanceId !== null` whenever the launch resolves to an already-open session's node (`packages/agent/gui/workbench/contribution.ts`), so re-launching (including from a completion-notification click) reuses the current size/position; brand-new launches are unaffected.

## Tests

- `packages/agent/gui/workbench/contribution.test.ts`: new case asserting a relaunch of the same session sets `preserveExistingNodeFrame: true` while the first launch does not.
- `packages/workbench/surface/src/host/session.test.ts`: new regression test asserting `launchNode` leaves a resized existing window's frame untouched when the host requests `preserveExistingNodeFrame`.
- Scoped test runs green; no Go files touched by this change.

## Note on FDvyAk (not addressed in this PR)

Also investigated the P1 perf complaint "claude code / codex 新起会话回复较慢" (recvoi2gFDvyAk — new sessions slow to first response, Claude Code sessions slow mid-run). This is a vague report with no repro/profiling data. A bounded investigation of session-start and turn-processing hot paths (including the areas touched by 8bd7c2ba "one live app-server process per agent session" and a2d48b50 "proxy direct-connect") did not turn up a concrete, confidently-fixable regression. Recommend requesting a repro or profile from the reporter rather than a speculative change; no fix included here.

author: minpeter
body: ## What this PR does Autonomous improvement pass over the middleware: I ran a live 12-model × 4-middleware × 7-scenario matrix against freerouter, distilled the failures into reproducible parser gaps, fixed them offline with regression tests, closed a set of AI SDK v7 (`LanguageModelV4`) spec-parity gaps found by auditing the provider spec against the wrap handlers, and split the two oversized protocol files into companion modules. ## Live-matrix results (same 336-run matrix, before → after) | Metric | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Passed | 257/336 | **270/336** | | `tool-input-delta` reconciliation violations | 13 | **2** | | qwen3Coder failures | 25 | **14** | 22 combos fixed outright; the remaining failures are model-side (nemotron answering in Python code blocks, gpt-oss emitting harmony format, infra flakes) — no regressions attributable to these changes were found when auditing every newly-failing combo. ## Parsing robustness (all captured verbatim from live models) - **qwen3coder**: recover schema-property parameter tags (`…` matched against the tool's input schema — Qwen2.5 emitted these and previously produced `input: {}`), `NAME` name-as-text openers (Llama 3.1), `function=NAME>` openers missing `<` and bare tool names after `` (GLM-4.7), literal `` element wrappers (Llama 3.1), plus a finish-time XML salvage backstop that re-runs the variant-tolerant generate parser before dropping buffered markup. - **qwen3coder streaming**: concatenated `tool-input-delta` chunks now always reconcile with the final `tool-call.input`. Closing-tag fragments (`` JSON payloads (IBM Granite) in both generate and stream paths. - **JSON recovery**: accept `function` as a tool-name envelope key (gpt-oss emits `{"function": …, "parameters": …}`). ## AI SDK v7 spec parity (from a full `LanguageModelV4` surface audit) - Protocol stream parsers now consume provider `text-start`/`text-end` envelopes instead of passing them through, which previously produced an empty duplicate text block with a dangling provider id on every streamed response. - Forced tool choice (`required`/named tool): scans all content parts for the JSON text (reasoning can precede it), keeps reasoning/file/source content in the output, reports missing text via `onError` instead of silently fabricating `unknown`, and preserves `length`/`content-filter`/`error` finish reasons so truncation is detectable. - `toolChoiceStream` emits `response-metadata` and re-emits reasoning content. - Provider-executed tool calls pass through byte-identical (no client-schema re-coercion) and no longer trigger the `tool-calls` finish rewrite. - Provider tools (`type: 'provider'`) dropped by `transformParams` now surface as spec `unsupported` warnings on generate results and `stream-start`. - Stale `v3Stream` naming cleaned up. ## Refactoring - `qwen3coder-protocol.ts` (3,105 lines) → protocol/stream machine (1,551) + `qwen3coder-call-parsing.ts` (1,603) - `hermes-protocol.ts` (3,215 lines) → protocol/stream machine (866) + `hermes-call-parsing.ts` (2,402) Both follow the existing companion-module pattern; no behavior change, verified by the full suite. ## Verification - 208 test files / 2,082 tests green (37 new tests pinning every recovered variant, delta-reconciliation invariants, text-envelope handling, and the v7 tool-choice/warning behaviors) - `tsc --noEmit` clean, biome clean, `pnpm build` clean - Full live matrix re-run after the fixes (numbers above) ## Known follow-ups (not in this PR) - Message/part-level `providerOptions` are still dropped across prompt transforms; assistant `file`/`reasoning-file`/`custom` history parts are still JSON-stringified into prompt text. - gpt-oss needs a harmony-format protocol to be genuinely supported. - The extended live-matrix harness lives as a local-only script (`examples/parser-core/src/94-extended-matrix.local.ts` pattern), consistent with the existing gitignored 95–99 scripts. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Hardens live-model parsing and brings the middleware to AI SDK v7 `LanguageModelV4` spec parity, raising the live 12×4×7 matrix pass rate from 257 to 270/336. Also splits the oversized Hermes and Qwen3Coder protocol files into smaller companion modules. - **Bug Fixes** - qwen3coder: recover malformed call openers and schema-property parameter tags; unwrap `` wrappers; trim whitespace in tool/param names; tighten boundaries (e.g. stop unclosed params at the next opener); optional raw-text pass-through for mixed XML+prose; streaming deltas now reconcile exactly with final tool-call input. - yaml-xml: salvage unquoted multi-line string values using the tool schema; recover embedded Hermes-style `` JSON (generate + stream); stream flushes ordinary prose while open and holds unfinished foreign JSON for salvage. - hermes: relaxed-JSON repair edge cases fixed (e.g. do not treat `//` inside quoted strings as comments; safe fallback when malformed arguments precede a primitive top-level field). - JSON recovery: accept `function` as a tool-name key alongside `name`/`tool`. - Stream parsers: consume provider `text-start`/`text-end` envelopes to avoid duplicate empty text blocks. - Forced tool choice: scan all content for the JSON text (reasoning may come first), keep non-text parts, surface missing JSON via `onError`, and preserve `length`/`content-filter`/`error` finish reasons. - toolChoiceStream: emit `response-metadata` and re-emit reasoning content. - Provider-executed tool calls: pass through byte-identical without client coercion; no `tool-calls` finish rewrite. - Provider tools (`type: 'provider'`): now reported as spec `unsupported` warnings when dropped by `transformParams`. - Cubic review parser: fixed edge-case handling. - **Refactors** - Split `qwen3coder-protocol.ts` into `protocol`/`stream` machine and `qwen3coder-call-parsing.ts`. - Split `hermes-protocol.ts` into `protocol`/`stream` machine and `hermes-call-parsing.ts`. - Cleaned up Biome diagnostics. Written for commit 463ab882a8ffeabc112081205c3d4f725e980429. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
Enrichment pass for `connected-space-oq-01` (*The Closure of a (Pre)connected Set Is (Pre)connected*).

## Gap
The Lean file has **6 distinct theorems** but Section III (and its annotation) bundled *both* dense corollaries — `connectedSpace_of_dense_connected` (64-67) and `preconnectedSpace_of_dense_preconnected` (70-73) — while the section title named only the connected one. These are not interchangeable: `ConnectedSpace` requires nonemptiness, `PreconnectedSpace` does not (the empty space is preconnected but not connected).

## Changes
- **Split Section III** into Section III (Dense Connected, 64-67) and new Section IV (Dense Preconnected, 69-73).
- **Split `ann-dense`** into `ann-dense` (64-67) + new `ann-dense-preconnected` (69-73), the latter explaining the version drops nonemptiness and holds even for the empty space.
- **Added one keyInsight** (5→6) making the nonemptiness distinction explicit.

## Verification
- Quality **93→100** (sections 8→10, annotations 20→25 per `find-targets.ts`).
- meta.json **12.4 KB** — well under the 60 KB cap.
- JSON valid; all 5 annotations have valid `type`/`significance` enums.
- Validated via JSON parse + enum check + quality recompute (no node_modules in worktree).
- Every added claim reflects the actual Lean theorems; no invented content.
