> Required if this PR fixes a bug

#### Root Cause
- **Pager never showed:** the shared V1→V5 mapper (`createBaseSpec`) computes `limit = limit || pageSize` for list/table, so the seed's internal `pageSize: 100` became a V5 `limit`, which the pager gate reads as an explicit user limit.
- **Dup/dropped rows & unreliable "next":** the backend emits `ORDER BY` verbatim (no auto tiebreaker), so `timestamp desc` alone is not a total order across separate offset queries.
- **NoData flash on kind switch:** `keepPreviousData` (added to keep the pager on page change) also retains the *previous* panel type's response across a query-key change; the new renderer can't read it.
- **Empty Order By on switch:** V1's `handleQueryChange` clears `orderBy` when switching to a list.
- **spanGaps:** a numeric threshold below one step interval breaks the line at every normal point.
- **New-panel double-add:** `applyJsonPatch` (run in `onMutate` before the request is sent) inserted each `op.value` by reference, so the cache's `layouts[0].spec.items` aliased the empty `items` array held inside the section-add op; applying the item op then mutated that op's value, and react-query sent a layout that already held the item *plus* the separate item-add op → two overlapping items. New-dashboard-only, since that is the only batch that adds a layout and an item into that same layout together.

#### Fix Strategy
- Strip `pageSize`/`offset` at the V2 conversion boundary (`toPerses`) so `limit` reflects only a real user limit.
- Enforce a total order (`timestamp desc, id`) at request-build time, request-only.
- Drive `canNext` from `nextCursor`; gate the full-panel loader on first-load only; require a retained response's type to match the current request before treating it as data.
- Re-seed the list default order in `usePanelTypeSwitch`.
- Clamp the numeric `spanGaps` to `max(minStepInterval, value)`.
- Clone the inserted value on `add`/`replace` in `applyJsonPatch` so the applied document never shares references with the input ops (restoring the purity the docstring already promises).

---

### 🧪 Testing Strategy
> How was this change validated?

- **Tests added/updated:** unit tests for `toPerses` (pageSize→limit strip), `buildQueryRangeRequest` (id tiebreaker + defaults), `usePanelQuery` (cursor `canNext`, `keepPreviousData`), `PanelBody` (first-load loader vs mounted refetch, cross-type stale response), `ListPanel/Renderer` (skeleton rows), `usePanelTypeSwitch` (default list order), `buildConfig` (spanGaps clamp), and `applyJsonPatch` (a later op targeting a just-added node must not mutate the input ops).
- **Manual verification:** ran the app and exercised list paging (next/prev, page-size change), panel-type switching, the discard dialog, and creating the first panel on a brand-new dashboard.
- **Edge cases covered:** last page (partial page → no cursor), traces list (no `id` tiebreaker, explorer parity), boolean `spanGaps` (span-all passes through), first fetch with no data (loader, not skeleton).
- `tsgo --noEmit`, `oxlint`, and `pnpm build` all green; pre-commit hook validated each commit.

---

### ⚠️ Risk & Impact Assessment
> What could break? How do we recover?

- **Blast radius:** V2 dashboards only. Mostly the List panel; the spanGaps change is Time-series-only; the discard-dialog and create-alert changes are editor-only; the `applyJsonPatch` clone affects every optimistic spec mutation.
- **Potential regressions:** the `PanelBody` loader-gate change (`isFetching && !hasData`) affects **all V2 panels** — a same-key background refetch now keeps the chart mounted instead of showing a full-panel spinner (time-range changes still show the loader). The request-time `id` tiebreaker only affects logs list requests and is not persisted. The `applyJsonPatch` change only deep-clones values already destined for the cache, so it is behaviour-preserving apart from removing the aliasing.
- **Rollback plan:** each fix is an isolated commit and can be reverted independently.

---

### 📝 Changelog

| Field | Value |
|------|-------|
| Deployment Type | Cloud / OSS / Enterprise |
| Change Type | Bug Fix |
| Description | V2 dashboard List panels now show the pager, page deterministically, and display skeleton rows while loading the next page; switching to a list keeps timestamp ordering; time-series spanGaps respects the step interval; discard-dialog button layout updated; and creating the first panel on a new dashboard no longer fails with an items-overlap error. |

- [x] Manually tested
- [x] Breaking changes documented
- [x] Backward compatibility considered

- The **list pagination runtime** fixes (cursor `canNext`, keep-pager, no-flash, skeletons) are in a single commit because they share `usePanelQuery.ts` / `PanelBody.tsx`; splitting them by hunk broke the pre-

author: fheinfling
body:
## Context

Reported: *the app did not automatically switch seats when codex seat 1 was limited.* Investigation of live state confirmed the limit **was** detected (seat 1 `limit_reached=True`, 5h window at 100%, `src=usage`) and the healthy seat is now active — but that only happened via the **startup `choose()` on the next run**, not mid-session.

Mid-session auto-switch fires only when the tool's out-of-quota **banner matches the stdout detector**. Codex frequently surfaces a real limit as a plain stream error / non-zero exit with no matchable banner, and this repo's own limit-*prose* can turn stdout scanning off earlier in a run — so a maxed codex seat could exit without hopping.

## Change

An **exit-time safety net** in `run()`: when a supervised child exits with a **non-zero** status and **no** stdout limit was caught, force-refresh the active seat's usage via the new `handle_exhausted()`. Only if the endpoint **positively confirms** the seat is out (a future `limited_until` stamped from `usage` — never a transient error) **and** a healthy seat is free (within the switch budget) do we hop + resume.

Guardrails:
- A **clean (0) exit** is never second-guessed — the fast path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- An **ordinary failure** (build error/crash; usage says the seat is healthy or is unreachable) is **surfaced untouched** — positive-evidence-only, so no spurious switch.
- Bounded by the existing `max_switches` budget; a maxed seat can't be re-selected by `choose()`.

`handle_exhausted()` mirrors `handle_limit`'s positive-evidence guard and calls `refresh` under the state lock exactly as `handle_limit` already does (no new lock/deadlock risk — verified).

## Tests
`test_handle_exhausted_*` (confirmed-out → switch; healthy → give_up; unreachable → give_up) and run-level `test_run_switches_on_silent_limit_exit` (hops + resumes) / `test_run_no_switch_on_plain_nonzero_exit` (propagated). Full suite: **339 passed, 1 skipped**.

## Note
Stacked on top of #22 (base = `fix/false-resting-and-proxy-flap`); GitHub will retarget to `main` once #22 merges.

author: peterus
body:
Follow-up to #49. Improves the release workflow in three ways.

## 1. Fix: real release was red on protected `main`
The first real release run failed at *Commit stamp, tag, and push*:
```
remote: error: GH013: Repository rule violations found for refs/heads/main.
- Changes must be made through a pull request.
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> main
```
`main` is PR-only (ruleset), so the workflow can't push the stamp commit. **Fix:** drop the branch push entirely. `app/VERSION` is stamped *ephemerally* for the build (so binaries still report the right version via `app_version.h`), and `softprops/action-gh-release` creates the tag itself via `target_commitish: github.sha`. Version now lives in the **tag + release + binaries** — the same model as linux-image (version == tag, no committed version file). No orphan-tag risk (single API call).

## 2. Attach build artifacts to every run (dry-run included)
Unconditional `actions/upload-artifact` step, so a `dry_run=true` build can be **downloaded and flashed/simulated for testing without publishing a Release**. Uploads `fm-sa818-2m.{bin,elf,native_sim}`, `fm-sa818-70cm.{bin,elf,native_sim}`, `SHA256SUMS` (+ cosign `.bundle`s on real runs). Name `fw-<version>` / `fw-<version>-dryrun`.

## 3. Memory-usage overview
Per real `fm_board` target, lift Zephyr's FLASH/RAM "Memory region" table into `MEMORY-USAGE.md` (uploaded + published), and echo it to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` so it renders on the run page. Example (verified locally): FLASH 155212 B / 2 MB (7.40%), RAM 24537 B / 768 KB (3.12%).

body:
## Resumen

Sigue al PR anterior (#8, ya mergeado) de guía visual de colocación del dedo. El feedback fue: el anillo se veía bien pero era puramente decorativo (posición fija arbitraria en el panel), sin relación real con dónde el algoritmo efectivamente muestrea los píxeles, y el sistema no confirmaba "perfecto" solo cuando el dedo estaba realmente sostenido en esa posición exacta.

### Cambios

- **`src/lib/ui/cameraPeek.ts` — `computeRoiScreenRect`**: traduce el ROI cuadrado que `PPGSignalProcessor.ts` realmente muestrea (mismo `ROI_SIZE_FRACTION` = 0.82 del lado corto del frame, ver `vitalThresholds.ts`) a coordenadas de pantalla, considerando el recorte `object-fit: cover` del `<video>`. El anillo que ve el usuario ahora coincide en pantalla con los píxeles exactos que se procesan — deja de ser un círculo puesto a mano. Incluye clamps de seguridad para aspect ratios extremos (p. ej. cámaras de escritorio en testing).
- **Nuevo nivel de guía `perfect`**: el sistema solo pasa a verde con **"¡Perfecto! Quedate quieto"** (+ check visual) cuando `contactState === 'STABLE_CONTACT' && placementStable === true` — el mismo veredicto tolerante que ya usa el resto de la UI (buffer elástico), no un umbral nuevo. Antes de eso el aro permanece rojo (sin contacto) o ámbar (ajustando), nunca "perfecto" prematuramente.
- **`drawFingerGuideRing`**: acepta la geometría real opcional; si el video aún no tiene metadata (arranque), cae a un círculo centrado como aproximación razonable.
- `PPGSignalMeter` recibe un nuevo prop `getVideoElement` (desde `Index.tsx` → `cameraRef.current.getVideoElement()`) para leer `videoWidth/videoHeight` en cada frame del loop de render.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm test` (282 tests, 45 archivos)
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] Verificación visual con Playwright + cámara sintética: confirmado que el anillo se posiciona y dimensiona según el mapeo ROI→pantalla (con clamp aplicado correctamente ante el aspect ratio landscape de la cámara falsa de escritorio).

author: zeus-deus
body:
## Problem

Toggling **Settings → Beta Features → Agent Chat** in one Codemux instance flipped it in every other instance on the machine — e.g. the installed release and a locally-running dev build, even when they're signed into different accounts.

## Root cause

All local state (sqlite db, auth tokens, settings cache) is isolated per build via `APP_DIR_NAME` (`~/.local/share/codemux/` vs `~/.local/share/codemux-dev/`) — except the feature-flag snapshot. `snapshot_path()` in `src-tauri/src/observability.rs` hardcoded the machine-shared `~/.codemux/observability.json`, so every build read and wrote the same file. `docs/features/observability.md` already documented the per-build data-dir location; the code never matched it.

## Fix

- `snapshot_path()` now resolves to `dirs::data_dir()/APP_DIR_NAME/observability.json`, mirroring `settings_sync::cache_dir()`.
- **One-time migration**: when the per-build file doesn't exist yet, the legacy `~/.codemux/observability.json` is read once and copied forward, so existing Beta opt-ins survive. The legacy file is left in place for older installed versions (downgrade-safe).
- Once a per-build file exists it always wins over the legacy one, so the leak can't return through the migration path.
- Removed the `ensure_git_exclude` call in `save_snapshot` — it only made sense when the snapshot could land inside a repo working tree.

## Tests

- `snapshot_path_is_build_scoped_and_cwd_independent` — pins both historical path bugs (CWD drift, cross-build sharing)
- `load_migrates_legacy_snapshot_once` — legacy opt-in adopted, copied forward, legacy file untouched
- `per_build_snapshot_wins_over_legacy` — migration can't reintroduce the leak
- `load_defaults_when_no_snapshot_exists` — fresh install: defaults, no files created

## Docs

Updated `docs/features/observability.md` (persistence path + migration), `docs/features/agent-chat.md` (dogfooding instructions pointed at the old path), and `docs/core/STATUS.md` (unreleased entry).

## Verification

`npm run verify` passes end-to-end: `cargo check`, full `cargo test`, `npm run check`, `npm run test` (136 files, 1972 tests).

## Note for testers

Each build adopts whatever the shared file said at the moment of migration. If the toggle was left "on" by one instance, both start "on" after updating — flip the unwanted one once and it now sticks per-app.

author: 0xh0b0
body:
Closes #42.

Restores an end-to-end test that runs the real installer under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the supported floor for `install.ps1`): install from the release zip, verify `cynative.exe --version`, uninstall, and prove the checksum-mismatch path fails closed. This was retired when PR CI consolidated in #35; it comes back as a release-confidence check rather than a per-PR gate.

## Shape

Build the release archives once with a goreleaser snapshot, then run the real installer against the same artifacts per OS, so Linux and Windows test the identical bytes a release ships (macOS can slot in later as another consumer):

```
detect -> snapshot -> { linux-install-e2e, windows-install-e2e }
```

- The heavy path runs only for release-please PRs and manual `workflow_dispatch`. Every normal PR skips all four jobs, and none is a required status check, so this never blocks a normal merge.
- `make snapshot` is the single definition of the goreleaser snapshot flags, reused by the local `make install-e2e` and the CI snapshot job.
- The Windows job stays hermetic: it stubs `gh` (no live attestation call) and serves the archive from the shared loopback `test/serve-fixture.py`.

## Windows coverage (`test/install.e2e.Tests.ps1`, Pester under PS 5.1)

- install via `-File` + user-PATH update; uninstall + PATH prune
- the documented `irm | iex` install and `& ([scriptblock]::Create(...)) -Uninstall` paths, which drive the dot-source guard differently than `-File` (where a 5.1 regression is most likely to hide)
- `cynative.exe --version` asserted against the goreleaser-stamped version from `metadata.json`
- the non-loopback base-URL guard rejection, and a fail-closed checksum mismatch by tampering the served zip

## Validation

- `make check` (Go + shell + PowerShell) passes locally.
- Linux install e2e passes against the real shared snapshot artifacts.
- The restored Pester suite and the Windows job's inline PowerShell parse clean and are PSScriptAnalyzer-clean.
- The real goreleaser Windows zip has `cynative.exe` at its root; the artifact upload/download flat-path behavior is confirmed.

The live PS 5.1 run happens on `windows-latest`; a manual `workflow_dispatch` on this branch exercises it before merge.

author: rubiii
body:
The type of an empty tag's value historically depends on its attributes:
* a plain empty tag becomes the :empty_tag_value
* a tag with attributes becomes a hash of the prefixed attributes

Callers cannot rely on a stable type for the same element across payloads.

With :consistent_empty_tags, the :empty_tag_value applies to every empty tag, whether it has attributes or not:
* a string value keeps the attributes accessible on the value, matching how text nodes carry theirs
* an explicit xsi:nil="true" wins over the option and becomes nil, honoring the document's own signal
* tags with text or children, and tags typed as "array", are unaffected

The option is off by default.
Without it, parsing behaves exactly as before.

author: themiron
body:
Add a prefix-set entry form that matches the Route Target carried in a Route Target Constrain (RFC 4684, rtc family) NLRI against the prefix-set trie, honoring masklength-range over the 96-bit NLRI key (<origin-as>:<route-target>[/masklen]). Unlike match-ext-community-set, which matches the path's extended-communities attribute, this matches the Route Target embedded in the NLRI key itself, and is mutually exclusive with ip-prefix within a prefix-set entry.

The rtc-prefix field is exposed through OpenConfig (prefix-set prefix rtc-prefix), the gRPC API (api.Prefix rtc_prefix) and the gobgp CLI (policy prefix-set prefix <as>:<rt>[/len]). RTC and IPv4 sets are kept apart since both share AFI_IP; an RTC set only matches RTC paths and vice-versa.

Promote the RT trie-key helper to pkg/packet/bgp as the shared allocation-free path (stack-serialized, netip.Prefix returned by value), keeping the policy evaluation hot path at 0 allocs/op for IPv4, IPv6 and RTC. Measured (13th-gen i7-13700H, benchtime=10s):

  BenchmarkPrefixConditionEvaluate/IPv4     30.47 ns/op    0 B/op    0 allocs/op
  BenchmarkPrefixConditionEvaluate/IPv6     25.98 ns/op    0 B/op    0 allocs/op
  BenchmarkPrefixConditionEvaluate/RTC      50.09 ns/op    0 B/op    0 allocs/op
  BenchmarkExtCommRouteTargetKey             4.87 ns/op    0 B/op    0 allocs/op

author: copilot
body:
Adds Work Unit 2 from the v1.0 roadmap: paste or load a reference sequence, align the Sanger read entirely client-side (no upload, no server), call substitutions/indels/ambiguous IUPAC positions with 1-based coordinates, review them in a filterable table, and export CSV or VCF-lite TSV.

## Alignment engine (`src/alignment/`)

- **Banded semi-global Needleman-Wunsch** (`aligner.ts`): semi-global gives free read end-gaps so a partial Sanger read places anywhere in a longer reference; bandwidth=20 diagonals keeps it near-linear. Strand auto-detected by comparing forward vs RC score.
- **IUPAC-aware scoring** (`iupac.ts`): ambiguous bases score by fraction of expansions that match (e.g. Y vs T → +0.5, not a full mismatch penalty).
- **CIGAR coordinate mappers** (`cigar.ts`): `readPosToRefPos` / `refPosToReadPos` give exact 1-based reference positions for every variant; insertions/deletions correctly return `null` for the consuming side.

## Variant calling + export (`src/variants/`, `src/export/`)

- `caller.ts`: walks CIGAR segments, collapses multi-base I/D runs, skips N bases, emits SNV/insertion/deletion/ambiguous records with confidence from quality score brackets (high ≥ 40, medium ≥ 20).
- `filter.ts`: four filter modes (all / high / ambiguous / indel) + suppressed-variant exclusion for export.
- `variants.ts`: deterministic UTF-8 CSV (`position,ref,alt,type,confidence,review`) and VCF-lite TSV; both exact-byte tested.

## UI (`src/components/`)

- **`ReferencePanel`**: textarea (FASTA or raw), "Load FASTA" file button, Align/Clear buttons, status line reporting strand + 1-based ref span.
- **`VariantTable`**: filter tab bar (All / High / Ambig / Indel), per-row review cycling (pending → confirmed → suppressed), export buttons; hidden while no alignment is active.
- CSS uses existing custom-property tokens throughout — no new color literals, full light+dark parity.

## State wiring

- `TraceSlot` gains `alignmentResult`, `referenceSequence`, `referenceId`, `variantReviews`; `makeSlot` initializes them; `_evict` clears `alignmentResult`.
- `PermalinkStateV1` gains optional `variantReviews` (array of `{id, review}` pairs). Reference sequence is intentionally **not** encoded — too large for a URL; the UI says so explicitly.
- Variant IDs are deterministic (`{alignmentId}:{position}:{ref}:{alt}`) so review state survives re-alignment to the same reference.

## Tests

| File | Count | What |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/core/alignment.test.ts` | 43 | Exact-value: IUPAC scoring, CIGAR ops, coordinate mapping, aligner placement + strand |
| `tests/core/variants.test.ts` | 29 | Exact-value: callVariants positions/types, filterVariants, CSV/VCF exact bytes |
| `tests/e2e/reference-alignment.e2e.test.ts` | 8 | Playwright: panel renders, Align enable/disable, status strand+pos, variant table, tab filter state, CSV header, Clear reset |

body:
Closes #1449. Follow-up gap filed as #1883.

## What (test-only — no production code changed)
Adds budget ratchets so a future refactor can't silently re-introduce per-row allocation/FFI-call blowups in the bindings:
- **Rust FFI-call budget** (`bindings/node/src/value.rs`, `#[cfg(test)]`): `set_map_ctor_lookups_bounded_per_result` asserts Set/Map constructor lookups ≤2 per result (pins #1448). **Synthetic-regression proven**: reverting #1448 to per-cell fetch turns it RED (2000 vs budget 2), restore → GREEN.
- **Node per-row heap budget** (`__test__/conversion-budget.test.js`, `--expose-gc`): `executeNative()` runs INSIDE the gc/heap-delta window; median-of-N per-row heap < **2000 B/row** (measured ~1295 warm on macOS arm64 release-unwind; budget leaves headroom for Linux/debug/GC drift while staying under the ~2086 value-graph-doubling regression signal). Pins the gross per-row value graph (a value-doubling regression goes RED at ~2086).
- **Python per-row alloc budget** (`tests/test_conversion_budgets.py`): `db.execute()` runs INSIDE the `tracemalloc` window; per-row peak < **14000 B/row** (measured ~9000). Fail-loud on present-but-empty (never skips).

## Honest coverage boundary (documented in-test; follow-up #1883)
An earlier roborev pass correctly flagged that the heap/alloc windows must include the conversion path — fixed (execute() moved inside both windows). Empirically, the binding-layer heap/alloc tests **cannot observe** #1447 (clone→move: the transient Rust-heap clone is freed before any V8/tracemalloc sample) or #1445/#1446 (V8 dedups property-name strings) — reverting either doesn't move the number. These budgets therefore pin the **gross per-row value graph** + the **ctor-lookup count** (#1448); the residual #1447/#1445/#1446 ratchet needs a **Rust-side alloc budget (dhat/allocator hook)**, filed as **#1883** (epic-H H2 territory). The tests state this boundary rather than overclaiming.

## Verification
- roborev (claude-code/opus): converged — the measurement-window Medium fixed; final pass had only a Low (Node budget headroom), addressed by widening 1800→2000. No correctness issues.
- Full agent-gate: **file-size / fmt / clippy / node-bindings PASS**; **python-bindings' `test_per_row_alloc_budget` PASS** (confirmed in-gate + direct). Two FAILs are pre-existing/environmental, NOT attributable: `core-tests` `issue_953_multichunk_cell_seek` (#1856) and the `python-bindings` `test_streaming_next_releases_gil` GIL flake. (The Node jest budget test isn't in the gate's scoped jest; validated directly, 3x green — the PR's Node CI lane runs the full suite.)

author: smolhaj
body:
## Summary
- **Fixes the reported bug**: "I keep getting the same words to review each time" in Flashcards
- Root cause: the shared `functions/_lib/fsrs.js` computed `due_at` as `Date.now() + Math.round(stability) * 86400000`. A struggling/new card's stability is routinely well under 1 day (0.02-0.4 is normal after a few "Again" grades), and `Math.round()` truncated all of that down to **0** — scheduling the card due at essentially the same instant it was just reviewed. Every subsequent review recomputed another sub-day stability, rounded to 0 again, so the card stayed permanently "due" and kept winning the soonest-due sort in every future session
- Fixed by removing the rounding and using the raw fractional stability directly — matches how real SRS systems (Anki's learning steps, etc.) genuinely re-show a failed card within minutes to hours, not after a full day
- **Because `scheduleReview()` is shared**, this one fix also corrects the adaptive session's `vocabulary_items` spaced-repetition scheduling, not just Flashcards
- Includes a full site QA pass triggered by this investigation: 20+ routes across desktop and mobile, logged-in/out states, a full lesson-completion flow, an adaptive-session round-trip, and edge cases (duplicate registration, wrong password, unknown routes, protected-route redirects) — no other issues found

author: davidamacey
body:
## Root cause: a pipe-masked CI gate

The **Backend Tests** job's main step runs `pytest tests/ ... | tee pytest-output.txt`. GitHub's default run shell is `bash -e {0}` **without** `pipefail`, so the step's exit code was `tee`'s (always 0) — pytest failures have been merging under green checkmarks. The latest "green" master run actually contained **7 real test failures**.

**Fix:** `set -o pipefail` as the first line of that run block (with a comment explaining why it must stay).

**Workflow audit** (all 5 workflows checked for the same hazard):
- `pre-commit.yml` — the one masked pipe, fixed here.
- `seam-guard.yml` — already `set -euo pipefail`. ✅
- `security-scan.yml` — the `|| echo ::warning::` fallbacks are deliberately non-blocking and documented as such; no masking pipes. ✅
- `docker-publish.yml`, `deploy-docs.yml` — no piped run commands. ✅

## The 7 masked failures — root cause and fix per test

| Test | Root cause | Fix (contract, not patch) |
|---|---|---|
| `test_files_streaming.py::test_download_stream_content_type` | The `audio_original` SSE ready-path presigns via minio-py, and presigning is **not purely local** — the SDK issues a bucket-region network lookup. `_resolve_ready_download` has **no SKIP_S3 branch** (the old docstring's claim was false), so CI hit a dead MinIO. | Test asserts only the SSE response contract, so the presign is stubbed at the service seam (`get_presigned_download_url`) — hermetic, no MinIO needed; docstring corrected. |
| `test_migration_endpoints.py::test_embedding_status_admin_ok` | **Real endpoint bug.** `get_migration_status()` only guarded `client is None`, but the OpenSearch client is constructed lazily without touching the network — with OpenSearch down, the first real call (`indices.exists`) raised and `GET /api/embeddings/migration/status` returned **500**. | Endpoint fixed: `OpenSearchException` on the index reads now returns the same documented degraded envelope as the no-client branch (`status: error, message: OpenSearch not available`) inside a 200; `mode_info`/`progress`/`stalled` always present. Contract documented in the endpoint docstring and asserted for **both** availability states in the test. |
| `test_speaker_profiles.py::test_occurrences_owner_200_empty` | **Real endpoint bug — not OS-related.** `GET /profiles/{uuid}/occurrences` eagerly constructed `SpeakerEmbeddingService`, whose `__init__` imports pyannote and loads the embedding model. pyannote is deliberately absent from `requirements-ci.txt` (GPU-worker-only), so the endpoint 500'd in CI — and wasted a model load per request everywhere else. `find_speaker_occurrences()` is a pure DB read. | Endpoint fixed: pass `SpeakerMatchingService(db, None)` (the same explicit-None pattern the suggestion endpoints in the same module already use). No test change needed — the 200-with-empty-list contract was already right. |
| `test_backup_alerts.py::{test_failure_sends_admin_notification, test_success_with_warnings_notifies, test_keys_notice_sent_once}` | Tests depended on ambient state — the dev DB's seeded admin as notification recipient. CI's fresh DB has zero admins, so recipient fan-out was empty (and the never-raises test was **vacuous**: the raising mock was never called). The alerts code itself is correct — recipient selection and fan-out behave as designed. | Tests take the existing `admin_user` fixture (savepoint-isolated), so a recipient always exists; all count assertions were already recomputed from `_admin_user_ids` on the same session, so extra ambient admins remain fine. `test_failure_alerting_never_raises` now actually exercises the guard. |
| `test_uuid7_migration_guard.py::test_v368_guard_...` | Hardcoded the local install's Postgres password (`CHANGE_ME_auto_generated_on_install`) and dbname `opentranscribe`; CI's service container uses `postgres`/`postgres` and db `transcribe_app`. | Connects via `settings.POSTGRES_*` — the exact canonical config the suite's engine is built from (conftest pins env before test modules import). **No credentials hardcoded anywhere**; reachability probe uses the same host/port. |

## Verification

- Full backend suite vs the live dev stack: **2282 passed, 373 skipped, exit 0**.
- CI-emulation run (`SKIP_S3=True SKIP_OPENSEARCH=True`, MinIO/OpenSearch pointed at dead ports): all affected files green, including the new degraded-contract assertions.
- ruff (check + format), mypy, and all pre-commit hooks pass on the touched files.
- The real proof is this PR's **Backend Tests** check running with the now-strict gate — watching it before this is mergeable.

Do not merge yet — awaiting the strict-gate CI result.

body:
## Summary

- Third and final piece of the multi-agent perf fix set (PR 1: activity throttling, 0bdd9d5e6, merged; PR 2: sidebar redraw caching, parallel effort). Background: `project_perf-activity-invalidation-storm` in agent memory, referenced from PR #38.
- `TaskFileWatcher` fires (150ms debounced) on ANY fs event anywhere in `.ghostties/tasks/`. `TaskStore.loadFromDisk()` used to respond by fully re-enumerating the directory and re-reading + re-parsing **every** `.md` fixture, including done/graveyard tasks that are never pruned. Under concurrent multi-agent load, one agent's single-file MCP write triggered a full-corpus reparse in every window watching that directory, with cost scaling on total historical task count rather than active-task count.
- `loadFromDisk()` now keeps a per-file `(mtime, size)` signature cache from the last successful load. On each fire it enumerates the directory (cheap — attributes only, no content read), diffs against the cache, and only reads + re-parses files that are new or changed via the existing `TaskFixtureParser.parse` (unmodified). Removed files are dropped from the in-memory map. `recomputeLanes()` still runs once per load (already O(tasks), untouched).
- First load naturally degrades to a full load since the signature cache starts empty — no special-casing needed, and initial-load behavior is unchanged.
- Pure performance change: `TaskFixtureParser` parsing logic is untouched, `recomputeLanes()` is untouched, `TaskFileWatcher`'s debounce/event-mask/public interface are untouched.

author: seansmithworks
body:
## Summary

PR2 of the 3-PR perf-storm follow-up plan (see #38 for PR1, which throttled the activity signal itself and guarded `WorkspaceStore.recordActivity`). PR1 fixed the *frequency* of `objectWillChange` fires during multi-agent streaming; this PR caps the *cost* of whatever fires remain, per two adversarial code reviews done during PR1.

- **`WorkspaceStore.sessionGroups(forProject:)` and `.sectionedProjects` are now memoized.** Both were previously recomputed on every read — an uncached O(sessions) filter+sort / O(projects + sessions) full bucketing pass each time — even though most reads happen back-to-back with no underlying data change (e.g. every expanded `ProjectDisclosureRow`'s body evaluation).

  Invalidation is centralized via `didSet` on the four stored properties that feed these computations (`projects`, `sessions`, `globalIndicatorStates`, `activeSinceTimestamps`) rather than scattered across each mutating method. This is deliberate: I initially added per-call-site `invalidate...()` calls and found a real gap (`renameSession`/`moveSession` not invalidating `sectionedProjectsCache`), plus a subtler issue — both computations are also functions of wall-clock time (120s grace period, 24h recency window), so a "recompute whenever a render happens" replacement needed to invalidate on the exact same triggers that used to cause a fresh recompute, not just on data mutations. The `didSet` approach can't miss a call site by construction, matches the existing `sidebarMode`/`lastSelectedProjectId` `didSet` pattern already used in this file, and is simple to audit at the property declaration.

- **`ProjectDisclosureRow` now skips SwiftUI re-render when nothing it displays changed.** The row is split into a thin `ProjectDisclosureRow` wrapper and a private `ProjectDisclosureRowContent` that does the actual work, wrapped in `.equatable()`. `WorkspaceStore`/`SessionCoordinator` publish far more often than any single project's own data changes, so without a gate every expanded row redid its session grouping and activity scans on every fire. The content's `Equatable` conformance compares project data, expansion/selection, a snapshot of this project's sessions + indicator states (captured at construction, not read live inside `==` — `store`/`coordinator` are shared singletons, so reading them live at comparison time would always see "now" on both sides and never detect a change), and the currently-focused session id (read in the outer wrapper, since `@EnvironmentObject` isn't resolved yet inside a view's `init`).

- **Item 4 (extend `scripts/profile.sh` to simulate title-change bursts) is skipped.** The actual stress-injection mechanism (`GHOSTTIES_STRESS_SESSIONS`) lives in `SessionCoordinator.swift`, which is explicitly out of scope for this PR (PR1's already-merged code / PR3's territory). Extending it correctly would require adding a new code path there, so I'm flagging this rather than building a workaround.

## Test plan

- [x] `xcodebuild build` — `BUILD SUCCEEDED`
- [x] `xcodebuild test -only-testing:GhosttyTests/WorkspaceStoreSectionsTests` — `TEST SUCCEEDED`, including 6 new tests added for the cache: `sessionGroupsCacheReflectsAddedSession`, `...RemovedSession`, `...RenamedSession`, `...IndicatorStateChange`, `sessionGroupsCacheMatchesUncachedComputationAfterMutations` (compares the memoized instance-level result against a fresh static `computeSessionGroups` call), and `sessionGroupsCacheDoesNotLeakAcrossProjects`. All 100+ existing tests in that file (including the freeze/release and grace-period tests, which exercise `sectionedProjects` at the instance level) still pass unmodified — they act as a correctness net for the `sectionedProjects` cache too.
- [x] CI is expected to show red on this PR — this is a **known pre-existing issue**, not caused by this change (main has been red on both jobs since ~May 2026; see `project-ci-fix-track.md` in project memory). Confirmed this PR doesn't introduce a *new* failure mode by running the full local build + targeted test suite above.

body:
I have implemented several micro-UX and accessibility improvements to the `DownloadModal` component to make it more intuitive and accessible:

1. **Screen Reader Support**: Added `aria-label="Close dialog"` to the close icon button and `aria-live="polite"` to the "Ready to download!" status text. This ensures that users with assistive technologies are informed when the countdown finishes and how to dismiss the dialog.
2. **Keyboard Accessibility**: Users can now close the modal by pressing the **Escape** key, following standard web accessibility patterns.
3. **Intuitive Interaction**: Added a "click outside" handler to the backdrop, allowing users to close the modal by clicking the blurred area around it.
4. **Smart Focus Management**: Once the advertisement countdown completes and the "Download" button becomes enabled, the focus is automatically moved to that button. This streamlines the user journey, allowing for an immediate next action (e.g., pressing Enter to download).
5. **Code Quality**: Refactored the `useEffect` logic to avoid synchronous `setState` calls, resolving a `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` ESLint error and improving render performance.

Verification was performed using a custom Playwright script to confirm focus transitions, keyboard listeners, and ARIA attribute presence.

author: marcelocantos
body:
Remediates Fable-5 audit finding **F1** (`docs/audit/fable-2026-07.md`; HIGH, two-lens confirmed) — the first repo of the fleet audit-remediation pass, run as the calibration trial.

## The defect (🎯T33)
`spawn()` selected `StackClass::Small` purely from the per-entry **checkpoint-sampled** high-water table, with no `is_exact` gate and no analyser call — an independent path that preempted the sound analyser. That value is unsound as a slot bound: it is sampled only at `do_switch` checkpoints (a helper that grows and unwinds *between* two channel ops is never observed) and is keyed per `EntryFn` (a shallow instance's sample gates a deep instance's Small allocation). Arena Small slots have only a 4 KB software guard on arm64, so a mis-sized imp descends into a neighbour and **silently corrupts** it — no SIGSEGV. Also violated the repo's own T3.4.4 acceptance and paper 23's spec.

## The fix
Drop the `profile→Small` path. `Small` is now gated strictly on `analyze_stack_depth_cached().is_exact` (a sound static upper bound). The recorded high-water is preserved and still refines the analyser's `indirect_call_budget` for the never-shrinking Default slot, so the T3.4.4 residue is intact — it just no longer selects the slot class.

## Verification (parent-assembled, independently re-run on ARM64, `-DCSP_ANALYSE_STACKS`)
- `test/stack_slot_sizing.test.cc` is a **true differential**: FAILS on unfixed master (`small_delta==1` — an inexact-analyser entry with a 24 KB true peak wrongly placed in a 16 KB Small slot) and PASSES after the fix (`small_delta==0`). A second case asserts the profile table still survives a spawn for budget refinement.
- Full **ANALYSE=1 suite green: 757/757** (26 491 assertions, 0 failed).
- Adds an `ANALYSE=1` Makefile build dir + CI step: the `CSP_ANALYSE_STACKS` slot-selection path had **no CI coverage**, which is how the defect shipped.

## Dedup note
The worker's audit gate independently re-derived the pre-existing `analyze_stack_depth` ASan over-read (`stack_analysis_arm64.cc:1699`) that already landed on master as **🎯T31 (#86)** during this run. Not re-filed as a duplicate; T31 is corroborated and gains a `depends_on: T3.4.5` edge.

Closes 🎯T33 (retired in `bullseye.yaml` in this diff).

author: jfmeyers
body:
## What

**Palier 2c** — the final chart type: **Combo** draws several measures on one shared category axis, each rendered as a **bar or a line**. Front follow-up to the merged granit-business backend. **Closes Palier 2** (multi-series charts).

## How

The backend aggregates all measures in one group-by pass (`ExecuteGroupedAsync` + `GroupEntry.Aggregates`) and ships each measure's points in `buckets` keyed by `series`, plus an ordered `comboSeries` descriptor list carrying each measure's `renderAs`/valueKind/currency. The front maps each descriptor to a series with the declared type — ECharts renders mixed bar/line natively.

## Changes

- **Contract**: `ChartType` gains `Combo`; `ChartWidgetDefinition` gains `comboSeries: ChartComboSeries[]` + the `ComboRenderAs` (`Bar`/`Line`) enum; `ChartWidgetSnapshot` gains a `comboSeries: ChartComboSeriesSnapshot[]` descriptor list. `contracts/openapi/analytics.json` resynced.
- **Primitive**: new `ComboChart` (mixed bar/line series on shared axes; reuses the already-registered ECharts Bar/Line).
- **Renderer** (`chart-snapshot-widget.tsx`): a `Combo` branch (`buildComboSeries`) turns each measure descriptor into a series aligned on the shared categories, with its `renderAs`.
- **Editor** (`chart-config-form.tsx`): selecting `Combo` swaps the single aggregation/field for a **measure repeater** (aggregation + field + bar/line, add/remove), keeps `groupBy` as the shared axis, and seeds one measure on switch-in.
- **Catalog**: seeds `comboSeries: null`.

## Design decision (validated)

- **No new endpoint/runner/DI** on the backend: combo is a method on the existing `IChartRunner`; `renderAs` is a visual hint that flows definition → snapshot without touching the runner.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean (analytics, react-charts, react-ui-analytics, react-analytics, react-dashboards)
- ESLint clean; `@granit/arch-tests` green (ADR-010 — `react-ui-analytics` is UI-tier, may import `@granit/react-ui`)
- `@granit/contract-tests` oracle green; full affected + contract + arch suites green (3992+ tests)
- Added an editor guard test asserting the type dropdown offers **Heatmap/Scatter/Combo** (catches picker-list drift from the `ChartType` union) + a combo-repeater gating test.

## Notes

- `ChartComboSeriesSnapshot` mirrors the backend snapshot record (emitted as an opaque `JsonElement`, so not in the OpenAPI schema — same as the other widget snapshots).
- `Dashboard:Widget.Chart.ComboSeries.*` follow the host-provided i18n pattern; showcase supplies translations.

## Palier 2 — complete

| Phase | Types | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 2a | grouped/stacked bars, multi-line, stacked area, heatmap | merged (#922) |
| 2b | scatter | merged (#923) |
| 2c | combo | this PR |

author: chisanan232
body:
## _Target_

Close a LOW-severity hardening batch (sweep AAASM-4120): make the ai-sdk / openai-agents framework adapters fail **closed** on governance faults like the other wrappers, and stop the postinstall script resolving native package names that were never published.

* ### Task summary:

    Two independent node-sdk gaps, both verified in source at HEAD:

    1. **Adapters swallowed check/approval faults (fail-open).** `src/hooks/ai-sdk.ts` and `src/hooks/openai-agents.ts` wrapped the pre-execution gateway `check` and approval wait in `try { … } catch { return executeOriginal() }`. A caller-supplied `config.gatewayClient` (honored in `init-assembly.ts`) that throws on a transport error was therefore silently treated as **ALLOW**, while `with-assembly.ts` / `wrap-tool-with-assembly.ts` (no catch → propagate) would **DENY** — an inconsistent posture. Removed the swallowing catches so faults propagate (reject/deny under enforce), matching the other wrappers and `enforceGovernance`.
    2. **postinstall resolved unpublished package names (inert).** `scripts/postinstall.mjs` resolved `@agent-assembly/<platformKey>` binary packages that are neither declared nor published (the declared `@agent-assembly/runtime-*` optionalDeps ship the `aasm` CLI, not a `.node`), so `runPostinstall` always threw → caught → warned → no-opped, masking a real binary-provisioning regression. The napi `.node` binaries actually ship **in-package** under `native/aa-ffi-node/` and are resolved by `index.cjs` at load time. Reconciled the script to **verify** that bundled binding is present for the current platform, so a missing binary fails loudly at install rather than only at first native load. No dependency-confusion introduced — all names stay under the org-owned `@agent-assembly` scope.

* ### Task tickets:

    * Task ID: AAASM-4137.
    * Relative task IDs:
        * [x] AAASM-4120 (sweep parent).
    * Relative PRs:
        * N/A.

* ### Key point change:

    * `ai-sdk` / `openai-agents` adapter faults now **fail closed** (propagate/deny) instead of executing the original tool.
    * postinstall now **verifies the in-package native binding** instead of copying from a phantom per-platform npm package.

## _Effecting Scope_

* Action Types:
    * [x] 🔧 Fixing bug
    * [x] 🍀 Improving something (security posture consistency)
* Scopes:
    * [x] 🤖 Framework hooks
    * [x] 🧪 Unit testing
    * [x] 🚀 Building → 📦 Project configurations (postinstall)
* Additional description:
    Fail-open removal is only observable with a **caller-supplied** gatewayClient that throws; the built-in native client catches internally and never throws, so no behavior change for the default path. Under enforce this is a hardening, not a breaking change.

## _Description_

* `🔒 (hooks)`: Remove the swallowing `try/catch` around `check` / approval in the ai-sdk and openai-agents adapters; update the four contradicted tests to assert the fault propagates and the original tool does not run.
* `🐛 (postinstall)`: Verify the bundled `native/aa-ffi-node/` binding for the current platform (mirroring `index.cjs` resolution) instead of resolving unpublished `@agent-assembly/<platformKey>` packages; update the `.d.mts` and tests.

**How to verify:** `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` — full suite green (358 passed, 2 skipped). New/updated tests: a throwing `gatewayClient` under enforce now blocks the tool in both adapters; postinstall confirms/loud-fails on the in-package binding.

Closes AAASM-4137

body:
## Summary

Adds `GET /api/v1/chain/deregistrations` — network-wide neuron-deregistration activity over a 7d/30d window: a per-subnet leaderboard (distinct deregistered hotkeys, `NeuronDeregistered` count, deregistrations per hotkey) ranked by total deregistrations, a network rollup with the true distinct hotkey count (a hotkey deregistered on several subnets counts once), and a distribution summary of the per-subnet re-deregistration intensity — computed live from the `account_events` `NeuronDeregistered` stream.

This is the **network-wide leaderboard companion** to the merged per-subnet `GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/deregistrations` (#3137), and the **exit-side companion** to the existing `GET /api/v1/chain/registrations` — mirroring it exactly (window + limit + `?format=csv`, HEAD normalized through the GET cache key, most-active-first leaderboard, JSON-only network rollup + intensity distribution). `NeuronDeregistered` is an ingested `account_events` kind (`src/account-events.mjs`, category `registration`).

Pure shaping (`buildChainDeregistrations`) + a thin two-query D1 loader (`loadChainDeregistrations`, network aggregate then per-netuid GROUP BY). Null-safe: a cold store returns a schema-stable empty block (never 404).

## Contract / regeneration

- New source schema `ChainDeregistrationsArtifact` in `schemas/components/05-subnets.schema.json`; new `PUBLIC_ARTIFACTS` + `API_ROUTES` entries in `src/contracts.mjs`; consistent OpenAPI worked-example normalizer in `src/openapi-sample.mjs`.
- Ran `npm run build`; committed the regenerated `openapi.json`, `api-components.schema.json`, `types.d.ts`, `api-index.json`, `contracts.json`, `generated/metagraphed-api.d.ts`. `public/metagraph/r2-manifest.json` and `public/metagraph/schemas/index.json` are intentionally **not** in the diff (deploy-pipeline owned, reverted against `main`).

author: aimplemented
body:
## Root cause
The desktop mobile-mode reconciler calls `/api/mobile-handoff` with `action: "app-start"`. In the packaged desktop app, that route derived the Tailscale Serve backend from the packaged app request port, so relaunching the desktop app republished an authenticated random sidecar port instead of the tokenless native iOS server on `127.0.0.1:3000`. The native SwiftUI iOS app sends no browser cookie/token by design, so it hit `401`.

The shell runner also always spawned `tailscale` from PATH, which can hit the broken macOS app shim instead of the working lowercase binary.

## Fix
- Make native app mobile-mode choose its backend separately from browser invite handoff.
- In bundled desktop mode, publish `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (or `COVEN_CAVE_NATIVE_APP_BACKEND_URL`) for native iOS instead of the packaged authenticated sidecar port.
- Verify the native backend with `/api/familiars` before changing Tailscale Serve, returning an actionable error if the tokenless app server is not running.
- Let `scripts/mobile-tailscale.sh` honor `TAILSCALE_BIN` for `tailscale` commands.

## Verification
- `node --experimental-strip-types src/components/mobile-handoff.test.ts`
- `node scripts/mobile-tailscale.test.mjs`
- `node --experimental-strip-types src/lib/mobile-handoff.test.ts`
- `node scripts/mobile-tailscale-native.test.mjs`
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`
- `bash -n scripts/mobile-tailscale.sh`
- `node scripts/run-tests.mjs app` — 535 app test files passed
- Live smoke: `TAILSCALE_BIN=/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/tailscale corepack pnpm mobile:tailscale:status` reports Serve -> `http://127.0.0.1:3000`
- Live smoke: tailnet endpoints `/api/familiars`, `/api/sessions/list`, `/api/board`, `/api/theme`, `/api/openclaw-agents`, `/api/harnesses` returned HTTP 200
- Live smoke: `mobile:tailscale:app` with explicit `TAILSCALE_BIN` printed `chriss-mac-mini-2.taile39814.ts.net` and left Serve pointing at `127.0.0.1:3000`

author: squne121
body:
## Summary

`run_refinement_preflight.py` の `_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence` 関数は、呼び出し箇所（旧1600行目付近）と `if __name__ == "__main__":` トリガー（旧2326行目）の両方より後（旧2337行目）に定義されていた。そのため `main()` がモジュール読み込み中に即座に実行され、`run_preflight()` から `_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence` を呼び出す時点でまだ関数定義に到達しておらず、スクリプト実行時に必ず `NameError` で全面クラッシュしていた。本 PR ではこの関数定義を呼び出し元（`run_preflight` 関数）の直前に移動し、回帰防止用テストを追加した。ロジック自体は一切変更していない（純粋な定義位置の移動のみ）。

本 Issue（#1334）をこの PR でクローズする（Closes #1334）。

## レビュー対応（fix_delta）

人間レビュアー（squne121）から REQUEST_CHANGES を受け、以下を追加実装した。

- 既存の `test_module_imports_without_nameerror` は `importlib.util` でモジュールを import するだけで、`__name__ == "__main__"` にならず `main()` が実際に呼ばれないため、Issue #1334 で実際に発火した「`run_refinement_preflight.py` を直接 CLI 実行する」経路を再現・検証できていなかった。
- `test_direct_cli_anchor_comment_path_has_no_nameerror` を新規追加し、`subprocess.run()` で `run_refinement_preflight.py` を実際に `python3 <script>` として直接起動する（`__name__` が本当に `"__main__"` になる）。`--fixture` + `--anchor-comment-url` を併用し、GitHub API に依存せず `_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence` を呼び出す anchor comment 経路を通す。
- stdout/stderr に `NameError` / `Traceback` が含まれないこと、exit code が既知のラッパー exit code 範囲（0/1/2/3）であること、`STATUS:` 行が出力されていることを assert する。

## Scope Delta（人間承認済み・#1339 追加対応）

人間レビュアー（squne121）から、上記の direct CLI subprocess テストが実は **vacuous**（無効）だったという指摘を受けた。

- 原因: `refinement_preflight_input.schema.json` の `anchor_comments` 要素は `additionalProperties: false` で `id`/`body`/`issue_url` のみに制限されていた一方、`_build_anchor_comment_state()` は `html_url`/`api_url`（`url` 由来）/`user_login`（`user.login` 由来）/`author_association`/`comment_created_at`（`created_at` 由来）/`comment_updated_at`（`updated_at` 由来）を要求する `loop_state.schema.json#/definitions/anchor_comment` へ正規化しようとする。fixture 側にこれらのフィールドを渡す手段が存在しなかったため、schema-conformant なフィクスチャは必ず先に `ANCHOR_COMMENT_SCHEMA_INVALID` で `blocked` になり、`_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence` には到達し得なかった（定義順序バグの有無に関わらず同一の出力になる = ungameable な regression guard になっていなかった）。
- 一度は該当テストを削除して対応したが、人間から「同一 PR で Allowed Paths を Scope Delta として拡張し、direct CLI subprocess regression test を実際に到達させる形で再対応してよい」と承認を受けた。

### 追加された Allowed Paths（Scope Delta）

- `.claude/skills/issue-refinement-loop/schemas/refinement_preflight_input.schema.json`
  - `anchor_comments` 配列要素に **任意項目** として `html_url` / `url` / `user`（`login` 必須の object）/ `author_association` / `created_at` / `updated_at` を追加。
  - 既存の `id` / `body` / `issue_url`（必須）の意味・必須性は変更していない。後方互換な拡張のみ（`additionalProperties: false` は維持）。

### 対応内容

- 上記 schema 拡張により、fixture 経由で `_build_anchor_comment_state()` が要求する全メタデータを供給できるようになった。
- `test_direct_cli_anchor_comment_path_has_no_nameerror` を、schema-conformant な完全フィクスチャ（`html_url`/`url`/`user`/`author_association`/`created_at`/`updated_at` を含む）で再導入した。
- 到達性を独立に検証する `test_direct_cli_anchor_comment_path_reaches_target_function` を新規追加し、stdout に `ANCHOR_COMMENT_SCHEMA_INVALID` / `INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID` が出ないこと（＝schema normalization を実際に通過し `_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence` へ到達すること）を assert する。
- **Ungameable 性の自己検証**: 関数定義を呼び出し箇所・`__main__` トリガーの両方より後ろへ実際に移動した「壊れたコピー」に対して、同じ schema-conformant フィクスチャで direct CLI subprocess を実行し、実際に `NameError: name '_build_scope_delta_authority_evidence' is not defined` が発生することを確認した（`ast` でその関数定義ブロックを機械的に切り出し・再配置し、`ast.parse` で構文的妥当性も確認済み）。一方、修正済みコードでは同じフィクスチャで `STATUS: blocked`（`ANCHOR_COMMENT_SCHEMA_INVALID` は含まない別理由での blocked、または pass/warn）になり `NameError` は発生しない。
- 既存の anchor comment 関連テスト（`test_anchor_comment_preflight_normalization.py` / `test_anchor_comment_artifact_boundary.py` 等）は `_load_schema` を mock して input schema 検証自体をスキップしているため、今回の schema 拡張による影響を受けない。schema 検証を実際に通す既存テスト（`test_refinement_preflight.py` の B5 系等）は `id`/`body`/`issue_url` のみの最小フィクスチャを使っており、今回追加した項目はすべて任意のため影響なし。

- AC1（定義が最初の呼び出しより前）: PASS
- AC2（定義が main トリガーより前）: PASS
- AC3（direct CLI 実行 + anchor comment 経路の subprocess smoke test で NameError が発生しない、かつ実際に対象関数まで到達する）: PASS

author: raphael
body:
## Problem

After unknown-tool recovery records a `runtime.tool_unavailable` tool_use in the transcript, every subsequent history-compression pass fails hard on Bedrock:

```
history policy for agent <id>: bedrock: tool_use in messages references "runtime.tool_unavailable" which is not in the current tool configuration and tool_unavailable is not available
```

`Compress` counts the transcript via `countMessages`, which builds a `model.Request` from the raw history plus the agent's advertised tools. The advertised list never contains `runtime.tool_unavailable` — it is runtime-owned and injected only by `toolUnavailableConfiguredClient`, which wraps `Complete`/`Stream` but not `CountTokens`, and the compression client is typically the application's raw model client anyway. Bedrock's message encode (shared by Converse and CountTokens) requires every historical tool_use name to appear in the request tool configuration, so the count is rejected, the history policy errors, and the plan activity fails deterministically on every retry — the run dies.

Observed in production-shaped traffic: a task run whose agent hit its tool budget, had one unknown-tool recovery recorded, then failed every resume attempt inside the history policy.

## Fix

`countMessages` now applies `ensureToolUnavailableDefinition` to the counting request — the same guarantee the configured model client provides for `Complete` and `Stream`, at the same boundary contract: any request synthesized from history must carry a tool configuration that covers historical tool_use names. The summarization request is unaffected (it flattens history to text).

## Test

`TestCompressCountsToolBearingHistoryWithUnavailableDefinition` drives `Compress` over a transcript containing a recovered `runtime.tool_unavailable` tool_use with an advertised list that lacks it, and asserts every synthesized count request carries the definition. Fails without the fix with `got tools map[known.tool:true]`.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a full CI/CD pipeline via three GitHub Actions workflows triggered in chain: PR quality gates → merge-to-main auto-tag → release creation.

## Workflows

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — runs on PRs targeting `main`
  - `lint`: ruff
  - `test`: pytest
  - `hacs`: `hacs/action@main` — HACS compatibility validation
  - `hassfest`: `home-assistant/actions/helpers/hassfest@master` — manifest/integration structure validation

- **`.github/workflows/tag.yml`** — runs on push to `main` (skips bot commits to avoid loops)
  - Increments patch version in `custom_components/telnyx/manifest.json`
  - Commits with `[skip ci]` and pushes a `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` tag

- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — triggered via `workflow_run` on `Tag` workflow completion
  - Resolves the tag by SHA (`git tag --points-at <head_sha>`) rather than `git describe` to avoid ambiguity
  - Creates a GitHub release with auto-generated notes

author: copilot
body:
The `deploy` job in the GitHub Pages pipeline was failing intermittently at `actions/deploy-pages` after `gh-pages` branch updates. This PR removes the branch-push deployment path from `pkgdown.yaml` and deploys Pages directly from the workflow artifact.

- **Deployment path update**
  - Replaced `JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action` (push to `gh-pages`) with the official Pages flow:
    - `actions/configure-pages@v5`
    - `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`
    - `actions/deploy-pages@v4`
  - Upload source is now explicitly `docs/` as the Pages artifact.

- **Permissions alignment**
  - Updated job permissions to match artifact-based Pages deploy requirements:
    - `contents: read`
    - `pages: write`
    - `id-token: write`

- **Resulting workflow shape**
  - `pkgdown` now builds docs and deploys in one workflow path, instead of triggering a separate branch-driven Pages deployment run.

```yaml
- name: Configure GitHub Pages
  uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

- name: Upload Pages artifact
  uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
  with:
    path: docs

- name: Deploy to GitHub Pages 🚀
  id: deployment
  uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

## 1. 選択スタイルが反映されない問題（本番: book 6AICVsQ0OmvPrI28OB9G）

### 事象
pencil_sketch（やさしい鉛筆スケッチ）を選択したのに水彩風で生成された。

### 根本原因（構造的問題）
**スタイルの決定権が単一箇所に集約されておらず、複数の無関係なソースからスタイル語がプロンプトに流入する設計だった：**
- テンプレート `visualDirection` / `coverImagePromptTemplate` / `imagePromptTemplate` に画材語（"soft watercolor storybook style" 等）がハードコード（seed 全体で約250箇所）
- 対策の `stripInlineStyleWords` は存在したが、**一部の合成点（scene プロンプト）にしか適用されておらず**、`buildFixedStyleBible` → styleBible 経由の混入が素通し
- guided_ai でも visualDirection が未浄化のまま Gemini に渡り、生成される styleBible/imagePrompt に写経される

### 修正（choke point への集約）
| 箇所 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `buildFixedStyleBible` | visualDirection を浄化してから styleBible に合成 |
| `buildSystemPrompt` | guided_ai の Gemini プロンプトでも visualDirection を浄化 |
| `sanitizeStoryStyleBible`（新設） | 「選択スタイルに属さない画材語のみ除去」を cover / page / キャラ参照の**全合成点**に適用。Firestore 保存済みの汚染 styleBible にも効くため、**既存の壊れた絵本もページ再生成で救済可能** |
| `generate-template` | 新規テンプレ自動生成時にスタイル語埋め込みを禁止する指示に変更 |

回帰テスト7件追加（実テンプレ fixed-classic-mitten での混入検証・正当スタイル語の保持検証を含む）。

モバイルの横スクロールカルーセルを、テンプレ選択と同じ縦スクロールグリッド（2/3/5列）に変更。

`pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom,16px)]` はツールバー表示中に 0 になり、ボタンが画面最下端に密着して下端タップが Safari のツールバー展開に食われる。`calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)+12px)` で常に 12px 浮かせる（作成フロー8ページ＋avatar＋cinematic＋help の11箇所）。

## Summary
The admin layout only checked `admin:access` — any staff role could reach any `/admin/*` page directly by URL (e.g. a content editor hitting `/admin/pricing`), and `/api/admin/stats` returned every domain's counts to every staff role regardless of their actual permissions.

- Every admin sub-page now calls `requirePermission` with its specific permission (`pricing:write`, `leads:read`, `content:write`, `catalog:read`, `users:manage`, `settings:write`, `audit:read`) instead of relying solely on the layout's `admin:access` check — unauthorized direct navigation now 404s (hide, don't reveal, matching the existing API guard contract).

- `/api/admin/stats` now computes each field only if the caller's role holds the matching permission; `AdminStats` fields are optional and `DashboardTiles` renders only the tiles it actually received (with a fallback message if none apply).

## 概要

S4 外部ゲスト（#93・親: #91）の第 1 弾（DB 基盤）。保育園・ペット/ベビーシッターを**対象ペット・期間限定**のゲストとして受け入れるための `guest_grants` テーブルとゲスト RLS を導入します。**アプリの挙動はこの PR では変わりません**（新設列 `guest_visible` は既定 false・アプリ未使用、付与を作る導線は後続 PR）。

## 変更内容

### DB（`20260705000000_guest_grants.sql`）
- **`guest_grants`**: `household_id` / `user_id` / `scope_pet_id` / `role`（`guest:daycare` | `guest:sitter` CHECK）/ `valid_from` / `valid_to`（null = 取消まで）/ `revoked_at` / `created_by`。内部 role（`household_members`）とは別系統の付与テーブル
  - **ペット削除で付与は CASCADE**（UC-H11 の 2026-07-04 ヒアリング決定。記録側は従来どおり SET NULL で残置）
- **RLS ヘルパー**（SECURITY DEFINER + `search_path` 固定、`guest_grants` のみ参照で再帰なし）
  - `has_guest_access(household, pet)`: 「今日」有効な付与があるか（ペットプロフィール可視判定）
  - `has_guest_record_access(household, pet, record_date)`: 付与が今日有効 **かつ** 記録日が付与期間内（UC-G04 の期間外自動無効化を日付単位で判定）
- **D8 最厳格の可視範囲**（既定 deny）
  - `daycare_records.guest_visible boolean not null default false` を新設（世帯が記録単位で明示共有）

- **付与の管理は世帯 owner のみ**: editor・ゲスト自身は発行不可（自己昇格不可 UC-G06）、対象ペットは自世帯のペット限定（越境防止）。ゲスト本人は自分宛て付与の閲覧のみ可

`guest_grants_test.sql`: 可視範囲 8 系統（共有/非共有・期限切れ・期間外・クロステナント・写真・世帯情報）、書込制約 6 系統（追加成功・期限切れ/期間外/共有フラグ偽装の拒否・更新/削除不可）、管理権限（owner 限定・editor 拒否・自己付与拒否・越境付与拒否・失効）、失効後の遮断と記入の残置（UC-G07）、ペット削除 CASCADE（UC-H11）

なし（テーブル・関数・列・ポリシーの追加のみ。既存ポリシーは不変更で、ゲストポリシーは OR で併存）

author: jleechan2015
body:
## Background

Continues the Rust daemon crate from [#139](https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/139) (config.rs + telemetry.rs, Tasks 1-3) and [#145](https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/pull/145) (state.rs, Task 4), per the TDD plan [`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-03-auto-factory-daemon-rust-stage1.md`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/blob/main/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-03-auto-factory-daemon-rust-stage1.md) Task 5.

## Goals

Implement the tool boundary — the five traits (`Tracker`, `Scm`, `Sessions`, `Vcs`, `Llm`) that are the *only* traits in the system per [`docs/auto-factory-daemon-design-rust.md`](https://github.com/jleechanorg/dark-factory/blob/main/docs/auto-factory-daemon-design-rust.md) §4 — plus the shared `run_tool` subprocess helper every future `Cli*` impl will use, and scripted test-double fakes so downstream tasks (intake, router, dispatch, verifier) can unit test against fakes instead of real CLIs/subprocesses.

Also lands a parallelization amendment: one-line stub modules for the four downstream tasks so they stay file-disjoint and can proceed in parallel PRs.

## Tenets

- Traits at the tool boundary, structs everywhere else (design doc §1.3) — `tools.rs` defines exactly the five traits from §4, verbatim signatures.
- Shell out, don't link (design doc §1.1) — `run_tool` wraps `std::process::Command` only; no new dependency for timeout/polling.
- `DaemonError` reused from `errors.rs` (no new error variants) — `Tool`/`Timeout` cover every failure mode `run_tool` needs.
- Fakes have no subprocess use — a scripted `Vec`/`HashMap` of responses plus a `RefCell<Vec<String>>` call log per trait, so downstream unit tests assert both output and call shape without touching `br`/`gh`/`ao`/`git`/an LLM CLI.

## High-level description

- `daemon/src/tools.rs` (new): the five traits (`Tracker`, `Scm`, `Sessions`, `Vcs`, `Llm`) and their data types (`Bead`, `Issue`, `Permission`, `PrSnapshot`, `SpawnSpec`, `SessionId`) per design doc §4; `run_tool(cmd, args, timeout_secs) -> Result<String, DaemonError>` spawns via `std::process::Command`, polls `try_wait()` every 100ms tracked against a `std::time::Instant` deadline, kills + returns `DaemonError::Timeout` if the deadline elapses, `DaemonError::Tool{rc,...}` on non-zero exit, else stdout as `String`.
- `daemon/tests/common/mod.rs` (new): `FakeTracker`, `FakeScm`, `FakeSessions`, `FakeVcs`, `FakeLlm` — scripted responses + call logs, zero subprocess use.
- `daemon/tests/tools_fakes.rs` (new): exercises each fake — call-log recording, scripted-response return, and error paths.
- `daemon/src/lib.rs` (new): a binary-only crate has no externally importable modules, so `daemon/tests/*` integration tests can't `use daemon::tools::{...}` without a library target. Added `lib.rs` re-exporting all modules (`pub mod ...`); `main.rs` now pulls its modules from the lib (`use daemon::{...}`, later tasks add specific imports as they wire the poll loop) instead of redeclaring `mod` for each file, so there's exactly one copy of each module's source.
- `daemon/src/{intake,router,verifier,dispatch}.rs` (new, one line each): `//! stub — implemented by its own task PR` — reserves the files so beads jleechan-41f/49y/n54/b3m can build on them in parallel without colliding on file creation.
- `daemon/src/main.rs`: registers the four new stub modules + `tools`, wired via the new `lib.rs` (see above) instead of direct `mod` declarations.
- `daemon/src/state.rs`: one narrowly-scoped `#[allow(clippy::should_implement_trait)]` (+ comment) on the pre-existing `OverlayState::from_str` — the new `lib.rs` target surfaces a clippy lint that the binary-only crate previously did not trip, because `from_str` becomes part of the crate's public API surface. `from_str` mirrors `as_str()`'s SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE mapping (not general parsing), so the inherent method is intentional and the suppression is scoped to that one method — no other change to Task 4's file.

## Testing

Ran locally in an isolated worktree (`/tmp/factory-jleechan-eb5-r1`), `cargo test` inside `daemon/`:

```
running 15 tests
test config::tests::missing_key_is_config_error ... ok
test config::tests::parses_example_config ... ok
test telemetry::tests::emits_schema_compliant_jsonl ... ok
test state::tests::register_branch_upserts_on_conflict ... ok
test state::tests::illegal_state_string_rejected_by_schema ... ok
test state::tests::owned_branches_lists_only_registered ... ok
test state::tests::owned_branches_deletion_guard_survives_bead_overlay_delete ... ok
test state::tests::overlay_roundtrip ... ok
test state::tests::load_missing_bead_returns_none ... ok
test state::tests::overlay_roundtrip_updates_on_conflict ... ok
test state::tests::all_nine_overlay_states_accepted_by_schema ... ok
test tools::tests::run_tool_nonzero_exit_is_tool_error ... ok
test tools::tests::run_tool_success_captures_stdout ... ok
test tools::tests::run_tool_echo_captures_output ... ok
test tools::tests::run_tool_timeout_kills_child ... ok

test result: ok. 15 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 1.07s

     Running unittests src/main.rs
test tests::scaffold_compiles ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s

     Running tests/tools_fakes.rs
test fake_llm_returns_scripted_judgment_regardless_of_prompt ... ok
test fake_sessions_spawn_attach_stop_quiescent_roundtrip ... ok
test fake_scm_returns_scripted_permission_and_records_call ... ok
test fake_vcs_returns_scripted_head_shas ... ok
test fake_tracker_records_calls_and_returns_scripted_response ... ok
test fake_vcs_missing_head_is_tool_error ... ok

test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

22 passed total (0 failed). `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no issues found.

The bead-required `run_tool` tests are all in `tools.rs`, `#[cfg(unix)]`:
- **Success path:** `run_tool_success_captures_stdout` (`true`, no args) and `run_tool_echo_captures_output` (`echo hello` — captured stdout, not just exit status).
- **Non-zero exit:** `run_tool_nonzero_exit_is_tool_error` (`false`) → `DaemonError::Tool{rc:1,...}`.
- **Timeout kill:** `run_tool_timeout_kills_child` (`sleep 2` against a 1s timeout) → `DaemonError::Timeout`, and the child is actually killed (not left running) via `child.kill()` + `child.wait()` before returning.

`tests/tools_fakes.rs` covers all five fakes: call-log contents (exact method + key args recorded), scripted-response return values, and the not-scripted error path (`FakeVcs::base_head` on an unseeded branch returns `DaemonError::Tool`).

## Low-level details

- `run_tool` polls every 100ms (`Duration::from_millis(100)`) against a deadline computed once as `Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs)`, matching the TDD plan's Step 1 spec exactly.
- On timeout, `child.kill()` and `child.wait()` are both called (ignoring their `Result`) before returning `DaemonError::Timeout` — this reaps the zombie process rather than leaving it for the OS.
- `Permission::is_write_tier()` implements the write-tier gate boolean (spec §4.2.3: only `Write`/`Admin` may trigger dispatch) as a data-type helper method — the actual gating logic in `intake.rs` is Task 6's scope, not implemented here.
- `PrSnapshot` fields are shaped directly off the 7-green gate list in spec §4.2.5 (`ci_success`, `mergeable`, `coderabbit_approved`, `bugbot_error_count`, `unresolved_thread_count`) so `verifier.rs` (Task 8) can consume them without a data-shape renegotiation.
- No new crate dependencies — `daemon/Cargo.toml` is untouched; `run_tool` uses only `std::process::Command` / `std::time::{Duration, Instant}`.
- `tests/common/mod.rs` is included by test files via `mod common;` (the idiomatic Rust convention for sharing a module across multiple files under `tests/`, since each direct file under `tests/` is compiled as its own separate c

author: basmawebinfo-hub
body:
## Phase 3 · Admin Audit Log Viewer — writer + reader (Phase 3 part 3)

Closes **H-04** — `admin_audit_log` table existed but had no writes, no UI.
Also completes 3 of 4 Phase 3 milestones.

### What ships

**1. Audit log writer — `logAdminAction()` in `lib/supabase/db.ts`**

- New fire-and-forget helper that inserts an `admin_audit_log` row.
- Reads `auth.uid()` via `supabase.auth.getUser()` and writes it as `admin_id` (matches the `audit_admin_insert` RLS policy).
- Diff payload is optional; `{ before?, after? }` or free-form JSON accepted.
- **Never throws.** If the audit write fails (RLS mismatch, network, etc.) the underlying admin mutation still succeeds. Audit is best-effort.
- Called after every admin-side mutation succeeds.

**2. Instrumented mutations (16 call sites)**

| Action | Target | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `create` | `meal_plans` | `adminCreatePlan` |
| `create` | `sessions` | `adminCreateSession` |
| `update` | `meal_plans` | `adminUpdatePlanMeta` |
| `upsert` | `meals` | `adminUpsertMeal` |
| `upsert` | `products` | `adminUpsertProduct` |
| `delete` | `meals` | `adminDeleteMeal` |
| `delete` | `products` | `adminDeleteProduct` |
| `delete` | `meal_plans` | `adminDeletePlan` |
| `delete` | `profiles` | `adminDeleteClient` |
| `assign` | `plan_items` | `adminSetPlanItems` (non-empty) |
| `unassign` | `plan_items` | `adminSetPlanItems` (empty) |
| `status_change` | `orders` | `adminUpdateOrderStatus` |
| `status_change` / `cancel` | `sessions` | `adminUpdateSessionStatus` |
| `block` / `unblock` | `profiles` | `adminToggleBlock` |
| `upload` | `meal-images` | `uploadMealImage` |
| `upload` | `product-images` | `uploadProductImage` |

`adminUpsertPlan` is intentionally NOT instrumented — it's the legacy destructive-replace helper, superseded by `adminCreatePlan` + `adminSetPlanItems`. It still ships for backward compat and will be removed later.

**3. Audit log reader — 3 new helpers**

- `adminFetchAuditLog(page, pageSize, filter)` — DB-side pagination via `.range(from, to)`, newest first, resolves `admin_name` via profiles join.
- `adminFetchAuditLogCount(filter)` — head-only count with the same filter, for pagination controls.
- `adminFetchAuditAdmins()` — distinct admin identities for the filter dropdown.

All three accept the same `AuditLogFilter` shape: `{ action, targetTable, adminId, from, to, search }`. Filters compose server-side (no in-memory filtering after fetch).

**4. New page — `/admin/audit`**

- **Header:** page title + Filters toggle + Refresh button.
- **Filters panel (collapsible):** Action dropdown (12 values), Target dropdown (10 values), Admin dropdown (dynamic), Date range (from / to), Search input (matches target_id via `ilike`). All controls have visible focus rings, labelled `<label>` elements, and `aria-controls` on the toggle.
- **Row:** color-coded action pill + target chip + monospaced short-form target id + time-ago label + admin name + full ISO timestamp on hover. Rows with a JSON diff show a "Details" toggle that expands a syntax-styled JSON block (`aria-expanded` reflects state).
- **Pagination:** DB-side, 20 rows per page. Prev/Next buttons with `disabled` state at bounds, `aria-label`, focus rings. "Showing N-M of TOTAL" summary.
- **States:** distinct loading (6 skeleton bars) / error (red card with Try again) / empty (all-time no entries) / no-filter-match (empty with Clear filters shortcut).
- **Debounced search** at 250ms so typing doesn't spam DB.
- **Filter changes reset to page 0** automatically.
- Fully **responsive** and **localized EN/AR**. Time-ago labels + all filter labels + empty-state copy translated.

**5. Navigation**

- Added "Audit Log" nav item in the Insights group of `AdminShell`, right after Analytics. Uses `ClipboardList` icon.

### Design decisions

- **Best-effort audit writes:** `logAdminAction` never throws. Adding a fatal error handler here would create a class of admin mutations that succeeded in state but blocked the UI on an audit-log failure — worse than the current behaviour.
- **No IP / user-agent capture yet.** Both fields stay NULL when written from the client. A server-route wrapper could populate them, but every admin mutation would then need to route through an API endpoint. Deferred; the columns exist for a future migration.
- **Diff payload keeps `after` only for upserts** — I don't fetch the previous row before writing (would double the query count). The audit row still captures who / when / what type of change, plus the target id and the new state. Sufficient for compliance narratives.
- **No `admin_audit_log` UPDATE/DELETE** — the table is append-only by RLS design. No changes to schema, no new migration.
- **DB-side pagination** avoids loading all entries; only 20 rows + 1 count query per page.
- **No new dependency.**

### Files changed (3)

- `lib/supabase/db.ts` — full rewrite of 16 admin mutation return paths + new type exports (`AuditAction`, `AuditLogEntry`, `AuditLogFilter`) + 4 new exported functions (`logAdminAction`, `adminFetchAuditLog`, `adminFetchAuditLogCount`, `adminFetchAuditAdmins`). 41838B -> 48624B.
- `components/admin/admin-shell.tsx` — 2 minor edits: import `ClipboardList` + add "Audit Log" nav item.
- `app/admin/audit/page.tsx` — **new file** (22621B).

### Verification plan

- 35-route probe + `/admin/audit` (36 total).
- Anonymous `/admin/audit` should 200 → the middleware protects it via layout gate (already the pattern for the whole admin surface).
- No schema change, no DB migration, no dependency change.

### Rollback

- Revert this PR. No DB, no dependency change. Prior admin mutations continue to work unchanged; the only observable effect is that no new audit rows will be inserted.

### Advances Phase 3

- Phase 3 milestones: **3 / 4 done** (Sessions Booking #32, Analytics Dashboard #33, Audit Log this PR).
- Next: Full Onboarding Fields — SCHEMA CHANGE, will surface a review gate before implementation.

author: gmoon
body:
## Summary

v4.1: a **usability layer on top of the pure `fetch()` core**, plus a header-passthrough regression fix. v4.0's pure `fetch()` was the right correctness call, but it dropped v3's ergonomics and quietly narrowed response headers. This rebuilds the missing usability as thin, opt-in layers — each built on the one below, none touching `fetch()`:

```
fetch()      pure primitive — get a key, throw typed errors   (unchanged)
  └─ pipe() / middleware()   one-call ergonomics, honest status codes
  └─ staticSite()            index + error documents (S3 website parity)
```

## What's in here

- **Restore header passthrough** (`#125`) — re-emit `x-amz-meta-*` from the SDK `Metadata` map and forward the common S3 response headers (SSE, `x-amz-version-id`, storage-class, …) that v4.0 silently dropped.
- **`pipe()` / `middleware()`** (`#126`) — recover v3's one-call route handler **without** the empty-200 lie: a missing/forbidden key renders the honest 404/403/416. `pipe()` never rejects for a classified failure; `middleware()` forwards unexpected errors to `next`.
- **`staticSite({ indexDocument, errorDocument })`** (`#127`) — S3 static website hosting on a **private** bucket: index-document resolution (`/` → `index.html`, `/dir/` → `dir/index.html`) and a custom error document served with the original 4xx status. Config rides on the factory, not the constructor, so nothing leaks into `fetch()`.

## Design notes

- The purity guarantee lives in `fetch()`; every convenience consumes it. A test pins that `fetch('/missing')` still throws.
- All response-writing flows through one private `writeBody()`; handler-error policy through one `onHandlerError()`. New public `RequestHandler` type.
- Examples exercised by the smoke gate against a real bucket: `express-basic.ts` converted to `middleware()`, new `static-site.ts` added (mounted with `app.use` so `/` matches — the Express 5 `/*splat` wildcard doesn't).

## Testing

- `tsc` (src + examples) clean, biome clean, **64/64** unit tests (26 new).
- Full 4-example smoke passes against the live `s3proxy-public` bucket (health=200, index=200, missing=404), including `static-site` root→index resolution and error-document fallback.

## Not included (deliberately)

Two deeper ideas surfaced in review and are left for follow-ups: replacing the header allowlist with a generic SDK-middleware passthrough, and moving the adapters to a separate module with a public key-override on `fetch()`. Both change behavior or public surface beyond this PR's scope.

Part of #128.

author: tim4724
body:
## Why

The level-based music tempo scaling misbehaved and is a suspected cause of the reported "doubled / warbly" music. On **web** the bug is provable: `setSpeed` set `playbackRate = rate` **and** `detune = -log2(rate)×1200`, and for a raw `AudioBufferSourceNode` those multiply to `rate × (1/rate) = 1.0` at every level — so the tempo change cancelled itself out (measured computed rate ≈ 1.000 across levels 1→15), while the opposing ramps could smear the audio.

Rather than fix the feature, this strips it: **the track now loops at a constant rate everywhere.**

## What changed

**Web** (`public/display/`)
- `Music.js` — removed `setSpeed()`, `_rate`, and the `playbackRate`/`detune` writes.
- `DisplayRender.js` — removed the per-frame max-level → `setSpeed` driver and `lastMusicLevel`.
- `DisplayGame.js` — removed the `lastMusicLevel` reset.

**Portable engine** (`server/`)
- `PartyCore.js` — `frame()` no longer emits the `musicSpeed` command; dropped `_lastMusicLevel`.
- `PartyCore.d.ts` — removed `MusicSpeedCommand` from the union/type/docs.
- `constants.js` — `MAX_SPEED_LEVEL` **kept** (still caps gravity); comment updated.
- Tests + `partycore-commands-golden.json` regenerated (musicSpeed scenario/test removed).

**Android TV** (`android/`)
- `MusicPlayer.kt` — removed `setLevel()` + `PlaybackParameters` rate.
- `MainActivity.kt` — removed the `setLevel` call + `setMusicLevel` override.
- `EngineConstants.kt` — removed `musicRateFor()`; deleted `EngineConstantsTest.kt`.
- `FrameResult.kt` / `DisplayOutput.kt` / `DisplayCoordinator.kt` — removed `MUSIC_SPEED` / `setMusicLevel` + comments.

**Apple TV** (`appletv/`)
- `MusicPlayer.swift` — removed the `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` node (rewired `player → mixer`) and `setLevel()`.
- `RootScene.swift` — removed the `setLevel` call. `DisplayCoordinator.swift` / `Snapshot.swift` — comment cleanup.

## Verification
- **JS: 559 tests pass, build clean.** Web display verified live through a real game — exactly one audible looping source, `playbackRate = 1`.
- **Native ports not compiled here** (no Gradle/Xcode in this env); edits are precise deletions verified by a clean cross-repo grep for `musicSpeed`/`setSpeed`/`setLevel`/`timePitch`/`playbackRate`. Please confirm with a Gradle + Xcode build.
