author: shai-almog
body:
## Summary

Adds deeper AR/VR support to the framework as two new core packages, with native backends, a simulated backend for the simulator, build-pipeline integration, unit tests and developer guide chapters.

### `com.codename1.ar` (ARKit on iOS, ARCore on Android)
- World tracking, plane detection (horizontal/vertical), screen-point hit testing, anchors, glTF / `gpu.Mesh` content placement, light estimation, image tracking and face tracking.
- API modeled on the camera package: `AR.isSupported()` / `AR.getCapabilities()` / `AR.open(ARSessionOptions)`; single active `ARSession` owning an `ARView`, anchors and planes.
- SPI `com.codename1.impl.ARImpl` mirrors `CameraImpl` (one impl per session, `Display.getARBackend()` accessor). Implementation events may arrive on any thread; the core bridge marshals them to the EDT and coalesces high-frequency refinements (anchor/plane updates, camera pose, light) to latest-per-id.
- Content model: ports never see glTF bytes - `ARModel` parses via the (new) device-free `GltfLoader` overloads and hands raw interleaved buffers + a decoded base-color image to the backend.

### `com.codename1.vr` (pure core, no platform dependency)
- `VRView`: side-by-side stereo rendering of a `VRRenderer` on the existing gpu pipeline, per-eye cameras from `VRCameraRig`, head tracking from `HeadTracker` (deterministic complementary fusion in `OrientationFilter`).
- `Media360View`: equirectangular panorama viewer with drag and gyroscope look, mono and cardboard-style stereo. `TextureSource` is the documented extension point for dynamic content; 360 video and lens distortion are deliberately scoped out (no placeholder API) pending a media-to-texture path and render-to-texture support.

### Platform backends
- **iOS**: `CN1AR.{h,m}` wraps an ARKit `ARSession` composited through an `ARSCNView`; content buffers become `SCNGeometry`. Gated by a new `INCLUDE_CN1_AR` define (uncommented by the builder only for apps referencing the API), compiled out on tvOS/watchOS, with unconditional stub bridge symbols so non-AR apps link cleanly.
- **Android**: typed ARCore code in the deletable `com.codename1.impl.android.ar` package (external-OES camera background + lit/textured mesh renderer on a `GLSurfaceView`); reached reflectively from `AndroidImplementation`, deleted by the builder for non-AR apps. The port maven module excludes the package from its own compile (ARCore is not in cn1-binaries) while still shipping it in `android_port_sources.jar`.
- **Simulator**: `JavaSEARImpl` renders a virtual room (floor/wall planes detected after a realistic delay, mouse-look + WASD camera, deterministic ray-cast hit tests) through the software 3D device, so the full AR loop is debuggable with breakpoints. A new Simulate > AR Simulation window drives tracking failures, light estimates, reference image detection and face toggling. VR/360 run in the simulator through the desktop GL backend with the existing Motion Simulation window feeding the head tracker.

### Build pipeline
- New `AiDependencyTable` entry for `com/codename1/ar/`: camera permission + `NSCameraUsageDescription`, ARCore gradle dependency, `android.hardware.camera.ar` feature and `com.google.ar.core=optional` manifest meta-data (new `androidMetaData` table capability); `android.ar.required=true` flips to AR-only. ARKit/SceneKit linked explicitly by `IPhoneBuilder` and weak-linked on the tv/watch/mac slices. Apps that never reference the package pay no size, permission or store-visibility cost.

## Test plan
- `mvn test -Punittests -pl core-unittests`: 3830 tests pass, including new suites for the AR session/event bridge/pose math, VR fusion determinism, camera rig, sphere primitive and device-free glTF parsing.
- `mvn test -pl codenameone-maven-plugin`: 197 tests pass, including new `AiDependencyTableTest` coverage of the AR entry.
- iOS: generated hellocodenameone Xcode project (which now references the API) compiles and links with ARKit enabled (`BUILD SUCCEEDED`); the compiled-out stub path is verified clean with a standalone clang syntax check.
- Android: generated Gradle project compiles the ARCore backend against the injected dependency; manifest/gradle output verified (meta-data, permission, feature, minSdk 24).
- Simulator: scratch app verified the full loop end to end - plane events, hit test at the mathematically expected point, anchor + sphere placement rendered in the virtual room.

author: andregoepel
body:
Closes #57 (F8 — `MailMessage` handler has no origin/authorization guard).

## What

`SendEmailMessageHandler.Handle` now takes the Wolverine `Envelope` and drops (with a warning) any `MailMessage` that did not originate in-process. Messages published via `IMessageBus` are routed to a `local://` queue, so the guard accepts only a `local` destination scheme (a `null` destination — direct in-process invocation — is also treated as local, so the normal send path is never blocked). Anything arriving over an external transport (`rabbitmq://`, `tcp://`, `sqs://`, …) is refused.

## Why

`MailMessage` is an internal, in-process contract, but the `AppFoundationOptions.ConfigureWolverine` extension point invites consumers to add external transports. If `MailMessage` ever became reachable over an untrusted transport, an attacker who could place a message on it could send arbitrary email (recipient, subject, HTML body) from the app's SMTP identity — spam/phishing from a trusted domain. This closes that latent path at the foundation level rather than relying on every consumer to avoid it.

## Design notes

- The origin signal is `Envelope.Destination`. I verified against Wolverine 6.16's API that in-process routing uses the `local://` transport scheme and that `Envelope` is constructable with a settable `Destination` (used by the tests). `ReceivedAt` was considered but is a timestamp that also fires for local-queue delivery, so it can't distinguish origin.
- Drops-and-logs rather than throwing, to avoid retry/dead-letter churn if a consumer misconfigures a transport or an attacker floods one.
- Classification extracted to `internal static bool IsLocalOrigin(Uri?)` for direct unit testing.

## Tests

`SendEmailMessageHandlerTests`: local origin still forwards all fields / sends exactly once; external origin sends nothing; `IsLocalOrigin` theory over `local`/`rabbitmq`/`tcp`/`sqs` schemes and null.

## Verification

- `dotnet build -c Release` — 0 errors.
- `dotnet test -c Release` — 73/73 passing (7 new/updated).
- Two files changed; independent of the other open PRs.

author: laboef1900
body:
Supersedes #111 (Dependabot's `@prisma/client` 6→7 bump, which was incomplete — it left the `prisma` CLI at 6.x — and branched from a pre-OIDC main 56 commits back).

## Why this isn't a version bump
Prisma 7 ships a **Rust-free client and removes the built-in query engine**. Two hard breaking changes result:
1. `datasource.url` is **no longer allowed in `schema.prisma`** — the connection string moves to a `prisma.config.ts` (for the CLI) and is passed to `PrismaClient` via a **driver adapter** at runtime.
2. Every `PrismaClient` must be constructed with an adapter (`@prisma/adapter-pg`).

## Changes
- Bump `@prisma/client` + `prisma` to **7.8.0** in lockstep; add **`@prisma/adapter-pg`** (bundles `pg`) as a runtime dep.
- `schema.prisma`: drop `binaryTargets` (no engine binary in v7 → the old DHI/OpenSSL pinning is obsolete) and the datasource `url`.
- New **`apps/server/prisma.config.ts`**: schema path, `migrations.seed`, and `datasource.url` from `process.env.DATABASE_URL`. Deliberately **not** `prisma/config`'s `env()` — that resolves eagerly and throws, which would break the DB-less `prisma generate` CI step.
- Wire `new PrismaPg({ connectionString })` into all **five** `PrismaClient` sites (server plugin, test setup, testcontainer global-setup, seed, xlsx import). The server plugin reads the connection string from the validated `env`.
- Remove the obsolete `package.json#prisma` seed block.
- `Dockerfile.server`: correct the now-inaccurate "query engine" comments; **keep** the libssl copy — the boot-time `migrate deploy` still uses Prisma's native **schema** engine.

## Validation (local, against the exact CI pipeline)
- ✅ `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- ✅ `prisma generate` (the original #111 failure — P1012 — is gone)
- ✅ lint · typecheck (server + web) · **337 tests** on a real Postgres testcontainer (all 10 migrations applied via the v7 schema engine; adapter exercised across every route/service)
- ✅ `build` (web bundle + server compile)
- ✅ Production plugin path: `new PrismaClient({ adapter })` + `$connect` + query + `$disconnect` against real Postgres
- ✅ Docker entrypoint path: `node prisma/build/index.js migrate deploy` loading `prisma.config.ts`
- ✅ `pnpm deploy --prod` bundle contains `prisma.config.ts`, schema, migrations, prisma CLI, adapter-pg, pg, dotenv (and correctly omits `tsx`)

## Known non-issue
The `pg` driver emits one deprecation warning ("Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is deprecated … pg@9.0"). It's a future-removal notice from `pg@8`, not an error; Prisma's adapter owns this and it does not affect the passing test run.

author: wilbrt
body:
# fix(pi-session): honor Settings-page provider/model or fail loudly

## Summary

Pi sessions were silently ignoring the `pi_default_provider` /
`pi_default_model` values configured on the Web UI Settings page. Although the
settings persisted to and round-tripped from `.tesseraft/settings.json`
correctly (the storage path was healthy), newly created Pi sessions always
fell back to the SDK's default model with no error shown anywhere.

Root cause: `createRealPiSessionAdapter.createSession` in
`web/src-server/lib/piSessionAdapter.ts` had a three-layer silent-fallback
cascade that swallowed every settings-resolution failure:

1. `readPiDefaults()` wrapped the `tesseraft control-plane settings get` call in
   `try/catch { return {}; }`, masking CLI/parse failures.
2. `resolveSettingsModel()` wrapped `AuthStorage.create()` /
   `ModelRegistry.create()` / `registry.find(provider, model)` in
   `try/catch { return undefined; }`, masking construction/lookup failures and
   catalog misses.
3. A blind `createAgentSession(withDefaults) → catch → createAgentSession(baseOptions)`
   retry discarded the resolved `Model` and the original error, degrading to
   the SDK default.

Each layer independently produced the symptom "my configured model/provider
isn't applied" with no visible error.

The SDK's `CreateAgentSessionOptions` has no string `provider`/`modelId`
fields (only `model?: Model`, `modelRegistry?`, `authStorage?`), so resolving a
real `Model` via `ModelRegistry.find` and passing `model`/`authStorage`/
`modelRegistry` together to `createAgentSession` is the correct shape; the
defect was purely the silent fallbacks.

## Implementation notes

Branch: `fix/pi-session-settings-model` (two commits ahead of `origin/main`,
not pushed):

- `6a2be57` — server-side resolution fix
- `e62fc4f` — frontend error surfacing + regression guards

Changes (6 files, no Clojure/SDK/settings-schema/Tesseraft-workflow edits):

### `web/src-server/lib/piSessionAdapter.ts` (primary fix)

- Extracted `readPiDefaults`, `resolveSettingsModel`, and `createSessionWithModel`
  to module scope (exported) so they are unit-testable without spawning the SDK.
- **Distinguish "unconfigured" from "misconfigured"**: when **both** provider and
  model are absent, settings are genuinely unset → `model` is omitted so the
  SDK uses its own default (the only legitimate "use SDK default" path). When
  **either** is set, the user configured defaults and resolution must succeed
  or the session must fail loudly.
- **Surface resolution failures**: when provider/model are set but
  `ModelRegistry`/`AuthStorage` are missing from the SDK build, construction
  throws, or `registry.find(provider, model)` returns `undefined` (catalog miss),
  throw a typed `PiSettingsResolutionError` (`status=400`,
  `code='pi_settings_resolution'`) with an actionable message naming the
  provider/model and pointing to `pi auth` / `models.json`. No silent
  `return undefined`.
- **Remove the blind `baseOptions` retry**: `createAgentSession` is called
  **exactly once** with options built from the resolution result; errors
  propagate. `handlePiError` in `web/src-server/routes/api.ts` maps the thrown
  `{status, code, message}` to the 400 HTTP response, so the UI surfaces the
  message.
- **Diagnostic provenance**: the `session.created` event now carries
  `data` = `{ source: 'settings', provider, modelId }` when resolved, or
  `{ source: 'sdk-default', defaults: 'none (SDK default)' }` when
  unconfigured — giving the Pi Sessions panel's Diagnostics view concrete
  evidence of which model was applied. (Resolved `Model` objects are never
  serialized — only the `{ provider, modelId }` provenance.)
- **Dynamic-import boundary preserved**: kept the
  `new Function('specifier', 'return import(specifier)')` dynamic import so
  `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` stays out of the Vite/tsx bundle graph
  (a static import would break `web:build`).

### `web/src/components/PiSessionsPanel.tsx` (frontend error surfacing)

- Added a dedicated `createError` state separate from the load/stream `error`
  state, so a post-failure refresh cannot clobber the actionable
  `pi_settings_resolution` message.
- `createSession` sets both `createError` and panel `error` on catch,
  preserving the message text thrown by `postJson`.
- Renders an assertive inline error region
  (`className="error inline pi-session-create-error"`, `role="alert"`,
  `aria-live="assertive"`) anchored inside the create control card next to the
  "Create session" button; the top-of-panel banner also gains `role="alert"`.

### Tests

- `test/web-pi-session.test.js` (new, 11 tests): unconfigured → `model`
  omitted; configured+resolvable → `{model, authStorage, modelRegistry}` passed;
  catalog miss / `find()` throws / construction throws / missing
  `ModelRegistry` / missing `AuthStorage` → typed `PiSettingsResolutionError`;
  `createSessionWithModel` single-call behavior (verified **no blind retry**).
- `test/web-server.test.js` (+28): asserts `POST /api/pi-sessions` returns
  `400` with `error.code === 'pi_settings_resolution'` and a message including
  the provider/model and the `pi auth` remediation hint — the exact contract
  `postJson` relies on to surface the message.
- `test/web-ui.test.js` (+8): asserts the `pi-session-create-error` region has
  `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"`, and that `createSession` wraps the POST
  in try/catch and calls `setCreateError`.
- `web/package.json`: one-line addition of the new test file to the `web:test`
  script.

## Validation/tests

Automated:

- `npm run web:build` — passed (TypeScript + Vite build; guards the
  dynamic-import boundary and type edits).
- `npm run web:test` — 53 tests, 0 failures:
  - `web-server` (22)
  - `web-pi-session` (11)
  - `web-ui` (13)
  - `web-studio` (7)
- `bb test` — "Smoke checks passed.", no failures (Clojure regression guard,
  unaffected by this change).

Manual (real Pi SDK adapter, Pi auth present, worktree-rooted test server):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Unconfigured (both fields empty) | ✅ `session.created` event `data.source: "sdk-default"` |
| Configured + resolvable (`opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4-flash`) | ✅ `session.created` event `data.source: "settings"`, provider/model recorded |
| Misconfigured (unresolvable provider/model) | ✅ visible error alert naming provider/model + `pi auth` guidance; no silent default session |
| Browser console | ✅ clean |
| Mobile viewport (390×844) | ✅ no horizontal overflow |

Code review (round 2): **PASS** — implementation faithfully realizes the
design, closes all open issues, adds meaningful regression guards; no overbroad
changes.

## Risks or follow-up

- **Intentional UX change**: removing the blind retry turns a previously-silent
  misconfiguration into a **visible failure**. A user who configured a model
  that cannot be resolved (typo, unconfigured auth, missing `models.json`
  entry) will now get an actionable 400 error instead of a silently-wrong
  session. This is the intended behavior per the design; the error message
  points to `pi auth` / spelling / `models.json`.
- **Auth-vs-resolution coupling**: a valid provider/model that resolves in the
  catalog but has no API key in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` will create the session
  (model resolved) and fail at the first `prompt()` with an auth error via
  `session.error` — already surfaced. Acceptable and visible.
- **Per-`createSession` control-plane call**: `readPiDefaults` shells out to
  `tesseraft control-plane settings get` on every session creation (cheap,
  keeps values fresh). Caching is out of scope; not added here.
- **Minor non-blocking UX follow-up (filed, not addressed)**: the Settings
  panel's provider/model fields do not auto-populate from the API on mount
  until "Refresh" is clicked, and `.value` reactivity requires the native
  `HTMLInputElement.prototype.value` setter. API returns correct values; this
  is a separate Settings-form auto-population issue, not part of th

body:
Introduces special reserved foundries (`global` and `global_<mold-type>`) that are automatically merged into all Forge configurations. This allows users to define baseline macros, styles, and sparks across their entire dashboard without repetitive foundry references.

### Changes
* **Implicit Resolution**: Modified `_resolveFoundryConfig` to prepend `global` and `global_<mold-type>` (e.g., `global_card`) to the resolution chain for top-level Forge instances.
* **Merge Precedence**: Enforced the merge order: `global` -> `global_<mold-type>` -> explicit foundry (and its bases) -> local config.
* **Recursion Safety**: Extended the `visited` Set propagation to ensure implicit global resolutions properly track visited nodes and prevent circular dependencies.
* **Documentation & Testing**: Added the `global_foundry.yaml` visual test scenario and updated `docs/source/forge/foundries.md` to detail the new merge behavior.

### Example

Defining a `global` foundry automatically applies its configuration to all Forge elements:

```yaml
# In UI Foundries or uix_foundries.yaml:
global:
  forge:
    macros:
      theme_color: "'rgb(0, 100, 200)'"

# Any Forge instance will now inherit `theme_color` without an explicit `foundry:` key:
type: custom:uix-forge
forge:
  mold: card
element:
  type: tile
  entity: light.kitchen
  uix:
    style: |
      ha-card { background-color: {{ theme_color }}; }
```

## Problème (P1 — découvert en QA live le 2026-07-04)

Le tunnel matching (étape date, [apps/web/app/matching/date/page.tsx](../blob/main/apps/web/app/matching/date/page.tsx)) garde la position **uniquement en localStorage/URL**. Or `POST /matching/search` ne propose que les candidats dont le **profil** a `lat`/`lng` en base (`WHERE rp.lat IS NOT NULL…`).

**Conséquence : deux nouveaux riders qui suivent le tunnel normal ne se trouvent jamais** (reproduit sur blobsurf.com avec 2 comptes neufs compatibles à 13 km — 0 résultat des deux côtés ; après persistance manuelle de la position via PUT /profile/me, le match fonctionne immédiatement de bout en bout).

## Fix

Au succès de la géolocalisation, on persiste la position au profil via `apiClient.updateProfile({ lat, lng })` — même mécanisme que l'ancienne étape `matching/location` (page abandonnée par le tunnel actuel).

## Privacy

Aucun changement d'exposition : la recherche ne renvoie aux autres riders que la distance arrondie en km, jamais lat/lng (invariant Gate B conservé).

- `jest app/matching/date` : 5/5 (dont nouveau test : persistance appelée au succès géoloc)

## 這一刀做了什麼（主軸切片 808·玩家親手玩）

主軸至 807 全打勾。換維度避開剛連發兩拍的「居民內心/記憶」軸（做夢 805、說夢 807），回到 PLAN_ETHERVOX「維護者也想享受這世界」這條**玩家親手玩**的療癒線。

**真缺口**：莓果叢 806 給了世界第一種多年生作物，玩家可蓋起莓園走過去摘一把——但採來的**莓果(77)至今唯一用途只是送禮**，沒有任何下游加工。本刀補上：**莓果放進熔爐小火慢熬 → 一罐莓果醬(78)**，乙太方界第一種「甜點」熟食，把莓園接進既有「採集→熔爐烹製→自己享用(779)/餽贈(660)」的循環。

**與既有熟食的區隔**：麵包/烤魚/烤地薯/暖湯全是「正餐」（填肚子）；莓果醬刻意是**甜點**（酸甜、小確幸），故享用暖句與居民道謝台詞都**另立甜味專屬版**，是情緒上真正新的一味、不是「又一道菜」。走熔爐煨煮（比照烤魚單食材下爐的慣例）。

屋後莓園結果了，摘滿手莓果回熔爐前放進去，爐火幽幽烤著，一會兒「莓果醬 ×1」出爐。舀一口自己熬的醬，酸甜在舌尖化開；剩下拿去送露娜，她眼睛一亮：「哇……甜甜的莓果醬！我從沒嚐過這麼甜的東西，謝謝你！」🫐🍯💛

- `web/voxel/main.js`：`JAM` 常數/顏色/名/熔爐配方/`EDIBLE_DISHES`

## 濫用防護
不觸發 LLM／不收玩家自由文字／不開對外端點／不動帳號權限——配方合成由**伺服器查背包權威判定**（材料真足才熬得成）、熔爐走既有持久化管線；台詞全固定模板、只嵌玩家顯示名與料理名，**永不回放記憶原文或玩家原話**（無注入/NSFW 面）；療癒沙盒無限資源、莓果醬只是額外一味甜點、無經濟破壞面。

零 LLM、零 migration（走既有背包/熔爐 append-only 持久化，格式不變）、零協議破壞（管線既有、前端配方欄位 additive）、零新美術、FPS 零影響。

author: derekadams
body:
## The single Dependabot fix on a live runtime path

Per the security triage (108 raw alerts → 35 unique), **exactly one** advisory is both high-severity and on a reachable, shipped-code path: **`github.com/jackc/pgx/v4`**, the Postgres driver behind `core/rdb` — the query path every service uses.

`4.16.1 → 4.18.3` clears **two HIGH SQL-injection** advisories (protocol message-size overflow + line-comment creation) and pulls `jackc/pgproto3/v2 2.3.0 → 2.3.3`, clearing its SQL-injection HIGH.

## Why this is a dedicated PR (not grouped #188)
Dependabot bundled the pgx bump into grouped PR **#188**, but that group also bumps `graph-gophers/graphql-go 1.4.0 → 1.10.2`, which **adds a `sync.Mutex` to `Schema`** and trips `go vet`'s copylocks check in `NewGraphQLManager` across **all 7 GraphQL services** — so #188 fails the vet gate. This PR isolates the security fix; the graphql-go bump needs a separate code fix (pass `*Schema`) and should be handled deliberately.

## Minimal + effective
In-line patch within v4 — no v5 migration, no API break. **Only `backend/core/go.mod` is bumped**: under the Go workspace (`go.work`), MVS selects 4.18.3 for every module, so the fix is platform-wide without churning the services' indirect pins (avoiding the multi-module tidy landmine).

**Verified locally:** `go build` / `go vet` / `go test` green across all 11 workspace modules (incl. `core/rdb` and the services). CI runs the same per-module under the workspace.

author: dbtlr
body:
## MMR-153 — Node write path over Norn

Implements the Norn-backed `Store.transact` + `StoreWriter` (Mimir-on-Norn Phase 3, initiative MMR-126, ADR 0016). Every write verb over the Norn backend accumulates its effects, coalesces them per document, and applies **one atomic `vault.apply_plan` MigrationPlan** — `create_document` / `set_frontmatter` / `append_to_section` — retried on drift. Entirely behind the **unselected** backend: SQLite remains the sole active store; the Norn write path is exercised only by the conformance/parity harness until the Phase 4 cutover.

### What's here
- **`norn/plan.ts`** — `MigrationPlan`/`MigrationOp` types + op builders; **`NornClient.applyPlan`** (the client previously wrapped only 8 of ~14 MCP tools).
- **`core/history-codec.ts`** — the shared `### <ISO> — <kind>` `## History` record codec (render + parse), also used by the MMR-154 read surfaces.
- **`norn/writer.ts`** — the accumulating `StoreWriter`: transact-start snapshot + in-flight overlay for read-after-write, per-document coalescing, H3 `{{seq}}` allocation via `create_document`, per-field `expected_old_value` CAS, bounded drift-retry.
- **`vault/schema.ts`** — additive node-create incremental-path rule.
- **`core/parity.integration.test.ts`** — write-verb parity: each verb run on both SQLite and Norn from one seeded state, read surfaces compared (real `norn 0.42`).

### Design notes
- **Write mechanism proven empirically** against norn 0.42 (source + live probe): a plan carries frontmatter + section ops together, applied atomically per document.
- **Concurrency accepted at single-writer scale.** `apply_plan` writes frontmatter file-by-file, so a multi-document plan is *not* atomic across documents, and Mimir sends an empty `document_hash` (per-field `expected_old_value` is the live drift signal). Accepted for Mimir's personal scale — the only concurrency is agents on different tasks = different documents. True whole-plan atomicity is filed as Norn ask **H4**.

### Adversarial review (max tier)

`engine=code-review tier=max findings=12 fixed=8 dismissed=2 deferred=2(MMR-157,MMR-158)`

| # | Finding | Verdict | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unresolved create seq leaks negative sentinel → `MMR--1` | CONFIRMED | Fixed — throw on unparseable summary (regression test) |
| 2 | Created node returns negative `id` | CONFIRMED | Fixed — post-apply reload returns the real node (`id > 0`) |
| 3 | Description edit leaves `## Task Description` body stale | CONFIRMED | Fixed — emit `replace_section` (integration test) |
| 4 | Reason escape not injective (`\## …`) | CONFIRMED | Fixed — injective escape (round-trip test) |
| 5 | Empty-string reason → null | CONFIRMED | Fixed — normalize `''`→null |
| 6 | Unreachable retry-exhaustion throw | CONFIRMED | Fixed — exhaustion throws after MAX_ATTEMPTS |
| 7 | Duplicated `## History` literal | CONFIRMED | Fixed — use `renderHistoryBody()` |
| 10 | `appendTransition` silently drops same-transact transition | PLAUSIBLE | Fixed — fail-loud like `stemOf` |
| 11 | Drift detection = substring match on norn error prose | PLAUSIBLE | Dismissed — norn surfaces CAS refusals only as untyped text; string-match is the sole signal (real fix = norn typed-error) |
| 12 | Present-`null` field → CAS never matches | PLAUSIBLE | Dismissed — the frontmatter mapper omits absent fields, never writes explicit `null` |
| 8 | Non-idempotent create replay on partial multi-doc apply | PLAUSIBLE | Deferred → MMR-157 (latent; rides the H4 atomicity gap) |
| 9 | Echo path reads throwing `store.db` trap | PLAUSIBLE | Deferred → MMR-158 (Norn store not wired active yet; pairs with MMR-154) |

All 8 fixes have a regression test observed red→green.

### Scope boundaries (tracked, not dropped)
- `annotate` write (`## Annotations`) → **MMR-154** (body-section concern).
- Making the Norn node backend CLI-selectable / default → **Phase 4** (MMR-131); depends on MMR-158.

### Verification
`bun run verify` green: format (322 files), lint/type (0 warnings), **737 + 150 tests** pass, including the norn-gated write-verb parity suite against `norn 0.42`.

author: omar-zarka
body:
## What

Raise the `@gorhom/bottom-sheet` floor from `^5.2.8` → `^5.2.14` (plus the matching single lockfile entry).

## Why

On the **Expo SDK 56 stack** (`react-native-reanimated` 4.3.1 / RN 0.85, new architecture — i.e. **`develop` since #294**), gorhom **5.2.8**'s imperative `BottomSheet.expand()` / `snapToIndex()` become **silent no-ops** — the ref is valid and exposes the methods, the calls run with **no error**, but the sheet's open animation never fires. Not z-order, not the snap-point type, not `FullWindowOverlay`; the gorhom open animation itself is dead on 5.2.8 under reanimated 4.3. **≥5.2.14 fixes it.**

I hit this in a downstream SDK 56 migration: it broke the mini-player → full-player expand (the tap *was* firing — play/pause on the same control worked — the sheet just never presented) and cost a build plus a few hours to bisect. The bisection that isolated it: force-call `expand()` from a temp effect over Metro and flip only the gorhom version.

## Scope / risk

- **Correction to my original framing:** `develop` has been on SDK 56 / reanimated 4.3.1 since #294 merged (2026-06-29), so this is an **active fix, not forward-looking** — any imperative `expand()`/`snapToIndex()` on `develop` today silently dies on 5.2.8. (I first opened this reading `main`, which is still SDK 55, and wrongly assumed `develop` matched.)
- Pure JS, **within the existing `^5.2.8` caret** — no native rebuild.
- 5.2.14 has **identical `dependencies` + `peerDependencies`** as 5.2.8 (`@gorhom/portal` 1.0.14, `invariant` ^2.2.4), so the lockfile delta is just this one package's `version`/`resolved`/`integrity`.

body:
## What

Two-part hardening pass ahead of new users onboarding:

- **Install→first-verify fixes from clean-environment cold runs**: verify/pair say so once when no `.vine/` exists (instead of citing rules in a missing file); verify gitignores `.vine.local/` before the first PROFILE.md write; init's scaffolding reaches git history (`.gitkeep`, commit reminder, verify sweeps it); domain+slug batched into one prompt; commits announced with their branch; README restructured around a Quick Start ("start with verify — the rest finds you"); new one-pager [docs/precedence.md](docs/precedence.md); update command corrected to the verified syntax (`claude plugin update vine@moduloMoments`).
- **Over-spec audit applied in full**: the framework machinery init used to copy into every consuming repo's shared.md (~140 lines) now ships with the plugin as `plugins/vine/PROTOCOL.md`, loaded by every phase before the repo overlays. Init generates a slim (~45-line) repo-specific shared.md from extracted template files, its migrations step is gated by a trigger table (fresh runs skip it), and all 11 skills are tightened (~430 lines cut). Trellis Checks 12/13 follow the machinery; this repo's own overlays, CLAUDE.md, and docs are migrated.

## Why

Coworkers are about to try VINE, and repeated dry runs of the real onboarding path surfaced genuine failures: the documented update command didn't resolve, personal state sat one `git add -A` from a commit, and every fresh init paid ~230 lines of no-op migration reading. The machinery move also kills a structural risk — generated shared.md files version-skewing against the plugin as it evolves — and makes the personal-root/worktree rule available even in repos that never ran init.

Closes #104 — resolved by structural elimination: the machinery sections no longer live in shared.md or init's template at all, so there is no duplication left to drift. Trellis Check 13's shipped-surface scan now covers PROTOCOL.md (Check 12 guards the personal-root rule, #132).

## How to test

1. `sh .vine/scripts/trellis-check.sh` — 11/11 skills green, all repo-level guards pass.
2. Install the plugin from this branch in a scratch repo; run `/vine:init` then `/vine:verify <feature>` — expect a slim shared.md, no migration-section reading on a fresh repo, and verify loading `PROTOCOL.md` before the overlays.
3. Run `/vine:verify` in a repo with **no** `.vine/` — expect the one-line init nudge and a `.gitignore` created before PROFILE.md is written.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this in an actual VINE cycle (if changing command behavior) — four end-to-end cold simulations (init→verify chain, no-init verify ×2, plus fix re-validation) on fresh sample repos; live colon-form invocation remains auth-blocked for automation (#137)
- [x] Changes are focused on a single concern
- [x] Any new behavior is documented in the README or command file

body: Fix a race where direct workspace URLs could fail to become the remembered workspace before a later visit to `/`. The workspace layout previously persisted `shipfox.lastWorkspaceId` only after auth and query context were ready. In the E2E flow, a direct visit to workspace B could be followed by `/` while storage still pointed at the first workspace, so the root redirect sent the user back to workspace A. This moves the URL workspace persistence ahead of the auth-loading short circuit and makes the E2E assert that local storage has caught up before validating the `/` redirect behavior. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a race where the last workspace wasn’t saved early enough, causing “/” to redirect to the wrong workspace after a direct visit. We now persist the workspace ID as soon as the workspace route loads and make the E2E wait for storage before checking redirects. - **Bug Fixes** - Persist `shipfox.lastWorkspaceId` at the start of the workspace route `beforeLoad`, before auth/loading checks. - Keep `localStorage` write in a try/catch to handle private/quota cases without breaking routing. - E2E: add `readMaybeLastWorkspaceId` and use `expect.poll` to wait for storage to match the visited workspace before reload and “/” navigation. author: srobroek
body:
## What

Sets up **release-please** (manifest mode) plus a **release verification gate** for cutting versioned desktop-app releases. Config + workflows only — no tags or releases are created here.

## Files

- `release-please-config.json` — manifest-mode config, single root package.
- `.release-please-manifest.json` — version state (bootstrap `0.0.0`).
- `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` — maintains the release PR / tags on **push to main**.
- `.github/workflows/release-gate.yml` — single-verdict release gate.

## Design decisions

**Release type = `simple`, single root package.** The crates workspace has **no** `[workspace.package].version`; every crate independently declares `0.1.0` and none are published (crates.io/npm). The user-facing artifact is the **desktop app**, so there is exactly one meaningful version. Per-crate release-please components were rejected: they are internal, unpublished, and would produce meaningless per-crate tags/changelogs. `release-type: rust` was rejected because there is no single workspace version field for it to bump.

**Version-sync mechanism (three files, one version).** `extra-files` bumps all three app-facing version fields together on each release:
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` `$.version` — the version users see (Tauri).
- `apps/desktop/package.json` `$.version` — frontend package.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` `$.package.version` — the `desktop_shell` app-binary crate. (This *is* the "workspace Cargo.toml version" in practice; the workspace root has no version field — the app crate stands in for it.)

The ~30 internal crates stay at `0.1.0` untouched — unpublished, so their versions are irrelevant. Using `simple` + JSON `extra-files` (rather than release-type `node`) deliberately avoids treating `package.json` as a publishable npm package.

**Tag convention = plain `v{version}`** via `include-component-in-tag: false`. This follows the project lesson that APM/tag tooling resolves only plain `v{version}` tags; a single-package repo needs no component prefix. (agentic-packages uses `include-component-in-tag: true` **because** it is a multi-package APM monorepo needing per-component tags — not applicable here.)

**Changelog sections.** `feat`→Features, `fix`→Bug Fixes, `perf`→Performance, `refactor`→Refactors visible; `docs`/`chore`/`test`/`ci`/`build`/`style` hidden. Conventional commits are already enforced (squash-merge titles).

**Bootstrap = `v0.1.0` as the first tagged release.** Signals: everything in-repo is already `0.1.0` but **nothing has ever been released or tagged** (`git tag -l` shows only `backup/*`). So `0.1.0` is not yet released and should be the first tag. Mechanism: manifest seeded at `0.0.0` + `bump-minor-pre-major: true`, so the first accumulated `feat` bumps `0.0.0 → 0.1.0` (and pre-1.0 breaking changes bump minor, not to 1.0.0). `bootstrap-sha` is pinned to the redesign tip (`4d9c4d33…`, which enters `main`'s history via #349) so the first changelog contains only commits after that point instead of scanning all history.

## Release gate (`release-gate.yml`)

Runs on release-please PRs (`head_ref` `release-please--*`), pushed `v*` tags, and manual dispatch. Each check is **soft-failing** (`continue-on-error`) and records a row into the run summary; the final **`verdict`** step is the single required check. Per-check policy is configurable via the workflow `env` block:

| Check | Start policy |
| --- | --- |
| version-sync (4 fields agree) | **hard** |
| release build, dev-tools OFF (`cargo build --workspace --release`) | **hard** |
| dev-tools-off invariant (feature not default; not in release feature graph) | **hard** |
| full test suite (`cargo test --workspace`) | soft (warn) |
| changelog updated on the release PR | soft (warn) |

**Repo-specific invariant covered:** the `dev-tools` feature must be absent from release binaries (Constitution Principle V) — the gate asserts no `default` feature enables it and that the app crate's release feature graph does not resolve it.

**How the shepherd/user reads it:** look at the **`Release Gate / verdict`** check. Green = safe to merge (any soft warnings are shown in the summary table, not lost). Red = a **hard** invariant failed; the summary table names which. Because soft checks never block, a release can still be cut with warnings visible. To change what blocks, flip a `POLICY_*` value (e.g. set `POLICY_TESTS: hard`).

Gating pattern adopted from **srobroek/bellwether** (`publish-image.yml`): "the suite must be green before we publish", expressed here as a `needs:`-free single-job aggregation so one verdict check governs mergeability. Rejected bellwether's per-OS/full-matrix duplication — the cross-OS build/test matrix is already covered by `ci.yml`; the gate runs ubuntu-only and focuses on release-specific invariants.

## Operational notes

- **Runs on `main` only** — releases are cut from `main`, never from this redesign integration branch. The **first release PR appears only after this config lands on `main`** (via #349) and a subsequent `feat`/`fix` is pushed.
- **No conflict with the in-flight `ci-path-aware` PR** ("skip heavy jobs for docs-only changes"): that PR touches `ci.yml`; this PR adds two **new** workflow files and does **not** touch `ci.yml`. No coordination needed.
- Do **not** merge — the CI shepherd merges after gates are green.

body:
Closes #118.

Adds parse support for the last of Table 1's small, self-contained tags. (`<m>` — mnemonic — was already supported ✅.)

## What each tag does

| Tag | Behaviour |
|-----|-----------|
| **`<varsub var=NAME>`** | Inside `<msg>` text, emits an ISPF `&NAME.` reference resolved at display time by `MessageCatalog.format` — exactly like a literal `&NAME`. |
| **`<t>`** | Inside a `<cmd>` external name, marks the truncation point: characters before it become the command's minimum abbreviation. `<cmd>CANC<t>EL` → `trunc=4`. Wins over a `TRUNC=` attribute; a `<cmd>` with no `<t>` is unchanged. |
| **`<rp>`** | Reference phrase (a hypertext link to another help panel): inline emphasis like `<hp>` — one `Text.rich` whose phrase run is underlined by default. |
| **`<pdsep>`** | A divider row between an action-bar pull-down's `<pdc>` choices. |

## Notes

- **`<rp>` is mono byte-identical.** Like `<hp>`, the underline is colour-only, so the mono data stream matches the plain concatenated line byte-for-byte — safe to drop into any panel.
- **`<pdsep>` fixes a latent crash.** `_show_pulldown` in `server.py` indexed `p['label']` on every entry; a separator has no label. It now renders separators as a non-selectable rule and keeps the choice numbering continuous across them.
- **`<t>` keeps the stored command dict clean.** The `<cmd>` text is captured only to locate `<t>`; `Screen.commands[NAME]` still holds just `{action, trunc}`.
- This is the tag set the guide's `ex127.dtl` uses (`<PDSEP>`); it now records the separator between "Update Entry" and "Exit".

## Verification

- 8 new tests in `test_dtl.py` (including driving `_show_pulldown` with a fake socket to prove the separator renders and the numbering stays continuous).
- Full suite: **615 passed** (was 608). Corpus render baseline unchanged (these tags add metadata / inline emphasis; they don't move the renderable count).

author: manursutil
body:
## Problem

Plan 010 workstream B. Cleanup could only ever dry-run: it printed the keep/delete retention plan but never freed anything, so old frontend artifacts kept accumulating in S3.

## Change

Implement destructive cleanup behind an explicit opt-in flag; **default stays dry-run**.

- `FrontendArtifactStore` gains `delete(storageKey)`; both adapters implement it — S3 `DeleteObjectCommand` (aws) and filesystem `rm` (sim), both idempotent.
- `src/core/cleanup.ts` adds the narrow `ArtifactDeleter` seam, `executeArtifactRetention(deleter, plan)` (deletes **only** the plan's `delete` set — never the `keep` set or current version), and `formatCleanupExecution(...)`.
- CLI: `cleanup releases|artifacts --env <e> [--dry-run|--execute]`. Default dry-run; `--execute` deletes; passing both is rejected. `artifacts --execute` deletes pruned frontend artifacts through the shared store seam (S3 in aws, filesystem in sim).
- `releases --execute` is **refused up front** (before any history reads): backend release deletion must go through the same AWS/SSM boundary as deploy, and that mechanism is not yet confirmed. Dry-run remains available for backend.

## Safety

- Deletion is never the default; requires explicit `--execute`.
- Only the plan's `delete` set is removed; current + `keep` are untouched.
- Artifact storage keys embed `env` + `tenant` (`<prefix>/<commit>/<env>/<tenant>-<fingerprint>.tar.gz`), so a staging cleanup can never delete a production- or other-tenant-current artifact from the shared bucket.
- No SSH / no direct server file reads — backend release deletion is deferred rather than faked (respects the plan STOP condition).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm test` — 208/208 (+8 new).
- New tests: `executeArtifactRetention` delete-set-only + empty-set, `formatCleanupExecution`, adapter `delete` idempotency (S3 fake client + filesystem), CLI sim `--execute` (deletes only the pruned artifact, keeps current), and the two refusal guards.
- Self-review (`/code-review` high): no correctness findings survived; the one efficiency item (refuse `releases --execute` before history reads) is applied.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

Backend release deletion (`cleanup releases --execute`) — needs the confirmed SSM cleanup mechanism + on-disk release layout under `backendDeploy.releaseRoot`. Remaining plan-010 workstreams: D (pipeline + IAM), C (staging verification), E (packaging).

| 2 | `docker-compose.yml` | `PORT: 80` (port privilégié) incompatible avec l'utilisateur non-root | `PORT: 3000`, mapping `3000:3000` |
| 3 | `controllers/tenantController.js` | `createTenant` : double `conn.release()` + transaction jamais annulée sur slug dupliqué (corruption possible du pool) | `rollback()` puis libération unique dans le `finally` |
| 4 | `controllers/taskController.js` | Clé du cache de stats incluant `tenant_<id>_` en lecture mais pas à l'invalidation → stats **périmées** en contexte organisation | Helper unique `statsCacheKey()` partagé lecture/invalidation |
| 5 | `controllers/taskController.js` | `importTasks` n'écrivait pas `tenant_id` → tâches importées **invisibles** en contexte organisation | Ajout de `tenant_id` à l'`INSERT` |
| 6 | `controllers/taskController.js` | `getReminders` incluait les tâches archivées | Ajout de `is_archived = false` + parenthésage explicite |
| 7 | racine | Répertoire parasite `{config,routes,...` (mkdir avec accolades non expansées) | Supprimé |

## Nettoyage du code mort

Suppression de 16 fichiers inertes jamais chargés (vérifié : aucun `require` de l'app ne les cible) :

- **Restes de l'ancienne implémentation PHP** : `app/Core/*.php`, `app/Middleware/*.php`, `config/db.php`, `router.php`, `.htaccess`.
- **Modules JS orphelins** référençant des dépendances absentes de `package.json` : `config/pgDb.js` (`pg`), `utils/logger.js` (`winston`), `utils/schemas.js` (`joi`), `middleware/requestLogger.js`, `middleware/joiValidator.js`, `utils/cache.js` (`redis`).
- Dépendance `redis` retirée de `package.json` (seul consommateur : `cache.js`).

Le projet est désormais **100 % Node** et cohérent.

- `server.js` se charge sans erreur après chaque étape (boot test Node).
- Fichiers modifiés vérifiés via `node --check`.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
## OMN-13902 — sibling version-alignment automation (canary: omnimemory)

Closes the recurring stale-sibling-lock drift class. Detection existed
(sibling-pin guard, orphan-pin gate) but alignment was manual, so drift
recurred and blocked work — OMN-13156 / OMN-13402 / OMN-13814 were all
one-off repin tickets, and the 2026-07-03 R3 stability refresh was blocked
by a stale core pin.

### What this adds
`.github/workflows/sibling-lock-refresh.yml` — a Dependabot-shaped, per-repo
scheduled workflow (the approach the ticket explicitly sanctions). Daily (and
on `workflow_dispatch`) it runs `uv lock --upgrade-package` for each omninode
sibling and opens a bot PR (`chore(deps): …`) when `uv.lock` changes.

### Provenance-gate safety (no decision required)
Git/tag-pinned siblings in `[tool.uv.sources]` (here `omnibase-infra` per
OMN-13878) are **left untouched** — `uv lock --upgrade-package` cannot move an
immutable rev/tag. So only PyPI-range-pinned siblings move; the Dep-Provenance
state is preserved automatically with zero per-repo tuning. That's why the
default package list can safely include the git-pinned siblings.

### Proof the mechanism works (local run in this worktree)
```
$ uv lock --upgrade-package omnibase-core --upgrade-package omnibase-spi --upgrade-package omnibase-compat
Resolved 159 packages in 738ms
Updated omnibase-core v0.46.4 -> v0.46.5
Updated omnibase-spi   v0.23.0 -> v0.23.1
# omnibase-infra (git-pinned) untouched; exit 0; valid lock
```
This is exactly the stale-lock drift the ticket cites, auto-resolved.

### Canary → fan-out
Landed on omnimemory first per canary-before-fan-out. Once green, copy the same
workflow to the other PyPI-range consumers: **omniclaude, omniintelligence,
omnibase_infra**. Git-override-only repos (omnimarket, onex_change_control)
gain nothing until they move siblings back to PyPI pins (tracked by OMN-13878).

### Scope note
This is a docs/CI-only change (no runtime contract) → no OCC companion required.
Bot PRs opened by the workflow use `secrets.CROSS_REPO_PAT` so they trigger CI,
mirroring the existing `publish-downstream-pin-bump` bot.

DoD: next in-range sibling release produces an auto-opened repin PR with no
manual ticket. Release-trigger proof is deferrable to the next release cycle;
`workflow_dispatch` allows an immediate manual proof-run post-merge.

Ref: OMN-13902

Uma opção **Set de referência** no Planejar set: em vez de varrer a biblioteca toda, o planejador usa **só as músicas de um set escolhido** como base, e aplica o mesmo arco/pontuação/ordenação — dá pra refinar um set bom em sets menores e mais afiados.

E o **extra** que você pediu: com um set de referência ativo, os estilos marcados no "Estilos" **escapam** — aquelas pastas entram *também* da biblioteca toda, por cima do set. Ex.: sua playlist + todo o forró psicodélico do acervo.

## Como funciona
- `PlanConfig.reference_set_id` (vazio → nil).
- O Planner lê o pool de referência **antes de limpar** o set — então referenciar o próprio set num "Refazer" replaneja a partir das faixas dele mesmo.
- Em modo referência: passa `restrict_ids` (faixas do set) + `escape_styles` (estilos marcados) em vez do filtro de estilos; os **pesos** de tier ainda pontuam.
- `TrackQuery` restringe o pool com `id in restrict_ids OR genre_folder in escape_styles`.
- Quota de ouro, BPM, nota, menos-vozes, dedup, arco e ouro-nos-picos continuam valendo sobre o pool restrito.

TDD: pool restrito à referência; estilo marcado escapa pra biblioteca; auto-referência num replace replaneja das faixas pré-limpeza; parsing do config. 869 testes verdes, credo limpo.

body:
🚨 **Severity**: CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability**: Host Header Injection (Password Reset Poisoning risk)
🎯 **Impact**: Relying on untrusted request headers (`X-Forwarded-Host`) to construct base URLs allowed attackers to spoof the host. This meant dynamically generated absolute URLs, such as password reset links sent via email, could be poisoned to point to an attacker-controlled domain.
🔧 **Fix**: Modified `src/lib/public-url.ts`'s `getPublicBaseUrl` to prioritize the statically configured `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` environment variable when constructing absolute URLs, falling back to request properties only if absent.
✅ **Verification**: Tests passing, no regressions introduced. Added documentation of the vulnerability to `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: jpoley
body:
Reopened after addressing the Copilot finding from the prior PR (fallback kernel is now validated as a readable regular file). Same branch.

## Problem
`nanofuse image pull <any-normal-container>` failed — normal OCI images ship no kernel and the daemon lacked capabilities to reconstruct a container rootfs.

## Approach

author: tastybento
body:
## What

Adds an optional second argument to `admin team setowner` naming the island's current owner:

```
/[gamemode] admin team setowner <newOwner> [islandOwner]
```

## Why

Previously `admin team setowner` was `setOnlyPlayer(true)`, acted only on the island the executor was **standing on**, and required a **confirmation** prompt. That made it impossible to drive from the console — and therefore from automation such as Skript (e.g. a "capture the island by killing the owner" game mode).

## How it behaves

- **`setowner <newOwner>`** — unchanged. In-game admin, targets the island they're standing on, asks for confirmation.
- **`setowner <newOwner> <islandOwner>`** — new. Names the island by its current owner, so it's location-independent and **runs from the console**. Console execution **skips the confirmation** prompt (the console can't answer one).

The named form resolves the owner's **primary/active** island via `IslandsManager.getIsland(world, uuid)`. Behaviour left unchanged:
- **Concurrent-island cap** still applies — a recipient at their `island.number` limit is refused with `at-max`. Servers wanting capture-style transfers raise the limit.
- **Old owner** is still demoted to Member (not removed).

## Changes

- `AdminTeamSetownerCommand`: `setOnlyPlayer(false)`; two-arg island resolution by owner name; skip confirmation for non-player senders; tab-complete both name positions.
- `en-US.yml`: updated `parameters`/`description`; new `specify-island` message (shown if the console runs the one-arg form).
- `AdminTeamSetownerCommandTest`: added coverage for the console/two-arg paths (success, missing island arg, unknown island owner, owner-has-no-island); `testSetup` now asserts `isOnlyPlayer()` is false.

## Testing

`./gradlew test --tests "*.AdminTeamSetownerCommandTest"` — 12 tests, all passing.

body:
## Summary
- Deliver **FR-3.1/FR-3.2** (trmx-84): a tab owns a pure binary **layout tree** of one-or-more panes, split via **⌘D (Split Right)** and **⇧⌘D (Split Below)**. Each pane is an independent PTY session.
- The load-bearing constraint — **PTY sessions survive re-layout** ("move, don't recreate") — is met by rendering each leaf as an **absolutely-positioned, paneId-keyed sibling host** from `solveRects`: a split/close/resize mutates only geometry, never reparenting or remounting a terminal.
- `termixion-core` is **untouched** — the trmx-74 `SessionRegistry` (per-session open/close/resize, cwd honoring) is reused wholesale; a pane is exactly what a tab's single surface was. The only Rust change is thin-shell menu registration.

## What changed
- **`app/src/panes/layoutTree.ts`** (new) — pure tree + rect solver: `splitLeaf`, `removeLeaf` (sibling promotion), `setRatio`, `solveRects`, `canSplit` (min-size guard), `leaves`/`findLeaf`/`paneOrder` (the FR-3.5 seam). Exhaustive unit tests incl. property-based rect-tiling and a 16-leaf stress case.
- **`app/src/tabs/tabState.ts`** — a tab grows `tree` + `focusedPaneId` + `panes: Record<PaneId,PaneState>`; the trmx-75 title logic moves to **pane scope** (tab label + window title follow the focused pane; background panes isolated). New actions `splitPane`/`closePane`/`focusPane`/`setPaneRatio`; `paneBySessionId`.
- **`app/src/App.tsx`** — flat-rect pane rendering; all per-surface plumbing re-keyed tabId→**paneId**; per-pane cwd inheritance; **⌘W precedence pane → tab → window**; tab-strip × = whole-tab close (loops `close_pty`, no core bulk-close); click-to-focus (capture-phase, no `preventDefault` so xterm selection survives); the StrictMode per-pane orphan guard preserved.
- **`app/src/tabs/tabKeymap.ts`** — ⌘D/⇧⌘D → `split` actions (menu-less fallback; the native menu owns the accelerators in the packaged app).
- **`crates/termixion-tauri/src/menu.rs`** — Shell ▸ Split Right (⌘D) / Split Below (⇧⌘D) items + `menu_action` verbs (`split-right`/`split-below`); pure-map unit tests. No `main.rs` change (the existing `EmitTabsAction` path forwards any verb).
- **`index.css`** — `.pane-host` / `.pane-divider` (a plain 1px `--tx-border` line).

## Scope boundaries (kept)
Dividers render **static** (drag-resize = FR-3.3/trmx-85), focus is **click-only** (directional keyboard nav = FR-3.5/trmx-86), dividers are plain lines (active/focus chrome + dim = FR-3.6/trmx-87).

## Closes
Closes #84

## Test plan
- `pnpm --filter app test` — **940 passed**. New/updated: `layoutTree.test.ts`, pane-scoped `tabState.test.ts`, and 8 `App.test.tsx` pane tests incl. **survivor terminals never unmount across split/close** (the keep-alive proof), cwd-on-split inheritance, ⌘W pane→tab→window precedence, title-follows-focus + background isolation, and both the keymap and menu-verb split paths.
- `pnpm --filter app test:e2e` — **40 passed** incl. new `panes.spec.ts` (structural keep-alive: existing pane hosts stay attached across a re-layout).
- `cargo test --workspace` — all suites incl. `menu::tests::shell_split_items_broadcast_their_split_verbs` and the real-PTY `registry_close_reaps_only_its_own_child` / `registry_kill_all_leaves_no_zombies` that back "close one pane → sibling survives → no zombies".
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `pnpm --filter app lint`, `bash scripts/check-core-seam.sh` — all green.
- **Packaged / operator tier** (manual, not in this headless run): build a 2×2 grid, run `top` in a pane, split then close a sibling, resize the window — `top` never restarts and `ps` shows the same shell PIDs; no zombies after quit. The frontend + registry tests pin the invariant headlessly; this is the physical confirmation.

AI assistance was used to produce this change via the nine-step `/issue2pr` pipeline (Analyze → Plan → Execute), with **GPT-5.5 review and verified finding closure** at each phase (review-mode: full). Worker: Claude Opus 4.8.

The AI code review returned 5 findings (3 major + 2 minor); all closed in `3ed8883`:
- **correctness** — `solveRects` now caps the divider gap to the axis (`min(divider, rect.axis)`), so a rect narrower/shorter than the divider tiles instead of overflowing (added narrow/short/zero-bound tests).
- **correctness** — closing a focused pane mid-rename clears `renamingTabId`, so the rename input can no longer re-target the new focused pane on commit (added the pty:exited-mid-rename test).

body:
Hardening pass across the `http` and `service` layers, plus a small `sale_stock`/`sale_mrp` refactor. Seven focused commits, each with tests where there is a runtime surface.

## http
- **Reject invalid typed-route params** — `_coerce_scalar` now 400s on a container-for-str (was arriving as its `repr`), a fractional float for an int param (was silently truncated), and NaN/inf floats (poison comparisons, don't round-trip through JSON). Integral floats like `3.0` still coerce.
- **Confine static serving to `static/`** — `file_path` only guards the addons-tree boundary, so a `..` in the resource (`/web/static/../controllers/__init__.py`) escaped `static/` while staying in the addon, disclosing Python source. Re-assert containment (resolve-vs-resolve, matching the cold path's `safe_join`). Resolution is `lru_cache`d; only positive resolutions cache.
- **Reflect requested CORS headers on preflight** — echo `Access-Control-Request-Headers` verbatim instead of a hand-maintained allow-list that broke streaming clients until `Range` was added. Static list kept as the no-headers fallback.
- **ir.http protocol contract test** — `HttpExtension` was a hand-maintained comment with no type checker on this fork; `test_ir_http_contract` now asserts every hook exists on the real `ir.http` and binds positionally the way the http package calls it.
- **Cleanups** — drop dead `FilesystemSessionStore.list()` / `SessionStore.save_if_modified()` (both silently broken here); import `werkzeug.exceptions` (latent `NameError` behind `raise Forbidden`); clearer invalid-return `TypeError`; document `type='json2'`; give `MemorySessionStore.delete_from_identifiers` the `exclude_sid` param so `delete_old_sessions` stops `TypeError`ing.

## service
Single hardening commit covering:
- **Prefork** — swallow transient `os.fork()`/`Popen` `OSError` (EAGAIN/ENOMEM) so a resource spike can't kill the master; arm the fork-storm backoff on fatal signals (SIGSEGV/OOM-kill) not just non-zero exits; long-polling subprocess feeds the same throttle; `ODOO_GRACEFUL_STOP_TIMEOUT` override (floored 1s); FD_CLOEXEC on inherited listen sockets.
- **Env parsing** — reject non-finite floats; route `ODOO_REGISTRY_LRU_SIZE[_CRON]` and `ODOO_MAX_HTTP_THREADS` through guarded parsing instead of aborting startup.
- **db dumps** — SIGKILL a stalled SIGTERM-ignoring `pg_dump` from the stall timer; gate the timeout error on a non-zero returncode; close temp file before unlink on the restore decode path; `pg_restore --exit-on-error` so a partial restore isn't reported as success.
- **Transaction retry** — session re-fetch on every failure path, upload rewind only when a retry is certain.
- **model / lifecycle / cron** — `cls.__mro__` over `cls.mro()` per RPC; recurse `_force_lazy_in`; re-export `PG_CONCURRENCY_*`; skip `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` cap under free-threaded builds; fix preload-list LRU sizing; atomic `WorkerCron._connect_postgres`.

## sale
- **`_is_on_manufacturing_route()` hook** — `sale_stock` no longer references `reference_ids.production_ids` directly (that field only exists with `mrp`); `sale_mrp` overrides the hook and redeclares the compute's `@api.depends`.

Tests added under `test_http` and `tests/service`. Not yet run against a live DB in this branch.

author: nirziv
body:
BILLING_ISSUE and SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED were in REVOKE_EVENTS, so a failed renewal set isPremium=false immediately. Apple/Google attempt the renewal charge shortly before the paid period ends, so BILLING_ISSUE can fire while the user is still inside the period they paid for — revoking up to ~a day of paid access early. It also silently defeats a store billing grace period if one is ever enabled (the standard involuntary-churn reducer).

- Move BILLING_ISSUE + SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED to a new SOFT_EXPIRY_EVENTS bucket: keep isPremium=true and set premiumExpiresAt = event.expiration_at_ms, letting the caps predicate (services/capabilities.ts) govern live access. No grace → expiration is at/just-past period end (lapses on schedule); grace on → expiration is the grace end (access retained through it). Missing expiration → hard-revoke fallback (can't bound access safely).
- REVOKE_EVENTS is now ['EXPIRATION'] — terminal revoke only.
- Grant path: guard against a grant event without a numeric expiration_at_ms; skip the write instead of persisting a null (lifetime) premiumExpiresAt, which the predicate treats as permanent premium.
- Add 'revenuecat_billing_issue' to CapsInvalidatedReason.

author: 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv
body:
## Description

Library scans (especially of newly-added items) were slowed down by the server-side **tag cache**. `TagCacheMonitor` subscribes to `ILibraryManager.ItemAdded` / `ItemUpdated` / `ItemRemoved`, and Jellyfin raises those events **synchronously, one at a time, on the library-scan thread**. The old handler did heavy work inline for every event — `BuildEntryForItem` → `item.GetMediaSources()` plus DB queries — and for **every episode** it additionally re-resolved and rebuilt the parent **Series** and **Season** entries, each running an ordered "first episode" DB query. Adding a 300-episode series therefore rebuilt the series entry ~300 times on the scan thread, so the scan blocked on all of it.

This change decouples tag-cache maintenance from the scan thread.

## Measured impact (before/after)

Benchmarked on a Jellyfin 12 instance with a large TV library (945 series / ~104k episodes). Each metadata edit fires the exact same `ItemUpdated` event a library scan raises, on the same handler and calling thread, so it is a faithful, network-free probe. Identical operation on the same 200 items, warm cache, only the plugin DLL changed (baseline = this PR's merge base):

| Build | Median per-event cost on the calling thread | 200-event wall-clock |
|---|---|---|
| Before (synchronous handler) | **~1660 ms** | **380 s** |
| After (this PR, off-thread) | **~113 ms** | **70 s** |

~15× lower per-event cost. A control run repeated *after* the baseline run reproduced the "after" numbers exactly, ruling out drift. During a full scan that raises this event for every one of ~104k episodes, the old path blocked the scan thread on ~1.5 s of work per episode — this PR removes that from the scan thread entirely.

## Implementation Notes

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude/GPT). I have reviewed and tested all changes and understand the implementation.

- **`TagCachePendingChanges`** (new) — a coalescing set of pending changes (`ConcurrentDictionary<Guid, bool>`, `bool` = is-removal). `Record` is O(1) last-write-wins; `Drain` returns the batch and empties it. A burst of events for the same id collapses to a single unit of work, so the 300× series rebuild becomes ~1 per flush.
- **`TagCacheMonitor`** handlers now only record ids — no DB query, no media probe. For episodes they enqueue `ep.SeriesId`/`ep.SeasonId` (in-memory properties, no DB). This is what unblocks the scan thread.
- **`TagCacheService`** gains `EnqueueUpdate`/`EnqueueRemoval` (record + arm a debounced timer) and a background `FlushPending` worker (threadpool, non-reentrant via an `Interlocked` guard) that drains the batch off-thread, resolves each id, rebuilds/removes entries, and schedules one debounced disk save. Debounce is 3 s with a hard 30 s max-wait cap so a continuous scan still flushes periodically. Semantics are unchanged: the same items are cached with the same data — only the timing/threading differs (batched, off-thread, coalesced).
- **Shutdown durability** — `Dispose` takes ownership of the flush guard, then drains and applies any changes still queued in the debounce window before persisting, so a change made moments before a graceful restart isn't lost (matching the old inline-apply behavior). Runtime-verified: an edit made <3 s before a restart survives the restart.
- No new user- or admin-facing settings, and no client/UI changes; this is a server-internal performance fix.

## Guardrail against regressions (rule S1)

To keep this class of bug from coming back, the same "synchronous scan-thread event handlers must be record-and-defer" rule is now documented as **S1** in `docs/advanced/performance-rules.md` (+ a CONTRIBUTING checklist item) and **enforced by a test** — `LibraryScanEventGuardTests`:

- Fails the build when a new file subscribes to `ILibraryManager.ItemAdded/ItemUpdated/ItemRemoved` without being reviewed onto the record-and-defer allowlist.
- Fails when `TagCacheMonitor`'s handler regains an inline `GetItemById` / `GetMediaSources` / `GetItemList` / `GetFirstEpisode` call.

Auditing the existing subscribers for the allowlist surfaced two milder instances of the same pattern, fixed here so the allowlist is honest: `WatchlistMonitor` (a Seerr request lookup returns synchronously on a cache hit, so the per-user file writes ran on the scan thread) and `ContinueWatchingPlaybackEvents` (enumerated all users synchronously). Both now do only the cheap check on the event thread and defer the rest. The record-and-defer sites are tagged `// PERF(S1)`.

## Testing

- [x] Tested on Jellyfin 12 (`jellyfin-12`, 12.0.0) — deployed, plugin loads, monitor subscribes, cache loads.
- [x] Before/after benchmark (above): ~15× lower per-event cost on the calling thread, with an after-the-baseline control run to rule out drift.
- [x] Runtime: an `ItemUpdated` edit is applied to the cache ~3 s later (one debounce window) off-thread, with zero TagCache errors in the logs.
- [x] Runtime: pending change persists across a graceful restart inside the debounce window (Dispose durability).
- [x] `dotnet test` — 236 passing (13 new: coalescing + the debounce-cap math + batch-dispatch resilience).
- [x] Release build clean (`TreatWarningsAsErrors`, 0 warnings); client gates (typecheck / lint / client tests / syntax) green.
- [x] Committed Playwright e2e suite — 12/12 passing (admin + user), including both tag specs.
- [x] Multi-dimension review + adversarial verification and three `codex` passes; all confirmed findings fixed (Dispose durability, a busy-spin under a >30 s flush, flush-machinery test coverage, a dead `using`).

author: ssatama
body:
## Problem

The scraper cron was crashing on every run (Railway `thriving-appreciation` deployment showing **CRASHED**; Sentry `PYTHON-FASTAPI-2M`, 29 occurrences). Root cause was **not** a build or dependency issue (PRs #261/#262 were red herrings) — it was a Postgres sequence desync on the production DB.

`services/railway/sync.py` copies rows into `scrape_logs`, `organizations`, `service_regions`, and `animals` with **explicit ids**. Explicit-id inserts do not advance the pkey sequence, but only the `animals` sequence was reset afterward (`_reset_animals_sequence`).

On production, `scrape_logs_id_seq` sat at **1133** while `MAX(id)` was **1891**. Every cron `create_scrape_log` did `INSERT ... RETURNING id` via `nextval`, landing on an already-occupied id → `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "scrape_logs_pkey"`.

Failure chain:
1. `create_scrape_log` returns `None`
2. `base_scraper._setup_scrape` returns `False` → that org's scrape aborts before scraping
3. All 11 orgs abort → `railway_scraper_cron.py` hits `sys.exit(1)` → Railway marks the deployment CRASHED

Confirmed in the Railway deploy logs: 11/11 orgs failed on `scrape_logs_pkey`, no build failure.

## Fix

- Generalize `_reset_animals_sequence(conn)` → `_reset_sequence(conn, table)`
- Call it after **all four** table syncs, not just `animals`

## Production remediation (already applied)

The desynced sequences were reset manually on the Railway DB and verified aligned (`seq == MAX(id)`):

```sql
SELECT setval('scrape_logs_id_seq',     (SELECT MAX(id) FROM scrape_logs));
SELECT setval('organizations_id_seq',   (SELECT MAX(id) FROM organizations));
SELECT setval('service_regions_id_seq', (SELECT MAX(id) FROM service_regions));
```

This PR prevents recurrence on the next sync.

## Tests

- New `tests/services/railway/test_sync_sequences.py` (5 cases) covering the generalized helper for each synced table + error handling
- Railway service suite: 8 passed; ruff clean

## Notes

The legacy `_sync_*_to_railway_in_transaction` variants (not on the active `_independently` → `_with_mapping` path) were intentionally left unchanged to keep the diff surgical.

## Qué

Pulido de la barra de filtros del **DynamicTable** (feedback con screenshot de `ops.asteby.com/app/m/orders?f_status=eq%3Aready&view=list`).

### 1. Una sola afordancia de "limpiar"
Antes se veía **doble**: el botón `Limpiar filtros (n)` del toolbar **y** una fila de chips de filtros activos (`Estado: eq:reception ×  |  Limpiar todo`). Se elimina la fila de chips del DynamicTable. La señal de "filtro aplicado" ya la da el **embudo verde con conteo** de cada columna, y el toolbar conserva el único `Limpiar filtros (n)`.

> La fila de chips (`FilterChipsRow`) sigue intacta en el **DynamicKanban**, que sí la usa. No se toca el kanban ni los facets.

### 2. Hidratación desde URL con operador de igualdad
`?f_status=eq:ready` se hidrataba como texto crudo `eq:ready`, así que el embudo no marcaba la opción ni el popover mostraba la selección. Ahora el operador de igualdad por defecto (`eq:`) se desenvuelve al valor pelado (`ready`) — el mismo valor que las opciones de la columna matchean y que `buildFilterParams` reenvía sin prefijo. Embudo verde + opción marcada al reabrir.

### 3. Humanización de valores con prefijo de operador
`summarizeFilterValues` y `chipValueColor` ahora desenvuelven los operadores de igualdad (`eq:`/`EQ:`/`NEQ:`/`HAS:`, cualquier caso) y mapean el valor al label de la opción (`eq:reception` → "Recepción") en cualquier superficie que muestre el resumen (p. ej. chips del kanban, `valueSummary` del panel de filtros).

author: rolandwalker
body:
## Description

Add `--ssh-jump` CLI argument, restoring functionality removed in v2.0.0, under a different interface, and with a different internal implementation.

In the new interface, there is a single argument `--ssh-jump`, which accepts values in the form `user@host:port`.  Cleartext SSH passwords on the CLI are no longer accepted.  The user will be prompted for a password if the connection is not otherwise configured.

Deprecated arguments such as `--ssh-host` now refer to `--ssh-jump`.

Remote sockets are accepted.  The user should give the MySQL endpoint exactly as it would be accepted from the jump host.

A keyring field is added for the ssh-jump value, if any, but the field is not appended unless present, so existing keyring values are not invalidated.

The internals of the new implementation are completely different: instead of using complex Python libraries (paramiko/sshtunnel) we simply open a tunnel using the `ssh` executable in a thread.  This is more robust in a few ways: paramiko for example is not capable of reading nontrivial SSH config files.

A new `[ssh]` section is added to myclirc with some recommended CLI arguments to SSH when establishing tunnels.

Fixes #1960.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Adds V-trace targets (Espeholt et al. 2018, IMPALA, Algorithm 1) as an off-policy alternative to GAE for the rollout buffer, wired into the A2C trainer behind a config flag. V-trace corrects for the mismatch between the behavior policy that collected a trajectory and the current target policy, which is the prerequisite for sound learning on stale/replayed trajectories (unblocks the Phase 3 actor-learner step, #280).

## Changes

- **New `src/buffer/rollout/vtrace.rs`** (sibling to `gae.rs`):
  - `compute_vtrace_single_env` — inner per-env kernel (`pub(super)`), independent `rho_bar` / `c_bar` clipping, backward recursion with interior episode-boundary reset. Final-step bootstrap precedence matches `compute_gae_single_env`, making on-policy V-trace an exact drop-in for GAE(λ=1).
  - `compute_vtrace_advantages` — buffer-level entry point; behavior log-probs come from the buffer's stored `log_probs`, target log-probs are passed in `[num_steps][num_envs]`. Writes into `advantages`/`returns` so `get_batch()` works unchanged.
- **`src/buffer/rollout.rs`** — re-export `compute_vtrace_advantages` + convenience method on `RolloutBuffer`.
- **`src/train/a2c/config.rs`** — add `use_vtrace: bool`, `vtrace_rho_bar: f32`, `vtrace_c_bar: f32` (defaults `false` / `1.0` / `1.0`, zero behavior change); `validate()` rejects non-positive clip thresholds.
- **`examples/games/cartpole/train_cartpole_a2c.rs`** — capture behavior log-probs, build a `RolloutBuffer`, branch on `config.use_vtrace` between GAE and V-trace before the training step. Opt-in via `USE_VTRACE=1` (`VTRACE_RHO_BAR` / `VTRACE_C_BAR` overridable). Replaces the local flat GAE helper with the buffer's GAE path.
- **`scripts/vtrace_ref.py`** — numpy-free reference implementation generating the hand-checked test constants.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| `vtrace.rs` with inner + buffer-level fns, re-exported | ✅ | `compute_vtrace_single_env` + `compute_vtrace_advantages` exported from `buffer::rollout` |
| Independent rho/c clipping, observable in tests | ✅ | `clipped_rho_matches_reference`, `independent_rho_c_clipping_matches_reference` (rho_bar=0.5, c_bar=1.5) |
| `A2cConfig` gains 3 fields, defaults unchanged | ✅ | `test_default_config` asserts `use_vtrace=false`, clips `1.0` |
| Trainer/preprocessing calls `compute_vtrace_advantages` when enabled | ✅ | example branches on `config.use_vtrace` before building the batch |
| Unit tests: clipped rho, clipped c, on-policy n-step recovery, episode boundary | ✅ | 8 tests in `vtrace.rs` all pass |
| Learning-curve sanity check (regression) | ✅ | see Test Plan |
| `validate` rejects `vtrace_rho_bar<=0`, `vtrace_c_bar<=0` | ✅ | `test_config_validation` |

## Test Plan

**Unit tests** (`cargo test --features training --lib`): 8 V-trace tests + 3 A2C config tests pass; no regression in `buffer` (79), `train::a2c` (10), `train::ppo` (11). `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --lib --examples` clean.

**Numerical equivalence (rigorous regression):** On-policy V-trace (`target == behavior`, `rho_bar = c_bar = 1`) is proven equal to GAE(λ=1) to floating-point ULP (~1e-6), including mixed interior + terminal-last-step terminations, by `buffer_on_policy_matches_gae_lambda_one`, `on_policy_recovers_nstep_returns`, and `terminal_last_step_bootstraps_like_gae`. An instrumented run on real CartPole rollouts confirmed `max|vtrace_adv − gae_adv|` stayed at ~1e-6 across 1000 updates.

**Learning-curve sanity check** (CartPole A2C, 200k steps, `NdArray` CPU): V-trace runs learn to mean episode length **100.5** and **136.2** (random baseline ~22). GAE and V-trace show statistically indistinguishable outcomes — both reach ~100–165 when they converge and share the same run-to-run collapse rate. The occasional entropy-collapse abort is a **pre-existing** instability of the A2C example (GAE collapses at the same rate on unseeded runs) and is orthogonal to V-trace; on-policy V-trace is numerically identical to GAE, so it neither helps nor hurts, exactly the expected regression result.

Closes #263

author: ericxu-0805
body:
## What
E2E has burned its full 30-minute timeout on **every CI run since 6/25** (zero green runs). Two independent root causes, both landed that day:

1. **Onboarding modal intercepts every click.** The first-visit tour (#274/#276) is a full-viewport `z-[60]` dialog; every click-based test in a fresh browser context timed out at 30s (96 timeouts/run, serial, to the job cap). → `e2e/global-setup.ts` now pre-seeds `ONBOARDING_SEEN=1` via Playwright `storageState`.
2. **E2E traffic silently hit the production backend.** `next.config.js` rewrites are baked into `routes-manifest.json` at **build** time; the E2E build (872d482) had no `BACKEND_URL`, so all non-mocked `/api/*` calls proxied to the live Render backend while the local uvicorn sat unused — admin specs saw prod's 401 instead of the expected 503. → CI E2E build step now bakes `BACKEND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8100`.

## Also
- `maxFailures: 10` in CI — future systemic breakage reports red in minutes instead of hanging to the cap.
- `i18n.spec`: the Accept-Language test asserted pre-#272 behavior; first-visit-English-always is intentional (`i18n/server.ts`) — test now encodes that.
- `perf-budget.spec`: `response.body()` measures the decompressed payload; switched to `request().sizes().responseBodySize`. Real wire size: **289KB** (vs 984KB decompressed) against the 600KB budget.
- Removed the `frontend/node_modules` **symlink accidentally committed in #397**, and dropped the trailing slash from `node_modules/` ignore patterns so symlinks match too.

## Verification
Local CI-mode run (production server, proxy-neutralized): full chromium suite **96 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed in ~3m** (was: 30m hang). The two admin failures seen mid-investigation were local-env artifacts of root cause #2 (prod `ADMIN_TOKEN`) — gone once rewrites target the local uvicorn.
