author: sheepdontmoo
body: ## What this is The third app in the niche-finder lineup, per [`research/round-2-candidates.md`](research/round-2-candidates.md): **DocStash**, a one-time-purchase document scanner cloning CamScanner's paid tier (1M+ installs, one-time $1.99 unlock, **2.4★** after the parent app pivoted to subscriptions and left paying users charged-but-shown-"not purchased"). Built around Google ML Kit's free on-device Document Scanner API (`GmsDocumentScanner`) and Text Recognition API. Branched off `claude/play-store-app-analysis-0mbyru` (not the repo's registered default branch) since that's where all prior research and the other two apps actually live — this PR targets that branch so the diff is a clean addition alongside them. **Status: ready for the Play Console steps.** Signed release AAB verified building clean, reviewed by Bugbot (6 issues found and fixed), live-tested on an emulator (3 more real bugs found and fixed that a code review never would have caught), store listing copy + hi-res icon + feature graphic + a real screenshot all in the repo, and a concrete upload checklist for the remaining human-only steps (Play Console account, upload keystore, clicking through the listing form). ## Architecture note (per the task brief — flagging this explicitly) This app is **not** structured like the other two. OBD2 and golf each had a genuine pure-JVM "core" module wrapping the hard, novel logic (protocol parsing, geo math). A document scanner doesn't have an equivalent — the actual hard part (scanning, OCR) *is* Google's Android-only ML Kit, with nothing to extract into a testable JVM module. So [`scan-core/`](scan-core/) holds only what's genuinely ours and genuinely testable: hand-written searchable-PDF assembly, file naming, OCR-text search, and one-time-purchase entitlement logic. **46 tests, all passing.** ## What's built | Deliverable | Where | |---|---| | 1. App scaffold (Gradle/toolchain matching `android-app`) | [`android-scan/`](android-scan/) | | 2. ML Kit document scanning end-to-end | [`scanner/ScannerLauncher.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/scanner/ScannerLauncher.kt), [`ocr/OcrProcessor.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/ocr/OcrProcessor.kt) | | 3. Document library + search + export | [`ui/LibraryScreen.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/ui/LibraryScreen.kt), [`ui/DocumentScreen.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/ui/DocumentScreen.kt), [`data/DocumentStore.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/data/DocumentStore.kt) | | 4. App icon/branding | [`ui/theme/Theme.kt`](android-scan/app/src/main/kotlin/com/nichefinder/docstash/ui/theme/Theme.kt), [`store-assets/`](android-scan/store-assets/) (hi-res icon, feature graphic, screenshot) | | 5. Play Store listing draft | [`store-listing-docstash.md`](store-listing-docstash.md), [`docs/privacy-docstash.html`](docs/privacy-docstash.html), [`PLAY_STORE_CHECKLIST.md`](android-scan/PLAY_STORE_CHECKLIST.md) | Plus Play Billing wiring for the one-time `pro_unlock` product, and a backfilled root README (golf's row was apparently never added when that app shipped). ## Hard product rules — how each is enforced in code 1. **One-time price, no subscription, ever** — exactly one `INAPP` product, `pro_unlock`; no subscription product exists anywhere in the code. 2. **No forced account, no cloud upload** — `DocumentStore` is 100% local file I/O; the only network calls are ML Kit's Play services delivery and Play Billing itself. 3. **No watermarks, no page/upload limits, no ads** — `PdfAssembler` never stamps anything; `setPageLimit()` is deliberately never called; no ad SDK anywhere; free tier is fully functional — Pro only adds combined PDF export. 4. **Original branding** — name "DocStash", package `com.nichefinder.docstash`, hand-authored "ink on paper" icon/theme — nothing resembling CamScanner. ## Two review/testing passes, both found real bugs **A Bugbot review** (`git log`: "Fix 6 issues from a Bugbot review pass") found 2 high-severity issues — a delete-then-append file-naming collision that could silently overwrite a page's saved image, and a failed Play Billing query that could revoke a paying user's Pro status (the exact "charged but shows not purchased" bug this app exists to avoid) — plus 4 medium ones (manifest corruption handling, a concurrency race on the document manifest, an OCR crash on degenerate text boxes, a hidden-error-dialog bug). All fixed. **Live emulator testing** (installed the actual signed release APK, seeded it with sample documents, clicked through the UI) found 3 more issues no code review caught: - Two different Material3 color roles (`primaryContainer`/`secondaryContainer`, and separately `surfaceContainer*` — a newer M3 1.3.0+ mechanism I didn't know Card had switched to) were left unset and silently fell back to Material's baseline *purple* instead of the app's own palette. Only visible once there was real content on screen to look at. - `DocStashViewModel.init` read the manifest from disk synchronously on the main thread at every app launch. All fixed and re-verified. ## Build verification - `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `./gradlew lint`, `./gradlew assembleRelease`, and `./gradlew bundleRelease` all pass clean with a real (throwaway, sandbox-only) signing key — a genuine signed + minified (R8) release APK and AAB come out the other end, with ML Kit, Play Billing, kotlinx-serialization, and Compose all surviving R8 with zero issues. - Installed the release build on an unaccelerated (no `/dev/kvm` in this sandbox) emulator and confirmed it runs correctly. - `adb logcat` confirms ML Kit's Text Recognition client genuinely initializes and `BillingManager` genuinely reaches Google Play's billing service (correctly reporting "no account" / "API not supported" on a bare AVD — expected, not a bug). [DocStash Library screen, populated with sample documents](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-cdefe4e1-3c54-478e-b12b-85a90e22a971/artifacts?path=%2Fworkspace%2Fandroid-scan%2Fstore-assets%2Fscreenshot-1-library.png) **Still not verified** (needs a real device/emulator with a signed-in Google account): the actual scan capture flow through ML Kit's dynamically-delivered module, and a real Play Billing purchase. `PLAY_STORE_CHECKLIST.md` and `android-scan/README.md`'s manual verification checklist cover exactly this. One dependency note: `billing-ktx` is pinned to **8.0.0** rather than 9.1.0 — 9.x ships Kotlin metadata newer than this repo's Kotlin 2.0.21 can read. Documented in `android-scan/README.md`. ## What's left (all human-only, all covered in `PLAY_STORE_CHECKLIST.md`) Google Play Developer account + closed-testing requirement, generating a real upload keystore (never something this agent should generate on your behalf), clicking through the Play Console listing form, setting up the `pro_unlock` product, and grabbing 2–3 more real screenshots (trivial on a real/accelerated emulator — this sandbox's unaccelerated one made even one screenshot a fight, documented in the checklist). To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: vinayakkamboj
body:
## Summary
The previous fix traded one failure for another: cutting the big-pass token budget 16k → 10k kept passes inside the ~300s function limit, but on GLM the hidden reasoning tokens count against `max_tokens` — a complex prompt (the Minecraft build) burned most of the 10k on reasoning and emitted no `<file_patches>` block at all, twice, producing **"Astra couldn't produce a valid file patch for this request."**

This bounds passes by **time** instead of guessing a token number:

- **`generateTimeBoxed()`**: streams the model call and cuts it at a deadline (`ASTRA_PASS_TIME_BUDGET_MS`, default 200s — comfortably under the 300s function limit). Whatever arrived is kept; the truncation-tolerant parser salvages every complete file.
- **Token budget restored to 16k** for big builds (env-overridable) so reasoning never starves content again.
- **A time-sliced pass always chains a continuation pass**, with a dedicated continuation note when everything emitted so far is clean (that path previously produced an empty repair note).

Net: big passes can neither be killed by the platform mid-generate nor starved of content by their own reasoning — the two failure modes that took turns breaking big builds.

author: sethmorrowsoftware
body:
## Summary

A deep, adversarial audit of the entire project (dispatched as **9 parallel Opus 4.8 agents**, one per subsystem plus a cross-cutting failure-mode agent) found a cluster of correctness, reliability, and security defects — concentrated on the **safety-critical generator load-shed path** and on **crash/power-loss durability** (this app runs on generator power, so it *expects* power events). This PR fixes the CRITICAL/HIGH findings plus cheap high-value mediums. **Every behavioral change is backed by a standalone test** run during development.

The system's fundamentals were sound — the scheduler's active-period math, the automation edge detection, and the paho 2.x shim all verified correct. The fixes below harden the failure paths around them.

## Highest-impact fixes

**Durability (new `storage.py`)** — every JSON state file was written with a non-atomic `Path.write_text` (truncate-then-write). A crash mid-write could corrupt `tokens.json` (bricked auth → on-site re-OAuth) or `rotations.json` (lost an in-progress load-shed). All persistence now goes through an atomic writer (temp file + `fsync` + `os.replace`) with a `.bak` fallback on load.

**Rate limiter no longer freezes the whole system** — `acquire()` used to `time.sleep()` *while holding its lock*, so tripping the hourly cap could stall **every** API call — including a load-shed — for up to an hour. It now computes the wait under the lock and sleeps outside it.

**Load-shed can't silently half-apply or overload the generator:**
- Network/timeout errors are now wrapped as `HoneywellError` (they used to tear out of the per-zone loop, silently skipping the rest of the zones).
- The trigger's rising edge is latched **only after actions succeed**, so a failed shed retries instead of falsely logging success.
- Each rotation tick drives the **full** desired state, so drift or window re-entry can never energize more than `run_count` zones.
- `snapshot` is non-clobbering and `restore` clears on success, so a retained "on" replayed after a restart can't overwrite the good pre-outage snapshot and drive every zone permanently Off.
- On a restart mid-outage, the startup schedule assertion is **deferred while a rotation is active** (it used to re-energize all shed zones at once).

**MQTT reliability** — added the missing `on_disconnect` (the `connected` flag was stuck `True` forever, hiding the one outage the system calls critical), `clean_session=false` + QoS 1 + retained status so a "utility restored" message survives a reconnect, and an operator alert on broker drop.

**Scheduler** — a single malformed `time` in a hand-edited `schedules.json` used to crash startup into a permanent `systemd` crash-loop; bad rules are now skipped on load. Fixed the `SCHEDULE_TZ` bug where cron fired in the host timezone (not the configured one). Added a lock around the rules.

**Security** — OAuth `state`/CSRF validation, XSS-escaped `/auth/callback`, exact-match token-gate path, `X-Token` header instead of token-in-URL, setpoint clamping + mode validation, install.sh scoped ACLs (instead of world-widening ancestor home dirs) + systemd sandboxing, and a loud startup warning when bound to a non-loopback interface with no dashboard token.

## Changed files

| File | Area |
|------|------|
| `storage.py` *(new)* | atomic JSON persistence + `.bak` fallback |
| `honeywell_client.py` | rate-limiter lock, wrapped errors, single-flight refresh, atomic tokens |
| `automation.py` | edge-latch-on-success, full-drive rotation, non-clobber snapshot, atomic state |
| `app.py` | per-device write locks, poll health + reaping, startup-shed guard, CSRF/XSS, sole-control single-flight |
| `mqtt_bridge.py` | `on_disconnect`, `clean_session=false`, QoS 1, retained status, locked topics |
| `scheduler.py` | load-validation (no crash-loop), timezone fix, `_rules` lock, atomic save |
| `state_store.py` | numeric coercion, `isAlive` carry-forward, in-lock alerts, device reaping |
| `config.py` | fail-safe bool parsing, poll floor, placeholder-cred rejection |
| `static/index.html` | per-field dirty, non-2xx surfacing, header token, input validation, Run-now confirm |
| `install.sh` / `authorize.py` | scoped ACLs, PORT/HOST validation, sandboxing; loopback bind + escaped errors |
| `requirements.txt` | pinned major-version upper bounds (APScheduler <4, paho <3, …) |
| `README.md` | docs updated for the rotation, snapshot, and MQTT-reliability behavior changes |

## Verification

- All modules `py_compile`; full app imports and boots under `uvicorn` with the engine, scheduler, and poller starting cleanly.
- Live HTTP smoke test: token gate (401/200), schedule/automation validation (400 on bad input), OAuth `state` CSRF rejection, XSS escaping.
- Targeted unit tests for: atomic write + `.bak` recovery, rate-limiter lock behavior, 401 refresh-and-retry, `nextPeriodTime` handling, edge-latch-only-on-success + retry, non-clobber snapshot, full-drive rotation (never `> run_count` on), restart retained-replay safety, string-temperature poll survival, `isAlive` carry-forward, device reaping, scheduler load-validation + timezone.

## Notes / follow-ups for maintainer review

- The default `HOST=0.0.0.0` with an optional token is **unchanged** (it's the documented LAN model). Instead of altering the deployment model, startup now logs a loud warning when bound non-loopback with no token. Consider whether to fail-closed in a future change.
- Full write **arbitration/priority** (shed strictly outranks a schedule for its zones) is out of scope here; the per-device lock + local-cache coherence prevents lost updates, and the startup-shed guard covers the restart case.

Implements **Layer 5** of the roadmap (`AGENTS.md` §10: *Editor/TUI 統合 — TUI renderer (IR 対応)、Neovim plugin、GitHub preview 連携*).

Everything lives under a new **`editors/`** directory and touches **no existing `src/`**, so it lands conflict-free alongside the Layer 1–4 worktrees.

## What's included

### `editors/tui-ir/` — IR-driven TUI renderer (ratatui)
- Standalone crate (own `[workspace]`, decoupled from the root manifest) that renders the Generative-UI **IR** (§4) in the terminal — the *same* IR JSON the web (Preact) renderer consumes (§1.1).
- Interactive viewer **and** `--print` mode (pipe/CI friendly, no TTY).
- Honours the design invariants: drawable-subset rendering with a text + "open in web" fallback for graphical nodes (§5.2), reading-position **spoiler control** (§9.3 `Visibility::UntilRead`), and the **registry allowlist** (unknown `kind`s rejected by serde).
- `src/ir.rs` is a **provisional mirror** of `mdpeek-core::ir`; when Layer 3 lands, depend on that crate and delete it — the wire format is identical, so `render.rs` is unaffected.
- **9 tests** (each node kind, alignment, spoiler hide/reveal, unknown-kind rejection, a headless `TestBackend` paint), clippy clean.

### `editors/nvim/` — mdpeek.nvim plugin
- `:MdPeek` (live browser preview), `:MdPeekStop`, `:MdPeekTerm` (terminal render), `:MdPeekStatus`. Auto-stops the server on `VimLeavePre`.
- Shells out to the `mdpeek` binary (no re-implemented rendering).
- Verified end-to-end in **headless Neovim**: commands register on autoload, `start()` launched a real server, `status()` reported it running, and it auto-stopped on exit.

### `editors/github/` — GitHub preview 連携
- `render.sh` exports a PR's changed Markdown to static HTML + `index.html` (verified locally against the real binary, incl. `static/` asset copy).
- Composite `action.yml` + an example `workflows/md-preview.yml` that renders changed docs, uploads a `mdpeek-preview` artifact, and posts a sticky PR comment.

## Verification
- `cargo test` in `editors/tui-ir` → 9 passed; `cargo clippy` clean.
- `mdpeek-tui-ir --print fixtures/design-doc.json` renders all node kinds; `--reveal-line` toggles spoiler visibility; unknown-kind input exits non-zero.
- Neovim plugin drove a live `mdpeek serve` from headless nvim.
- `render.sh` produced 23 KB HTML for README/SAMPLE with a working index.

- Table padding is by char count → CJK/ASCII mixes can misalign (switch to display width later).
- Rendered HTML uses absolute `/static/` asset paths → preview must be served from a web root; a first-class `mdpeek export` emitting relocatable HTML is a natural follow-up.

Previously only `ios/` existed, there was no Android project or Android config, `eas.json` was minimal, and there was no documentation or example env file for the values builds need. The recommended path is **EAS Build**, which builds iOS in the cloud (no Mac required) as well as Android. This PR configures that, plus enables local/CI Android builds by generating the native project. ## Changes - **`app.config.js` (new):** dynamic Expo config layered on top of the known-good `app.json`, so the working iOS setup is untouched. Adds: - Android `package` (`com.jchau.toodaloo`) - Foreground location permissions + the `expo-location` config plugin (usage strings for iOS, permissions for Android) - `android.config.googleMaps.apiKey` read from `GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_API_KEY` (required by `react-native-maps` on Android) - **`eas.json`:** `development` / `preview` / `production` profiles with EAS Update channels, per-`environment` variable selection, APK for internal distribution, App Bundle + `autoIncrement` + `remote` version source for production. - **`android/` (new):** native Gradle project generated via `expo prebuild`, matching the committed `ios/` pattern. Build artifacts stay gitignored. - **`.env.example` (new):** documents the Supabase + Google Maps variables. - **README:** new "Native builds & deployment" section (config source of truth, EAS profiles, env var setup, local Android toolchain requirements + JDK 17 gotcha), updated repo layout and prerequisites. ## Verification - `npx expo config` resolves the merged config correctly (Android package, permissions, and Maps config present). - `npx expo prebuild --platform android` succeeds; generated `AndroidManifest.xml` has the location + internet permissions. - **Gradle configuration check passed:** installed the Android SDK (platform 36, build-tools 36.0.0) + JDK 17 and ran `./gradlew :app:help` — **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, all 33 tasks (RN gradle plugin composite build, Expo autolinking, every native module's Gradle config) evaluated cleanly. - **Toolchain finding:** JDK 21 fails during configuration (`JvmVendorSpec ... IBM_SEMERU`, a Gradle 9 toolchain-resolver incompatibility); **JDK 17 is required** and is now documented. - iOS config is only layered onto, not changed; iOS can't be compiled from a Linux agent — verify via EAS or macOS. ## Notes / follow-ups - To finish enabling the Android map, create a Google Maps Android API key, set `GOOGLE_MAPS_ANDROID_API_KEY`, and re-run prebuild before building. - `expo prebuild` reported `userInterfaceStyle` needs `expo-system-ui` for full native dark-mode theming on Android; the in-app `ThemeContext` already handles color scheme, so this is optional polish. - Full local Android *compilation* additionally needs the NDK/CMake (new architecture is enabled). author: michaeltaylor3d
body:
## Summary

Implements super-repo issue [DIG-Network/dig_ecosystem#33](https://github.com/DIG-Network/dig_ecosystem/issues/33): a lightweight, cheap background watcher that detects when a served store's on-chain state changes and invalidates the resolver's CloudFront cache the moment a change is seen.

- A new 1-minute EventBridge-scheduled Lambda (`on-dig-net-watcher`) reads (read-only `Scan`) the shared `dighub` table for currently-Active `*.on.dig.net` domains, checks each backing store's on-chain singleton lineage via a minimal coinset.org HTTP client, and fires a coalesced `cloudfront:CreateInvalidation` for the resolver's two dynamic paths (`/`, `/__dig/config.json`) the moment a store's lineage advances — instead of relying only on their passive 300s/30s max-age.
- The watcher's own state (last-known chain tip per store) lives in a NEW dedicated table (`on-dig-net-watcher-state`) this service owns; the shared `dighub` table stays strictly read-only (`Scan` only, never a write) — `pinned_root` is changed only by the domain owner's explicit re-pin action in hub.dig.net, confirmed by research into the hub's write paths, so the watcher never touches it.
- Chain reads use a minimal, purpose-built coinset.org adapter (`chia-protocol` wire types only) rather than `chia-query` (whose `ChiaQuery::new()` requires a live P2P peer connection unsuitable for a stateless Lambda) or `digstore-chain`'s full CHIP-0035 decode (heavier than needed — the watcher only needs to detect a *possible* root change via the singleton's tip coin, never decode the root's actual value).
- **Known, documented limitation:** CloudFront's `CreateInvalidation` API discriminates by path/query string, never by header — and the resolver's cache key for `/` and `/__dig/config.json` discriminates by the `x-dig-host` header. So a true single-subdomain-scoped invalidation is not achievable without a cache-key redesign (out of scope, a bigger/riskier change to an already-live distribution). The watcher invalidates the two dynamic paths distribution-wide, coalesced to at most once per tick — still cheap (CloudFront bills per path, not per header-variant) and never touches the long-TTL immutable static-asset paths.

## §2.0 tooling

`npx gitnexus@latest analyze` was run against `modules/services/on.dig.net` before editing (389 symbols / 824 edges / 32 flows indexed). Blast radius: the new `src/watcher.rs` module and `src/bin/watcher.rs` binary are net-new (zero existing callers); the only touched existing symbol is `src/lib.rs`'s module list (adding `pub mod watcher;`), which is additive and does not change any existing export's behavior. `active_store_ids` reuses `Domain::effective_status`/`Domain::is_reclaimable` (existing, unmodified) read-only. No existing resolver route, CSP, or config.json behavior changed.

## Version bump

**Minor** (0.2.0 → 0.3.0): a new capability (a new Lambda binary + supporting infra) with no breaking change to the existing resolver's external contract (routes, CSP, config.json shape all unchanged).

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo clippy --bin bootstrap --features aws -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo clippy --bin watcher --features aws -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --all-targets` — 43/43 passing (14 new watcher tests: the full `decide_store` decision matrix, `active_store_ids` dedup/status filtering, and `run_tick` orchestration over mocked chain/ledger/invalidator ports — no AWS/network needed)
- `cargo deny check advisories licenses sources bans` — clean (new deps: `chia-protocol`, `hex`, `reqwest`, `aws-sdk-cloudfront`, `lambda_runtime`)
- `terraform -chdir=infra fmt -check -recursive` / `terraform -chdir=infra validate` — clean
- `node --test test/sw.test.mjs` — 20/20 passing (unaffected, sanity-checked)
- `cargo lambda build --release --arm64 --features aws --bin watcher --output-format zip` — succeeds, produces a real deployable zip (and confirmed no regression on `--bin bootstrap`)

## Docs / spec

- `SPEC.md` §10 (new): the watcher's design, what it tracks, why it never writes `pinned_root`, why invalidation can't be scoped to a single subdomain, why coinset.org over chia-query/digstore-chain.
- `README.md`, `runbooks/deploy.md`, `runbooks/local.md`, `llms.txt` updated in the same unit.
- docs.dig.net: checked (background research) for any latency/propagation claim about `*.on.dig.net` — none found; this is a backend-only latency improvement with no user-facing behavior/wording change, so no docs.dig.net edit is needed.

Not merging per the driving task's instructions — leaving this PR for review/CI to go green, then merge separately.

author: ozykhan
body:
Design spec and implementation plan for **Plan 2** (epic #10): public HTTPS from behind NAT/CGNAT via an outbound tunnel to a relay, with TLS terminating on the box.

## Contents
- **`specs/2026-07-04-piper-relay-tunnel-tls-design.md`** — approved brainstorming output. Locked decisions:
  - **Tunnel:** hand-rolled over `hashicorp/yamux` (keeps piper one pure-Go / `CGO_ENABLED=0` / arm64 module; frp is heavy, rathole is Rust).
  - **TLS:** `go-acme/lego` DNS-01 **in-process** in `piperd`; **stock Caddy** just loads the PEM (no `xcaddy` custom builds).
  - **Relay trust:** per-agent tokens from day one (small SQLite enrollment store; zero-trust intact — relay holds tokens, never keys/plaintext).
  - **DNS ownership:** agent owns the domain + DNS creds (**Dokploy/Coolify-like**); relay never touches DNS. Vercel-like managed brokering is a documented later layer.
- **`plans/2026-07-04-piper-relay-tunnel-tls.md`** — 7 TDD tasks: `tunnel` → `certs` → `caddy :443` → `piper-relay` → `piperd` relay-mode client + cert wiring → loopback e2e → wrap-up. Each independently testable; `make test` + `make cross` stay green.

Design refinement in the plan: wildcard cert + relay suffix-routing means the agent registers once and new deploys need no cert/relay change — so `deploy`/`api`/`store`/`client` are untouched.

Docs only — no code. Implementation lands as separate PRs per task under #10.

Part of #10.

author: copilot
body:
The Documentation workflow was failing with `Deployment failed, try again later` due to two independent issues in `.github/workflows/docs.yml`.

## Root Causes

- **Race condition**: Multiple rapid pushes to `main` caused concurrent deploy jobs; GitHub Pages rejects all but one active deployment at a time (observed: runs #6 and #7 colliding).
- **Duplicate SHA deployment**: `tags: '*'` triggered a second deployment for the same commit SHA already deployed by the preceding `main` push (tag `v0.1.0` → same SHA as run #4; tag `v0.2.0` → same SHA as run #6).

## Changes

- **Remove `tags: '*'` from `on.push`** — tag pushes redeploy an already-live SHA, which Pages rejects. Docs are fully up-to-date after the corresponding `main` push.
- **Add top-level `concurrency` group** — serializes deployments; `cancel-in-progress: false` preserves in-flight deploys rather than killing them.

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

body:
## Problem

Admin login was failing because there was no way to force-reset the admin password to a known value without database access. The existing `POST /admin/auth/reset-default` endpoint only resets the account on module init and does not return the password that was actually applied, making it hard to confirm what credentials to use.

## Solution

Added `resetAdminPassword(password?)` to `AdminService` and wired it to a new unauthenticated `POST /admin/auth/reset-password` endpoint in `AdminController`. The endpoint accepts an optional `?password=` query parameter; when omitted it falls back to the `ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` env var (default `Admin@12345`). It finds or creates the `admin@votacao.com` account, bcrypt-hashes the new password, re-activates the account, and returns the email and plaintext password in the response so the caller can immediately verify the credentials.

### Changes
- **Modified** `src/admin/admin.service.ts`
- **Modified** `src/admin/admin.controller.ts`

author: pharnos-mvp
body:
## Rémanence de cache local entre comptes (trouvée en recette CS1)

Découvert en recette CS1 à 2 comptes sur le **même navigateur** : l agent scopé `clientdu229` voyait **7 dossiers** de Gold Pharma au lieu du **1** accordé.

**Cause** : IndexedDB est un cache PARTAGÉ par origine, mais `signOut()` ne faisait que `supabase.auth.signOut()` — sans vider Dexie. Le compte suivant héritait donc des données synchronisées du précédent. `purgeLocalData()` existait mais (a) n était appelé qu à la suppression de compte, (b) était incomplet (10 tables sur 18 oubliées, dont `lifecycleEvents`/`correspondences`/`parties`).

**Ce n est PAS une faille RLS** — le serveur bloque tout fetch hors périmètre (prouvé : la RLS renvoie 1 dossier ; le resync après purge ramène bien 1). C est une **exposition de données locales rémanentes sur machine partagée**, critique pour CS1 dont le principe est d inviter des agents externes.

### Correctif (2 volets)
- **`lib/local-data.ts`** : `clearLocalData()` vide **les 18 tables Dexie** + curseurs `pharnos.lastPull*` + `pharnos.orgId` ; conserve les préférences d UI. Itération `localStorage` indexée (fiable en jsdom comme en prod).
- **`reconcileLocalDataOwner(uid)`** : garde de changement de compte — si le cache appartient à un AUTRE utilisateur (swap de session sans logout propre), **purge avant le 1er rendu porteur de données**. Marqueur `pharnos.localDataOwner`.
- **AuthProvider** : purge au `signOut` + `publish()` passe la garde avant de publier la session (boot ET `onAuthStateChange`) → jamais de flash des données du compte précédent.
- **`purgeLocalData`** (suppression de compte) délègue à `clearLocalData` (source unique = schéma complet).

### Tests & preuve
- 5 tests unitaires (purge complète des 18 tables, curseurs vs prefs UI conservées, 1er login / re-login / swap de compte).
- Vérifié EN PROD dans le navigateur : après purge + resync, la vue scopée tombe de 7 à **1 dossier** (KV-10D · Bénin), nav réduite au Workspace.
- Suite complète : 597/597.

author: os-zhuang
body:
修复 #2588:Studio 运行时创作的 hook 的 `body` 从不执行(发布后不执行,重启后也不执行)。

## 根因(比 issue 描述的更深一层,共两个缺口)

1. **metadata-service 绑定路径没有 bodyRunner**(issue 已定位):`bindHooksToEngine` 对带 `body` 但无 runner 的 hook 直接跳过,而 `engine.setDefaultBodyRunner()` 在整个仓库中从未被调用,兜底 `_defaultBodyRunner` 永远为空。
2. **绑定集合根本看不到 authored 行**(验证中新发现):env-scoped 内核(`standalone-stack` 的 `proj_local`,即 `pnpm dev` 复现场景)没有 DatabaseLoader,`metadataService.loadMany('hook')` 完全不返回 sys_metadata 行 —— 所以重启后该 hook 甚至不是"被绑定但跳过",而是从未进入绑定流程。`GET /meta/hook` 能列出它只是因为 `getMetaItems` 直接查 sys_metadata。仅修 (1) 无法修复 issue 中的重启场景。

## 修复内容

- **runtime/AppPlugin**:`init()`(Phase 1,先于所有 `start()`)安装引擎级默认 hook body runner —— 与 defineStack hook 使用同一个 QuickJS 沙箱 runner(capability-gated + 超时)。空环境(empty env)也安装。逃生阀:`OS_DISABLE_AUTHORED_HOOKS=1` 让运行时创作的 body 保持不执行。
- **objectql/ObjectQLPlugin**:新增 authored-hook 重绑定 `resyncAuthoredHooks`(串行化,防并发交错落下旧快照):
  - 数据源 = `metadataService.loadMany('hook')` ∪ sys_metadata 活跃 `hook` 行(直接读表,跨所有 org —— 引擎 hook 本就进程级触发,与 flow trigger 语义一致);同名时 DB 行优先;
  - 触发时机 = `kernel:ready`(冷启动)、`metadata:reloaded`(dev artifact 重载 / 包发布,镜像 #2576 的 flow re-sync)、以及新的 protocol 变更监听(见下);
  - 全量替换 `'metadata-service'` 包集合,幂等;删到 0 条时显式 `unregisterHooksByPackage`(`bindHooksToEngine` 对空列表在 unregister 之前就 early-return,否则删除的 hook 会永远继续触发)。
- **metadata-protocol**:新增服务端 `onMetadataMutation(listener)`(与 `loadMetaFromDb` 同级的 server-side 扩展,不进 wire contract)。`saveMetaItem` / `publishMetaItem` / `deleteMetaItem` 持久化成功后通知订阅者 —— 这是所有创作入口(rest-server、dispatcher、AI builder)的唯一汇聚点,直接保存(默认 `mode='publish'`,不经 publish-drafts、不发 `metadata:reloaded`)也能即时生效。
- **双重执行防护**:metadata-service 绑定路径现在排除代码包 artifact 自带的 hook(`registry.getArtifactItem` 判定)—— 它们已由 AppPlugin 以 `app:<id>` + 显式 runner 绑定。此前 string-handler 的 artifact hook 在两条路径下已经潜在双绑;装上默认 runner 后 body hook 也会每事件跑两次,该过滤同时消除两者。

## 运行时验证(全新 showcase 实例,复刻 issue 步骤)

| 场景 | 结果 |
|:---|:---|
| 运行中直接保存 authored hook → PATCH `showcase_task` | ✅ `assignee='HOOKED'` 即时生效,无需重启 |
| draft 保存(`?mode=draft`)→ PATCH | ✅ 不执行(draft 不上线) |
| `publish-drafts`(issue 原始流程)→ PATCH | ✅ 新 body(`HOOKED-V2`)生效 |
| 完全重启 → PATCH | ✅ 生效(issue 的重启场景) |
| DELETE hook → PATCH | ✅ 停止触发(teardown) |
| 对照组:defineStack hook `showcase_normalize_task_title` | ✅ 照常 trim,且不再有双绑风险 |

测试:`pnpm test` 全绿(129 tasks);objectql 762 / runtime 453 / metadata-protocol 11 通过,新增 binder 默认 runner 回退、resync 各分支、mutation-listener 契约、AppPlugin 安装逻辑(含 opt-out)等用例。

## ⚠️ 需要平台负责人确认的设计决策(issue 中已标注)

**是否允许运行时创作(DB 存储、未经代码评审)的 hook 执行沙箱 JS?** 本 PR 采取 issue 中倾向的答案(是):QuickJS capability-gated、有超时、`hook.form.ts` 与完整 `HookSchema` 表明产品意图;同时提供 `OS_DISABLE_AUTHORED_HOOKS=1` 关闭开关。若评审结论是"hook 仅限代码定义",应改为让 Studio 拒绝创作此类 hook,请在合并前定夺。

## 已知边界(记录,不在本 PR 范围)

- 对代码包 hook 的 overlay 定制(改包内 hook 的 body)不会生效 —— artifact 版本继续执行(与 ADR-0010 artifact-wins 一致);如需 overlay-wins 语义需另行设计。
- 运行时创作的 `function`(string handler 目标)仍是死角,issue 中已列为伴生问题。

Closes #2588

author: bh462007
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1267

This PR adds proper error handling for Supabase operations in the Whiteboard Canvas. Previously, several database reads and writes ignored the returned `error` object, causing failures to happen silently. If a request failed due to a network issue, an expired session, or an RLS policy, the drawing would still appear locally but would never be saved to the server.

## What Changed

### `src/components/Whiteboard/Canvas.tsx`

- Added `toast` from `sonner` (already available in the project).
- Updated `persistEvent()` to check the result of the insert operation and display a toast if saving fails.
- Updated `initializeBoard()` to check for errors while loading whiteboard history. If loading fails, a toast is shown and the function exits early.
- Updated `undoLastStroke()` to handle delete errors and notify the user if the undo action couldn't be synchronized.
- Updated `clearBoard()` to handle delete errors and notify the user if clearing the board fails.

## Before vs After

| Operation | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Save drawing | Failed silently | Toast: **"Drawing could not be saved"** |
| Load history | Blank board with no feedback | Toast: **"Could not load whiteboard history"** |
| Undo | Failed silently | Toast: **"Undo could not be saved"** |
| Clear board | Failed silently | Toast: **"Board could not be cleared on the server"** |

## Testing

- [ ] Open a Study Room with the Whiteboard.
- [ ] Draw on the canvas and verify everything works normally.
- [ ] Simulate a network failure (DevTools → **Network → Offline**).
- [ ] Draw again and verify a **"Drawing could not be saved"** toast appears.
- [ ] Click **Undo** and verify a **"Undo could not be saved"** toast appears.
- [ ] Click **Clear** and verify a **"Board could not be cleared on the server"** toast appears.
- [ ] Restore the network connection and confirm the whiteboard syncs normally again.

## Notes

- The `whiteboard_events` table still uses an `as any` cast because it is not included in the generated Supabase types. This is an existing schema issue and is outside the scope of this PR.
- No new dependencies were added. Error notifications use the existing `sonner` toast system already used throughout the project.

## Related

- Closes #1267
- Updated `src/components/Whiteboard/Canvas.tsx`

author: jerpelea
body:
## Summary

Here is one proposal, how we could save a bit of flash on small systems.

First commit (not too significant one) doesn't change functionality, just cleans up a tiny amount of flash (64 bytes on 32-bit arm) by removing a duplicate string and an extra function call. The duplicate string was not cleaned up by linker because the string was only almost the same, the other one had one extra space.

The second one adds two new CONFIG flags giving more granularity to configure what to dump at crash:

CONFIG_SCHED_DUMP_STACK : Output stack dump at crash, consumes ~1kB flash ( If disabled, it still dumps the current stack, irq stack and kernel stack base and size )
CONFIG_SCHED_DUMP_TASKS : Output tasks dump at crash, consumes ~0.5kB flash

By removing these two, 1.6kB can be saved in flash size.

author: steipete
body:
## Summary

Removes the Code-Hex/vz cgo dependency and renames the provider from `apple-vz` to `apple-vm`.

All Virtualization.framework work now lives in `crabbox-apple-vm-vmd`, a dependency-free Swift daemon under `vmd/` (VM hosting, EFI/virtio configuration, bounded console log, VSOCK reverse SSH proxy, doctor probe). The Go helper is pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), embeds the daemon at release build time (`scripts/build-vmd.sh` + `-tags vmdembed`), and installs/entitlement-signs a content-addressed managed copy under the state root itself — so the backend's managed-helper copy/codesign machinery is deleted entirely.

### Why

- Code-Hex/vz was the only cgo dependency; its cgo/ObjC bridge layer (fd lifetimes, dispatch queues, KVO) is exactly the bug class upstream keeps patching. Swift talks to Virtualization.framework natively with no bridge and no third-party code.
- Same architecture as tart, without the FSL licensing questions (all first-party code).
- Opens a natural path to macOS guests (`VZMacPlatformConfiguration`) later.

### Rename compatibility

Old names keep working as deprecated aliases:

- provider names `apple-vz` / `applevz` (registered aliases)
- `appleVZ:` config key (merged when `appleVM:` is absent)
- `--apple-vz-*` flags and `CRABBOX_APPLE_VZ_*` env vars
- claim lookups canonicalize stored provider names via the alias registry, so pre-rename leases stay resolvable/cleanable
- the `state/apple-vz` directory migrates to `state/apple-vm` on first use
- legacy daemon process-identity checks still recognize `crabbox-apple-vz-helper` processes from older releases

### Protocol notes

The helper↔daemon contract is unchanged from the old helper↔serve contract: same CLI (`serve --state-root --name --startup-fd`), same startup-authorization byte, same `instance.json` metadata schema (the Swift daemon passes unknown keys through), same kinfo process-identity format, same VSOCK activate/ready channel protocol — the guest cloud-init proxy is untouched.

## Verification

- `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (full suite; two pre-existing flaky controller timing tests pass on rerun), `go test -race` on `internal/applevmhelper`, `internal/providers/applevm`, `internal/providers/all`
- `npm test --prefix worker`, `node --test scripts/*.test.js` (56/56)
- `scripts/check-docs.sh` (command surface, provider matrix, links, docs site)
- Release-style build: `sh scripts/build-vmd.sh && go build -tags vmdembed ./cmd/crabbox-apple-vm-helper`; `vmd-info` reports the embedded payload; daemon minos verified 13.0
- Live on Apple Silicon (macOS 26): `crabbox doctor --provider apple-vm` fully green (embed extraction → codesign → probe VM creation), and a real end-to-end boot:
  `crabbox run --provider apple-vm -- uname -a` → downloaded/converted Ubuntu 26.04, booted via the Swift daemon, SSH over the VSOCK reverse proxy, synced the checkout, ran the command (`Linux ... aarch64`), released and cleaned up the lease
- Codex autoreview: initial run found a release build-tag conflict (`cli_stub.go`) and stale JS release-contract tests — both fixed; re-run clean

## Config/secret implications

None. No new secrets; entitlement signing remains ad-hoc (`codesign --sign -`) and moves from the backend into the helper. `CRABBOX_APPLE_VM_VMD` is a new optional override for the daemon binary path (source builds).

body:
## Summary
Replaces **one Listmonk campaign per post** with a **weekly digest**: publishing a post no longer emails anyone; a weekly job aggregates the last 7 days of posts into **one campaign per language** (a "this week" intro + a section per post with its blurb and a link). Implements the `weekly-newsletter-digest` OpenSpec change.

## How it works
- **`publish.py`** no longer calls `create_campaign` — it just publishes the post and records its publications.
- **`boosternews.digest`** (`run_digest`): per language, take posts published **since the last digest** (bounded to 7 days), compose the body, create one Listmonk campaign, optionally auto-send, and record the digest. Idempotent — no post is included twice, and an empty week creates nothing.
- **Draft by default**, review-and-send in Listmonk; set `NEWSLETTER_DIGEST_AUTOSEND=true` to send automatically. Subject/intro are configurable per language.
- **Schedule**: `deploy/weekly-digest.sh` via a weekly cron (Mondays), running `boosternews digest` as an ephemeral Swarm job.

## Changes
- migration `0006_newsletter_digests`; `repository`: `last_digest_end` / `posts_for_digest` / `record_digest`
- `listmonk.start_campaign` (auto-send); config digest strings + autosend flag; CLI `digest`
- `deploy/weekly-digest.sh` + cron; `deploy/NEWSLETTER.md` updated

## Testing
On the VPS: confirmed publishing creates no campaign; ran the digest → one draft campaign per language aggregating the week's post (verified subject + aggregated body); re-ran → "no new posts" (window consumed). Test campaigns and digest rows were cleaned up so the first real weekly run starts fresh.

## Problem

Details that grow with the portfolio were hand-typed as fixed numbers, so they rot fast. The clearest proof: the store header claimed **"Twenty-eight games"** while actually rendering **31** cards — already wrong by 3.

## Fix

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `play/index.html` | "Twenty-eight games… Five are art-finished" | **Derives the count live** from the game cards; "Several are art-finished" |
| `index.html` | "Browse all 28 games in the store →" | "Browse the full store →" |
| `README.md` | "Twenty-six games… The core twenty-one…" | "A growing portfolio… The core set…" |
| `branding/d-applications.html` | "40 tests ✓ · 11 examples verified" | "tests passing ✓ · every example verified" |

Principle: where the data is present (store cards), derive the number so it's always right; where it isn't, phrase it count-free. Historical journals (BUILDLOG, LESSONS) are dated snapshots and left alone; per-game facts (Kintsugi 30 rooms, lanternfold 42 levels) are fixed truths and kept.

## Regression guard

`AGENTS.md` now states the rule under **Adding a game**: never hardcode a portfolio total in copy.

## Verification

body:
This PR updates [numpy](https://pypi.org/project/numpy) from **1.20.3** to **2.5.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.5.0
   ```
   Numpy 2.5.0 is a transitional release. It drops support for Python 3.11,
marking the end of distutils, and expires a large number of deprecations made
in the 2.0.x release. It also improves free threading and brings sorting into
compliance with the array-api standard with the addition of descending sorts.
Python 3.15 will be supported when it is released.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.14.

 Highlights

- Distutils has been removed,
- Many expired deprecations, see below,
- Many new deprecations, see below,
- Many static typing improvements.
- Improved support for free threading,
- Support for descending sorts,

See New Features below for other additions.

 Deprecations

- `numpy.char.chararray` is deprecated. Use an `ndarray` with a string or bytes dtype instead.

  ([gh-30605](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30605))

- `numpy.take` now correctly checks if the result can be cast to the provided
  `out=out` under the same-kind rule. A `DeprecationWarning` is given now
  when this check fails. Previously, `take` incorrectly checked if `out`
  could be cast to the result (the wrong direction). This deprecation also
  affects `compress` and possibly other functions. (Future versions of NumPy
  may tighten the casting check further.)

  ([gh-30615](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30615))

- The `numpy.char.[as]array` functions are deprecated. Use an
  `numpy.[as]array` with a string or bytes dtype instead.

  ([gh-30802](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30802))

- Setting the dtype attribute is deprecated because mutating an array is unsafe
  if an array is shared, especially by multiple threads. As an alternative,
  you can create a view with a new dtype via `array.view(dtype=new_dtype)`.

  ([gh-29244](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/29244))

- Setting the `shape` attribute is deprecated because mutating an array is
  unsafe if an array is shared, especially by multiple threads. As an
  alternative, you can create a new view via `np.reshape` or
  `np.ndarray.reshape`. For example: `x = np.arange(15); x = np.reshape(x, (3, 5))`.
  To ensure no copy is made from the data, one can use `np.reshape(..., copy=False)`.

  While setting the shape on an array is discouraged, for cases where it is
  difficult to work around, e.g., in `__array_finalize__`, it is possible
  with the private method `np.ndarray._set_shape`.

  ([gh-29536](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/29536))

- Using the `generic` unit in `numpy.timedelta64` is deprecated since this
  can lead to unexpected behavior such as non-transitive comparison, see
  [gh-28287](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/28287) for details. As
  an alternative, specify an explicit unit such as `'s'` (seconds) or `'D'`
  (days) when constructing `numpy.timedelta64`. Due to this change, operations
  that implicitly rely on the `generic` unit are also deprecated. For
  example:

      arr = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype="m8[s]")

       `1` is implicitly converted to generic timedelta64
      arr + 1

  ([gh-29619](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/29619))

- Resizing a Numpy array in place is deprecated since mutating an array is
  unsafe if an array is shared, especially by multiple threads. As an
  alternative, you can create a resized array via `np.resize`.

  ([gh-30181](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30181))

- `numpy.fix` is deprecated, use `numpy.trunc` instead. It is faster and
  follows the Array API standard. Both functions provide identical
  functionality: rounding array elements towards zero.

  ([gh-30644](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30644))

- `numpy.ma.round_` is deprecated. `numpy.ma.round` can be used as a
  replacement.

  ([gh-30738](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30738))

- `numpy.typename` is deprecated because the names returned by it were
  outdated and inconsistent. `numpy.dtype.name` can be used as a
  replacement.

  ([gh-30774](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30774))

- Inputs other than integers are deprecated for `numpy.triu_indices` and
  `numpy.tril_indices`. Non-integer values for the `M`, `k` and `N`
  parameters of `numpy.tri` are deprecated. Non-integer values for the `k`
  parameter of both `numpy.tril_indices_from` and `numpy.triu_indices_from`
  are deprecated.

  ([gh-30869](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30869))

- Deprecations in custom `dtype` property and `__array_finalize__`.

  Previously `arr.view(dtype=new_dtype)` called `arr.dtype = new_dtype`
  also for subclasses, i.e., the attribute setting. That path is now
  deprecated and refined, meaning that even subclasses that do not see this
  `DeprecationWarning` may wish to update their code.

  A subclass that does any `dtype` specific logic (i.e. verifying the dtype
  in `__array_finalize__` or has a `dtype` property) should now:

  - Set `_set_dtype = None` in which case `arr.view(dtype=new_dtype)`
    will call `__array_finalize__` with the new dtype, ensuring that
    any validation `__array_finalize__` will run is done.
  - Or, for a quick fix, define `_set_dtype` as a function (calling
    `ndarray._set_dtype()` to avoid `DeprecationWarnings`.
    (Future versions might migrate towards the `_set_dtype = None` path.)

  Ideally, follow NumPy\'s deprecation to prevent `dtype` mutation by users.
  The use of `ndarray._set_dtype()` may be necessary for some subclass
  finalization patterns, but should otherwise be avoided.

  ([gh-31293](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/31293))

 Expired deprecations

- `numpy.distutils` has been removed

  ([gh-30340](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30340))

- Passing `None` as dtype to `np.finfo` will now raise a `TypeError`
  (deprecated since 1.25)

  ([gh-30460](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30460))

- `numpy.cross` no longer supports 2-dimensional vectors.
  (Deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30461](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30461))

- `numpy._core.numerictypes.maximum_sctype` has been removed.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30462](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30462))

- `numpy.row_stack` has been removed in favor of `numpy.vstack`.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30463](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30463))

- `get_array_wrap` has been removed.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30463](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30463))

- `recfromtxt` and `recfromcsv` have been removed from `numpy.lib._npyio`
  in favor of `numpy.genfromtxt`.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30467](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30467))

- The `numpy.chararray` re-export of `numpy.char.chararray` has been removed.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30604](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30604))

- `bincount` now raises a `TypeError` for non-integer inputs.
  (deprecated since 2.1)

  ([gh-30610](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30610))

- The `numpy.lib.math` alias for the standard library `math` module has
  been removed.
  (deprecated since 1.25)

  ([gh-30612](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30612))

- Data type alias `'a'` was removed in favor of `'S'`.
  (deprecated since 2.0)

  ([gh-30613](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30613))

- `_add_newdoc_ufunc(ufunc, newdoc)` has been removed in favor of
  `ufunc.__doc__ = newdoc`.
  (deprecated since 2.2)

  ([gh-30614](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30614))

 Compatibility notes

 `linalg.eig` and `linalg.eigvals` now always return complex arrays

Previously, the return values depended on whether the eigenvalues happen to lie
on the real line (which, for a general, non-symmetric matrix, is not
guaranteed).

This change makes consistent what was a value-dependent result. To retain the
previous behavior, do:

    w = eigvals(a)
    if np.any(w.imag == 0):   this is what NumPy used to do
        w = w.real

💡 **What:** Refactored `capture_screen_base64` to convert screen capture objects directly into `PIL` images using `Image.frombytes` and an `io.BytesIO` buffer instead of saving to disk and reloading. Added fallback logic for environments with a single monitor.
🎯 **Why:** Writing to and reading from disk introduces severe IO bottlenecks on the hot-path (e.g. for `vision_control.py` screen capturing loops). Converting directly in-memory provides an immediate and massive performance boost.

author: afflicted6998
body:
## What this changes
Addresses every finding from the Gemini CLI review of PR #3 (report run by Steve, 2026-07-04). All four were valid; nothing was skipped.

1. **(High) Empty GPS parameters no longer corrupt data.** In JavaScript, an empty `lat=` converts to the number 0 — so a glitchy ping could have been stored as coordinate (0,0), a point in the Atlantic off Africa, blowing the walk's PostGIS distance past the QA plan's 10% tolerance. Same for `timestamp=` becoming 1970. These now get rejected as malformed (HTTP 400). I also fixed the same trap Gemini didn't flag on the *optional* fields: an empty `speed=` now stays empty instead of becoming "0 m/s", which would have looked like a genuine standstill reading. **4 regression tests added (17 total, all passing — `node supabase/functions/traccar-receiver/ping.test.ts`).**
2. **(Medium) The device-id check can no longer be skipped by mistake.** If the `TRACCAR_DEVICE_ID` secret is missing, the function now fails loudly with a 500 — Traccar keeps the fixes buffered, so no data is lost while you set the secret — instead of silently accepting any device that has the URL token.
3. **(Low) Visit lookup is NULL-proof.** Postgres sorts NULLs first on descending order, so a malformed active visit with no check-in time could have outranked the real one. Now explicitly ordered NULLs-last.
4. **(Low) Database errors are logged.** All three failure paths now write the underlying Postgres error to the edge function logs, so a live failure is diagnosable from the Supabase dashboard instead of being a generic "500".

Housekeeping note: the first commit accidentally included `node_modules` (the `.gitignore` is in still-open PR #5); the second commit removes it and adds the same `.gitignore` here. The PR diff you see is the true change — five files.

author: mctils12-arch
body:
## [REPAIR] Part 1 of the three-part directive — recurrence, so root-cause, not re-patch

### Measured root cause (production tiles, pixel-analyzed)

Six real tiles pulled through the prod proxy and decoded: **temp_new is a uniform 76/255-alpha wash; wind_new runs 15–53/255; not one pixel in any tile exceeds 120/255 alpha.** OWM Weather Maps 1.0 palettes are pale, low-alpha overlays designed for *light* basemaps. Chain of attenuation: intrinsic alpha (0.3/0.1) × client raster-opacity (0.6) × dark satellite background = **3–18% effective visibility**. The layers were rendering — invisibly.

### Why two prior fixes missed it (the actual generator)

v1.0.63's verification checked HTTP 200 + content-type + byte size of a tile — never pixels. v2.4 fixed status/note display — never pixels. Nothing in the pipeline ever asserted the layer's **pixel contribution**. That blind spot is the generator; it gets a ratchet:

- **DESIGN.md**: tile-layer pixel-verification lesson (overlay tile layers are verified by pixel contribution, never HTTP 200s).
- **`scripts/verify_weather_prod.mjs`** (compiled check): loads production at 390/768/1440, screenshots the map canvas with fields off, toggles temp+wind on via the real panel switches, screenshots again, and asserts a mean-pixel-diff floor — an invisible layer scores ~0.

### Fix at the generator

GL raster paint can only *reduce* opacity below a texture's baked-in alpha — no client setting can fix this. The proxy we already own now **amplifies each tile once per 10-min TTL** (pngjs, pure JS, no native deps): alpha ×3.2 (temp) / ×5.5 (wind — from its measured floor), capped at 230 so the basemap stays visible, +1.6× saturation around luma for the pale palette. Fully-transparent pixels stay transparent (no field invented where none exists); the transform is fail-open (undecodable input → raw buffer served). Client raster-opacity 0.6 → 0.85 — now a mild blend, not the visibility mechanism.

### Regression pin

The test fixture is a **real captured production wind tile**: the test first asserts it exhibits the defect (zero strong pixels — if OWM ever fixes their palettes, the test tells us to retune), then that amplification produces a readable field under the cap.

### Gates

Node **88/88** (2 new) · python **120 passed / 1 skipped** · harness green ×3 + zero-cost step · new dep: `pngjs` (pure JS) · version 1.0.68 → **1.0.69**.

### Post-merge proof (per the directive)

`node scripts/verify_weather_prod.mjs` against voltradeai.com after the deploy — screenshots at all three widths + pixel-diff numbers land in the session report and experiments.md.

body:
Follow-up hardening and polish on the multi-tenant system (#67, #69) — the "further work" items from the review.

## Safety
- **User deletion no longer orphans client data.** `workspaces.owner_user_id` was `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting a departed teammate left their client workspaces ownerless (manageable only by super-admins). Deleting a user now **reassigns their owned workspaces to the acting admin**; sessions and memberships still cascade away.
- **Brute-force throttling on credential endpoints.** Login, signup and passkey-login get a tight per-IP limit (default **10/min**, via `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`/`_WINDOW`), far below the global 300/min. Proven with a 429 assertion in the HTTP test.

## Docs (README)
- New **"Accounts, workspaces & sign-in"** section: the tenancy model diagram, member management, and the automatic single-tenant→multi-tenant upgrade behaviour.
- **Sign-in methods** table (password+TOTP, passkeys with the HTTPS caveat, SSO).
- Full **SSO / OIDC env-var reference** — previously undiscoverable, so SSO effectively shipped invisible.
- Configuration table gains `APP_SECRET`, the rate-limit vars, and the SSO vars. Renamed the old "Authentication" heading to "Connecting Google" so it isn't confused with dashboard login.

## Tests
- **`backfill.test.ts`** — seeds a legacy single-tenant DB (workspace-less sites, Google accounts and a global Bing key) and proves first-user bootstrap claims everything with nothing left unassigned. De-risks real production upgrades.
- **`http-authz.test.ts`** — boots the *real* server and asserts over HTTP that a user gets **404 on another workspace's site across every scoped route** (GET urls, analytics, performance, PUT, DELETE), the owner is unaffected, and repeated bad logins hit **429**. This guards the actual wired-up authorization boundary, not just the helpers.
- Excluded test files from the `tsc` build — they never belonged in `dist`, and shipping them made vitest double-run emitted copies (two servers fighting for a port).

## UI
- **Per-site Bing account picker** in the site config tab (backend already accepted `bing_account_id`; falls back to the workspace's first key).

## Verification
- Backend `tsc` build + **20 tests** green; frontend lint (0 errors) + build green.

body:
## What

Adds two commands to the dashboard's Ctrl/Cmd-K command palette that show or hide the Groups-tab **palette dock** (the right-side panel of drag-to-spawn profiles / templates / roles, `js/dock.js`, JOH-374):

- **Show right panel** — wizard: *Unfurl the grimoire*
- **Hide right panel** — wizard: *Furl the grimoire*

Offered as a directional pair (like the existing *Collapse / Expand all groups* commands) so both verbs are always listed and findable by either word; running the redundant direction is a harmless idempotent re-apply.

## How

- `dock.js` now **exports** `isDockOpen` and a new **`setDockOpen(open)`** — the single mutation point behind *every* show/hide control. The edge tab and the in-dock collapse button now route through it too (`toggleDock = () => setDockOpen(!isDockOpen())`), so no caller can persist one state and paint another.
- `palette.js` imports those and adds the two commands. **Show** first switches to the Groups tab (the dock is Groups-tab-only, so it'd otherwise be invisible), matching the group-fold commands; **Hide** just flips the persisted `dashPrefs` flag.
- Labelled **"right panel"**, not "palette", to avoid colliding with the command palette's own name. The dock's own vocabulary (dock / sidebar / drawer / profiles / templates / roles / grimoire …) rides in the keywords + hint so it stays findable either way. `show`/`hide` already bridge to `focus`/`reveal` and `unfocus`/`veil` via the scorer's `SYNONYMS` map.

## Naming note

The operator asked whether there are better names than "show/hide right panel". I kept **"right panel"** as the plain label because within the Ctrl+K palette, calling it "palette" clashes with the palette itself and "dock" is internal jargon. Happy to rename if you'd prefer e.g. "Show/Hide dock" or "Show/Hide sidebar".

- `go build ./...`, full `go test ./pkg/claude/agentd/…`, `node --input-type=module --check` on both edited modules — all green.
- New string-pin coverage in the command-palette / dock / wizard HTML tests (project convention for embedded JS assets).
- **Eyes-on via dashsnap (headless Chrome), both skins:** opened the palette, filtered to `panel`, confirmed both commands render with correct icons/hints, and the dock still renders correctly open + collapsed after the `setDockOpen` refactor.

body:
## Production blocker: refund org-ledger over-credit (money correctness)

Third of the four go-live money/identity blockers Bryan prioritized (72h deactivation ✅, **refund ledger correctness ← this**, invite-only registration, auditor lifecycle).

### The bug
Stripe's `charge.amount_refunded` is **cumulative** across partial refunds. `handleChargeRefunded` posted that cumulative total to `org_ledger` on **every** `charge.refunded` delivery, and the ledger is append-only keyed only loosely on `charge.id`. Result:

- Two $50 partial refunds on a $100 charge → post **$50 then $100 = $150** refunded (a **$50 over-credit**).
- A plain webhook **re-delivery** of the same event → **double-post**.

The invoice reconciliation path (`invoices.amountPaid`) was already idempotent — it recomputes net from `invoicePayments`. This closes the remaining leak on the **org ledger** side.

### The fix
Post **only the incremental delta**:

```
alreadyPosted = Σ(org_ledger refund rows for this charge.id)     // ≥ 0
refundDelta   = round2( max(cumulativeRefunded − alreadyPosted, 0) )
post ledger row only when refundDelta > 0
```

- Multiple partials each post their own increment; the sum equals the true refund, never more.
- A retry/re-delivery of the same event contributes delta `0` → no row (idempotent per event, belt-and-suspenders with the existing event-id lifecycle guard).
- Negative "impossible lower cumulative" is clamped to 0 (no phantom reversal row).
- Delta keyed per `charge.id` so unrelated charges don't cross-subtract.

Ledger `direction: 'credit'` (cash leaving → balance down) is unchanged from the prior GAP-26 fix; only the **amount** changes from cumulative → delta.

### Tests
`tests/unit/billing/refundLedgerIdempotency.test.ts` (8 tests, all green):
- Invariant model (replays deliveries against an append-only ledger): two partials, webhook re-delivery, uneven partials, fractional-cent rounding, negative clamp, per-charge keying.
- Source guard: asserts the handler computes `alreadyPosted` from prior refund rows and posts `amount: refundDelta` — and **fails** if anyone regresses to posting the raw cumulative `refundedAmount`.

### Verification
- `npm run check:server-core` — clean
- `npm run check:money-idempotency` — PASS (no new keyless money-moving Stripe calls)
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/billing/refundLedgerIdempotency.test.ts` — 8/8 pass

### Scope / safety
- No Stripe API calls added or changed; no live-money flag touched. Pure org-ledger posting math.
- Additive + defensive: a correct single-refund path still posts exactly the refund amount once.

author: allmight97
body:
## Summary

Completes the metadata intent-flow audit for the stages PR #415 did not touch: container routing, chapter/cover passthrough, the remux and ffmpeg-dict adapters, artifact readback, and the encoder adapters' metadata finalize seams. One high-severity fix ships here; everything else audited clean or is classified below.

## The fix: external FDK artifacts silently lost series and album-sort tags

- **Root cause (empirically verified):** the FFmpeg mov muxer only writes dictionary keys in its known-atom table. `series`, `series-part`, both `----:com.apple.iTunes:*` freeform mirrors, and `sort_album` are all silently dropped on remux — only `title`-class keys and `media_type` survive.
- **Blast radius:** the external FDK adapter finalized its freshly encoded M4B with a bare `rewrite_metadata_with_ffmpeg`, so every FDK-encoded audiobook lost series, series number, and album-sort metadata that the native and Apple AAC paths preserve via their mp4ameta finalize. This is caller-side adapter substitution on an MP4 container — the exact behavior the root invariants ban ("container routing from actual classification, not caller-side substitutes").
- **Fix:** new single owner `metadata::finalize_artifact_metadata(path, metadata, passthrough)` — the remux carries chapters and cover art, then MP4-family tag truth is rewritten through mp4ameta chosen by real container classification. The external adapter now calls the owner. The bare-remux re-export is removed from the boundary so no future adapter can reach it.
- **Proof (failing-first):** `artifact_finalize_preserves_series_tags_and_chapters_on_mp4_route` ran red against the old remux-only behavior (`series: None` on readback), green after the fix. It asserts three things on a real lane-produced M4B: ABB readback truth, **external `ffprobe` truth** (the audit's named blind spot — not just our own reader), and that chapters written by the remux **survive** the mp4ameta tag rewrite.

## Also in this PR

- **Passthrough chapter offsets** now round like the synthetic-chapter math instead of truncating (mechanical; the two paths disagreed by up to 1ms per file).
- **Linux agent environment:** `setup-codex-agent-env.sh` and `scripts/AGENTS.md` now put the FFmpeg prefix `bin` on `PATH`, and the media-lane ffprobe helper honors an `ABB_FFPROBE` override with a self-explanatory failure message. This also unbreaks PR #415's ffprobe test on the documented Linux lane (it currently dies with a bare `NotFound` there).
- **Canon:** metadata Public API Strip gains `finalize_artifact_metadata` (+ crate-root re-export for the lane); processor AGENTS.md finalize invariant now names the owner; DECISIONS.md entry records the mov-muxer evidence and guardrail; CHANGELOG Fixed entry in user terms.

## Audit classification (stages not covered by #415)

- **Fix:** external FDK metadata finalize (above).
- **Fix (mechanical):** chapter offset truncation/rounding drift.
- **Fix (env):** ffprobe missing from the documented Linux lane PATH.
- **Reject (audited coherent):** container routing — real classification via FFmpeg format name, typed error on open failure, no extension-based substitutes; cover-art precedence — single owner (`ResolvedCover::select`: explicit wins, empty = clear, passthrough embed failures degrade to warnings while explicit failures stay fatal); outcome planning — `plan_metadata_outcome` is planned once per job in `processing/plan.rs`, and naming + written metadata derive from the same effective metadata (no dual projection); clear semantics on the ffmpeg-dict path — keys are actually removed, not written empty; preview chapter gating — both adapters skip chapter passthrough in preview (native via `skip_chapter_passthrough`, external via `cover_art_only`).
- **Defer (product decision, issue-worthy):** merging a chaptered source with unchaptered sources passes through only the chaptered file's chapters — the unchaptered spans get none and synthesis doesn't trigger (it only fires when *no* source has chapters). Real-world mixed merges get a partial chapter timeline. Needs an owner decision (synthesize per-file chapters for gap files vs. document first-wins).
- **Defer:** `copy_chapters` in `remux.rs` treats `Some(passthrough)` with empty chapters as "write no chapters" rather than "copy source chapters" — coherent for every current caller (the external temp artifact is chapterless by construction), but it's a seam worth a comment if a new caller appears.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p audiobook-boss --all-targets` (no new warnings; pre-existing platform-cfg dead-code warnings on Linux untouched)
- `cargo test -p audiobook-boss` — 368 lib + 78 integration, all green on the Linux lane (with the PATH fix this PR documents)
- No IPC/binding changes — `finalize_artifact_metadata` is crate-internal + test re-export, not a command.

Relationship to #415: complementary, no shared file overlap except `integration_media_execution_tests.rs` (both add an ffprobe helper — trivial merge either direction; mine honors `ABB_FFPROBE`).

author: oussamalakhdar90
body:
Fixes the blocker from the live bulk-fix run: Jira rejected the ticket with a cryptic **`400 — Field 'summary' cannot be set. It is not on the appropriate screen, or unknown`** (then `description`, then `labels`) — *after* cloning the framework repos. When Jira reports **every** field as "not on the appropriate screen," it almost always couldn't resolve a create screen at all (the **project key or issue type is wrong**), not a genuine field-config issue. Nothing had validated the typed project, so a doomed `createIssue` was sent post-clone.

## Fixes
1. **`SnykBulkFixService` validates the project up front** — resolves the typed key against the accessible Jira projects (`listProjects`) **before creating any epic/ticket or cloning any repo**:
   - unknown key → clear `400` ("project 'CIAM' wasn't found — check the key in Settings"),
   - a case-variant → resolves to the canonical key,
   - and because `listProjects` exercises the Jira token, a **missing token surfaces here as a connection error** instead of a half-run batch that clones first.
   
   This is the *"validate the project is correct / check it exists / don't start without a token"* from the feedback.
2. **`JiraClient.explainCreateFailure`** turns the raw create-screen 400 into an actionable message naming the **project + issue type**, wired into both the Server and Cloud `createIssue` catch blocks. A generic (non-screen) error is passed through unchanged.

## Regression
Additive to the bulk path; error-only change on `createIssue` (generic errors keep the old wrapping). **124 tests green** across every `createIssue` consumer (Defect, TestPlan, SnykFixJira, both clients, bulk service). New tests: unknown-project fail-fast (no Jira write, no train), case-insensitive canonical resolution, token error before cloning; `explainCreateFailure` direct + a WireMock `createIssue` surfacing the hint.

> Note on `CIAM`: the exact 400 means Jira couldn't create a **Task** in the project you typed. Once the wizard (next PR) uses the picker, you'll select a validated project + a real issue type. If `CIAM`/`Task` is genuinely the intended target, this now tells you *why* clearly (wrong key/type, or your token can't create Tasks there).
