author: mahesh-sangawar
body:
Closes #460. Two payout-hold race conditions from the 2026-07-03 audit (epic #403). Flag-gated — hold columns are plain DB state, no live money moves until the escrow flags flip — but a money-path change, so it went through plan → plan-check → independent verify.

## Race 1 — full-row `Save(&order)` lost-update of hold columns
`chefs.go UpdateOrderStatus` loaded the whole `Order` row (incl. `payout_hold_status`/`customer_confirmed_at`) then persisted with `tx.Save(&order)`. A re-submitted `delivered` (allowed idempotent no-op) that straddled a concurrent customer-confirm / auto-confirm sweep / admin-release commit wrote the row's **load-time** hold columns back over the newer values (e.g. `release_eligible` → `awaiting`).

**Fix:** replace full-row `Save(&order)` on the orders table with a targeted `Updates(map)` writing only the columns each handler owns — hold columns are never in the map, so a concurrent transition survives. Applied to all four full-row-Save sites:
- `chefs.go UpdateOrderStatus` (the live bug) — `{status}` + `fulfillment_type` (when a carrier is chosen) + the single lifecycle stamp for the transition.
- `delivery.go:503`/`:1430` (AcceptDelivery / ManualAssign) — `{delivery_id, status, picked_up_at, estimated_delivery_time}`.
- `orders.go:832` (CancelOrder) — `{status, cancelled_at, cancel_reason}`.

The delivery/cancel sites operate where the hold is provably empty today, but they were the same anti-pattern; hardening them stops it becoming a bug if a hold can exist earlier.

## Race 2 — dispute check not atomic with the transition
`ConfirmOrderHold`/`ConfirmMealPlanDayHold`/`ConfirmGroupOrderHold` read `HasOpenOrderIssue` **outside** the tx, then `applyHoldConfirm` did a separate guarded UPDATE — an `OrderIssue` filed in that window still committed `release_eligible`.

**Fix:** fold the dispute predicate into the guarded UPDATE. `applyHoldConfirm` now takes `issueOrderID *uuid.UUID` and runs the **disputed (EXISTS open issue) update first**, then the **release_eligible (NOT EXISTS, from `awaiting` only) update**. The disputed-first ordering makes a dispute that races the confirm fail safe: if the issue lands after the disputed update no-ops, the release update's `NOT EXISTS` catches it and the row stays `awaiting` (money held). Both guards also gained `customer_confirmed_at IS NULL`, making confirmation idempotency DB-enforced (a stale in-memory caller can't re-stamp/re-emit). Public `Confirm*Hold` signatures are unchanged, so the sweep cron and handlers are untouched.

## Tests
- New **race-1** regression (`chef_delivered_gate_test.go`): a concurrent customer-confirm is injected (one-shot GORM `Before(gorm:update)` callback) into the load→persist window; the re-stamped `delivered` must not revert the advanced hold.
- New **race-2** regression (`payout_hold_test.go`): a pending `OrderIssue` is injected just before the confirm's transition UPDATE; the confirm must land in `disputed`, never `release_eligible`.
- Both were proven **RED against pre-fix code** first, and confirmed green after. All existing `payout_hold` / chef-status tests still pass; full `apps/api` module suite green.

## Gates
- **plan-check:** GO-WITH-CHANGES — both conditions adopted (RED-first proof; DB-enforced idempotency guard).
- **independent verify:** GO — column-completeness confirmed for all four sites, two-statement design traced through every state/interleave (no double-emit, no released→release_eligible), subquery SQL confirmed correct on sqlite + Postgres.

## Follow-up (out of scope, filed separately)
Verifier flagged the same check-then-act shape in `payout_release.go ReleaseHold` (admin release reads the open-issue block outside the tx). Pre-existing, not part of #460 — will file its own ticket.

author: hyperxpro
body:
## Gate 3c — peer-quorum AnchorWitness: R-a′ election-safety closer

Closes residual **R-a′** (ratification item 11): a within-term `votedFor` rollback → a second, conflicting vote at the same term → two leaders → split-brain. Realizes the frozen §A1.7 `AnchorWitness` SPI as a peer-quorum witness. Per `docs/design/anchor-witness-peer-quorum-2026-07-04.md`.

### The mechanism (no at-rest format change)
Under the merged ⟦SEC-MERGE⟧, casting a vote **is** an anchor write that raises the strictly-monotone `anchorSeq` (`persistTermVote` → `AnchorFile.writeTermVote` → `withSeq(anchorSeq()+1)`). So a within-term vote rollback **is** an `anchorSeq` rollback. Peers witness each other's `anchorSeq`; at boot, if a peer holds evidence we existed at a higher `anchorSeq` than the disk we booted from, the disk was rolled back → **refuse to start**. The witnessed quantity is the anchor's *already-frozen* `anchorSeq` — **zero new at-rest bytes**.

### What changed (all logic/wire; frozen at-rest layout untouched)
- **Wire — additive raft messages** `RAFT_WITNESS=0x12` / `RAFT_WITNESS_REPLY=0x13` (`MessageType`, `BY_CODE`→0x14). Fixed **29-byte** body `[selfAnchorSeq:8][selfTerm:8][selfVotedFor:4(-1=null)][seenOfYouSeq:8][flags:1(bit0=QUERY)]`, coded in `RaftMessageCodec` (checkRemaining-bounded, fail-closed on wrong-type/truncation/null-from). The **sender is NOT on the wire** — injected from the mTLS-authenticated `InboundMessage.from` (the coalesced-heartbeat precedent), so an authenticated-but-hostile peer cannot spoof another peer's id (W5). Frame stays `ver=0x02`, dormant `epoch` untouched/MBZ. Existing raft goldens byte-identical; new `raft_witness.bin`/`raft_witness_reply.bin` goldens added.
- **In-memory witness state** (per group; no persistence, rebuilt at boot): `bootAnchorSeq`, `witnessOfPeer[P]`, `peerAckOfSelf[P]`, `votingCleared` latch.
- **Boot gate (`evaluateBootGate`)**: `W = max` responders' `seenOfYou`; **`W > bootAnchorSeq` ⇒ REFUSE** (one-shot handler → halt(71) + `{action=anchor.rollback.detected}` audit record; stays latched forever — a rolled-back node never votes until an operator intervenes); else quorum (default `isQuorum(responders∪self)` / strict peer-majority) ⇒ clear the latch. Non-blocking — replies accumulate across ticks, never a blocking call on the owner thread.
- **Vote gate**: latch `witnessOk = !witnessArmed || votingCleared` gates the grant (`handleRequestVote`) and both election starts (`startElection`, `startPreVote`); **announce-before-grant** ordering (`grantVoteWitnessed`: persist s1 → broadcast to peers → *then* voteGranted; strict mode defers voteGranted until a peer-majority acks). `becomeFollower` term adoption stays ungated (adoption isn't a vote and only moves `anchorSeq` forward). Persist-before-memory preserved.
- **Cadence**: piggyback on the heartbeat tick + event-broadcast after a vote-granting write + boot QUERY. Off the ack path.
- **`PeerQuorumAnchorWitness implements AnchorWitness`**; `record`→broadcast, `lastSeen`→QUERY-quorum. Per-scope (gid per-shard, NODE_SCOPE freshness-only). External-store provider (TPM/RPMB — the R-a / N=1 closer) is the same SPI, left as the documented seam.

### As-built activation (reviewed + accepted, not a design change)
The witness is **armed** at the production wiring point (`ConfigdServer:1798`, `if (tcpTransport != null)`) rather than intrinsically default-on, to preserve ~53 existing bare-RaftNode unit tests. This is sound: `tcpTransport == null` ⟺ no configured peers ⟺ every group is single-replica ⟺ split-brain is void (R-a′ not a live threat) ⟺ inert is correct; `tcpTransport != null` ⟺ real multi-replica cluster ⟺ armed ⟺ R-a′ closed. Within an armed cluster a peerless group self-disables via `votingCleared = peersEmpty`. So R-a′ is closed in exactly the deployments where it is a live threat, and the un-armed path is byte-identical to pre-Gate-3c.

### Modes (`-D` only, no data-dir-read control)
- **Strict — the out-of-box DEFAULT** (operator-ratified after the red-team finding below): the boot gate requires a **peer-majority** of replies and `voteGranted` is deferred until a peer-majority acks the announce. This **absolutely closes R-a′** at all N (two peer-majorities intersect ⇒ a witness is always in the boot-reply set). Cost: reduced election availability during reboots/partitions (a rebooting node, and casting a vote, needs a peer-majority of peers reachable). Correct for a config store where split-brain = divergent/corrupt config.
- **Available mode** (`-Dconfigd.raft.witnessStrict=false`, explicit opt-in): boot gate clears on a self-counting cluster quorum (self+1). Higher availability, but carries a **documented adversary-reachable residual** — see below.

### Red-team finding (MEDIUM) → operator ruling
The independent red-team found that the *available* mode's boot gate (self+1 clear + never-re-evaluate) is defeated by **ordinary announce packet-loss to one peer + a boot-reply timing race** (a non-witness peer completes the quorum before a healthy-but-slower witness replies) → a rolled-back node false-passes → double-vote → split-brain. This needs **no peer crash**, so the design's original "non-adversarial / vanishing" framing understated it. Per the operator's ruling, **strict is now the default** so the recommended configuration genuinely closes R-a′; the available mode remains as an explicit availability opt-in with the residual documented honestly (`docs/design/anchor-witness-peer-quorum-2026-07-04.md` §0/§3.1, and `AnchorWitnessRedteamTest.finding_defaultMode_singleNonWitnessReplyRace_falsePass` which documents it).

### Boot-window catch-up (brick-on-rolling-restart fix)
Arming the gate by default surfaced a real false-refuse: a healthy node **caught up** (a follower append or term adoption — both ungated, both raise `anchorSeq`) **during its boot window** advertised its *live* (advanced) seq; peers witnessed it above `bootAnchorSeq` and reflected `W > bootAnchorSeq` → a rolling-restart node bricked with no rollback. Fix: while the boot gate is latched, `advertisedAnchorSeq()` broadcasts the **frozen** `bootAnchorSeq`, not the live one (used in `broadcastWitness` + the QUERY reply); after clear it advertises live. Detection is unchanged (`W > bootAnchorSeq`) and no rollback can be missed — advertising a *lower* value only ever *raises* a peer's `max`-memory, never erases a rolled-back node's peers' higher pre-crash memory. Regression: `AnchorWitnessPeerQuorumTest.catchUpDuringBoot_healthyNode_notFalseRefused`.

### N=1 / N=2
N=1: gate disabled (`votingCleared=true` at arm), self-elects, no brick; freshness residual **R-a** remains (closable only by the external-store witness). N=2: rollback caught iff the single peer is available (already the precondition for any N=2 progress).

### Tests (each PERFORMS the attack)
`AnchorWitnessPeerQuorumTest` (10, file-backed nodes + delivering-queue transport): **headline double-vote BLOCKED** (real on-disk rollback of V's whole durable image to `{T,null,s0}` → boot gate refuses → no second leader at T), grant→announce crash race, no-false-positive W1/W2/W4-no-brick/W6/W7, strict mode, N=1, rollback-exception fields. `RaftWitnessCodecTest` (10): 29-B golden + round-trip + directional-decode reject + truncation/null-from reject + W5 spoof-resistance. `RaftTransportAdapterLoopbackTest` (real-socket from-injection over TCP), `MessageTypeTest` (27). Independent red-team pass. Full reactor green (14 modules, consensus-correctness safetyViolations=0 + durability crash matrices intact).

(Fences: no keyring/keyTerm — Gate 4. External-store witness (R-a / N=1 closer) — documented SPI seam, later.)

Frontend (app/page.js):
- Fix React hydration mismatch: Watchlist read localStorage in the useState initializer, so the client's first render differed from the server-rendered HTML for anyone with a saved watchlist. Now restores the saved list in an effect after mount.
- Fix expiration dropdown fetching the wrong symbol: it used the raw text-input value instead of the symbol the chain was loaded for, so typing a new ticker (without loading it) and switching expiration mixed one symbol's expirations with another's chain.
- Fix duplicate data fetch when loading a symbol via Enter/Load button (loadExp ran both directly and again via the useEffect on symbol).
- Fix rows with no quote data being styled green ("up").
- Fix literal "0" rendering when risk/reward ratio is exactly zero.

Suggestions API (app/api/suggestions/route.js):
- Construct the Anthropic client inside the handler and return a clear JSON error when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, instead of crashing the whole route at module load with an opaque 500.
- Fix bogus ATM strike selection: the chain was sliced to the 10 lowest strikes (deep ITM) and matched with a hardcoded <5 proximity check that fails for high-priced tickers. Now picks the strike nearest the live spot price from the full chain.
- Guard .toFixed()/formatting against non-numeric quote fields so a partial Tradier response can't 502 the route.
- Extract the text block from the Claude response defensively instead of assuming content[0] is text.

Site-wide link rule via a Goldmark **link render hook** (`layouts/_default/_markup/render-link.html`):

- **Motor ELO-lite** (`web/lib/dominio.ts`): puntaje progresivo 0→100 por nodo, determinístico, sin IA. Acertar algo difícil a nivel bajo suma mucho; lo fácil a nivel alto casi nada; bajar resta la mitad (asimetría pro-motivación). Reemplaza (retira) la regla de ventana.
- **Estados derivados**: `dominado` = puntaje ≥ 70 + cobertura histórica (≥2 `producir`, ≥1 difícil al 1er intento) + **≥ 50 ejercicios respondidos**; hito pegajoso (solo lo tocan el override docente y el decaimiento futuro). `a_reforzar` sigue siendo señal de conducta.
- **Nunca repetir (DP5)**: un chico no vuelve a ver un ejercicio que ya respondió; Practicar filtra por su historial completo.
- **Pool con reposición automática**: Edge Function `generador-ejercicios` (deployada v3, migración `0012` aplicada) — pool inicial estratificado 36/nodo al publicar (idempotente), lote de 12 cuando quedan < 16 sin ver (gate server-side espejo, solo genera si hace falta), **tope diario estricto de 240** (Regla 4). Mock por defecto hasta la API key.
- **Generación por banda de grado** (1°-2° / 3°-4° / 5°-7°, sobre `programa.grado` — cero datos nuevos del menor, Regla 5).

Spec → plan → ejecución con subagentes (review por tarea) → review final de rama: **Ready to merge**. Los 3 findings Important del proceso quedaron fixeados y verificados (reset de estado ante falla de red, gate de reposición, copy de publicar).

author: kevinqz
body:
## Problema (achado pelo red-team SotA do `readiness_score`)

`model_dropdown` ordenava por `readiness_score`, mas essa chave **nunca é emitida** nas entradas do `catalog.json` (o readiness vive em `readiness-scores.json` sob `score`). Resultado: o sort desabava para **ordem alfabética** e o default pré-selecionado do nó VLM era **`gemma-4-12b-mm-warshanks`** (score 48, grade **F**, experimental) — o 2º menos pronto de 82 modelos. Uma feature "melhor primeiro" entregava o pior.

## Fix

- **Hard-gate** (`_runs_on_this_mac`): mantém só modelos utilizáveis neste Mac — artefato `available`, não `not_published`, e não explicitamente não-mac. `device_support.mac == "unknown"` é **mantido** de propósito (não penaliza entradas da comunidade/fabric, evitando o viés de curadoria que o red-team apontou).
- **Ordena menor-primeiro** (`_artifact_size_bytes` parseia `"969MB"`/`"1.7 GB"`): o menor modelo utilizável vira o default — honesto e cego a "qualidade" (que o catálogo não mede).
- O ComfyUI **não lê mais `readiness_score`** → resolve a chave-fantasma pelo lado do leitor (a direção decidida no red-team).

## Resultado ao vivo
| Nó | Default antes | Default agora |
|---|---|---|
| VLM | `gemma-4-12b` (F, 6.4GB) | `qwen3-vl-2b` (2.3GB) |
| Depth | — | `depth-anything-3-small` (54.5MB) |
| Detection | — | `yolox-s` (36MB) |
| Segmentation | — | `efficientsam3-tinyvit` (374MB) |

Testes unitários offline (CI-safe) travando gate + ordenação. **ruff limpo · 12/12 testes.**

author: grant-l
body:
## What

`verify-md-links.py` crawled only `*.md` and explicitly skipped `.tex` targets, so `\kbleaf{...}` citations in the rendered manuscript were never existence-checked — a dead KB path passed `make verify` silently. This class surfaced twice in the PR #519 review (a nonexistent `vol2/particle-physics/` path cited as the sole canonical anchor of a flagship figure, while the leaf lives under `vol4/circuit-theory/`).

Two commits, bisectable order (each passes `make verify` on its own):

1. **`manuscript:` repair 7 dead + 3 split `\kbleaf` cites** — all mechanical repoints to verified-existing targets; no claim content changes.
2. **`tools(verify-md-links):` the new pass** — wired into the existing `make verify-md-links` gate, so it rides `make verify` and the precommit hook with no Makefile-target changes.

## Checker design (why these rules)

- **Path-suffix resolution.** A cite resolves iff every directory segment it names lies on the tail of a real repo path. This accepts the corpus's tail-of-path shorthand (`ch01-gravity-yield/leaf.md`, `figures/gen_field_ladder.py`) while a wrong-directory cite still **fails even when a same-named leaf exists elsewhere** — the PR #519 class. A plain basename fallback for multi-segment paths would have masked exactly that class.
- **Bare filenames** resolve by basename, gated on a known file extension. `\kbleaf` doubles as a generic monospace typesetter (skill names, Python identifiers, shell snippets, leaf stems); those are **skipped and counted** (32 on the current tree), not guessed at.
- **`...` ellipses / `[..]` ranges** resolve as globs (the corpus writes `eq_axiom_[1-4].tex`, `vol4/.../regimes-of-operation.md`).
- **`AVE-<Repo>/` targets** resolve against the sibling-repo umbrella dir and classify `broken inter` — warn under the default `--inter-repo warn`, same semantics as md inter-repo links (siblings are legitimately absent on a fresh CI checkout).
- **Split cites** `\texttt{prefix-} \kbleaf{tail}` are flagged as gating `split kbleaf`: the tail alone resolves against the wrong leaf or nothing. Live example repaired in commit 1: the vol9 ch12 `H_infty` row's tail `hubble-tension.md` **false-resolved** against `vol2/nuclear-field/ch10-open-problems/hubble-tension.md` while the cited claims (`clm-2e9j97`, `clm-wx5324`) live in vol3's `lattice-genesis-hubble-tension.md`.
- **Waivers reconcile, not declare.** `WAIVED_KBLEAF` holds adjudicated report-don't-fix `(source, argument)` pairs; a waiver that stops matching a live dead cite fails as `stale kbleaf waiver`, so the list cannot outlive its subject.

## Repairs (commit 1)

| Site | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| vol9 ch02:79 | `src/ave/core/scale_invariant.py` | `src/ave/axioms/scale_invariant.py` (unique file, wrong dir) |
| vol9 ch12:120 | `\texttt{lattice-genesis-} \kbleaf{hubble-tension.md}` | merged single cite (was false-passing to the vol2 leaf) |
| vol9 ch12:123, :124 | `\texttt{omega-freeze-} \kbleaf{cosmic-grain-cascade.md}` | merged single cites (tail resolved to nothing) |
| vol9 ch16:173 | `vol_0_engineering_compendium/backmatter/ch7-universal-saturation-kernel.tex` (never existed) | `backmatter/07_universal_saturation_kernel.tex` (input by the Vol 0 manifest) |
| vol9 ch07:180, ch15:48 | `vol_ponder/chapters/04_ponder_05_dc_biased_quartz.tex` (resolves nowhere intra-repo) | qualified `AVE-PONDER/manuscript/...` (prose already names the sibling repo) |
| backmatter ch7:148 | `ave-kb/...vol_virtual_media/ch12-sigmoid-saturation.tex` | `AVE-VirtualMedia/manuscript/vol_virtual_media/chapters/12_sigmoid_saturation.tex` (KB vol8 activation-geometry tree was removed from this repo) |

## Report-don't-fix (1 item, needs adjudication)

**`manuscript/vol_2_subatomic/chapters/06_electroweak_and_higgs.tex:370`** — "Four lemmas are proven from Axioms 1 and 4 (see `\kbleaf{p2.9b_goldstone_proof.md}`)". The target **never existed in tracked history** (`git log --all` has no such path; commit 48e62baf shows the P2.9b Goldstone derivation landed via a gitignored `.agents/handoffs/` session artifact + the chapter itself). Repointing needs a judgment about the correct canonical anchor for the four-lemma Goldstone derivation (a vol2 KB leaf? re-anchor to the chapter's own proof body? mint a leaf?). Carried as a tracked `WAIVED_KBLEAF` entry (warn-only, stale-guarded) until adjudicated.

## Validation

- Live-fire on the pre-fix tree: **981 cites checked, 32 non-path args skipped, 7 dead + 3 split found** — exactly the survey set, no false positives (the previously-dead tail-shorthand cites `figures/gen_*.py`, `ch01-gravity-yield/...`, `ch11-experimental-bench-falsification/...`, `regime_1_linear/hexagonal_lattice.py` all resolve under suffix matching).
- Post-fix tree: **0 gating / 1 waived**, exit 0.
- `make test-tools`: 308 passed (4 new tests + `texcheck` fixture tree; fixtures stay excluded from real crawls and from the target index).
- Full `make verify`: ALL PHYSICS PROTOCOLS PASSED (both commits individually gated by the precommit hook).

author: jasoneplumb
body:
## Summary

Implements #181: a step-by-step first-time setup guide with screenshots that sets customer expectations for what appears on the device, the phone, and the website at each step — published as a web page linked from the landing page and as a single downloadable PDF, both stamped with the release version.

## Changes

- **`packages/web/src/setup-guide/content.ts`** — single source of truth: 6 steps (power-on → join `InfoBento-XXXX` → captive portal Wi-Fi + Device ID → claim at `/pair/:code` → design → reset), each with instruction text and per-surface "what you'll see" expectations. Copy verified against shipped behavior (`gen-reset-screen.ts`, `integrated.ino`, `pair.ts`).
- **`packages/web/setup-guide.html` + `src/setup-guide/page.ts` + `setup-guide.css`** — second Vite entry rendering the guide; no sign-in required; footer shows `InfoBento v<version>` via the existing `__APP_VERSION__` define; links to the PDF.
- **`packages/web/index.html` / `style.css`** — visible "Setup Guide" link in the landing/editor header.
- **`packages/api/src/server.ts`** — friendly `/setup-guide` route in the production static block.
- **`scripts/gen-setup-guide-pdf.ts`** (new, pdfkit dev-dep) — builds `dist/setup-guide.pdf` from the same content module; release version (root `package.json`) + page number in the footer of **every** PDF page. Runs via the web build script.
- **`scripts/gen-reset-screen.ts`** — now always emits `public/setup-guide/device-setup-screen.png` from the same framebuffer baked into the firmware, so the guide image cannot drift from the device (firmware headers unchanged, byte-identical).
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — web bundle built via `npm run build -w @infobento/web` so the PDF ships to production.
- **Screenshots** (`packages/web/public/setup-guide/`) — captive portal (reconstructed from the firmware's exact HTML), pair page + editor (captured from the running app), sample pairing sticker (from `gen-stickers`).

## Test plan

- New `content.test.ts`: structure invariants, image files exist with alt text, expectation-setting copy covers refresh cadence + captive portal + fallback IP.
- Full quality gate green locally: `npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm test (455 passed) && npm run lint && npm run format:check`.

FEAT-PC013 built red-first over the audited substrate. **Migration `20260704192549`** (applied to dev + repaired): 3 new SECURITY DEFINER contracts + 1 internal helper + 1 replacement-in-place + 1 additive read amendment + 2 policy drops. **No new table, no trigger changes.** Consumed next by FEAT-H016 (no migration of its own).

Nothing in v2 called the legacy body (`admin_exit_user_from_platform` inlines its own tracks). Legacy refusal strings leaked group existence — refusals now follow the house map (P0002 no-leak).
2. **Member-exit DELETE policies dropped (Open Q2).** `memberships_delete_leave` + `memberships_delete_remove` — the raw paths bypassed the enrolment freeze, orphaned `user_group_roles` rows, and let a sole Steward strand a group headless. Contracts are now the only client-role exits. **Audit:** 6 policies remain on `group_memberships`; the admin pair (`gm_delete_admin`/`gm_insert_admin`) intact and integration-asserted via a promoted platform admin. Pre-drop bypass demonstrated red first.
3. **Paused-row visibility (Open Q3).** `membership_status` rides the members payload; paused rows render only for `pause_members`/`activate_members`/`remove_members` holders. **Build finding folded in:** management keys now also imply member-list visibility itself (the minimal-permission pauser persona could otherwise pause blind) — spec amended.
4. **Self-target refused on pause/remove (Open Q4).** `P0001` — leave is the self-exit path.

### Also for the gate
- **AC amendment at build start:** non-engagement group ids resolve `P0002` (visibility precedes the type check — the original AC's `P0001` would have made group ids enumerable). Spec updated with the amendment note.
- **Guards the triggers can't express:** last-**active**-Steward counting (`active_steward_count`, internal-only — no client execute) refuses pausing/removing/leaving past the last active Steward; a **paused Steward is not cover** (the raw-role-count trigger would accept it) — all three matrices integration-asserted.

- **Direct-caller answer (ADR-U038):** post-drop, a direct PostgREST caller — including an anonymous-session Mist — can do nothing to `group_memberships` the contracts refuse, beyond the pre-existing DeusEx-walled admin policies. Direct UPDATE-to-paused and both direct DELETEs asserted refused; PC012's decline asserted policy-independent.
- **Labelled honestly:** regular-leave cascade asserts were green against the legacy body (carried-forward behaviour); one in-flight test-expectation correction (Tier-1 platform-baseline permissions are context-free and survive a group pause — the group-scoped grant is what goes dark, asserted).

author: qiaeru
body:
Fixes from a full review of the server and client code: three data-affecting bugs, several robustness and accessibility gaps, and a few build and CI corrections.

## Data integrity

- Migrations now run with foreign keys disabled and check referential integrity before committing. Rebuild-style migrations used to fire ON DELETE CASCADE when dropping the old table: migration 002 wiped bans and history on every instance that upgraded through it. Verified empirically: a database with only 001 applied plus user data now goes through 002-005 with all rows intact.
- Undo after a draw is now durable. The toast undo only reverted local state while the action had already been flushed, so the entry returned on the next state load. Undo now purges the pending outbox item and issues an idempotent `DELETE /api/history/:clientUuid` (new route, covered offline through the outbox).
- Local Docker builds no longer bake `server/var/` (dev database) into the image; `.dockerignore` patterns are context-root-relative so `var/` did not cover it.

## Behavior fixes

- Expired lockouts reset the failed-attempt counter; previously one wrong password re-locked the account for another 15 minutes, indefinitely.
- The demo account acknowledges locale changes without persisting them, so one visitor's choice no longer leaks to the next.
- The SPA router discards renders overtaken by a newer navigation instead of overwriting the newer view.
- A pending pile-launch timer is cancelled on unmount so quick navigation is no longer yanked to the draw screen.
- The Settings change-password dialog is rebuilt on `withModal()`: Escape, backdrop click, focus trap, and focus restore now work like the other dialogs.
- The forced first-login password meter follows the server policy instead of hardcoded thresholds.

## Maintenance

- CI installs the root dependencies before the license check; the step previously inspected an empty tree.
- Service worker: manifest precached, dead background-sync plumbing removed, `/api/cards` cache exemption made exact.
- Migration 005 drops the redundant `idx_users_username` and indexes `bans.card_id` for the delete cascades.
- Backup docs now cover WAL mode (copy the `-wal`/`-shm` companions, or stop the container first).

## Expected behaviors after merge

- Undoing a ban or return survives a reload, online and offline.
- A user whose lockout expired gets 10 fresh attempts.
- Existing instances upgrade cleanly; migration 005 applies on boot.
- Wrong-screen flashes during rapid navigation are gone.

Verified locally: syntax checks on all touched files, a migration regression test (v1.0-shaped database with data upgraded through all migrations without loss), and 10 API tests against a live dev server (lockout reset, demo locale guard, history delete) all pass.

body:
**Answers the user's question: which agent should author our UK content (we AUTHOR, not translate)?** gpt-5.5 tends to go solo — this gives the data to delegate.

**Method:** new deterministic scorer `scripts/audit/probe_uk_writing_score.py` (reuses `content_surface_gates` + `_judge_eval_lib` + `vesum` — VESUM validity, russicism rate minus heritage attestation, per-level immersion policy; no LLM) + test. 5 candidates (codex/agy/claude/deepseek/cursor) × 3 profiles (A2 English-support, B1–C2 pure, seminar), identical brief.

**Result — all 5 wrote 0-russicism, 95–100%-VESUM UK content across all profiles → gpt-5.5 is not uniquely best; delegate:**
| Profile | Recommended |
|---|---|
| A1–A2 English-support | **agy** (best immersion voice) ≈ **codex** |
| B1–C2 pure | **codex ≈ agy ≈ claude** |
| Seminars | **deepseek** (most scholarly) ≈ **agy** |

⚠️ **cursor**: usable UK but emits non-canonical apostrophes (U+2019) + text-dependent russicism («перекатні») → keep a VESUM/normalization gate.

**Caught 2 scorer bugs mid-run** that would have produced a WRONG ranking (a fair reminder to verify the instrument, not just the output): apostrophe-variant false-russicisms (cursor U+2019 vs VESUM U+0027 — falsely showed '5 russicisms') and junk tokens (`---`/ХХІ). Both fixed + regression-tested.

Report: `audit/2026-07-04-uk-writing-probe/REPORT.md`. Updates the served `model-assignment.md` UK-content row with the bakeoff-backed ranking. Honest caveat noted: claude is a candidate (self-judgment) — deterministic numbers are unbiased; a blind panel could refine subjective ordering.

author: xxxluckyxxxx
body:
## Water (der Brunnen bugt nicht mehr)

The old fountain was two coplanar stone boxes with two coplanar water slabs flush on top — three z-fights at once ("verschwindet, man erkennt die 2 Wassertexturen"). Rebuilt:

- **True octagonal basin**: 8 rim wall segments with staggered course heights — no two overlapping stone faces share a plane anywhere in the fountain (bowl tops AND bottoms staggered too).
- **Real animated water** (new FRAG3 water mode): a sunken pool disc with concentric ripple rings radiating from where the overflow lands, fresnel-weighted sky reflection that follows the weather, pinprick sun glitter (tight lobe — a broad one whitewashed the whole pool), foam lapping at the rim, a painted basin floor seen through the surface, and 4 falling overflow streams from the brim-full upper bowl.
- **Robust on real GPUs**: uTime wraps seamlessly at 10π (every shader frequency is a multiple of 0.2 → integer cycles) so fp16/mediump GPUs never quantize the animation; the churn ring avoids `pow()` on a negative base (undefined in GLSL ES 1.00); water draws before enemies so a zombie in front of the fountain covers it.

## Navigation (Zombies bleiben nicht mehr stecken)

Zombies used to steer greedily and wedge on the B196+ fences, gardens and market stalls. New system:

- **Flow field**: a 123×123 walkability grid (0.6 m cells, same blocking rules as enemy steering, zombie-radius inflated) + a BFS distance field flooded from the player every 0.45 s / 0.9 m of movement. Closed doors overlay as temporary walls; diagonals can't cut blocked corners.
- **Movement**: zombies descend the field (smooth weighted-gradient heading, old greedy probe kept as local polish), and lunge straight when close with a clear line.
- **Anti-stuck watchdog**: per-enemy progress checks every 1.2 s — a sideways shove first; if still wedged >4 s, far away AND out of view, a quiet relocation.
- **Spawn hygiene**: spawn/leash points reject nav-unreachable pockets (e.g. the sealed fountain basin), softening after 20 tries so a player barricaded indoors still gets a wave outside.

## Verification (blind ship)

- All 17 existing reflective harnesses green (village, shadows, windows, editor, …).
- New **NavTest**: 97 % outdoor cell coverage; doors gate 19/19 interiors (closed=0 reachable, open=19); fountain basin sealed; **12/12 simulated zombies** reach the player through the real `navFlowDir`/`steerDir`/`collide` code path.
- New **WaterTest**: zero coplanar overlapping fountain faces, pool clearances, well-formed 408-vert water mesh, shader branch dispatch.
- All 6 shader programs compile+link in a real WebGL1 (GLSL ES 1.00) context; the water branch was rendered with the real shader in headless Chromium across three uTime samples and visually tuned over four iterations.
- Adversarial multi-agent review over the diff; confirmed findings (negative-base pow, fp16 uTime, draw order) fixed before build.

Build 202, signed with the standing key (SHA-256 `258b1f2f…02061`) — installs straight over any previous build.

## Summary

Design spec for Phase 3 — grocery lists. Following the phase 2 pattern (spec first, then a separate implementation-plan PR).

- Materialized `grocery_lists` + `grocery_list_items` tables; multiple concurrent lists.
- Derived items aggregated from schedule entries in \`[start, end]\` where \`meal_id IS NOT NULL AND eating_out = false\`, both defaults and overrides.
- Canonical unit normalization (string map — no unit conversion).
- Regenerate-merge: overwrites derived quantities; preserves manual rows and check-off state where the key still matches.
- "At the store" view grouped by ingredient category.
- Read-while-offline for grocery detail, calendar, and meal detail (SW StaleWhileRevalidate).
- Check-off writes queued via \`workbox-background-sync\` — the only write that queues offline in v1.
- Carry-over: unchecked items copied to a target list as manual rows.

## Design decisions to confirm during review

Locked from our conversation:

- Many concurrent lists supported; usually one active.
- Preset date ranges (this week / next week) + custom.
- Display-text-only ingredients → \"Miscellaneous\" section (rendered verbatim under \"other\").
- Unit normalization ON; no unit conversion.
- Regenerate overwrites derived quantities.
- Group by category; custom aisle order deferred.
- Offline: cache calendar + meal + grocery detail; queue check-off writes.

Defaults I picked for the unanswered questions — please flag if any feel wrong:

- **Carry-over is in scope** as a one-button action (§8). Cheap once manual-add exists.
- **Which schedule rows feed the list:** defaults + all overrides. Each \`(schedule_entry, meal)\` contributes the meal's full ingredient list once. No per-serving math in v1 (§5, revisit §16).
- **Eat-out rows** are excluded (obviously).

## Notes

- Phase 2's docs landed directly on \`main\`, but your global rules say never commit to main — hence the PR. Same content-only, docs-only shape.
- No code changes; the spec references a wire-up item in \`next.config.ts\` (the existing \`runtimeCaching\` block has a \`grocery-list\` placeholder pattern that this phase replaces).

author: miacorindolf
body:
## The diagnosed deepest gap
The accurate-FSM JEM event histogram proves **CHILI is TRIM-BIASED**: `live_sell_into_strength` ×556, `live_ofi_exhaustion_lock` ×556, `live_trail_ratchet` ×14 — but **`live_pyramid_add` / `live_pullback_add_fill` / micropullback = 0**. It shrinks a runner Ross grows (JEM +$121 vs Ross +$46k on the same name). **Not entry, not cooldown — the lack of laddering** (adds never fire while trims fire constantly) is why CHILI << Ross on a big runner.

## Fix
Flip `chili_momentum_pyramid_enabled` default `False → True`. The confirmation-pyramid is **risk-NEUTRAL by design**: adds only when `cushion >= min_cushion_r*R0` (default **1.0R banked**) AND new-HOD AND OFI thrust AND `stop>=breakeven`, and `pyramid_blend` re-bases the #769 max-loss circuit to the **starter R0** so the enlarged worst-case stays **≤ R0** (INVARIANT-A; stop only tightens). An add is funded by realized cushion, never new risk → default-ON is safe.

## Accurate-FSM proof (real `tick_live_session`)
The historical windows have sparse L2 depth so the pyramid OFI reads None → validated with a **live-representative OFI substitute** (the condition that holds live, where the depth bridge now covers 120 names). Laddering is net-positive on **both** a runner and a whipsaw name:

| Symbol | trim-only | + pyramid | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| JEM (runner) | +$121.56 | **+$160.33** | **+$38.77** |
| CELZ (whipsaw) | +$100.48 | **+$127.73** | **+$27.25** |

Kill-switch `CHILI_MOMENTUM_PYRAMID_ENABLED=0` = byte-identical baseline (verified: JEM reverts to exactly +$121.56).

⚠️ The +$27–39 are OFI-sim **upper bounds**; live real-OFI selectivity (skips false-HOD adds) will refine — confirm via live A/B (the kill-switch is the safety net). Stacks on #842 (timer) + #843 (buyers-confirm).

body:
## Relevant issues

Stacked on #31772 (the token-exchange config UI/API PR); its base is that branch and it retargets down the stack as the parents merge. This completes the frontend/API parity for the `entra_obo` backend added in #31983 (LIT-4163): that PR taught the token-exchange arm Microsoft Entra's On-Behalf-Of dialect, but the profile could only be set through config.yaml

## Linear ticket

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy on `localhost:4000` backed by Postgres (master key `sk-1234`). Create an entra_obo server and an rfc8693 (default) server through the API, then read them back and inspect the DB column

```
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"server_name":"entra_demo","url":"https://graph.microsoft.com/mcp","transport":"http","auth_type":"oauth2_token_exchange","token_exchange_profile":"entra_obo","token_exchange_endpoint":"https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token","credentials":{"client_id":"entra-app-id","client_secret":"entra-secret","scopes":["api://graph/.default"]}}'
# [201]

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"server_name":"rfc_demo","url":"https://up.example.com/mcp","transport":"http","auth_type":"oauth2_token_exchange","token_exchange_endpoint":"https://idp.example.com/oauth2/token","credentials":{"client_id":"cid","client_secret":"sec"}}'
# [201]
```

The DB column holds the selected dialect for the entra server and stays null for the default, and the read path fills in rfc8693 for the null case

```
SELECT server_name, auth_type, token_exchange_profile FROM "LiteLLM_MCPServerTable" WHERE server_name IN ('entra_demo','rfc_demo');
 server_name |       auth_type       | token_exchange_profile
-------------+-----------------------+------------------------
 entra_demo  | oauth2_token_exchange | entra_obo
 rfc_demo    | oauth2_token_exchange |

GET /v1/mcp/server
 entra_demo -> token_exchange_profile = 'entra_obo'
 rfc_demo   -> token_exchange_profile = 'rfc8693'
```

Dashboard: at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers, Add New MCP Server, pick Streamable HTTP, choose auth type "OAuth Token Exchange (OBO)", then set Profile to "Microsoft Entra OBO". The Scope field becomes required (hinting api://<app-id>/.default) and Audience/Subject Token Type hide since that dialect ignores them; fill Client ID/Secret and a scope, then create

### Dashboard Profile selector (before / after)

Rendered from the real create-form components on the parent branch head `ff6dc33291` (before) vs this PR's head `de8debc750` (after), same steps each time: Add New MCP Server, Streamable HTTP, auth type "OAuth Token Exchange (OBO)"

Before (parent #31772): the token-exchange section has no dialect control, so a dashboard user can only ever create an rfc8693 server

![before: token-exchange section with no Profile control](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..b6ejgVWLMfmbGIUaf43mEotisd9IQ2TNR4a4hB2W1xk)

After: a Profile dropdown appears, defaulting to "RFC 8693 (standard)" with the standard Audience, Subject Token Type and optional Scopes fields intact

![after: Profile dropdown defaulting to RFC 8693, standard fields intact](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..EuQtAE2b6sr_4nFVTGv8MCyHZSya-HRUGcJ-nWUojSg)

The dropdown offers the two wire dialects

![after: Profile dropdown open showing RFC 8693 and Microsoft Entra OBO](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..Ejhh-aMjLSI-dKQk7jhrIr-kQh2LIyRFWvO-iBE4RWM)

After, Microsoft Entra OBO selected: Audience and Subject Token Type disappear (that dialect ignores them) and Scopes flips to required with the `api://<app-id>/.default` hint

![after: Microsoft Entra OBO selected, Audience/Subject Token Type hidden, Scopes required](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..7ALb3rwYsZ-AjppD_CAWPFh0cjLTYVkm6J-TL3kehx8)

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Changes

The token-exchange arm supports two wire dialects through `token_exchange_profile`: `rfc8693` (the default standard token-exchange grant) and `entra_obo` (Microsoft Entra On-Behalf-Of, the RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant with `requested_token_use=on_behalf_of`). The backend already reads it from config.yaml and the credentials blob, but the create/update REST API and the dashboard had no way to set it, so dashboard and API users could only ever create rfc8693 servers. This surfaces the selector, completing the parity the parent PR started for the other token-exchange fields

`token_exchange_profile` becomes a dedicated column on `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable`, mirroring the sibling fields exactly. It is added to `NewMCPServerRequest`/`UpdateMCPServerRequest`, read column-first in `build_mcp_server_from_table` with the credentials blob as a back-compat fallback and a default of `rfc8693`, and carried through both runtime-to-table builders so a registry round-trip preserves it. Although it is a non-secret dialect selector, it is scrubbed from non-admin and virtual-key responses like every other token-exchange setting: those views receive no token-exchange config at all, matching the uniformity rule #31772 settled on for `subject_token_type`

On the dashboard a Profile dropdown is added to the token-exchange section. Selecting Microsoft Entra OBO makes the scope required, since that dialect carries the target resource in the scope and the exchanger fails closed without one, and hides Audience and Subject Token Type since the Entra dialect ignores them

Tests cover the profile column read, the credentials-blob fallback, the rfc8693 default, the table round-trip

author: henshaw
body:
## What

Adds **Title** and **Description** fields to the top of the SEO section on Posts and Pages — above Schema Page Type — in both the block editor's document-sidebar panel and the classic meta box.

## Behavior

- **Live defaults.** Title is pre-filled with the post title; Description with the AI-written summary when one exists, otherwise the manual excerpt — the exact values the front end uses. Until a field is manually edited, it tracks its source in real time in the editor.
- **Overrides.** A manual edit stores an override in the existing `_coywolf_seo` post meta (a value matching its default is not stored, mirroring the canonical field's pattern). Overrides flow to the title tag, meta description, `og:title`/`og:description`, and the schema `WebPage.name`/`Article.headline`/descriptions via `managed_title()` / `source_description()`.
- **Hidden where they don't apply.** "Exclude meta description" hides the Description field; the static front page and posts page hide both fields (their title/description come from Site Details, so an override would be silently ignored). Hidden fields preserve stored overrides on save.

## Hardening (from the adversarial review round)

A 17-agent review workflow was run on the initial diff; every confirmed finding is fixed and regression-tested:

- **Classic-save stale-default trap (high):** each field's render-time default rides in a hidden input; save() compares sanitized-vs-sanitized against both the render-time and current defaults. Renaming a post, editing the excerpt, an async AI summary landing mid-edit, kses'd excerpt markup, or a double-spaced title can no longer pin a phantom override.
- **Schema consistency (high):** `WebPage.name` and `Article.headline` now use `managed_title()`, so JSON-LD can't contradict the title tag on overridden posts.
- **Clear-then-retype (medium):** a per-field focus draft keeps a cleared field empty while typing instead of re-filling it with the default mid-keystroke.
- **REST sanitization (medium):** `register_post_meta` now has a `sanitize_callback` mirroring the classic-path sanitizers, so block-editor writes store clean values (previously raw).
- **Force-rewrite titles (low):** replacement now via `preg_replace_callback`, so titles like "Save $25" survive literally instead of being eaten as PCRE backreferences.
- **Help-text accuracy (low):** names the AI-written description as the default when that feature is on; notes the appended site name when that setting is on.

## Verification

- `php -l` + `node --check` clean; Plugin Check reports no findings in the changed files.
- **7/7 front-end assertions** (wp70-test, real HTTP): defaults track title/excerpt; overrides replace them in `<title>`, meta description, `og:title`, `og:description`, and JSON-LD name/headline/description.
- **11/11 classic-save regression tests** (`wp eval-file`): rename trap, real override, HTML-excerpt phantom, double-space phantom, REST sanitize, preserve-when-hidden, `$25`/`$0` force-rewrite.
- Block editor via headless preview: field order, live-default tracking, override persistence, clear-then-retype, exclude-setting hiding, front-page/posts-page hiding.

author: aditya01889
body:
## The actual root cause (reproduced in a real browser)

This is the bug that survived PRs #17–#20. Every earlier fix targeted the wrong layer because the failure was silent. I reproduced it with a Playwright test that loads `/ingredients` logged-in and captured the real error:

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access '_ingMatrix' before initialization
```

A **temporal dead zone (TDZ)**. The `_ing*` state variables (`_ingMatrix`, `_ingOrders`, `_ingSelected`, …) were declared with `let` *after* the `checkLogin()` IIFE in the script.

- On a **browser refresh** onto `/ingredients`, `checkLogin()` runs *during* initial script execution → `showApp()` → `loadIngredientTab()` → `loadIngMatrix()`, which reads `_ingMatrix` **before** its `let` declaration is reached → throws. Because `loadIngOrders()` is `async`, the throw surfaced as an **unhandled promise rejection** (no red error anywhere), so the tab just sat on "Loading orders…" forever.
- On a normal tab **click**, the whole script had already finished running, so the variables existed — no TDZ. That's exactly why the bug was **refresh-only** and why it was so hard to pin down.

## Fix

1. **Move the `_ing*` declarations above the `checkLogin()` IIFE** — eliminates the TDZ. This is the core fix.
2. **Harden the order sort**: `String(a.billNo || '').localeCompare(...)` — a purely numeric bill number from Sheets comes back as a JS number, and `.localeCompare` on a number throws. Latent second crash, now defused.
3. **Regression test** (`tests/ingredients-refresh.spec.js`): loads `/ingredients` while logged in, asserts the orders render and there are **no uncaught errors / unhandled rejections**. Fails on the old code, passes on the fix.

This pull request introduces a full-featured scene graph to the raytracer, enabling hierarchical grouping of objects and more flexible scene manipulation. The main changes include the addition of a new `ASceneObject` base class for scene nodes, a `Group` node type, and comprehensive support for parent-child relationships, local/world transforms, and scene graph flattening. The `Scene` class is extended with methods for adding groups, reparenting nodes, and maintaining a list of top-level roots, with all relevant interfaces updated accordingly.

**Scene graph system and node hierarchy:**
* Added new abstract base class `ASceneObject` providing parent/child links, local/world transforms, and default implementations for scene-graph operations. (`srcs/common/scene/ASceneObject.hpp`, `srcs/common/scene/ASceneObject.cpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-79b29769171fe279769ab8de3453d4027ae659fbbf1772a6d89ec4a87d381610R1-R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a6165636a503fb5ae623eb1de7ce85845d7b76a7fa2e55d53a2cdfac134da7e2R1-R76)
* Introduced `Group` node type (inheriting from `ASceneObject`) to represent transformable, non-geometry scene-graph groups. (`srcs/core/scene/Group.hpp`)
* Updated `IPrimitive` and `ILight` to inherit virtually from `ISceneObject` for proper multiple inheritance with `ASceneObject`. (`srcs/common/scene/IPrimitive.hpp`, `srcs/common/scene/ILight.hpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed24ff88eb7ac92c3f45be280fe8eeb6ee94af97c15cc3f16214fb930dffee5bL33-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cf1e9cb7e0285127e07ada0c1cd65d233e4d04b8f53893e4e238a450c8f8b42cL20-R20)
* Extended `ISceneObject` interface with parent/child management, local transform accessors, and a new `GROUP` object type. (`srcs/common/scene/ISceneObject.hpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fdb4cc40a7fcda95c4d32c3b769010a9c2505c5da01dae4e0a3a92a618139f31R7-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fdb4cc40a7fcda95c4d32c3b769010a9c2505c5da01dae4e0a3a92a618139f31R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fdb4cc40a7fcda95c4d32c3b769010a9c2505c5da01dae4e0a3a92a618139f31R28-R30) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-fdb4cc40a7fcda95c4d32c3b769010a9c2505c5da01dae4e0a3a92a618139f31R44-R63)

**Scene management and graph operations:**
* `Scene` now maintains a list of top-level roots, supports adding groups, and provides robust reparenting logic that preserves world transforms and prevents cycles. (`srcs/core/scene/Scene.cpp`, `srcs/common/scene/IScene.hpp`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-271a9163d23be18bef9127ce0a9bae034ab4d336d2f3477c08e34c2a97800006R24-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-271a9163d23be18bef9127ce0a9bae034ab4d336d2f3477c08e34c2a97800006R49-R52) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1995e8beba4986abcd5cf3cd9b2614681a819d248b6e698c866df2e928813e2dR43-R161)
* Implemented scene-graph flattening: before BVH construction, local transforms are recursively composed into world transforms for all objects. (`srcs/core/scene/Scene.cpp`)

**Math and utility functions:**
* Added per-component degree-to-radian conversion and a mathematically correct inverse rotation function to `Vector3f` utilities, supporting transform composition and decomposition. (`srcs/common/Vector.hpp`)
* Added component-wise multiply/divide helpers for transform math. (`srcs/core/scene/Scene.cpp`)

**File and build system updates:**
* Registered new source files in the build system. (`Makefile`)

These changes collectively enable hierarchical scene editing, grouping, and transform inheritance, laying the groundwork for advanced features like outliner panels and group manipulation in the editor.

author: jinbe
body:
Follow-up to the add-project modal (#97). Adds an optional Repo URL field so you can register a repo you don't have locally yet: deck clones it and registers the result in one step.

## Behaviour

The path field is dual-purpose:

- **No repo URL**: unchanged. The path is an existing directory, registered as-is (`POST /api/projects`).
- **Repo URL set**: the path is a parent directory (must already exist). deck derives the repo name from the URL, clones into `<parent>/<repoName>`, then registers that. The name auto-fills to the repo name until you edit it, and there's a live preview of where it will clone.

## Server

New `POST /api/projects/clone`:

- Validates the parent against the picker boundary ($HOME or a project root, the same boundary the path picker already uses for not-yet-registered dirs). The derived dest sits under the parent, so it's covered too.
- Rejects unsafe URL schemes: only https / ssh / git / scp-style pass. That blocks the `ext::sh -c` transport trick, `file://`, bare/local paths, and option-like values.
- Clones synchronously via `git clone -- <url> <dest>` (positionals after `--`, both args asserted flag-safe, no shell).
- On failure registers nothing and returns the git stderr; an existing non-empty or already-registered dest is a 409.

The existing `POST /api/projects` is untouched.

## Notes

- `repoNameFromUrl` and `isCloneUrlSafe` are pure and node-free (`$lib/repo-url`), shared by the modal and the route, and unit-tested. `cloneRepo` is covered against a real local repo.
- Out of scope for v1: depth / single-branch / submodule options, streaming clone progress, `file://` / local-path clones.

`pnpm check` and `pnpm test` pass.

Closes #96

author: lcj-claude-coder
body:
## What & why

Pure internal consolidation + micro-optimization inside `rust/sensorwatch-cli`,
with **zero observable behavior change** except one narrow, pre-approved caveat
(below). It collapses the five cross-module duplications the LEO-337 `report`
review flagged and takes the four cheap streaming/allocation wins — all
deferred, non-blocking cleanup that was batched so the `report` PR could land
correctness-first. No new dependencies; MSRV 1.82 unchanged.

Blocked-by: LEO-337 (merged). Related: LEO-345 (cost flow), LEO-349 (DuckDB
deep-analysis surface, sequenced later).

## The nine items

**Cross-module de-duplication**
- **A** — `filter_label`: `snapshot`'s and `report`'s verbatim 10-arm match over
  `cli::TypeFilter` collapse into one `labels::filter_label`, with a drift-guard
  unit test pinning it in lockstep with `CANONICAL_LABELS`.
- **B** — JSON render: `digest::render_json` and `snapshot::render`'s
  compact/`PrettyFormatter` body extract into `render::to_json_string`.
- **C** — filename builder: `digest::candidate_files` and `logger::log_path` now
  share `logger::daily_file_path`, so the `sensors_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` writer and
  the `report` reader can't drift.
- **D** — config+rules loader: `report.rs` and `watch.rs` share
  `Config::load_rules_and_config`; the divergent no-config arms stay at the
  callers by design.
- **H** — integration-test harness: the 4th copy of `sensorwatch()` /
  `run_bounded()` / `TempDir` / `write_config` consolidates into
  `tests/common/mod.rs`. Two gotchas fixed: `run_bounded` now drains
  stdout/stderr concurrently (the old poll-then-drain **deadlocked on >~64 KB
  stdout**), and the `violation_cap` test switches to it as living proof; and
  the test `MAX_LINE_BYTES` is single-sourced (see I).
- **I** — `MAX_LINE_BYTES` moves to `src/limits.rs`; `replay.rs` and the
  `report_cli` oversized-line fixture both reference the one const (via `#[path]`
  include) so the fixture can't silently stop probing the real cap.

**Streaming / allocation efficiency**
- **F** — `Aggregator::observe` drops its per-sample `HashSet`, adopting the
  engine's `last_seen`-stamp pattern.
- **G** — `report` gains a leading-timestamp precheck: an out-of-window line
  whose canonical `{"timestamp": "` prefix parses is dropped without
  materializing its readings. `watch --replay` never sets a window and is
  unchanged.
- **E** — `fit()` binary-searches the smallest fitting drop count instead of
  re-rendering once per dropped item (O(n²) → ~⌈log₂ n⌉ renders), byte-identical.

Suggested review order matches the commit sequence: (1) H+I, (2) A+B+C, (3) D,
(4) F, (5) G, (6) E — each commit compiles and `cargo test --workspace` is green.

## Scope decisions (pre-approved, TICKET decisions 1–2 — not relitigated)

1. **Item 6 narrowed to shared-read-only.** The shared loader reads the file
   once; **both parsers stay as-is**. `rules.rs` deliberately parses raw text so
   `toml::de::Error` keeps line/column spans, while `config.rs` walks a
   `toml::Table` for warn-and-fall-back leniency; deserializing rules from a
   pre-parsed `Value` would drop spans on semantic errors (a stderr regression).
   Documented in the loader; no parser changed.
2. **Item 7 ships the full precheck with ONE approved semantics caveat.** A
   *syntactically valid but semantically invalid* out-of-window line (e.g.
   missing the `sensors` key) is now skipped **uncounted**, where before it
   incremented `skipped_lines`. Everything else is exact: invalid-JSON garbage
   and Python-token lines fall through to the full parse, so garbage is still
   counted with the same reason and out-of-window fixup records are still
   window-dropped by `report`. Hostile-input-only edge; pinned by a unit test,
   with the no-window (`watch`) path proven to still count the line.

## No-behavior-change evidence

- **Frozen contracts pass untouched:** snapshot byte-lock tests, logger
  golden/rotation/retention tests, jsonl key-order test, digest fit tests,
  `report_cli` exact-bytes tests, replay golden round-trip.
- **Test counts:** CLI crate `199` lib unit tests (+ new: labels drift guard,
  4 replay caveat/precheck tests, `leading_timestamp` test, `fit == naive_fit`
  oracle sweep) and `42` integration tests (report 22 / watch 11 / log 4 /
  snapshot 5) all green. `fit()`'s old one-drop-at-a-time loop is kept as a
  `#[cfg(test)]` `naive_fit` oracle and a sweep test asserts `fit == naive_fit`
  byte-for-byte (both the Ok strings and the terminal Err string).
- **A/B determinism harness** (master vs branch release binaries, byte-diffing
  stdout/stderr/exit over golden logs + a synthetic multi-day dir with gaps,
  a violation, an intra-sample duplicate reading, in-window NaN/CRLF/oversized
  hostile lines, and out-of-window padding lines): **byte-identical** for
  `report` compact/`--indent 2`/small `--max-bytes` (exercises E)/`--type`
  (A)/`--match`, all with absolute windows; for the golden logs; for the three
  **D error paths** (missing config, unreadable config, malformed rules TOML —
  stderr byte-identical); and for `watch --replay` (same event, exit 10). The
  **only** diff is the item-7 caveat input (out-of-window, valid JSON, missing
  `sensors`): master `"skipped_lines":1`, branch `"skipped_lines":0`, rest of
  the digest byte-identical — exactly the approved delta.
- **Live host run** (real machine, HWiNFO running): branch `snapshot` returns
  live sensor JSON; a master-vs-branch A/B of `report` over the real
  `sensors_*.jsonl` logs (compact, `--indent 2`, a fit-forcing `--max-bytes`,
  `--type`, `--last 7d`) is **byte-identical**; a `watch --replay` of the PSU-sag
  series fires exit 10 with a real spooled critical event.
- Local gates green: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo +1.82.0 check
  --workspace --all-targets --locked`.

## Documentation surfaces checked (checklist §1)

Internal refactor — no CLI/flag/exit-code/output/config change, so the docs
table does not apply and no `SKILL.md` recipe changes. I grepped
`skipped_lines` across `README.md`, `skills/sensorwatch/SKILL.md`, and the crate
READMEs: the only prose description (`SKILL.md`: "malformed lines the parser
dropped") stays accurate — the item-7 caveat is a hostile-input-only counting
edge below that altitude, so **no docs affected**.

## Deferred

Nothing new. Out of scope per the ticket: any change to digest/snapshot output
bytes or the CLI contract beyond the item-7 caveat; fixture unification across
test files (the `watch_cli` and `report_cli` series are deliberately different).

## What & why

WS1 of the Clone Watch design-convergence + owned-media plan. The June "Australian Clone Watch" LinkedIn edition was posted from an **un-pushed local branch**, so `main`'s `/admin/report-card` diverged from what shipped and the entire LinkedIn automation (client + CLI + export) lived on one laptop. This PR lands it all on `main` and — per the founder decision to fold the redesign in — ships the **final 8-slide carousel** in one pass rather than the transitional 3-card design.

## Contents

**Rebased onto main (3 pre-existing commits):**
- `lib/linkedin/client.ts` — org document-post client (refresh-grant OAuth, versioned Community Management API) + safe validation CLI.
- `app/admin/report-card/*` — the "Modern LinkedIn monthly report" **ledger** design (paper + navy + terracotta, Archivo + JetBrains Mono).
- `turbo.json` — 5 new `LINKEDIN_*` globalEnv vars. (Merged cleanly; `LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN`/`LINKEDIN_ORG_ID` **retained** — still read by `lib/social-publish.ts`, so not dead vars.)

**New in this PR (commit `bbd2583`):**
- **8-slide super-hook carousel** (`page.tsx`): 01 hook · 02 scale + MoM delta · 03 top AU brands · 04 why a lookalike works · 05 global brands · 06 registrar accountability (aggregate) + WHOIS-hidden count · 07 what we did · 08 civic CTA + method link. Page numbers derive from `SLIDE_COUNT`.
- **Live MoM delta** (`report-card-data.ts`): a second reconciled fetch over the prior month, computed live (no dependency on the future `clone_watch_report_summary`). `FIRST_FULL_MONTH` gates the delta so June (Clone Watch launched 2026-05-24 → May is a launch stub) shows a **"first full month tracked" baseline**; the first real delta is July-vs-June.
- **Publish hardening** (`linkedin-post-test.ts`): Dev-Tier 403s on comment-create. Previously an `addComment` throw exited non-zero **after the post was already live** → operator retry → **double-post**. Now best-effort: log the first-comment text to paste manually, treat the live publish as success.
- **Export** (`clone-watch-report-export.ts`): `SLIDE_COUNT` 3 → 8.

## Verification

- `typecheck` + `lint` clean; full web test suite (642) passes incl. `registrarCanonical`.
- June aggregate re-verified against **prod** — reconciles exactly to the internal digest: **804 detected / 129 brands / 628 Netcraft / 25 phishing / 51 parked / 378 WHOIS-hidden**.
- All 8 slides verified to fit 1080×1350 (≥220px spare) via a static Puppeteer harness rendering **real June data + the actual CSS** — screenshots reviewed for both the June baseline and a July-style MoM-delta render.
- Honesty guardrails baked into copy: "lookalike/copycat/suspected" never "confirmed clones"; Netcraft = reported for review, not a takedown; registrars in aggregate only; MoM window always stated.

## Reviewer note

`ADMIN_SECRET` isn't in local env, so the live `report-card:export` loop couldn't run here — **the Vercel preview is the live visual gate**. After preview goes green, open `/admin/report-card?month=2026-06` and eyeball the 8 slides before merge.

No schema changes. No migrations. No new env vars beyond the rebased `LINKEDIN_*` (already set in Vercel Prod+Preview).

author: emrebulutlar
body:
## P5.1: the failover E2E — P1's acceptance test on a clean clone

`e2e/failover_e2e.py` (stdlib Python) brings up a **real 3-node Aeron cluster** (embedded media drivers, SHARED threading, 1m term buffers) plus a **real OMS** against Postgres and Redis, then:

1. streams crossing limit orders (80 pre-kill),
2. `kill -9`s the **current leader** mid-load and keeps submitting through the election (80 more; requires ≥20 accepted),
3. restarts the killed node and waits for rejoin (with retry past the mark-file liveness window),
4. drains to quiescence and asserts, exactly:
   - every order terminal, nothing stuck open
   - per-order `filledQty == SUM(executions)` (PG)
   - every tradeId = one BUY + one SELL, equal price/qty
   - balances = seed ± execution deltas **to the satoshi**, `locked = 0`
   - `/api/v1/positions` = net of executions (dogfoods oms#40)
   - the failover was real (leader changed, orders accepted post-kill)

Runs as the new `e2e` CI job (Postgres/Redis services, log artifact on failure). Safe on a dev box next to a live stack: isolated ports (19000), isolated aeron dirs, own database (refuses `oms`), optional `E2E_CPUSET` pinning — see `e2e/README.md` for the war stories (an unpinned 16m-term run can freeze a 31G box and blip a live cluster's 1s leader heartbeat).

## Three real bugs found and fixed en route

1. **Stuck PENDING_NEW zombies after a quiet failover.** Orders whose create/ack died at the seam were still inside the 10s orphan age gate when the post-reconnect reconcile ran — and on a quiet cluster nothing ever triggered another reconcile. They sat PENDING_NEW forever, uncancellable ("in-flight, retry shortly"), eating slots. Fix: 1s **stale-orphan sweep** (`OmsCoreEngine.hasStaleSubmittedOrphans` + `OmsEgressAdapter.sweepStaleOrphans`, sharing the existing 5s resnapshot rate limiter; self-quenching). Unit-tested.
2. **oms#23 — executions FK race, measured.** An instant crossing fill reaches the `executions` insert before the order row's first upsert: **232 ground-truth ledger rows silently lost in one 160-order run**. `persistExecution` now upserts the order row and retries once.
3. **`V001__init_schema.sql` fails on PostgreSQL 16** (partitioned `ledger_entries` PK lacked the partition column). The live dev db silently has no `ledger_entries` table for this reason. PK is now `(entry_id, entry_time)`.

## Verification
- Local run (pinned, isolated): **PASS** in 70s — 160/160 orders, failover node1→node2 with 80 accepted through the election, all invariants exact.
- Unit suites all green (oms-core 25 incl. the new sweep test).
- New jar (sweep + FK fix) **deployed to the dev box** and healthy.
- The CI `e2e` job runs on this very PR ↓

Closes #41

## Summary
- Extend the existing PyTorch matmul device compatibility hook to patch `matvec` as well.
- Move `matvec` operands to an existing non-CPU tensor device before dtype promotion and multiplication.
- Add backend-portable regressions for raw PyTorch under the NumPy-selected public backend and for the selected public PyTorch backend.

## Bug fixed
`pyrecest._backend.pytorch.matvec(torch.eye(2), torch.ones(2, device="meta"))` previously materialized the matrix on CPU while preserving the vector on `meta`, so the subsequent PyTorch matrix-vector operation hit a mixed-device runtime error. The same pattern can occur with accelerator tensors. The patched helper now follows the same preferred-device behavior as the existing `matmul` compatibility hook.

author: kgdunn
body:
## What this adds

Two topics the optimal-designs section already motivated (adding runs to an existing design; mixed continuous/categorical factors) but did not develop. Both are new subsections in `optimal-designs.rst`.

### 1. "Augmenting an existing design"

After a screening experiment leaves several competing models, you add runs rather than start over. Covers:

- the combined-information view: the follow-up maximizes `det(X1'X1 + X2'X2)`, the determinant of the *total*, not `det(X2'X2)` on its own, so new runs go where information is still scarce (the interactions) instead of re-measuring main effects the original runs already pin down;
- the coordinate-exchange search run over the new rows `X2` only, holding `X1` fixed;
- a block term coded +1 for the original runs and -1 for the follow-up runs, to absorb any drift in the process mean between the two campaigns;
- why the follow-up needs only as many runs as new terms, contrasted with the classical foldover (which doubles the run count and de-aliases only a fixed set of effects);
- comparing the surviving models with R², RMSE, and the corrected AIC (AICc).

### 2. "Categorical factors with several levels"

A categorical factor with more than two levels needs indicator (dummy) columns; all of them plus an intercept are collinear (they sum to the intercept column), so `X'X` is singular. Covers:

- the remedies: drop the intercept, drop one dummy (reference level), or sum-to-zero (effects) coding, noting the book's -1/+1 two-level coding is exactly effects coding for L = 2;
- robustness via interactions between a categorical (noise) factor and the continuous factors: choosing continuous settings where the predicted response is flat across the categorical levels;
- why I-optimality (prediction) suits such a response-surface model better than D-optimality (estimation), cross-referencing the material already in the chapter.

## Supporting changes

- Adds labelled anchors to the foldover section and the exchange-algorithms subsection so the new `:ref:` links resolve.
- Adds the Goos and Jones optimal-design book to the chapter reference list, cited where both topics are developed. `CITATION.cff` already carries today's date, so it is unchanged.

## What did not change

No existing prose, figures, code, or analysis was altered. The changes are two new subsections, two anchor labels, and one reference entry.

## Verification

- `make text`: succeeds with no new warnings. The only warnings are the pre-existing "image file not readable" / "include file not found" ones from the `figures/` submodule not being present in the build environment; there are zero cross-reference, undefined-label, or table warnings, and all new `:ref:` links resolve.
- `make html`: succeeds; pages build as extensionless files; `grep -r goatcounter _build/html/contents` returns zero hits.

## Note for reviewers

This branch is off `main` and adds the Goos and Jones reference entry independently of the open PR #199, which adds the same one-line entry. If #199 merges first, expect a trivial, identical-line conflict on that single reference line.

author: omarshahine
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the bundled `imsg` skill read like a generic CLI reference and did not guide OpenClaw agents through DM vs group targeting, bridge-only features, or safety-sensitive iMessage actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The skill now starts from the agent workflow: resolve the conversation, choose DM/existing group/new group, pick the lowest-capability command, confirm sends and visible state changes, and then execute with stable identifiers. It also documents current `imsg` surfaces for replies, formatting, reactions, polls, watch, long-running RPC, and private API actions while keeping public AppleScript permissions separate from bridge-backed IMCore behavior.

## User Impact

OpenClaw agents get clearer guidance for using `imsg` correctly across direct messages and group chats. They should be less likely to send to ambiguous recipients, mutate groups accidentally, confuse public `react` with bridge `tapback`, or run `imsg launch` without user approval.

## Evidence

Documented commands verified against the installed **imsg 0.12.2** on macOS 26 (this is a docs change, so proof = the documented surface matches the real CLI):

```console
$ imsg --version
0.12.2

# Poll surface the skill documents — --question/--option/--reply-to/vote flags exist,
# and there is deliberately NO --comment (that lives in openclaw/imsg#155, not shipped):
$ imsg poll --help | grep -E '^\s+--'
  --chat <value>        chat guid or rowid
  --chat-id <value>     chat rowid
  --question <value>    poll question
  --reply-to <value>    guid of message to reply to
  --option <value>      poll option text; pass at least twice
  --poll <value>        vote: guid of the poll message to vote on
  --option-id <value>   vote: UUID of the option to select
  --option-index <value>  vote: 1-based option number to select

# Capability keys the skill tells agents to gate on:
$ imsg status --json | jq '{bridge_version, v2_ready, basic_features, advanced_features}'
{ "bridge_version": 2, "v2_ready": true, "basic_features": true, "advanced_features": true }

# The documented poll-read jq filter returns real poll objects from history:
$ imsg history --chat-id <id> --limit 40 --json \
    | jq -s '[.[] | select(.poll != null) | {kind: .poll.kind}] | group_by(.kind) | map({(.[0].kind): length}) | add'
{ "created": 5, "vote": 3 }
```

Also: `git diff --check -- skills/imsg/SKILL.md` clean; `pnpm docs:list` used to identify relevant iMessage docs context.

**Scope note:** an earlier revision documented the poll caption echo, `--comment` override, and inbound question backfill; those live in openclaw/imsg#155, not shipped imsg 0.12.2, and were removed in 01e9c38 so this skill documents only shipped behavior (see the `poll --help` proof above). They'll be re-added once a release ships #155.

author: mzdnick
body:
On the Mazda platform ignitionLine remains high after ignition is turned off, resulting in a false positive that keeps the device onroad. This change prioritizes ignitionCan once seen, which is a more reliable signal that immediately goes low when ignition is turned off. Resolves CAN bus errors users see from using third-party harnesses that supply 12V through the harness.

Validated against Comma's dataset of 188k car segments, identified no cases which would cause regression. Test shortcoming - the dataset is likely missing beginning/ending segments.

author: millyinvr
body:
Social-first plan **step C2**. Two supply-side growth levers for the Looks social loop. Requires AM1 (UGC moderation queue, #497) — DONE.

## 1. Milestone nudges → the look author
A new `LOOK_MILESTONE_REACHED` event fires a one-time **"Your look hit N likes / N saves"** notification each time a like/save threshold is crossed — likes **10 / 50 / 100**, saves **10 / 50**. These double as posting nudges (the "your content is performing, post more" signal).

- Detection is a **range crossing** (`previous < T <= current`), never equality — counts are recomputed by full re-count and can jump under concurrency. The like/save routes diff the pre-mutation count (now added to `lookAccessSelect`) against the recomputed count post-commit.
- A **permanent per-threshold** `dedupeKey` (`look:<id>:milestone:<metric>:<T>`) makes each threshold fire **exactly once ever**. Downward moves (unlike/unsave) never notify.
- Routed to the pro **or** client author via the existing `lookAuthorRecipient`. **In-app + push** (A4's social-push decision). Emitted outside the tx, best-effort, guarded by the notification-kick check.
- Also surfaces on the client **Activity feed** (the pre-existing `milestone` icon kind).
- Registered across the full surface: Prisma enum, `eventKeys.ts` (definition + PRO/CLIENT lists), `preferenceCategories.ts` (Social category), `renderNotificationContent.ts`, `activityFeed.ts`.

## 2. Unlock client looks — decision **(b) per-look flag**
Client-shared looks were gated out of discovery until the author's whole **profile** was public, so the share-your-look pipeline produced content nobody saw. Now:

- New **`LookPost.publicToFeed`** column — a per-look opt-in independent of profile. The feed OR clause switches from `clientAuthor.isPublicProfile` → `publicToFeed`.
- Client looks are created **`moderationStatus: PENDING_REVIEW`** → they land in the **AM1 `/admin/looks` PENDING queue** and are **not publicly visible until a human approves** them (App Store UGC pre-moderation). `publicToFeed` carries the client's public/unlisted choice so an approved public look surfaces immediately; unlisting pulls it back.
- Migration **backfills** `publicToFeed=true` for existing eligible client looks (public profile + PUBLIC visibility) so there's **no feed regression**.
- The `MODERATION_SCAN_LOOK_POST` processor stays a **deferred stub** — rather than enqueue a throwing job, `PENDING_REVIEW` + the AM1 human queue **is** the moderation gate (the AM1-note's sanctioned "at minimum" path). Real automated content scanning remains a separate project.

## Migration
`20260704040000_add_look_milestone_and_client_feed` — additive: `NotificationEventKey` enum value + `publicToFeed` column + backfill. Applies on the next `vercel --prod` (**now 6 migrations queued** behind it: Phase 2 ×3, B2, AM1, this).

## iOS parity
**Automatic / server-decided** for both parts — milestone notifications flow through the existing push/in-app pipeline, and the client-look gate + moderation status are set server-side (the iOS share flow already sends `isPublic`; the feed API applies the new gate). No iOS change.

## Verification
`typecheck` + `lint` (0 errors) + `check:static-guards` (all pass, api-schema in sync) + **731 vitest** green across `lib/notifications` / `lib/looks` / `lib/search` / `app/api/v1/looks` (16 new: milestone crossing/dedupe/routing unit tests, activity-feed milestone render, updated feed + clientLookService fixtures). Not runtime-verified (needs seeded looks + authed users + SUPER_ADMIN browser — Tori to eyeball, per the AM1/B2 precedent). No deploy.
