author: pinkiiilqwq
body:
## Review series

This is PR 3 of the stacked OpenTag message-area polish series:

- #24 / upstream #166: Markdown readability and rendering support (merged upstream)
- #25: chat message layout and composer polish
- #26: agent reply preview / streaming identity state machine
- #27: daemon/runtime reliability

This PR is stacked on #25. It focuses on the preview identity and realtime reply protocol. Runtime crash hardening remains split into #27.

## Problem

The previous realtime preview contract had several user-visible gaps:

- A message could wake an agent while the chat looked idle until the final persisted message arrived.
- Empty preview messages could exist in state but render invisibly because the UI only showed bodies with non-empty `content`.
- Runtime deltas, server wake events, errors, and final persisted messages did not share a stable preview identity.
- Two quick messages to the same agent/channel could create multiple preview cards while the daemon debounce buffer kept only one stream id, leaving an orphan `Thinking...` preview.
- The final persisted message could replace the preview with a different React key, causing a perceptible remount/jump after streaming finished.
- Users could send a message and remain away from the live tail, requiring manual scrolling to see their own send or the agent preview.

## Changes

- Publishes an ephemeral `agent:reply start` as soon as the server determines that a message will wake an agent.
- Uses a stable stream identity based on the trigger message and target agent.
- Maintains a frontend contract of one active preview per `agentId + channelId`.
- Supersedes older same-agent/same-channel previews when a newer wake arrives inside the debounce window.
- Ignores stale `delta` / `done` / `error` events for superseded stream ids.
- Preserves independent previews across different agents or channels.
- Keeps ephemeral previews separate from persisted messages in the frontend reducer.
- Delays the preview card by `1s`, then shows localized `Thinking...` / `正在思考...` immediately when there is no text yet.
- Typewrites incoming preview text quickly once daemon/runtime output arrives.
- Forces own sends and agent previews back to the live tail so users do not have to drag the scrollbar manually.
- Keeps a UI-only `clientRenderKey` from preview through final persisted message replacement, preventing the end-of-stream remount jump.
- Deletes the final persisted message from the new-message animation queue when it is absorbed by an existing preview.
- Consumes stale same-agent/same-channel previews when the final persisted message arrives.
- Shows a visible error state if the reply stream fails instead of leaving an empty card behind.
- Forwards `streamId` from server wake messages through daemon delivery.
- When deliver debounce merges multiple wake events, keeps the latest server stream id so later deltas/done events target the visible preview.

## Daemon release/docs

This changes the daemon/server wire contract, so this PR also:

- updates `ARCHITECTURE.md` with the `agent:reply` preview protocol;
- bumps `packages/daemon/package.json` to `0.8.2`;
- adds a `CHANGELOG.md` entry for the daemon reply-preview streaming contract.

The UI can still degrade gracefully with an older daemon, but the intended preview identity behavior requires the updated daemon to reuse the server-provided `streamId`.

## Visual evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a36e419-59f3-4f1a-a122-3eef976e17b5

## Scope boundary

This PR does not make an underlying runtime emit tokens if that runtime adapter only reports final text today. It makes the OpenTag reply-preview channel generic and stable; true first-token streaming still depends on each runtime adapter forwarding live text deltas into the preview channel.

Daemon/runtime failure hardening is intentionally kept out of this PR and split into #27.

## Validation

- `node --test --import tsx test/agentReplyPreview.unit.test.ts test/messageHeaderLayout.unit.test.ts test/showcaseOpenHoverHighlight.unit.test.ts src/daemon/agentManager.test.ts` - 39/39 passed
- `npm run typecheck` - passed
- `npm run build --prefix web` - passed
- `npm run pkg:daemon:build` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

Full `node --test --import tsx "test/**/*.unit.test.ts"` was attempted locally before this stack update, but the sandbox blocked unrelated subprocess IPC and Redis/network access (`EPERM` on tsx IPC pipe and ioredis connection attempts). The targeted preview/identity tests above cover this PR's regression paths, including the same-agent consecutive wake orphan-preview case.

author: greven145
body:
## Why

Basic Azure Container Registry is a flat **~$5/mo** and, after scale-to-zero + Log Analytics capping already shipped, it's the dominant fixed cost in the infra. GHCR is free for this repo (already hosts `frontend-ci`). This moves the API image to a **public GHCR package** and removes ACR entirely.

## What changed

**Infra — remove ACR, pull from public GHCR**
- `api-containerapp.module.bicep`: drop the `registries` block and the ACR-pull managed identity from `userAssignedIdentities` (ACA pulls the public image anonymously); keep only the API's own identity for the Cosmos data-plane connection.
- `env.module.bicep`: remove `env_mi`, the **AcrPull** role assignment, the `env_acr` reference, and the `AZURE_CONTAINER_REGISTRY_*` outputs.
- `main.bicep`: remove the `env-acr` module + ACR outputs.
- Delete `infra/env-acr/env-acr.module.bicep`.
- `api.tmpl.bicepparam`: drop the two ACR param lines (kept in sync).

**CI — build/push to GHCR instead of `azd deploy api`**
- Replace `azd deploy api` with: `dotnet publish /t:PublishContainer` (no Dockerfile — same SDK container mechanism azd used) → push to `ghcr.io/greven145/yet-another-factory-planner/api:<sha>` → apply the **same committed api module** via `az deployment group create`, feeding the GHCR image + pinned `BLUE_REVISION` (module params sourced from `azd env get-value`).
- Blue-green traffic pinning / smoke / shift / rollback are **unchanged** (all pure `az containerapp`).
- `deploy` job: `packages: read` → `write`.

## Verification

- ✅ `az bicep build` passes for `main.bicep`, `env.module.bicep`, `api-containerapp.module.bicep` (remaining lint warnings are pre-existing unused-param lints).
- ✅ API image **builds** via the new SDK container command (`mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0` base).
- ✅ Image **boots & serves** — ran the container, `/alive` returns 200 in ~2s; the Cosmos warmup failure against a dummy endpoint is correctly non-blocking (matches the liveness design).
- Note: the changed **deploy** path is `main`-only, so branch CI runs only the build/test gates; the GHCR push + `az deployment` steps first execute on merge to `main`.

## ⚠️ Two one-time manual steps (the savings depend on these)

1. **Make the GHCR `api` package public** after the first push — it's created private by default, and ACA's anonymous pull 401s until it's public.
2. **Delete the orphaned ACR** — `azd provision` uses *incremental* ARM deploys and will **not** delete the registry once it leaves the template. Run `az acr delete` on the existing Basic ACR to actually stop the ~$5/mo.

## Out of scope / heads-up

`AppHost.cs`'s `PublishAsAzureContainerApp` still describes the old ACR setup, but the committed bicep is authoritative for deploys (already diverged, e.g. `minReplicas`). Running `azd infra synth` would regenerate ACR wiring — not addressed here.

author: robfrank
body:
## What does this PR do?

Deepens the Java Bolt certification from 4 smoke tests to the full **39-scenario** shared conformance spec (`bolt/conformance/spec.yaml`, A1/#4883), driven by the real `neo4j-java-driver`, so the Java column of the compatibility matrix (#4892) is comparable to the already-merged JS (#4888) and Go (#4887) columns.

Certification only - **no production Bolt code is changed**. Every unsupported cell is proven and documented as a known limitation tracked by #4890, never silently omitted.

Two certification layers:

- **e2e** (`e2e/RemoteBoltDatabaseIT`): `@Nested` per feature-matrix area, real driver against `arcadedata/arcadedb:latest`. Every test embeds its scenario id in a `@DisplayName` (spec traceability convention). The original 4 tests are preserved.
- **bolt-module**: `BoltTlsIT` gains `[CONN-002]`/`[CONN-005]` tags on its existing TLS tests; new `BoltTypeRoundTripTest` pins the wire-level serialization contract for temporal/Duration so a #4890 fix is caught exactly where it lands.

Expected-fail scenarios use a small `assertExpectedFailure` helper mirroring the JS suite's `it.failing` (passes while the gap reproduces, fails loudly when it closes). `@Disabled` is used only for the two un-drivable scenarios: CONN-004 (needs a real 3-node HA cluster) and ERR-003 (needs a raw socket to send RUN before LOGON).

Driver-version range (AC4): the suite runs on the 6.2.0 baseline by default; an opt-in `-Pbolt-driver-legacy` Maven profile resolves the `oldest-supported-4.x` band to 4.4.20 and runs a stable-API `RemoteBoltLegacyDriverIT` (the full suite uses 5.x+ driver API, so it is excluded from compilation under that profile). The full driver-version matrix and nightly scheduling remain #4891.

### Verdict reconciliation (per the spec README)

Running against the real image settled the `unverified`/hinted scenarios; `spec.yaml` is updated in this PR to match reality:

- TYPE-007..010 (temporal) confirmed **native** (already `passing` on main; `BoltTypeRoundTripTest` pins this at the wire level).
- TX-005 / ERR-004: write-write conflicts **do** surface `Neo.TransientError.*` (retryable). Certified positively via two overlapping explicit transactions, matching e2e-js/e2e-go.
- TYPE-003 (Path), TYPE-011 (Duration), TYPE-012 (Point), ERR-002 (semantic code), RESULT-004 (counters), PROTO-002 (Bolt 5.x): remain documented gaps (#4890).
- Flipped TX-004, CAUSAL-001, MDB-002, RESULT-002, PROTO-003 `unverified` -> `passing`.

## Motivation

Part of epic #4882 (Bolt Driver Compatibility Certification), Group B. Certify depth, not presence, from one shared spec across all five official drivers.

## Related issues

- Part of #4882
- Implements #4889
- Surfaces/certifies gaps tracked by #4890

## Additional Notes

- **CONN-003** (`neo4j://` routing) is certified as a passing test but is only fully verifiable in Linux CI: `handleRoute` advertises the server's bound bridge IP (e.g. `172.17.0.x`), which is host-routable on the CI runner but not through Docker Desktop's VM on macOS/Windows. This is documented inline and matches the identical e2e-js/e2e-go treatment. `bolt://` scenarios are unaffected (mapped host port).
- Local run (macOS/Docker Desktop): 35 pass, 2 disabled, CONN-003 CI-only.
- `bolt/conformance/validate_spec.py` passes (39 scenarios, 9 areas).

## Checklist

- [x] I have run the build using `mvn clean package` command (e2e + bolt test modules compile; e2e ITs and BoltTypeRoundTripTest run green locally except the CI-only CONN-003)
- [x] My unit tests cover both failure and success scenarios (passing, expected-fail/xfail, and disabled paths all represented)

Successfully installed and configured Vercel Speed Insights for this React + Vite project following the latest official documentation from https://vercel.com/docs/speed-insights/quickstart.

## Changes Made

### 1. Package Installation

- Updated `package.json` to include the new dependency
- Updated `package-lock.json` with the new package and its dependencies

### 2. Component Configuration
Modified `src/App.tsx`:
- Added import statement: `import { SpeedInsights } from '@vercel/speed-insights/react'`
- Added `<SpeedInsights />` component alongside the existing `<Analytics />` component at the root level of the application

author: isazajuancarlos
body:
More attack coverage on the newest surface.

### New: honey parser fuzzer (`src/lab/honey_fuzz.rs`)
Feeds **adversarial byte strings** to `honey::decrypt` and asserts it **never panics** and never allocates unbounded — only `Ok(decoy)` or a structural error. A panic is caught via `catch_unwind` and reported as a breach. Strategies: pure random bytes, valid-magic + random tail, giant declared length (probes the `MAX_TOKENS` cap), insane KDF params (probes the `is_sane` anti-DoS gate), and truncated / tail-padded valid containers. 1000 inputs per run.

### Red-team soak knob (`examples/redteam.rs`)
- Adds the `honey-fuzz` surface to the consolidated runner.
- `QUIPU_REDTEAM_SCALE=N` multiplies every attack budget (default `1×`) for soak runs, without changing CI defaults.

### Evidence
- Full test matrix green: default **139**, honey **150**, lab **154**, slh **155**, lab+slh+honey **184**.
- Red-team (normal, all features): **10 surfaces · 2586 attempts · 0 breaches**.
- Soak `×10`: **15 450 attempts · 0 breaches · defenses intact**.
- The parser fuzzer found **no panics** across every input class.

CI runs the fuzzer in the security-lab job.

body:
Sub-project 3 on the live Commerce Core: tenants run their own store on their own Stripe Connect account, gated by the `store` add-on, surfaced as a public-site block with guest checkout. Includes the spec + plan. **Backend deployed + smoke-tested on the demo tenant; frontend deploy follows this merge.**

## What's here (Tasks 1–4, each reviewed)
- **Tenant catalog RPC** `gw_store_list_tenant_products(slug)` — SECURITY DEFINER, add-on-gated, tenant-scoped, catalog-only.
- **Guest tenant checkout** — `store-checkout` resolves the tenant from a validated `tenant_slug` for guests (JWT still wins), applies the `store` add-on gate, resolves the tenant's Connect account **before** creating the order, tenant `success_url` returns to the tenant's own site.
- **Store public-site block** — rewired `merch.tsx`: tenant catalog + cart (no price) + guest tenant checkout + a display-only success banner.
- **`store` module** — `hasStore` flag, billing-module catalog row, admin hard-gated on `hasStore`, Connect prompt reusing `box-office-connect-onboarding`.

## Review loop caught + fixed
- Guest could spam `pending` orders before the Connect check → moved the check above order creation.
- Tenant buyers bounced to the platform `/shop/success` → tenant `success_url` now returns to their own site.

## Smoke test (prod, demo tenant) — PASSED
Guest checkout (no login) → Connect direct charge on demo's account → fulfill → paid → refund via `store-refund` (Connect-aware) → refunded.
**Also found + fixed a live prod bug:** the Stripe Connect webhook endpoint was subscribed to `account.updated` only — added `checkout.session.completed` so Connect direct charges (tenant stores AND Box Office tenant tickets) now fulfill via webhook.

## NOT done / notes
- **Frontend deploy** (store block + admin gating) follows this merge — the tenant store block isn't visible until main is rebuilt + rsync'd.
- Migrations already applied to prod; `store-checkout` already deployed.
- Follow-ups: `gw_products` base-table permissive policy (mitigated by tenant-isolation, low risk); Connect onboarding `return_url` bounces to Box Office (account still set); `store` module price left dark.

## TelemetryOS instrumentation PR

Implements OpenTelemetry instrumentation for **12 SLIs** on **Go-rest-api**, as agreed in the [SLO contract](https://telemetryos.vercel.app/slos/cmr4br2nr0001la04ibk9it57/cmr4br2qe0002la04otssv65e) (v1).

> ⛔ **Opened as a draft.** The automated self-review found blocking issues it couldn't auto-resolve within the iteration budget. Review the outstanding items below before marking ready.

> Wove instrumentation into **3 existing files** and added 3 new files, generated against `094fa38` (`main`). ⚠ 1 edit(s) couldn't be applied automatically — see `telemetryos/INSTRUMENTATION.md`.

### Setup & self-review
**Detected setup:** go · go-modules · host: docker · telemetry: none → wiring model **app-sdk** _(low confidence — please confirm)_
**Self-review:** 3 generation passes — ⛔ unresolved blocking issues — opened as DRAFT.
**Auto-fixed during review (6):**
- qr-not-a-noop (`cmd/server.go`): main() never calls initMetrics(), so globalMetrics stays nil and every RecordAuthAttempt/RecordFlowOutcome/RecordValidationOutcome and the saturation/flow middleware early-return without emitting any metrics. None of the custom instruments are ever created.
- qr-preserves-behavior (`cmd/server.go`): The otelhttp-wrapped handler is assigned to instrumentedRouter and then discarded with `_ = instrumentedRouter`; api.StartServer is called with the raw `router`, so http.server.request.duration is never emitted and the otelhttp wrapping is dead code.
- qr-not-a-noop (`cmd/otel_middleware.go`): otelSaturationMiddleware and otelFlowMiddleware are defined but never registered on the chi router in server.go, so active_requests, flow.outcomes and flow.duration are never recorded.
- general (`cmd/telemetry.go`): activeRequests, flowValidationOutcomes and RecordValidationOutcome are declared/created but never invoked anywhere in the diff (the validation-outcomes SLI is never recorded), leaving them as unused instrumentation.
- general (`go.mod`): go.mod requires go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.27.0 (imported in cmd/otel.go) and go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace / sdk/resource, but the semconv package version v1.27.0 is not present under otel v1.33.0's semconv tree — otel v1.33.0 ships semconv/v1.26.0, not v1.27.0, so the import will fail to resolve and the build breaks.
- qr-preserves-behavior (`cmd/otel_middleware.go`): The statusRecorder wraps the ResponseWriter but does not implement http.Flusher/http.Hijacker/io.ReaderFrom, and it silently discards these interfaces. More importantly, since the otelFlowMiddleware wraps every response and the deleteThing handler calls resp.WriteHeader(204) then ReturnText, wrapping changes nothing there — but the wrapper is placed inside the chi middleware chain that also handles the /metrics Prometheus handler, whose streaming/flushing capability is lost, degrading existing behavior.
**Outstanding (4):**
- ⚠ qr-endpoint-env-driven (`cmd/otel.go`:4): Hardcoded OTLP endpoint "localhost:4317" — wrong in every real deployment. — _Read the endpoint from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT / config instead of a literal._
- ⛔ general (`cmd/server.go`:24): gotelhttp.WithServerName is not a valid option in the otelhttp package; the correct option is otelhttp.WithServerName does not exist — the package provides WithServerName only via... it is not present, causing a compile error (undefined: otelhttp.WithServerName). — _Remove the WithServerName option (use gotelhttp.NewHandler(router, "") or a valid option such as WithSpanNameFormatter)._
- ⚠ general (`cmd/otel.go`:11): The diff imports go.opentelemetry.io/otel/semconv/v1.26.0 but this package is only provided by go.opentelemetry.io/otel (already a dependency); however resource.WithProcess and resource.WithOS pull in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource which is part of the sdk module — fine — but semconv v1.26.0 exists only in otel v1.28+, and pinned otel v1.33.0 does include it, so ensure the version path matches the module. — _Confirm the semconv/v1.26.0 path exists in otel v1.33.0; otherwise use the semconv version shipped with the pinned otel release._
- ⛔ edit-not-applied (`pkg/auth/jwt.go`): An intended edit to pkg/auth/jwt.go could not be applied (its target text wasn't found verbatim, wasn't unique, or overlapped another edit), so the file was left unchanged to avoid a half-applied result: Anchor edit — RecordValidationOutcome is wired inside the existing JWT middleware body below. — _Re-express this as one or more SMALL hunks whose oldString is copied verbatim from the CURRENT source and is unique; don't restate a large block. Keep declarations and their uses in edits that apply together._

### SLIs

- **Go-rest-api — HTTP Response Time P95** (`go-rest-api-http-latency-p95`) — target < 200ms over 1-hour — from: SRE Book, Ch. 4 — customer-facing latency

author: nathanielshochat2021
body:
## What

Two CRM dashboard fixes the owner flagged from live use.

### 1. Cold-outreach prospects were flooding "Needs your attention"
The lead-finder creates a CRM `Client` card per discovered dispensary (so the outreach engine can enroll it from there). Once the engine sends a **cold email**, the send logs an `email` touch — which flipped the old `everContacted` suppression and made every scanned shop demand a "next step," burying the owner's real work.

`classifyHeadsUp` now holds a **not-yet-warm outreach prospect** (tagged `dispensary`/`cold-email`, no `warm` tag, non-customer) *out of the heads-up feed entirely* **unless** the owner personally touched it (`call`/`text`/`visit` — `email` excluded so an automated send never counts) **or** scheduled a follow-up. It re-enters automatically the moment it replies (warm-handoff stamps `warm` + a follow-up) or the owner sets a next step. Non-destructive, and it mirrors the existing "warm-handoff is the graduation" model — the cards stay in the collection so outreach can still enroll them.

### 2. "460% likely to land"
The Conversion card divided the weighted forecast over **all** stages (realized won/customer deals carry probability 1) by the **open-only** base — so a book with more landed clients than open pipe read 460%. `summarizePipeline` now also returns `weightedOpenValue` (expected value of the **open** stages only); the frontend divides that by the open base, so numerator and denominator share one stage set and the rate is inherently ≤ 100%.

## Testing
- `npm test` → **856 pass**. New coverage: an enrolled+emailed cold prospect earns zero attention items; an owner-touched (call) or replied (warm) prospect still surfaces; `weightedOpenValue` never exceeds the open base.

Ships with the frontend Conversion-card fix. First slice of a larger CRM-hygiene pass (chains cleanup, bulk cold-prospect archive, and the action-framed cockpit still to come).

author: thellert
body:
## Summary

Hardens a fragile, nondeterministic test pattern surfaced while investigating #331 (the #327 fix). Several "architectural wiring guard" tests asserted on `inspect.getsource(...)` **substrings**. This PR replaces them with behavioral assertions (where a function's effect can be exercised directly) and deterministic fresh-file reads (for module-level "this wiring line exists" guards).

## Why

`inspect.getsource(fn)` locates a definition by slicing file lines using the code object's `co_firstlineno` against a `linecache` copy of the file. When the loaded bytecode (`.pyc`) and the on-disk source drift — a transient `.py`/`.pyc` skew, e.g. right after editing a module and clearing its `__pycache__` — the line numbers and content disagree and `getsource` **silently returns an adjacent definition** instead of raising.

Concretely, `test_ensure_okf_server_alias_exists` failed once in a full-suite run with `inspect.getsource(server_launcher.ensure_okf_server)` returning the source of the *neighbouring* `ensure_lattice_dashboard_server`, while passing in every isolated run. It is not order-dependent (an identical-order rerun passed), and it cannot recur on a clean CI checkout (bytecode compiled once) — but the underlying pattern is unreliable in both directions: it can false-fail (observed) or false-pass (if the mis-sliced neighbour happens to contain the expected string). The reproduction was confirmed with a controlled `linecache`/`co_firstlineno`-mismatch experiment.

## What changed

`tests/registry/test_okf_panel_registration.py`:
- `ensure_okf_server` delegation → patch `ensure_web_server`, call the alias, assert it forwarded `"okf"`.
- `_launch_okf_server` → assert it populates `app.state.okf_server_url` (the attr the proxy reads) and delegates to the launcher.
- `okf_server_config` endpoint → call the handler directly and assert it returns the `/panel/okf` proxy path (available and unavailable states).
- Lifespan gate and `build_profile`/`manifest` "reads `BUILTIN_PANELS`" guards → read the module source **fresh from disk** via a small `_fresh_source()` helper instead of `inspect.getsource`.

`tests/mcp_server/ariel/test_capabilities.py`:
- The AST no-registry-import check reads the module source fresh from disk instead of via `inspect.getsource`.

No production code changes; no user-facing behavior change.

## Verification

Affected tests green; `ruff` clean. No `inspect.getsource(<function>)` assertions remain in the test suite (only `getsourcefile`/`getfile` path lookups and the deterministic fresh reads).

body:
## Merge order

**Get Paid 25 of 36.** Merge this PR only after #53. The next PR in the landing sequence is #55.

Base: `pr23-automated-backup`

## Client-side scope

Adds payer-side LUD-22 direct payment to the mobile Send flow. When the recipient exposes the supported endpoint, the app can settle a Bull Lightning Address directly over Liquid instead of creating a Lightning swap.

- Exposes the Liquid UTXO asset ID and derivation address index from the existing LWK wallet boundary.
- Selects an owned, unspent, confidential L-BTC UTXO worth at least 1,000 satoshis and builds the proof-of-funds payload.
- Signs the contract digest with the selected P2WPKH key and sends only the outpoint, public key, DER signature, value, and value/asset blinding factors. No private key or blinding key is transmitted.
- Pins the LNURL callback to the discovered host and strictly validates the direct-pay response and Liquid destination address.
- Treats a missing endpoint or a recoverable direct-pay failure as a soft failure so the existing Lightning-swap rail remains available.
- Clears stale swap state when the direct Liquid rail commits, and shows a small non-blocking success annotation.
- Preserves exact wire amounts: the callback amount is expressed in millisatoshis while the proof value is expressed in satoshis.

This PR changes the Flutter client only. It does not add or modify server behavior.

## Restack intervention

The original eight commits were replayed onto the corrected #53 head. The English ARB fragments introduced by the original branch were malformed at two points; this boundary repairs their object structure, supplies the missing placeholder metadata, regenerates translations, and formats the touched Dart files. The fix is placed here—the earliest branch that introduces those strings—so every descendant inherits valid localization input.

## Validation

- `jq empty localization/app_en.arb`
- `make translations`
- `make build-runner`
- whole-project analyzer
- formatting and fix checks
- focused Send/LUD-22 and wallet-mapper suite: 86 tests passed
- full `TZ=UTC make checks`: 1,103 root tests, 17 `bull_ui` tests, and 1 catalogue test passed

No APK was built, and no server repository was touched.

body:
## Summary
- Make explicit `--top-k` values override the default top-k set instead of appending to it.
- Preserve the default `(1, 3, 5, 10, 20)` behavior when `--top-k` is omitted.

## Rationale
The CLI used `action="append"` with a non-empty default list, so a command such as `--top-k 1` still evaluated the default top-k values too. This made user-requested focused metrics such as `oracle_top1_3d_m_mse` produce extra top-k columns and could invalidate existing CLI expectations.

## Testing
- Covered by existing `test_fit_and_apply_clis_write_truth_free_outputs`, which asserts that `--top-k 1` writes only top-1 metrics.
- Not run locally in this environment; relying on CI.

# Retro — three.js · voxel→realistic HVAC pipeline · 2026-07-04 · Research-SDD self-retrospective

> Run reviewed: bootstrap + B1-B12 (whole run so far, single session). Trigger: budget-cap STOP (12-block
> cap fired with 2 gaps — G11, G13 — still read-only-investigable; §18 fires at corpus-level STOP, which
> this run treated as met).
> Method: a FRESH-CONTEXT agent read the current kit (`PROMPT-LOOP.md` + `METHODOLOGY.md`) FIRST, then the
> run's blocks, commits, RESEARCH-STATE.md, INDEX.md, TARGETS.md, tool-registry.md, and sources/, and
> proposes kit deltas. READ-ONLY on the kit — this report only PROPOSES; kit changes are human-reviewed and
> human-committed (METHODOLOGY §18).

## Proposed kit deltas

| # | Proposed change | Target (file · §/section) | Evidence (block / commit / § / transcript ref) | Type | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add an explicit BOOTSTRAP step: register the new target in `$KIT/TARGETS.md`'s master table (path, maturity, artifact type, toolbelt, language) before/while creating INDEX.md/RESEARCH-STATE.md. | `PROMPT-LOOP.md` §BOOTSTRAP (steps a-f) | `TARGETS.md` master table lists exactly 12 targets ("master registry of the 12 research targets"); three.js is absent. `toolbelt/sweep-retros.sh` derives its ENTIRE scan list from `grep -oE '`/[^`]+`' TARGETS.md` — it cannot discover a target's `retros/` dir unless that target's path is in TARGETS.md. This retro (and any future one for this target) is invisible to the sweeper as things stand. | new | HIGH |
| 2 | Add a tool-registry.md row / METHODOLOGY §5 clause for "docs retrieved via MCP (context7 et al.)" as a distinct source type, and state explicitly whether load-bearing `[CERT-web]`-via-MCP claims must be preserved via `fetch-doc.sh` (like a web link) or are exempt because the MCP source is versioned/re-queryable. | `toolbelt/tool-registry.md` (new row) + `METHODOLOGY.md` §5 | 61 `[CERT-web]` citations across B1-B12, all sourced from context7 MCP queries, zero files landed in `sources/web-snapshots/` (`ls` empty). The target's own `sources/SOURCES.md` self-invented a convention ("Note on context7": treat as `[CERT-web]`, "cross-checked against, and when possible preserved from, threejs.org") that was never executed in 12 blocks — i.e. the operator improvised a policy the kit doesn't specify, then didn't follow their own improvisation. | new | HIGH |
| 3 | Extend METHODOLOGY §15 (corpus versioning) with a sub-rule for the "corpus dir doubles as the subject dir" pattern: gitignore/scope guidance so the SUBJECT's own artifacts (not just orchestrator-local caches) never get swept into the corpus's git history. | `METHODOLOGY.md` §15 | This target's repo IS the HVAC prototype directory: 8 realistic + 15 voxel `.html` files sit alongside the corpus. `git ls-files` = 19 files, zero `.html`, confirming only explicit `git add <corpus-file>` was used per commit (verified on 2 commits' `--stat`) — but `.gitignore` only covers `.atl/`, `.claude/`, `*Zone.Identifier`, `__pycache__/`; it does NOT exclude the subject `.html`/`voxel/` files. The current safety is 100% operator discipline (never running `git add -A`), not a structural guard — §15 today only names orchestrator-local caches as the thing to gitignore, not subject-owned material sharing the dir. | new | MEDIUM |
| 4 | Clarify METHODOLOGY §8's remittance definition: restrict "closed by remittance" to a genuinely PRIOR (already-committed-before-this-iteration) block/section, and name the distinct case where a gap is closed by NEW content that lands in the SAME block/iteration that was investigating a different (related) gap — this is not remittance (no new substance) and not a second full block (violates "one block per iteration" only in spirit, not fact, since it's still one block file). | `METHODOLOGY.md` §8 (remittance paragraph) | Iteration 11 / B11: the CHOSEN gap was G12 (performance); §11.3 (BatchedMesh availability + API + fit) is NEW content written in that same iteration, yet RESEARCH-STATE.md/INDEX.md label G15's closure "closed by remittance → [Block 11] §11.3". Per the current §8 text, remittance requires citing an EXISTING cited block with "NO new substance" — §11.3 is new substance, just serendipitously answering an already-queued adjacent gap in the same sweep. The label is a plausible-but-imprecise improvisation, not a clear kit violation. | refinement | MEDIUM |
| 5 | Distinguish "PAUSED (budget-cap, N gaps still investigable)" from "STOPPED (investigable=0)" in RESEARCH-STATE.md vocabulary, and state explicitly in §8/§18 whether the full TERMINAL TRIGGER machinery (focus-closing synthesis block, mandatory §18 retro) applies the same way to a budget-cap-triggered halt as to a genuine investigable-exhaustion stop. | `METHODOLOGY.md` §8 (stopping criteria) + §18 ("when it fires") | RESEARCH-STATE.md line 15 and INDEX.md both say "RUN STOPPED" for a halt where 2 gaps (G11, G13) remain read-only-investigable — same word used for genuine exhaustion. The run nonetheless wrote a terminal SYNTHESIS block (B12/G14) and triggered this §18 retro, treating the budget cap exactly like corpus-level exhaustion. §8 lists budget cap as a "safety net" (implying lesser status than the PRIMARY exhaustion criterion) but never says whether the synthesis-block/retro apparatus should still fire, or how the report should be worded so a future reader doesn't mistake a budget pause for genuine completion. | refinement | LOW-MEDIUM |

For each delta above, one line of rationale (WHY it matters, what it costs, expected impact):

- **#1** — Without this, EVERY future retro for an unregistered/newly-bootstrapped target is silently unreviewable by the sweeper — the exact failure mode §18's "review lifecycle" section was built to prevent. Cost: one line added to an existing BOOTSTRAP step. Impact: closes a real hole in the propose→sweep→review loop for any target created after `TARGETS.md` was last hand-edited.
- **#2** — context7/MCP is now a first-class research channel (this whole run used it as the PRIMARY source for a docs/web target) but the kit's source-preservation contract (§5) was written with URL-fetch (`fetch-doc.sh`) in mind and never named MCP explicitly. Leaving it unstated means every docs/web target will independently improvise (as this one did, then didn't follow through) instead of following one policy. Cost: a decision + a paragraph. Impact: removes citation-rot risk on `[CERT-web]` claims that currently have zero durable evidence behind them beyond "we queried context7 that day."
- **#3** — The risk is currently zero-cost-to-fix (a `.gitignore` line) but high-blast-radius if it fires (subject IP or bulky prototype files landing in a research corpus's git history via one careless `git add -A`, which is explicitly the anti-pattern §15 already warns about for a DIFFERENT reason). Impact: makes the existing discipline structural instead of tribal.
- **#4** — Low cost (wording only), but matters for corpus self-consistency: a reader auditing "remittance" closures later (§13 audit mode) would reasonably expect the cited block to predate the gap's closure, not be contemporaneous with it. Mislabeling erodes the precision the marker/closure system is designed to guarantee.
- **#5** — Cheap (vocabulary + one clarifying sentence) but prevents a subtle failure: a future session reopening this target (§8 "Reopening a STOPPED loop") needs to know immediately that 2 gaps are still open BY DESIGN (budget, not exhaustion) — the current wording technically already says this in the body text, just not in the headline STOP/PAUSE word choice.

Routing **decision table** (answer inline vs `run_in_background` vs `tell` vs `background_status`). 4. **"Steward, not initiator"** frame + "reaching for justifications = wait" tell (worker). 5. **Reversibility gate**: reversible→act, irreversible→wait/escalate. 6. **Quiet-down rule**: repeated no-op cycles shrink footprint, no "nothing to do" filler. 7. SKILL.md schema (TASK-331) should include an **`unwanted-for` / negative-trigger** field. 8. **Don't silently fall through to a worse tier on skill/MCP error — surface it.** 9. (Larger) effort tiers + hard finding caps for review/analysis workers. ## Relationship to existing work Reinforces **SPR-063 / TASK-331** schema direction (adds the negative/`unwanted-for` field) and adds an orthogonal prompt-copy layer (items 1–6, 8) — wording/behavioral changes to the system prompts, not code, cheap to land and independently testable. ## Purpose

Markdown highlight support in the CLI REPL transcript (requested via cameronhunter/ink-markdown): assistant prose now renders emphasis, inline code, fenced code blocks, lists, quotes, headings, and links with terminal styling instead of raw markdown source.

## What changed

- `apps/cli/src/tui/markdown.tsx` — new `<Markdown>` component, vendored after **cameronhunter/ink-markdown**. We could not depend on the package itself: `ink-markdown@1.0.4` ships CommonJS and `require()`s ink, and ink 7 is ESM with top-level await, so importing it throws `ERR_REQUIRE_ASync_MODULE` at runtime (reproduced before vendoring). Same marked → marked-terminal → `<Text>` pattern, with two improvements: a private `Marked` instance (no global `setOptions` mutation) and a parse-failure fallback to raw text.
- `apps/cli/src/repl/components.tsx` — committed assistant messages render through `<Markdown>` (keeping the ◆ gutter); streaming messages stay raw text until they commit so unclosed fences never flicker mid-parse. Parse is memoized per message; `<Static>` transcript items pay it exactly once.
- Deps: `marked@15.0.12` + `marked-terminal@7.3.0` (exact pins; marked-terminal 7 peers `marked <16`) in `apps/cli` only; lockfile updated. Local `marked-terminal.d.ts` since `@types/marked-terminal` (6.1.1) targets marked <12.

## Verification

- 53 tests pass across the new `markdown.test.tsx` (emphasis/inline-code/fence/list rendering, malformed-markdown fallback) and `components.test.tsx` (committed prose renders markdown with markers consumed; streaming prose stays raw with cursor).
- `pnpm typecheck` and `eslint --max-warnings 0` clean.
- Real ink runtime render captured (`verifications/…/cli-markdown-render.ansi`): heading, bold, inline code, bullets, indented code block, and link all styled with ANSI codes present.

author: mdavistffhrtporg
body:
Closes #18.

## Summary

The threat-model chain builders (`_build_service_chains`, `_build_atproto_chains`) each walked analyzer hints ad-hoc to reason about service-to-service structure. This PR lifts that walk into a reusable, inspectable graph.

## New module: `attackmap.topology`

- `ServiceNode(name, role, files_seen)`
- `ServiceEdge(source, target, kind, file, evidence)`
- `ServiceGraph` — first-seen node order, edge dedup by `(source, target, kind)`
- `build_service_graph(scan)` — computes the graph from an existing `ScanResult`

**Non-invasive:** the graph is computed on demand, **not** attached to `ScanResult`. No changes to the analyzer contract, report schema, or existing merge behavior. All existing 197 tests unchanged.

## Node discovery

1. `service_name:<slug>` hints (across auth, service, and edge hint families)
2. `service_role:<name>` hints annotate the matching node
3. Repo layout fallback: files under `services/<n>/`, `packages/<n>/`, or `apps/<n>/` imply a node named after the directory

## Edge kinds

- **`analyzer-declared`** — explicit `edge:src->dst` hint
- **`http-call`** — outbound URL whose host prefix looks like a peer service
- **`env-configured`** — outbound `env://<VAR>_URL` peer name (node-service pattern)
- **`async-queue`** — `queue://bullmq/<name>` or `queue://kafka/<topic>` from node-service 0.2.0's worker detection

Each edge carries a `file` citation. Callers whose service can't be attributed (no `service_name:` hint, no `services/*` prefix) are dropped — we don't invent sources.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Identify at least basic service boundaries — via explicit hints + layout fallback
- [x] Produce a simple service interaction graph — `ServiceGraph` with typed nodes + edges
- [x] Doesn't require deep protocol understanding — pure heuristic, consumes existing hint prefixes
- [x] Integrates with existing pipeline without breaking it — computed on demand; no schema change

## Tests

**197 → 209 passing (12 new in `tests/test_topology.py`).** Coverage:
- empty scan → empty graph
- service_name hints → nodes
- repo layout fallback
- service_role → `node.role`
- `edge:src->dst` → analyzer-declared edge
- `env://X_URL` → env-configured edge
- `https://peer.example` → http-call edge
- `queue://bullmq/x` and `queue://kafka/x` → async-queue edges
- dedup by `(source, target, kind)`; different kinds coexist
- callers we can't attribute are dropped
- `peers_of` returns first-seen ordered neighbors
- end-to-end multi-service scan mirroring the Bluesky-shape fixture

## Out of scope (worth follow-ups)

- Refactoring the existing chain builders (`_build_service_chains`, `_build_atproto_chains`) to share the graph. Both currently re-derive edges independently; migrating them to consume `ServiceGraph` is safe but cross-cutting.
- Exposing the graph in the LLM prompt / JSON report. Additive — a downstream `review_prompts.py` change can pull it once we validate the shape reads well.
- Trust-boundary annotations on nodes (public / internal / privileged). Requires either a signal from analyzers or a heuristic on which services expose public routes.

author: alandtse
body:
## Summary

### 1. Size the menu canvas 1:1 to the helper panel
Root cause from the helper-side pointer-divergence investigation: the stock ImGui DX11 backend renders draw data into a `DisplaySize`-sized viewport anchored at the panel's **top-left** (it overwrites the blit's panel-sized viewport). The canvas must therefore equal the helper panel's **exact pixel size** — aspect-matching alone shrinks content toward (0,0) while the helper's wand hit-test UV spans the full panel, skewing clicks/aim toward the bottom-right by the size ratio.

Open Shaders' logical canvas (1080-tall × panel aspect) currently equals the 1920×1080 panel exactly, so this is **hardening** (no visible bug today): the identity mapping is now by construction instead of by coincidence, and survives a future supersampled or resized panel. Fonts size from the live canvas height (same physical size on the panel, crisper rasters when larger).

### 2. Own the cursor instead of deferring to the helper's default
`kClientFlag_OwnCursor` was never set at registration, so this client's leftover `MouseDrawCursor` management (predating VR support entirely -- it forced the ImGui software cursor on any time the menu showed, desktop or VR alike) was silently clobbering whatever the helper's `PumpInput` had just set based on the absent flag. An earlier commit on this branch fixed that by gating the client's `MouseDrawCursor` writes to desktop-only, deferring to the helper's composited pointer in VR.

That traded away two things this client already had: its own per-widget content-aware cursor (I-beam over text fields, resize handles, etc. -- ImGui's built-in cursor rendering), and `CursorLoader`'s custom cursor theming, which only draws while `MouseDrawCursor` is true and would otherwise silently stop applying in VR with no indication why. Neither loss is necessary -- this client is already confirmed pointer-divergence-free (see above), so the helper-default's main selling point doesn't uniquely apply here.

Registers `kClientFlag_OwnCursor` so the SDK's own cursor management agrees with what this client already does, and drops the now-unneeded `ownsCursor` gating -- this client owns its cursor everywhere again, VR included, matching pre-existing desktop behavior with no regression.

## Testing
- [x] Built via `cmake --preset ALL && cmake --build --preset ALL` in the main checkout: clean build, `CommunityShaders.dll` produced with no errors.
- [ ] In-headset: cursor still tracks correctly at the wand hit position, and (if configured) `Theme.UseCustomCursor` art still shows in VR.

author: scouten
body:
## Summary

Brings this repo's GitHub Actions / release tooling in line with the sister [`asciidoc-parser`](https://github.com/asciidoc-rs/asciidoc-parser) project, adapted for this **two-crate** workspace (`asciidoc-html5` library + `adoc` CLI).

Before, this repo had a minimal `ci.yml` (stable-only `fmt`/`clippy`/`test` on one OS) plus `release-plz.yml`. This PR mirrors the parser's much richer setup, dropping the two jobs that are parser-specific and have no analogue here.

## Workflow changes

- **Renamed `release-plz.yml` → `release.yml`** to match the sister repo's naming convention. Content is unchanged — this repo's version keeps its SHA-pinned actions and the more robust stale-branch cleanup step, both of which are improvements over the parser's copy.
- **Expanded `ci.yml`** into the full parser job set:
  - `tests` — OS × MSRV matrix (`windows`/`macos`/`ubuntu` × `stable`/`1.88.0`) with `cargo-llvm-cov` coverage uploaded to Codecov (gated so fork PRs don't touch the token).
  - `test-direct-minimal-versions` — nightly `-Z direct-minimal-versions`.
  - `publish-preflight` — crate publish dry-run (see two-crate note below).
  - `clippy_check`, `cargo_fmt` (nightly rustfmt), `taplo_fmt`, `docs_rs`, `internal_docs`, `cargo-deny`, `unused_deps` (cargo-udeps).
  - **Omitted** the parser-only `benchmarks` (codspeed) and `spec-coverage` (`sdd/`) jobs — no equivalent exists in this repo.
- **Added `pr_title.yml`** — validates PR titles as Conventional Commits (feeds release-plz changelog generation).

## Two-crate adaptations

- **`publish-preflight` dry-runs only the `asciidoc-html5` library.** The `adoc` CLI pins the library with an exact (`=`) requirement, so a CLI publish can only be verified once the matching library version is on crates.io — which is exactly the order release-plz publishes them at release time. Dry-running the CLI in CI would fail to resolve the not-yet-published library, so preflight checks only the crate with no unpublished dependency.
- **`codecov.yml`** declares `html5` and `cli` coverage components.
- **`.commitlintrc.no-scope.yml`** allows the Conventional Commit type set this project actually uses (per `CLAUDE.md`: `feat`/`fix`/`docs`/`chore`/`refactor`/`test`/`ci`) plus `update` for Dependabot bumps, rather than the parser's smaller list.
- **MSRV declared** as `rust-version = "1.88.0"` in `[workspace.package]` (matching `asciidoc-parser`, this repo's own required dependency) so the MSRV matrix row is meaningful; both members inherit it.

## Supporting config (ported from the sister repo)

`rustfmt.toml`, `.taplo.toml`, `deny.toml`, `codecov.yml`, `.commitlintrc.no-scope.yml`. Manifests were normalized with Taplo (alphabetical key ordering), which accounts for the reordering in the `Cargo.toml` files.

## Verification

Run locally against this branch — all green:

- `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check` (existing code already conforms; no reformatting needed)
- `taplo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo build --workspace` on **stable**, **1.88.0**, and nightly `-Z direct-minimal-versions`
- `cargo +nightly doc` (docs.rs preflight + `--document-private-items`)
- `cargo deny check advisories` / `bans licenses sources`
- `cargo publish -p asciidoc-html5 --dry-run` (clean tree)
- All workflow YAML parses.

## Notes for reviewers

- The coverage upload requires a **`CODECOV_TOKEN`** repository secret (same as the parser). Fork PRs are gated out of the upload step, but pushes to `main` and internal PRs will need the secret configured, or that step will fail.
- `deny.toml` is a faithful port; `cargo deny` currently emits one harmless *"license was not encountered"* warning for `Unicode-DFS-2016` (allowed but unused in this smaller dependency tree). Left in for parity — it's a warning, not a failure.

author: ghostlygawd
body:
## B056 (P2) — the terminator fold's coverage set was incomplete

B053 shipped the non-Latin terminator-fold *mechanism*, but its set was hand-picked and missed the clause/sentence terminators of many living scripts — Arabic comma `U+060C` / semicolon `U+061B` (the standard separators of Arabic/Persian/Urdu), Armenian `U+0589`, Ethiopic comma, Tibetan shad, Khmer khan, Mongolian/Myanmar/Sinhala/Georgian/Syriac. Proven by internal inconsistency: CJK comma `U+3001` was folded, Arabic comma `U+060C` was not. The verb stays pristine ASCII, so it's genuinely in-scope.

## Fix — comprehensive, not one-glyph-per-cycle (L005)

Rather than add the three the red-team happened to find (the enumeration treadmill L004 warns about), this replaces the curated set with a **comprehensive fold across the major living scripts** to ASCII `.` — so the mechanism is **complete-by-construction**. Verified: all probed common-script terminators now reject; benign findings containing such marks still accept.

## Severity: P2, under a documented rubric (not down-rating to force convergence)

The module docstring now carries an explicit **mechanism-vs-coverage severity rubric**:
- **Mechanism missing / broadly broken → major (P1)**: no adverb handling (B048), line breaks not folded at all (B051), no terminator fold (B053).
- **Coverage gap in a shipped, comprehensive-by-construction mechanism → P2/P3**: one more script's terminator not yet in the fold when it already spans the major scripts (B056). Defense-in-depth, found only by Unicode enumeration, primary framing intact.

The independent red-team agent also rated this **Low**. A further missing terminator from here is **P3 corpus-growth**, not a mechanism defect.

## Tests

- reject-filter corpus **86 → 89** (adv-059 Arabic comma / adv-060 Armenian / adv-061 Khmer); benign 27 unchanged, 100% accept preserved.
- `tests/run-all.sh`: **14/14** green.

## Board (dogfood)

eb-self **B056** resolved; **B057** (P3, `count_scratch_findings` undercounts multi-finding scratch blocks — a labeled status lower-bound, non-security) intaked as tracked. No open blocker/major/P1.

## Convergence

C9's only reject-filter finding is **P2** (coverage gap in a now-comprehensive mechanism); the MCP/bash sweep and Track B/D were **clean**. Under the documented rubric, **C9 has no new blocker/major/P0/P1** — the first clean cycle toward criterion 1. C10 must independently confirm.

## Summary
- Add `papers/imu_dead_reckoning/` (102nd method): pure unaided strapdown INS compact baseline (claim tier T3) — the IMU-only lower-bound reference for the LIO family, complementing the aided DR trio (OdoNet / NN-ZUPT / NHC-Net)
- Static-window initialization (gyro bias estimate + gravity alignment), midpoint quaternion integration, double integration of specific force; opt-in ablation knobs: `--imu-dr-zupt`, `--imu-dr-euler`, `--imu-dr-no-gyro-bias`, `--imu-dr-static-init-sec`

## Honest results (NCLT full session, ~17 min)
| variant | ATE | RPE [%/100m] |
|---|---|---|
| pure DR (default) | 288.7 km | 67435 |
| + ZUPT | 14.5 km (−95%) | 2859 |
| forward Euler | 291.9 km | 68485 |
| no gyro-bias init | 672.3 km (+133%) | 139393 |

Family context: NN-ZUPT 257 m, NHC-Net 280 m, OdoNet 1398 m (KITTI CNN weights out-of-domain on NCLT). Key finding: gyro-bias init is the most load-bearing component; ZUPT removes ~95% of drift despite only 8.3% true stationary fraction (it bounds velocity-error growth between resets).
